“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”. Paul was one who understood that mystery. He wrote: “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains”.

Prophecy is a gift, and Paul had the gift of prophecy. He understood all mysteries. That is why, when we read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul explained a lot of things and took them to another level, making them plain for us, even things in the law that we do not fully understand.

He had all knowledge and all faith. So when Paul says “we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery”, he is speaking as a man who was given to understand the mysteries, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the world unto our glory. That hidden wisdom goes into Christ: who he was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages, and even the princes of this world did not know it, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”. Who are those that love him? Christ said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

There are two types of people in this world: people who say they love God, like the Christians who all say they love the Lord and love Jesus, and people who do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he said and you say you love him, you are a liar.

To the ones who keep his commandments he sends the Spirit: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. And: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. That is how we learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures; it starts with the apostles, and they teach the people.

So we do not teach with man's wisdom from a theology school or seminary; we teach “which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” The things God has prepared for us, the holy city, living forever, being with Christ even if we die keeping the commandments, are on another level. They are freely given to us of God; we just have to keep his commandments.

Christ said: “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given to the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; it is not given to everyone. Once these men understand it, God having revealed it to them, they reveal it to the people and the people understand it. It is given to the apostles first and foremost.

That is the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom. There is hidden wisdom even about Adam: did Adam have a kingdom? People think he was running around butt naked. No; it is hidden wisdom.

“but to them it is not given”. That is why there is no need to argue with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving. If God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it. As Paul says, “the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why try to force him to know it? Correct them and dust off your shoes, because everyone is not going to get the things of the Spirit of God.

“It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven”. What are the stories he builds in the heaven? The first layer, the second layer and the third layer: the sky of this earth, space, and paradise. Paul calls it the third heaven. Those are the stories, three different layers.

Above them is the Father, at the very top, the holy of holies. Where he is, is infinite; it is called eternity. That is why we call him the Majesty on high. He is the highest, and the Most High, the Highest, is one of the few titles Christ does not have. That title is his Father's. They are not the same person.

Read on: “and hath founded his troop in the earth”. The troop is us. “he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.” From there, back to Genesis 1:6: “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters”. The waters are space, and the firmament was made in the midst of space. Atmosphere means vapor sphere, and vapor means water: layers of water that circle the earth and protect it from the sun. So there are levels of heaven over the earth, then space, then paradise, with levels there too. As above, so below. Paradise was created on the second day, when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

Noah's ark was built the same way. “A window shalt thou make to the ark”: there is that window again, like the narrow windows of the temple. “and in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof”: the door is in the side of the boat. “with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.” A lower level, a second level and a third.

The ark had three levels, the same as the temple. It is basically a floating temple. God gave Noah the same pattern he gave Solomon, and both follow the way the heavens are built.

Temple, ark and heavens all show the same three stories, and that is how Paul could speak of being caught up to the third heaven. Paradise is the third story, and the Father dwells above all of it.

Paul explains the heavens: “I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.” Verse 4 names it: “How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.” You have the sky, then space, and then where the Lord dwells, paradise, the third heaven. Those unspeakable words likely go into the name, which it is not lawful to speak.

So when Genesis says God created the heaven, it is a similitude. It is not only the sky down here; he also created paradise. Wisdom of Solomon 9 shows it was made in the beginning. Solomon says, “Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: Thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning.” When was it prepared? From the beginning, which is Genesis: when God made the firmament and called it heaven. That is not only the firmament down here; it is paradise, the third heaven.

“And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments.” That is Christ; he was there. Then Solomon prays, “O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee.” That is how you know what pleases God: wisdom has to come and show you.

Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of what is in the heavens, and that is why the temple's pattern, which Ezekiel describes next, tells us how the heavens are built.

Ezra is shown “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, with an entrance so narrow that only one man can go at once. That city is the kingdom of heaven, our inheritance: “Even so also is Israel's portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, full of sorrow and travail. But “the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure”. The elder world is the old world, the kingdom of Adam, where all of us were with him, ruling.

Isaiah shows the Lord bringing that back: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

As at the first: that is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. There were judges set up then, and the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him at that time, ruling with him. Were we in the flesh back then? No; we were immortal. As at the beginning: the beginning is Genesis.

So the Lord is not only promising good rulers again. He is promising to restore the government of the old world, the judges and counsellors we had in the beginning, and to call that city the city of righteousness. That is the city full of all good things that Ezra saw, and it is Israel's portion.

“Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning.” As from the beginning: so the tribes of Jacob were with the Lord in the beginning, in Genesis.

In Genesis the sons of God were there. When Adam fell, the sons of God were there. There was a government set up, rulership, a kingdom set up with Adam; Adam was not running around naked. There were the gates of Levi, the gates of Benjamin, the gates of Manasses: all twelve tribes in the beginning with the Lord, in their spiritual bodies. People ask what tribe Abraham was from, what tribe Isaac was from. The twelve tribes were always there. When Moses says the sons of God, that is the twelve tribes.

“O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” We are named God's firstborn because he created us first, before the world began. “O be merciful unto Jerusalem, thy holy city, the place of thy rest”, and “Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

In these last days God has raised up the prophets that have been in his name. The prophets of old are back, in the tribes of Israel, in this building.

The entrances of the elder world “were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” Wisdom shows what that world was like: “For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth”.

The generations of the world were healthful: we were living forever. There was no poison of destruction in us and no kingdom of death. The kingdom of death was established after Adam fell, when Satan was given power over this earth and began ruling it, him and his children. The kingdom of death is the white man and Satan ruling the earth. Before that was the kingdom of Adam, the kingdom of heaven. That is why Moses could promise “the days of heaven upon the earth”: he saw Adam rule.

“For righteousness is immortal”: keep God's laws and you live forever. “But ungodly men with their works and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a covenant with it”. A lot of our people have made a covenant with death, worshipping Satan and living in the kingdom of death. That is why the last thing Christ has to conquer is death, and then there will be no more death, period.

Before the world was made, everyone obeyed, because we were not in the flesh. Paul shows the body we had and will have again: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” If this body is dissolved, we have a body, not made with hands like Adam formed of the dust of the ground, but eternal in the heavens: a celestial body.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”. We groan in this body because it is susceptible to sin, and we want our body from heaven. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” That is what Adam's nakedness was: not running around naked, but being in the flesh. Before, he had a spiritual body; God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That nakedness is the shame, the sinful nature.

We groan “not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” We want our immortal body. “we walk by faith, not by sight”, “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.”

So when you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. This is for every brother and sister who is sick, who has been told they do not have long to live, and for those who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don't be afraid. Conquer that fear. If you did what was right on this earth and dealt right with the saints, absent from this body, you will be with the Lord.

Ezra hears the Lord say, “when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” Before the earth was made, his children were with him and they obeyed. Revelation shows that the choosing was done back then: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

From where? From the foundation of the world. When was your name written in the book of life? At the foundation of the world. That goes back to Genesis 1, when the Lord divided the light from the darkness and separated good from evil. That is predestination.

There is no heathen in that book. I don't care how good you think he is; they are not in the book of life. They are in the book of slavery, the register of chains. Those whose names are not written there worship the beast, because they were not chosen from the foundation of the world. And those who were written there are the ones who, in the beginning, before the world was made, did not speak against him.

When the world was not yet made, “no man spake against me”: everyone obeyed. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic bodies, not in this wicked fleshly body. To see what that means, look at the angel who spoke to John.

John fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” I am a servant just like you. I am your brother. I am a prophet. And I am of them which keep the sayings of this book. That is heavy.

So now you understand a little more what the Lord means when he says that when we were with him in the beginning, we all obeyed. The angels are our brethren; we had that same celestial body with him before the earth was created, and that is why Christ says those who understand the power of God will be equal unto the angels. Now, covered in this flesh, we are rebellious, and the Lord has to keep whooping us for our idols and our evil. But you have to see who you are and believe it. This is not a fairy tale; this is real.

Colossians says Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things.” He was the first thing created, before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. God created him and told him to create everything else: the angels, stars, planets, galaxies and paradise in heaven, and a spiritual realm that cannot be seen.

Moses saw the secrets of that time, creation included, and wrote about it in a similitude, and a lot of it he hid. Those hidden things are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double: a scripture says one thing and also another thing, and when we read it again the Most High takes us to see it on another level.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets Moses hid, God reveals to His servants the prophets. Paul and the apostles understood the depth and width of the knowledge of God, because the spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last of the apostles’ students died, that understanding died with them and all kinds of paganism came into the church.

But God has sent His sons back on the earth, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out. People question it when they hear that the men of IUIC are prophets. We are going to show you the secrets, and you judge for yourself.

Daniel 7:25 is about the white man, about Edom: “he shall speak great words against the most High”. He has called himself the people of God, called himself Christ and the people of Christ, taken God's land, said God's laws are done away with, and changed all of the Most High's holidays. “and shall wear out the saints of the most High”: he wore us out in slavery. When something is worn out it does not look the same, and that is how we forgot who we are.

“and think to change times and laws”. There is a reason it says times. Genesis 1:14: “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The sun and moon are set up for time. The moon is used for time, so that we can tell when our festival days come in.

Times and laws go together. Antiochus changed all our customs and made it unlawful for us to keep festival days, and America did the same thing: you do not have to keep God's feast days any more, why are you keeping Passover or Dedication, Christ did away with those things. In their place came new holidays, Christmas and Easter, our customs twisted and mixed with paganism and fed back to us. There is always a counter, good set against evil: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

It says he will think to change times and laws because he is not going to be able to. The Most High is a mastermind. He has sent his sons, his prophets, back on the earth, and they teach the right times, the feast days and God's laws. The lights he set in the heaven still keep his times.

“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. The Lord made some of us inside here apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, and some brothers have several of these gifts. Why did God put his Holy Spirit in us and give us these gifts? Not so you can exalt yourself: I'm the mighty deacon, I understand all these things. It is “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry”. The gift is not for your own selfish reasons. It is to make the brothers better and the people perfect, and to help your people. You brothers travelling the world teaching the gospel are waking people up all over the world.

So Paul says “Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” Desire spiritual gifts, but rather prophesy. Why? “But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.”

When you prophesy you teach and edify the people. You exhort the brothers to continue in the faith and to have hope; that is how brothers develop hope and faith, when the prophets among us go into the scriptures and show certain things. That feeling inside when you hear brothers teach who can prophesy is exhortation, and it revives you.

And it comforts, because we need that comfort. We are all going through certain things, and we are all tired of this world and this life. But when we go into the scriptures and see the things the Lord has prepared for us, it comforts us and exhorts us to continue in this gospel and this work. That is why the gifts are for the body and not for oneself.

The gifts are given “For the perfecting of the saints”, and prophecy gives edification, exhortation and comfort. Paul prays for the same: “That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge”.

With all the saints you have to comprehend the breadth, the width, the length, the depth and the height. It goes into what the Lord has prepared for those of us that love him. Once you fully understand that, it gives you hope, exhorts you and comforts you to continue in this walk and not fall out and go back into the world.

Some brothers and sisters have been with us for years and say, I can't take it no more, five years and I ain't got none, and they go back into the world and let Satan overcome them. If you want a husband or a wife, go to the Lord first: pray and fast, Lord, send me a righteous sister, send me a righteous husband. But get yourself right first, or it is not coming your way. Sisters want an Abraham but are not like Sarah; brothers want a Sarah while still living with mama.

“that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God. Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end.” That world without end is the church, a precept with Isaiah 45. Rooted and grounded in love, we comprehend what the Lord has for us and are filled with his fulness.

Ezekiel 31 says the great cedar was “of an high stature”, and “All the fowls of heaven made their nests in his boughs.” The fowls of heaven are the angels: all the angels were under Adam when he was ruling, as it says, “let all the angels of God worship him.” Under his branches the beasts of the field brought forth their young, and the serpent was “more subtil than any beast of the field”: Satan was there, under Adam. And “under his shadow dwelt all great nations”, all the nations of the earth.

Ezekiel 17 shows the same cedar planted again: “I will also take of the highest branch of the high cedar, and will set it; I will crop off from the top of his young twigs a tender one, and will plant it upon an high mountain and eminent.” That is talking about Christ. “In the mountain of the height of Israel will I plant it: and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing; in the shadow of the branches thereof shall they dwell.” That is the same as Ezekiel 31. He will plant it in the height of Israel, where it was before.

“And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the high tree, have exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish.” He brought us down, and he raises us back up again. Ezra saw it too: on mount Sion, in the midst of a great people, “a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest.”

To understand the kingdom of Adam you have to understand the kingdom that is to come. It will be the same thing: us ruling with Christ in righteousness, with all the fowl dwelling under the goodly cedar, and nobody able to hurt us.

The great cedar that was lifted up in his height was driven out “for his wickedness”, and the Lord gives the end of it: “To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height, neither shoot up their top among the thick boughs, neither their trees stand up in their height, all that drink water: for they are all delivered unto death, to the nether parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with them that go down to the pit.”

We are all delivered unto death. All that drank the water, his boughs, his branches, Israel, now have to come down on the earth and die as men. Before that we had our spiritual body, our angelic body. They go down “in the midst of the children of men” because they were not regular men. That goes back to “I have said, Ye are gods”, and “ye shall die like men.”

Read on: “In the day when he went down to the grave I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods thereof, and the great waters were stayed.” The day Adam was cast out, the waters his boughs and branches were drinking were restrained. No water was coming to Adam anymore. Those great waters are the same living waters of Revelation 22; they stopped when Adam fell. Lebanon mourned for him and all the trees of the field fainted for him: his children.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell.” Hell there is the grave, the earth. When Adam fell, the Lord withdrew paradise, a spiritual realm connected to the earth, and it caused devastation, and millions died, as Ezra says, “as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” That is where Cain found his wife: not everybody died.

And “all the trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon”, Adam's top leaders, “shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth.” We are comforted here by the scriptures, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

Pharaoh is asked who he is like in his greatness, and the answer is the great cedar: “Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches.” The Lord speaks to the prophets by similitudes, saying one thing that means another, and here he compares the Egyptian kingdom to Adam's kingdom, Adam ruling, to give us more insight into what we read in Genesis. “The waters made him great”: the waters that came from the Father made Adam great, flowing from him through all his plants, all Adam's children. And “his boughs were multiplied.” What are the boughs that multiplied?

Asaph answers in Psalm 80, crying to the “Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock”: “Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river.”

Those boughs are Israel, the sons of God. All of this is talking about Israel: all of us that were drinking that water, and everybody was not getting that water like us. Isaiah says the same: “In that day shall the branch of the Lord be beautiful and glorious.” The branches of the Lord are Israel, those of us that escape the destruction and get the kingdom.

So the boughs multiplied on the great cedar are Adam's true children, Israel, and the same vine the Lord brought out of Egypt and planted is the vine that filled the land with its shadow in Adam's kingdom.

The great cedar was so fair that “all the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” The fir trees were not like his boughs, the chesnut trees not like his branches. His boughs and branches were his true children, his firstborn in the heavens, immortal and ruling with him. The other trees were the children Adam had on the earth before the fall, not created in his image, the multitude “born in vain.” They envied him, and they envied the twelve tribes that were with him.

Wisdom of Solomon shows who else envied him: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world.” The man God created was Adam. Adam was immortal and his sons were immortal; the children he had on the earth were created as men, sons of men, and were not immortal.

The devil also envied Adam. Satan went to war with Adam, and when he could not get him, he went through his woman to take him down: he jumped on his wife, played with her emotions and tricked her. Through the envy of Satan, that is how death came.

It will be the same in the future: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee.” When Christ returns and sets us back on this earth to rule, the nations will envy us, the same as back then, but they will not be able to do anything against us.

Ezra says the Lord spoke “from the beginning of the creation, even the first day”, saying “Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” The word that did that perfect work is Christ.

Read on and Ezra shows what was there before anything was made: “darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.” Nothing, a great void. “Then commandedst thou a fair light to come forth of thy treasures, that thy work might appear.” That fair light out of God’s treasures is the light of Genesis 1:3, and it is worded that way because that light is what made everything else: it came forth so that God’s works could appear.

So “in the beginning” is not only the making of the earth and the sky. It is the beginning of all creation, and it begins with Christ, the first thing God created, the light called forth on the first day.

John opens the way Genesis does: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” The Word that was with God is Christ. He was a God in the beginning, made in the image of his Father, creating angels, galaxies and planets. “The same was in the beginning with God”: two different persons, the Father and the Son.

“All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” Then: “In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness.” That is the same light God brought out of his treasures in 2 Esdras 6, the light of Genesis 1.

John the Baptist “came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”, and “He was not that Light.” Christ is “the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world”: the true light God created on the first day.

Christ says it himself: “I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” We read that Christ is the first thing created; we go to the first thing created and God says “Let there be light”; and here Christ says, I am that light. The scriptures line up.

That is why the light of Genesis 1:3 is not the light of the sun. The earth was “without form and void”, not yet made, and the sun and moon, the “two great lights”, were not made until “the fourth day.” Read with a carnal mind, it sounds like daylight; read with the spirit, it is the Son.

Moses was told to hide these things and not make them plain for everyone, which is why Christ is called the hidden wisdom. Even the dividing of the light from the darkness, the light called day and the darkness night, is a similitude.

Genesis 1 is an abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel. When Genesis 1:27 says “male and female created he them”, Genesis 2 shows how he did it.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man, and he wasn't walking around butt naked on earth. “and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: when he breathed into him, he put that spirit inside him, the spirit that is his Son from the beginning. “and man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

Then Eve: “And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Eve was created from Adam, and Adam from the ground.

2 Esdras 3 tells the same story and goes further: God breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could go there, until he sinned. That is why flesh and blood cannot be up there: flesh and blood has that sinful nature. The man who could walk into paradise wasn't running around butt naked. He was ruling.

What does it mean when the Lord says, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”? Wisdom of Solomon 2:23: “For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.” That is how Adam was created before he sinned: immortal. Being in God's image is not only about how we look. It goes into his power and his divinity too.

2 Esdras 8:44 says man “is called thine own image, because thou art like unto him, for whose sake thou hast made all things”. Adam was just like his father, the way someone says, you are just like your father, you are the image of your father. We are supposed to be in the image of Christ, and Christ is in the image of the Father. All things were created for Adam and for the sons of Adam, which is us. Not everyone was created in Adam's image; the sons of God are the ones created in Adam's image, because Adam was created in God's image.

“and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That is the kingdom of Adam, in so many words. Then in verse 28 God tells them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it”. To replenish means to fill something up again. There is a big gap after verse 27: a lot of time went by. Why would God tell Adam to subdue the earth if he already had dominion over it? That was left to be answered later in the class.

Deuteronomy 11:21 shows Moses saw Adam's kingdom: keep the commandments in the land, and your days will be “as the days of heaven upon the earth.” The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam ruled. 2 Esdras 7:26 speaks of the bride that “now is withdrawn from the earth”: that holy city, the access to the spirit realm, withdrew itself from the earth, so it must once have been on the earth, in the time of Adam. How Adam was on the earth is how we are going to be in the future.

“Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day”. This shows when the children of light were created. In Genesis 1 it was not only the light that was created; the light's children were created too. Christ said that he and the children are one. We were already in Christ, and when that light was formed we were in it. Then the Father chose: those on the right side are his children, and those on the left side, the two-thirds and those heathens over there, are the darkness.

God called the light Day, so we are the children of the day. That is why Day and Night are capitalized in the King James: a specific day and a specific night, good and evil, right angels and wrong ones, right spirits and wrong spirits. The apostles understood these things, and the translators did too. The spirit was on them as well when they put it in English; that council was divinely inspired. It wasn't regular men. Some of y'all dumb negroes don't speak a word of Hebrew and are trying to insult them; you're not on their level at all whatsoever. “we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” Day and night compare good and evil and the children of each, and all of that took place on the first day.

Paul goes on: “Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. For God hath not appointed us to wrath”. We should not be sleeping; we have to be aware of the time we are living in. God did not appoint us to wrath because we are the children of the day, the children of the light.

Who is the day? 2 Peter 1:19: “a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place, and the day star arising in our hearts is Christ. He is the day.

2 Esdras 9 shows the children of light before the earth: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed”. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic, celestial bodies, the body we will have when Christ returns, and we all obeyed. “but now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”. Covered in this flesh, we became rebellious. Knowing who we were is meant to give us the faith and hope to endure in this truth.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. To be predestinated means you are going to get it no matter what. The definition read was: of an outcome or course of events determined in advance by divine will or fate, with the synonyms preordained, foreordained, destined, predetermined, fated, predestined.

How do you know who is predestined? You don't. Nobody today knows it. When you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know you were predestined. Read on: “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.”

When were we predestined? When God chose to separate the light from the darkness, on the first day. Revelation 13:8 says the same thing from the other side: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. The choosing was done in the beginning, before the earth was made.

“And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.” Moses wrote these things the way God told him to, hiding them so that not everyone would understand. This is the first day, before the earth was created, and the first thing created was Christ. What else was created on that first day?

Isaiah 5:20 names light and darkness plainly: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Darkness is called evil and light is called good. So when the Lord divided the light from the darkness, he created good and evil. Moses is letting us know that something more is going on in Genesis 1.

On that first day spirits were created: angels were created, evil was created, Satan was created. The dividing of the light from the darkness is God choosing. The children of light are his chosen, and the rest he hardens, as the next scriptures show.

“The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.” Read on: “His mercy is manifest to every creature; and he hath separated his light from the darkness with an adamant.” The light stands for good and the darkness for evil, and he separates them with an adamant.

The annotation in the King James gives the meaning of adamant: refusing to be persuaded, or to change one's mind. That is what the hardening of Pharaoh was. God made Pharaoh not be persuaded to let us go. That is the adamant, and that is how God separates his light from the darkness: he hardens a heart so that it will not believe and will not follow. The same way he hardened Pharaoh's heart, he will harden hearts so that people do not believe these scriptures.

So in the beginning, when God separated the light from the darkness, spirits were created, and God said: you I will choose, you are my chosen people; you I will not choose, I will harden your heart. The children of light were chosen, and the darkness was left hardened.

“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything is made in pairs. When God divided the light from the darkness he made good and evil as a pair, and Satan and evil were created too. Nothing got into creation by mistake. There is always a counter, good set against evil all the time: we have our Passover, and Satan got Easter.

Look at what Genesis 1 mentions first, before the earth was formed: the waters of the deep, which is space, covered in darkness. Darkness is mentioned before the light because the Lord had it set from the beginning that, when we came down here, we would be evil anyway.

That is why “the evening and the morning were the first day”: the evening comes before the morning. That is why Cain was born first, Ishmael came before Isaac, and Esau, Edom, was born before Jacob. The evil, the darkness, goes first, and then the light comes after, which is why Christ said the first shall be last and the last shall be first. The double of Sirach, darkness set against light, runs through all of Genesis.

“And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.” The waters under the firmament are the sea; the waters above are in space. There are different waters above the firmament: drink that water and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude. “And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.” On the second day the firmament was created, and paradise, which is also called heaven, was created too.

The earth came after. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth”. There was no shape or form down here yet. The earth was made on the third day, with the grass, the herbs and the fruit trees.

2 Esdras 3 confirms the order: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth, so it was made on the second day.

This is why the class kept saying Genesis has levels. When Genesis says God made the heaven, it is not only the sky over this earth. Paradise was planted by God's right hand before the earth appeared, and Adam was led into it.

Our minds are earthly minds. Reading first, second and third day, we think of twenty-four hours. But when Christ was created, the earth had not been created. The sun and the moon had not been created. So did twenty-four hours exist? No.

“But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” This is saying that our time and God's time are not the same. Don't sit down and say God created the earth in seven thousand years. It only means that time with God is different; in that realm, time is not the same.

So to explain it to our human minds, Moses said first day, second day, third day. The best way to understand it is: the first thing God did, the second thing, the third, the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and then the seventh. What came out of the Father's mouth, Christ did. And it had to be given to us in human terms, because the Sabbath is counted from the creation account. If it had been given in God's terms, we would be lost and think every Sabbath comes every thousand years. He rested on the seventh day, so you rest too.

Moses saw these secrets, and God told him to write them but to hide certain things. Unless God's Spirit is in you, you will not understand them, even when they are taught to you.

“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he dwells in eternity. Christ was with him in eternity in the beginning; the Word was with God. Christ did not create everything all at once on the first day. The Lord told him what to do, and he did it. Christ learned from his Father: what he saw his Father do, he was able to do.

“I dwell in the high and holy place”: that is above the heavens, above paradise, the holy of holies, the fourth floor, with restricted access. No man has been up there. He dwells there “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.”

Sirach 18 explains eternity: “The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” In eternity, where the Father is, a thousand years is like nothing. Those are the days of the Ancient of days. Sirach 1:2 says the same: “Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one can count God's days. He exists outside of time, before time.

This goes with what Peter said: the days of Genesis are not earth days. They are measured from where the Father dwells, in eternity.

With a picture of the earth in space on the screen, 2 Esdras 16 was read: “He searcheth the deep, and the treasures thereof; he hath measured the sea, and what it containeth. He hath shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with his word hath he hanged the earth upon the waters.” All around the earth is space, and the earth hangs in it like an ornament the Lord just hung there. The water it hangs on is space. Astronauts train in the water because that is where they are going; spend too long in space and your bones get brittle, just as they get crushed if you go too deep under water.

Job calls that water something else: “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.” When you see the earth in space, it is on nothing. You cannot see any water, but the water is there surrounding it. The nothing is the water.

So why doesn't the earth move and float off one way or another? That is the Most High showing his power. 2 Esdras 16:59: “He spreadeth out the heavens like a vault; upon the waters hath he founded it.” A vault is an arch; it goes around, it is round, not flat. Founded means established: the earth stays in the spot where he founded it, while the sun moves. The devil says the opposite, that the earth moves; but God said the earth is founded, and it stays there. This is the same work as Genesis 1:6, where the firmament was set in the midst of the waters.

Balaam, “the man whose eyes are open”, saw the vision of the Almighty and said: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.”

People think these tabernacles are houses. They are our bodies. It is us being that tree by the river, planted by the Lord, beside the living waters. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters”: the waters are poured out from on high, from the Lord, and we will be swimming in those living waters, the waters from heaven above the firmament, not space. “and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” The king is Christ, and that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things were brought out to encourage us. They have been hidden for thousands of years, and understanding them builds up our hope.

Wisdom said her river became a sea. Revelation 15:2: “And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass”. We overcame the white man and his lies, and we stand on that clear water. The Lord divided the waters from the waters above, and the waters above are the wisdom in paradise.

Revelation 22 shows the river of Eden in heaven: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” A river, and the tree of life beside it, just as in the garden.

In Revelation 4, “a door was opened in heaven”, and the voice said, “Come up hither”. John went up into paradise, and that is where those things were shown to him. “And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal”. The sea of glass is the wisdom coming from the throne of God. Esau pictures it as the Bifrost, a bridge leading to paradise.

Psalm 148:4 calls on those waters: “Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” Song of Solomon 4 calls it “a well of living waters”. Christ said he is the living water, and told the woman at the well he would give her living water. Those are the waters above the heavens, the springs up there. The river out of Eden is that same water.

After the waters above the heavens, Sirach 19:19: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” The water that flows out of Eden is wisdom, the knowledge of the commandments, and the one who keeps them eats of the tree of immortality.

Song of Solomon 4 describes the same garden: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Everybody cannot go there. It has an orchard of pomegranates and pleasant fruits, “A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.”

That goes back to Genesis, where the Lord made every tree in the garden to grow that was good for food. The living waters feed the garden, and those who do the commandments receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, which Adam had access to before he sinned.

“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The first is Pison, which compasses the land of Havilah, where there is gold; the second is Gihon, compassing the whole land of Ethiopia; the third is Hiddekel, going toward the east of Assyria; and the fourth is Euphrates. The Most High is doing two things here. It is a similitude of the waters above, since he divided the waters below from the waters above. And it goes into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and that is Adam's governance. It speaks of the heavens, but it came down on the earth too.

Sirach 24 names the same rivers: “He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” These are the four rivers of Genesis, and the water is wisdom and understanding. What went forth through all those rivers was the wisdom of God, going to Adam's sons ruling this earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens, and it is on the earth too.

“The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.” The first man is Adam, and he did not know wisdom perfectly because he sinned. Wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.” The great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.” The best garden is paradise. The brook became a river and the river became a sea, and that sea is the sea of glass in heaven.

“And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”. That is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom comes down from the Father to Christ, it goes to the leaders, and the leaders issue it throughout the earth. “half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.” That means all year round. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth, and Adam is going to be back as king over the earth.

So when Genesis talks about the garden, it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God's glory and wisdom went out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and the other rivers. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions enforcing his laws. His trees were there on the earth too, on earth as it is in heaven. The living waters out of Jerusalem are how it will be again.

Back in Genesis 2:15, “the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and keep it means to rule. Adam ruled the heaven and the earth, and we don't know for how long. He died at 930, but his days only started to be numbered after he sinned. Before that he was immortal, so between Genesis 2 and the temptation in Genesis 3 there could have been hundreds or thousands of years. That is the kingdom of Adam. He had children in the heavens, his firstborn, the twelve tribes, and children on the earth.

2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted”, and Genesis 2:8 says the same thing: “the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” Adam's kingdom ruled the heaven and the earth. The man who could go to paradise, where the Lord is, did not walk around without clothes. Then verse 9: “And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food”. What is that talking about?

Isaiah 61:3: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: us, in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

Reading Genesis 2:9 again: the trees pleasant to the sight and good for food are a similitude for Adam's sons in the heavens, the righteous. “the tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “and the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: that is Satan. The tree people set up and worship in their houses at Christmas references that tree; Babylon referenced it, and Santa Claus is Satan Claus.

God works hand in hand with the prophets. He has Moses write something hard, and he has the other prophets come and explain what it is talking about. Isaiah explains the trees of Genesis: the planting of the Lord is his people.

Psalm 1 was read from the top: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

The man who delights in the law is the tree. He is planted by rivers of water and brings forth fruit. That is what the trees of the garden are: the righteous, the planting of the Lord, bringing forth fruit.

Going back to Genesis 2:9 with that in mind, the trees “pleasant to the sight and good for food” are Adam's sons in the heavens. The rivers of water point to the next verse: “And a river went out of Eden to water the garden”. The trees stand by the river, and that is Adam's governance: the righteous planted by the waters of God's wisdom, in the heavens and on the earth.

Genesis 3:20 is right there in front of our eyes: “And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” She was the mother, bringing forth many children. This was before she fell and before Adam was cast out. The living are children on the earth, created before the fall, and Eve was the mother of them all. Eve was a black woman and she was beautiful. That was Adam and Eve in their kingdom, not people walking around naked.

2 Esdras 3 shows how many there were: “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” When Adam broke God's law he was cast out of paradise and immortality was taken from him. But there were already nations, tribes, people and kindreds, out of number, so many they could not be counted. For all of that to be around, Adam must have been on the earth for hundreds or thousands of years.

2 Esdras 6:54: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures”. Adam was a lord on the earth, ruling the earth and the heavens. The creatures include the angels, and Adam was over them. “of him come we all”. The words “and the people also whom thou hast chosen” were read as speaking of after the flood, from Noah, because before Noah, and before Adam fell, there were people already. And verse 55: “thou madest the world for our sakes”.

That is how Cain was able to find a wife after he killed Abel. There were many people living on the earth, tribes and nations, and Adam was governing them all. And he was not alone: we were with him in the beginning, the twelve tribes, ruling the heavens and the earth with him. What we read about the future kingdom, governing the nations in angelic bodies, is how it was with Adam. Tobit 8:6 says of Adam and Eve, “of them came mankind”, but that is broad, since all mankind also came from Adam and Eve through Noah's three sons.

Why was Adam told to subdue the earth? Because he lost it. Satan says all the power and glory of this earth was given to him, and he can give it to whoever he wants. Adam lost rulership of the earth, so now he has to come and subdue it again, and kill Satan.

“And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Cain was not created in Adam's image. She said she got a man, and we keep reading about the children of men; his very name tells you he was not created in Adam's image or after his likeness. “And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Cain killed Abel. Abel was righteous and Cain was wicked, and Abel was supposed to be the righteous child created in Adam's image.

So what did the Lord do? Genesis 4 and 5 are the replenishing of the earth, filling it again with the righteous seed, his sons. Genesis 2 goes into Adam's rulership, Genesis 2 and 3 are the same as Ezekiel 31, Adam's rule and his fall, and Genesis 4 and 5 are Adam and Eve replenishing the earth after the fall.

Genesis 5: “This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”. Adam means from the ground. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Now the sons of God, the children above, start being sent down to the earth and born through Adam and his descendants. The twelve tribes are born into the earth through him. Seth's whole lineage is the sons of God, Israel, born in the image of God. Cain was not.

The command to replenish the earth and subdue it is not finished. The earth has not yet been subdued, and that waits for the kingdom.

“That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” What does Moses mean? When you go into the land and keep the commandments, it will be as the days of heaven upon the earth.

Moses saw Adam's kingdom. That is why he could say that going into the land and keeping the laws would be as the kingdom of heaven upon the earth. The kingdom of heaven was once on the earth, when Adam was ruling.

So the promise of Hebrews 4:1, “a promise being left us of entering into his rest”, is the same promise: heaven's days upon the earth again. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Those to whom the word was first preached “entered not in because of unbelief”, “For we which have believed do enter into rest”. The one who has entered into his rest has “ceased from his own works”: the works are our labouring in this earth to bring forth the kingdom of heaven.

“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” We want God's kingdom to be in earth as it is in heaven, and that is what we are praying for right now: the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

This ties to the rest of Hebrews 4. When Genesis says God “rested on the seventh day from all his work”, it does not mean God was tired and went to get some sleep. Moses is an analogy, a similitude. Hebrews says “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day”: God's rest is a place, paradise. 2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was planted before the earth, and leading Adam into paradise is entering into his rest.

That is the kingdom of Adam. When Adam had dominion on the earth, it was on a much higher level than people think. Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth, the only flesh, him and his wife, that could, until he committed sin; flesh and blood cannot be up there because of that sinful nature. How Adam was on the earth is basically how we are going to be in the future, the difference being that he was not in the flesh as we are. So when we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are praying for what was once on the earth in Adam's day to be on the earth again.

“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” Remember, it withdrew itself; now it is coming back.

2 Esdras 7:26 says it: “the bride shall appear, and she coming forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth.” That bride withdrawn from the earth is the holy city Jerusalem, the access to the spirit realm, which withdrew itself from the earth. For it to be withdrawn from the earth it must once have been on the earth, and it was, during the time of Adam. Adam was not running around butt naked; Adam was going back and forth to a spiritual realm.

The city is described with twelve gates for the twelve tribes of Israel and no heathens. So the tribes were around back then, and Adam went through a gate, the Judah gate. The twelve tribes around in the beginning were called the sons of God; Moses did not name them because the Lord said to hide these things. Jacob, Esau, will never go through those gates. They may stand outside and look at it and drop some stuff off in front of it, but they will never enter into those gates.

The city was prepared from the foundation of the world; it is already built, from the beginning. It is the rest God entered, the paradise Adam was led into, and the promise of Hebrews 4:1 that we must not come short of.

Moses was held on the mount a long season and told many wondrous things, the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded, “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” How did Moses hide them? Hosea says the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison, like a metaphor: you speak of a tree, but you are not really talking about a tree. When Genesis speaks of the trees in the garden, it is comparing trees to human beings. It is all going into Adam's kingdom, but it is hidden.

Job calls those hidden things the secrets of wisdom: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are the things Moses hid.

And they are double. You read a scripture, but it is not saying only one thing; it is saying two things. Many times we read a scripture and think we have it, then read it again and the Most High takes us to see something else on another level. That doesn't make what we first saw wrong; there is simply another level to it.

The Lord told Moses to hide these things because they are not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand them, because the Lord “revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

Solomon shows why man cannot understand the things above by himself: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” And hardly do we guess aright at the things that are upon earth, let alone the things that are in heaven.

Ezra wanted to know the things above the heavens and asked the angel to give him understanding. Did the angel reveal a lot of things in heaven to Ezra? Yes. So, in order to understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal them to you.

That is why the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Our corruptible body presses the soul down, and we read with an earthly, carnal mind. The things Moses was shown on the mount, the secrets of the times and the end, were hidden in similitudes, and it takes the Lord's spirit coming into you to show you what they mean.

Luke says Mary “laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is a hotel. Why was there no room in the hotels? Deuteronomy 16:16 shows it: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover; the feast of weeks is Pentecost. Three times a year all Israel had to go up to Jerusalem, and at that time every inn was full because everybody came up for the feast. There was no room in the inn because it was the Passover.

Christ was not born in the manger. The prophecy in Song of Solomon 8:5 says, “I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth”. Mary brought him forth under the apple tree, and after that took him to the manger, because the city was full for the feast.

“Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.” “And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.” When did Christ turn twelve? At the Passover. Christ was born on the Passover and he died on the Passover.

When is the Passover? Leviticus 23:5: “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The fourteenth at evening is the fifteenth day, and that is when Christ was born: Abib, the first month, not December 25th.

1 Corinthians 5:7: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ is our Passover. That is why the inn was full when he was born: all Israel was up in Jerusalem for the feast.

December 25th goes back to the 25th of Kislev, when Antiochus IV Epiphanes desecrated the temple, set up Zeus and swine's flesh, and forced our people to worship Greek gods. God has festival days and Satan does too: we have our dedication and Satan has Christmas; we have our Passover and Satan has Easter. Stop giving heed to Jewish fables and following St. Nicholas and the Pope; that lie turns you away from the truth.

“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” The shepherds were out in the field with the flock at night. That does not happen in the winter.

A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime the animals are brought into the barn to stay warm; nobody is abiding in the field then. Around tabernacles, the ingathering, is when they bring in all their animals and all the crops to prepare for the mean season. So shepherds in the field by night fits the springtime, and Christ was born in the springtime, at the Passover.

Christmas has nothing to do with Christ. Do not give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you away from the truth; that is what Christmas does, it turns you away from the truth and from serving God.

“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem”. East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem, “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.”

The star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today, not a celestial body in the night sky. A planet cannot do what this did: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” It guided them on the earth and stood over the house.

“And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother”. The house, not the manger. Christians show the wise men in a barn giving gifts to a baby, but time had passed; Christ was a young child now, a toddler of around two, walking and forming words. The wise men had been following that star at least two years. They were not three men; three is the number of the gifts, “gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” They came as a caravan. With those gifts Christ was taken care of; he was not poor.

Herod, an Edomite who converted to being a Jew, a white man set up as king of Judea by Rome, “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.” Thousands of black babies. That shows the child was around two when the wise men came. And when you see the synagogues of Satan killing babies in Palestine today, it does not surprise us; that is in their nature.

The children of the most High “walk on in darkness” and “die like men.” Ezra cries out over it: “it had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Adam ruled the heaven and the earth. Now we live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after death look for punishment. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him.

That is why Christ came and died for our sins. Through one man sin came into the world, so through one man life came. He walked perfect and died for our sins, and he will choose which of us go back with him to paradise to rule the heaven and the earth: the ones who are real, who ask forgiveness, who keep fighting and never give up.

Paul's wording shows where we came from: “Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ ascended, but first he descended. His being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity, the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out, and they descended the same way, by being born into the earth.

Even the fathers' names show it. Jared means descend, or descent: the sons of God came down to the nether parts of the earth and died, as Adam died. And Enoch, dedicated, trained, came down, trained himself to conquer the flesh, walked perfect, “and he was not; for God took him”: he went back up to paradise.

“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” We do not understand the power we have, or where we came from. Paul tells us: “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

A lot of times we read that and it goes over our heads, but pay attention to the wording. Jerusalem which is above is the mother of us all, meaning we all came from there. That is where we came from. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

So when Christ says he is not of this world, and tells us we are not of this world and to love not the world, understand what he is saying. When the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, understand what it is saying. And when it says that if we had been mindful of whence we came, we might have had opportunity to return, understand what it is saying.

We are the sons of God cast down to the nether parts of the earth, walking in darkness and dying like men, but our mother is the Jerusalem above. You have to believe these things and understand them, because that is who you are.

“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” What do we not know? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” God judges in the congregation of the gods, and we are those beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth. That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes”: it was not like that in the beginning. That is what happened after Adam fell.

Paul shows what we are waiting for: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens, the same body we had with Adam in the beginning. After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us must come on the earth through Adam in the flesh and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came and overcame.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis we are called the sons of God; we are called the twelve tribes of Israel. “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” We want to be delivered from this corrupted body.

Paul says of us, “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell. To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says. That is faith.

“Not giving heed to Jewish fables.” A fable is a lie, and it says Jewish because it pertains to the Jews. Christ was a Jew, and there is a lie being told that he was born on December 25th. That is a Jewish fable. Christmas goes back into slavery and into paganism too, and it turns you away from the truth of serving God. It has nothing to do with Christ.

Luke tells what happened: “the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger.” Her firstborn, meaning she had many sons; the Catholic Church says Mary was a virgin who never had sex, but she brought forth her firstborn. And before he was put in the manger, the prophecy in the Song of Solomon shows where he was born: “Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.”

So Mary had Christ under an apple tree, and after she gave birth to him there, she took him to the manger, “because there was no room for them in the inn.” Christ was not born in the manger. A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime they are not out there; they go in the barn to stay warm.

Why was there no room in the inn, the hotel? “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.” Everybody came up to Jerusalem at that time and the inns were full, because it was the Passover. Christ was born in the springtime, not in the winter.

That is how the scripture kills the fable. Stop listening to Santa Claus, aka Pope Nicholas, St. Nicholas. Don’t give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you from the truth: Christ was not born on December 25th.
