What was Paul's source material? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great”, leaders and students, teachers and students, “saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. Paul only taught what Moses and the prophets said.

And in Acts 28, when many came to his lodging, he “expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” His letters are based on the law and the prophets. He was not sitting around making things up.

That is why Peter mentions “the other scriptures”: to understand Paul's letters you must understand the other scriptures. Are there places where the spirit of Christ spoke through Paul and things were added? Yes. Paul's letters are 99.9 percent law and prophets, and maybe one percent is something like the unbelieving wife departing, which is not found in Moses, because under Moses, if she did not believe, she got death. Your wife could believe in Satan in the wilderness and she got death. That was added for that time, and that is “the wisdom given unto him”: Christ speaking through Paul.

When people don't study Paul, they say Paul's letters aren't authoritative, Mark and Luke weren't of the twelve, and they begin to speak evil of dignities. Then the Lord blinds their minds, and Satan has them teaching that nations can be saved. We have been thoroughbreds in Paul's letters since learning Acts 10 and Romans 11 at the Bishop's house in 2006.

Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

Paul says “we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin”, and the Gentiles there are Israelites. Acts 15 shows the same Gentiles being restored: “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.” That references what took place in Acts 10, and we understand that is talking about Israel.

“And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”. Build again: that is the reconciliation, that is the reparation. It had fallen down because we became filthy, and God restores the waste places. Who is that? All twelve tribes of Israel.

Then verse 17: “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”. The residue is the rest of the nations outside of the twelve tribes: Edom and the others. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: that is the Christians, and the Jews.

They try to include themselves in our reconciliation, our restoration and our adoption. But the building again is of David’s tabernacle, the twelve tribes; the residue only seeks after the Lord once Israel is set up again.

Acts 15 quotes the prophet Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. The breaches are the tear, the split, like the breach “great like the sea” in Lamentations. Remember, the root word of reparations is to repair.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”. This is the restoring of Israel, both kingdoms that Paul proved “are all under sin” in Romans 3, repaired and raised up as in the days of old.

Then: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.” That they, all twelve tribes, may possess the remnant of Edom and of the heathen called by his name.

So you see, other nations cannot be involved in our reconciliation, our restoration or our reparation. The ones called by his name, the Christians and the Jews, are not the tabernacle being raised; they are what Israel possesses once it is raised. This goes back to the classes before on Romans 11 and Acts 10.

Paul proves from the Psalms that Israel became filthy: “They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” The whole nation was broken. Jeremiah laments that same breaking: “What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?”

A breach is a split or a tear. Our breach is great like the sea. Who can heal us? Christ, our saviour.

Isaiah shows the healing: “And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.” When our souls are in drought, the Lord is going to water us and heal us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”, the waste places we made when we became filthy. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.”

The root word of reparations is repair. The repairer of the breach: that is the reparations right there. Both Jews and Gentiles, Judah and Ephraim, were “all under sin” and torn apart, and the one who heals that breach is Christ, repairing and restoring Israel.

Romans 4:4 says “Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.” To him that offers sacrifices, the reward is not reckoned of grace or mercy, but of debt, because under Moses there was no grace. Hebrews shows it: “He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses”. Without mercy means without grace.

If you chose to do something worthy of death that an animal could not atone for, you had to die. If you broke the Sabbath, you couldn't atone with an animal. Homosexuality, you couldn't atone with an animal. Idolatry, you couldn't atone with an animal. And if you chose not to sacrifice at all, you had to die. So you were indebted to offer continual sacrifices all the time: continual burnt offerings, drink offerings, sin offerings.

The prophets said the temple would be destroyed. Once the temple is gone, where are your works? If your salvation rests on sacrificing an animal and there is no animal, no priest and no temple to atone with, by default you have condemned yourself. That is why faith in Christ has to supersede the works.

“But to him that worketh not”, him that does not offer sacrifice, “but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.” Christ justifies the ungodly through his death. Just as with Abraham, who was counted faithful before he sacrificed animals, God “imputeth righteousness without works”. Israel could keep sacrificing while the temple stood, but Christ had to come first in their minds, or they were in debt.

Romans 4:2 says “For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.” What works is Paul talking about? Nehemiah condenses them into one verse: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Continual means it was done all the time, daily, annually. And “to make an atonement” goes back to the word justify: atone, justify and reconcile are the same thing. So the works Paul is talking about are temple sacrifice, temple law. When Paul wrote, the temple was still standing and the Jews in Rome were still going to it and still sacrificing, and they believed their works were enough.

Abraham shows the order. In Genesis 15 the Lord promised the old man an heir out of his own bowels and seed as the stars, “And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” He was promised the land and he believed. Only then was he told to take the heifer, the goat, the ram and the birds and divide them. Faith came first, then the works.

When brothers don't study Paul's letters, they start saying Paul's letters are not authoritative, and speak evil of dignities, of Paul, Mark and Luke, because they weren't of the twelve. When you speak evil of dignities, your mind is blinded and you end up teaching a whole different gospel: that the nations can be saved. House negroes are the worst kind of negro. But this is the college course of this school. Know what the works are from Nehemiah, and nobody can come to your school or camp and confound you at Romans 4.

Christ was delivered for our offences. Daniel shows the same thing on the prophetic clock: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. Seventy weeks, 490 years, upon thy people: Daniel’s people, Israel.

For what? “To finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” That is what Christ did when he died. Reconciliation goes back to the word atonement, and back to the word justification.

“From the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem”: the rebuilding under Persia. “Unto the Messiah the Prince”: Rome. “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”. He would be killed, but not for himself. Who was he killed for? His people. That is what Isaiah said, and that is why Daniel says not for himself.

“And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Titus and Vespasian. “And the end thereof shall be with a flood”: war, 70 AD. “And unto the end of the war desolations are determined”: Israel removed out of the land and scattered among all nations into slavery. When the temple was destroyed there was no priest and no temple left to atone with, so the one who put his faith in the animal instead of Christ condemned himself by default. Faith in Christ had to come first.

Isaiah 53 says “by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many”. Somebody says, see, many means anybody. Isaiah has something for that: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Not all the seed of Israel and anybody else outside of Israel. Not all the good nations. Not individual heathens who say they have black friends. All the seed of Israel, all twelve tribes, shall be justified.

How? My righteous servant justifies many by dying on the cross, by laying on himself the iniquity of them all. That is the “justification” Paul speaks of when he says Christ “was raised again for our justification”, and it is why Romans 5 opens, “Therefore being justified by faith”. Who, according to the Old Testament, would be justified? Israel.

So when you read justification all throughout Paul’s letters, there should be no confusion about what he is talking about or who he is talking about. Abraham’s faith was imputed to him for righteousness, and “it was not written for his sake alone”, but for his seed who believe on him that raised up Jesus from the dead.

Paul says Christ “was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification.” Our offences: whose? Isaiah 53 shows who Christ was delivered for. “Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows”: this is Isaiah speaking of his people. “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.” Maybe you are thinking that is everybody. Keep reading.

“All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.” Like sheep of the house of Israel. The us is the sheep. “He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth”; he did not say one word. Then: “for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.” Not all people, not all nations, not the good nations, not the not-so-bad ones. My people. And Isaiah was an Israelite. Now you know who the our is, who the all is, who the we is.

All the apologists online have to do is show us in the Old Testament where this changed and Christ came back a second time and died for heathens. Show where Isaiah says, oh yeah, I almost forgot the other nations. Peter said the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul’s letters as they do the other scriptures, but this is what Paul got it from.

“By his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities.” Many who? Israelites; the thought has not changed. “He bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.” An intercessor is a mediator, someone who steps in and dies in your place. Romans 5:11 says “by whom we have now received the atonement”, and the margin gives the word reconciliation. Atonement is Christ’s death, which brings us back to the Father. The theology of the world says atonement is the reconciliation of God and all humankind. But God was never one with all humankind. All nations were never one with Israel, ever. That is why Romans 5:9 says “being now justified by his blood”: his blood replaces the animals, the works we no longer receive justification from. And the time came, as Daniel 9 foretold, when the temple was destroyed, the priests scattered abroad and not one stone left standing. With no way left to atone with animals, we had to have faith in Christ; otherwise you condemn yourself, indebted to a law you can no longer keep.

So atonement, reconciliation and justification are three words for the same thing, for the same people, with the same God. Reconciliation is the restoration of a friendly relationship, a reuniting; you cannot reunite with someone you were never joined to. Israel was with God before, rebelled until “he was turned to be their enemy”, and through the death of his Son was brought back again. That is Romans 5:10: “when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Christ came and died for his people; he was cut off for his people. Romans 5:9 says we are “justified by his blood”, and Ephesians says it is that same blood that brings near those who were far off.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. That is the peace of Romans 5:1, “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ”. And it shows who is being spoken of. Who is the both? The two nations. When you read the history in the book of Kings, Israel and Judah split apart into two kingdoms, and Ezekiel prophesied that our king would come and die for the nation of Israel and the nation of Judah, so that they would no longer be two nations but one nation under Christ.

He “hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”. What was two is now one new man, with no more division.

“And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”. That is the same word as Romans 5:10, “we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son”. Reconcile means to bring together again, and the both being reconciled are the southern and northern kingdoms. So the audience in Romans is the same people God spoke to in the old covenant: the Jews in the church at Rome, and with them the Gentiles, who are the northern kingdom. Christ, by his death, brought both houses back to the Father as one.

“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men”. Yes, it passed upon all men; all nations are capable of sinning. The question is who God held accountable. Ezra tells the story. God “gavest a body unto Adam”, breathed into him the breath of life, and “unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The evil in Adam passed into all nations; Cain and them were wicked by default.

But out of Adam came a specific line God wanted to keep his laws. The flood came, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men”: not Ham’s or Japheth’s line, but Shem’s, the righteous line of Seth. They multiplied and “began again to be more ungodly than the first”, so God chose Abraham: “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”. Judith shows Abraham’s people left the gods of their fathers in Chaldea and worshipped the God of heaven. God promised “that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, and “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”. There is always that special line God deals with.

At Sinai he gave “the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel. And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart”. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same evil that was in Adam passed on to the righteous line. Then David built the city, and “they that inhabited the city forsook thee, And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart: And so thou gavest thy city over into the hands of thine enemies.”

It is a repeated cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets God’s laws, goes against them, destruction comes, they repent, and out of that line the righteous rise again. The accountability for sin fell on that line. That is what Paul does in Romans 5: he gives the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line.

Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, the same saints as at Rome. Who are the saints? “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” No other nation made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. As Eve was in Adam, we the bride were in Christ, chosen before the world was founded, “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. The adoption is the reconciliation, the atonement, the justification and the restoration.

So the many made righteous by the obedience of one in Romans 5 are the saints God chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. Adam’s offence brought death on the chosen line, and Christ’s obedience brings them back into the adoption that was always theirs.

If sin reigned unto death over the chosen line, has God given up on them? Paul answers: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

“God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Which he foreknew: that is Amos 3 and Romans 8 again. “You only have I known of all the families of the earth”, and “whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate”.

The cycle Ezra described, the righteous line receiving the law, going off, being destroyed and repenting, never ended with God throwing his people away. Every time, out of that line the righteous rose up again.

So where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, and it abounded upon the same people God foreknew. Paul, an Israelite of Benjamin, is himself the proof that God has not cast away his people.

“So by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” Who are the many? Romans 8 answers: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.” Foreknow means knew before. Before Adam was made, God knew the nation he would justify and glorify through his Son.

“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. The called are the elect Peter wrote to, the strangers scattered throughout Galatia and the rest, “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”, “a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation”.

“And whom he called, them he also justified”: justified through the blood of Christ. “And whom he justified, them he also glorified”: as Isaiah says, “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

Amos says it plainly: “You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” All nations sin, but God acknowledges only Israel’s sins and sent Christ for them. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” The free gift unto justification of life came upon the people God foreknew.

Paul’s heart is for his own: “For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh”. His kinsmen according to the flesh: his race. “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

Pertaineth means belongs. The adoption belongs to them, the adoption of Ephesians 1:5. The glory belongs to them: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all belong to the Israelites.

“Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

Christ came for Israel. The free gift that came “upon all men unto justification of life” in Romans 5 is the adoption, the glory and the promises that pertain to the Israelites, the people whose sins God held to account from Adam on and whom he justified by the obedience of one.

To covet is not simply to desire. It is to want what belongs to another inordinately: you violate God's laws to get it. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”. The daughter belongs under the father just like everything else in his house. Go around him to get her, never telling the fathers or the elders, and you have coveted. To entice is to allure, to bait, to induce to evil; it is trickery and deception. “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not”. And “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: if you love the sister, how did you use ill means to get her?

Peter shows what we are supposed to be doing instead: “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence”.

As brothers and sisters come in here, you are supposed to be escaping these worldly elements and truly repenting. When you look across the aisle, you are supposed to be looking for righteousness, not just her behind. Taking your sister for lust is the corruption that is in the world, and the same thing goes on on the other side. A man who talks to you under cover, without your father and without the leadership, does not have good intentions; the fact that he didn't do it the right way shows you where his mind is.

Do it with diligence, the right way. When we announce our marriages we say, this is the day the Lord has made between you two; you can bring forth righteousness right here, and the Lord, the angels and everybody are in agreement with it. When you do things the right way, you have a whole community behind you. The fathers and the elders have the vantage point: we see down the road where it is going, and we make the decision as fathers.

Exodus 22:17: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins”. He has to pay, but he still is not getting the daughter. Somebody might say, he paid, so he gets to take her. Leviticus 6 shows the principle: “Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away”.

Took violently away. To entice that daughter against her father's wishes is to violate him, and violation is violence. That is the same reason a man who steals an ox must “restore five oxen for an ox”: the owner was violated, and restitution is paid for the violent act against him.

“or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten”. The recent matter was deceit. Her fathers didn't know anything about it, the leadership didn't know anything about it, nobody knew until her sister discovered it, and they still weren't going to say anything. How are you going to come up later saying, here's the law?

“Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering”. The principal is the actual thing taken, and the fifth part is added on top. So you are not getting the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why the judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, to be beguiled by a wicked brother who says we're applying Exodus 22:16. That's a damn lie.

The Pharisees came to Christ “tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” They were trying to use Moses' law, the writing of divorcement in Deuteronomy 24. Christ took them back to the beginning: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?” From the beginning there was no such thing as divorce. What are you talking about, quoting Moses? It's the same as a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16.

“Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder”. God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That's why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call yourself love. You don't love anything but your own lust.

“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so”. The only reason Moses had to bring in that negro-proof law is that we were hard-headed and gave Moses hell. It is a failsafe law, a kind of bylaw to keep us from going all the way wicked. You are not supposed to be in failure at all for it even to come up, and quoting one after you went off and did wrong does not make you righteous.

That is covering violence with the garment: “for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the Lord of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously”. The Pharisees enlarged the borders of their garments, and the fringes represent the laws. A man who deceived to get a sister and then gives her a so-called law from the Bible is covering his violation with the law. Sisters and brothers, watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and stop playing games.

Habakkuk said, “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. The watchman on the tower sees what the people below cannot. Peter gives the elders that charge: “Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof”.

Listen to the wording: taking the oversight. The leaders stand at a vantage point the flock cannot see. From the experience and the level they have reached over their years in the truth, they see what younger men and younger women do not, and God gave them revelation through the scriptures to see how to guide you. If we believe there is a God, and that Christ is the brain of this whole operation, then we are supposed to trust the men he set up.

But a lot of brothers and sisters in the congregation get horny and antsy and will not follow the counsel. Then they end up asking the same leadership whose oversight they did not trust to counsel them on the matter after the fact. That is completely backwards, and nobody does that but us. That is the negro mind.

“Not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”. That is for the leadership: they feed the flock willingly and take the oversight because they love their people. Nobody is getting paid to do this. They do it of a ready mind, watching from the tower until the vision the Lord appointed comes.

Habakkuk stood on his tower demanding answers: how long are we going to be in this captivity? The Lord answered, “the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come”. Now that we know what time we are in, Isaiah says, “Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors.”

Be men and use your mind. God gave the sons of God a mind to envision greatness, to see things in the mind before the hands build them. He gave you that vantage point so you can set up a congregation and make sure evil does not come among the brothers and sisters. O ye transgressors: change.

“I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”. God declared the end before he said, Let there be light. Everything falls in the path he wants it to fall. He knew from ancient times that the fourth bird from the mother hen would fly over Wyoming on March 7th, 2028. You say that bird is insignificant; he says, I need that bird to do that because it is connected to something else you don't know about. That is his vantage point.

“Calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man that executeth my counsel from a far country”. While he causes that bird to come from the east, he calls another man to execute his judgment. “I have purposed it, I will also do it.” A sparrow shall not fall to the ground unless the Most High causes it. Everything is under his auspices; he knows why he holds the armies back so the earth is not destroyed. You and I are not on that level, and we try to move God while we will not keep the commandments. The only thing we need to do is obey what he said.

That is why the vision will not lie. We cannot reason out why he calls that insignificant raven, but in God's overall plan it is necessary, and the end he declared from the beginning will surely come.

Habakkuk was told, “the just shall live by his faith”, by the words of the book of our fathers. Isaiah shows what that faith requires of us: “Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.”

Those of us in wickedness must forsake it, and forsake the unrighteous thoughts of lasciviousness, lust, adultery and fornication. Get that thing out of your mind. He will pardon us if we are sincere, not pretending while on the back end doing evil and thinking nobody sees. The Lord understands the heartbeat of a raven, how many times a bird's heart will beat its whole life, and you think he don't see your black ass? You are playing with death.

“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways”. Looking down from heaven on the whole planet, he sees everything we cannot. Our only vantage point is our immediate circumference, and we cannot take that and tell the Lord what to do.

It works the same in the congregation. A manager of a department sees his space; the leadership over all the departments sees the interactions between them, and why something is happening here and not there. Leaders are in front to protect the flock because they see the danger you do not see. The man on the tower sees it coming and sounds the trumpet with a certain sound, so the people know what to prepare for.

“So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please”. As the rain waters the earth and does not return void, everything the Lord sends has a purpose. So when leadership says, brother, leave the sister alone, or sister, leave the brother alone, there is a vantage point you do not see, and if you will not hear it, it gets revealed in judgment after you done laid with the dude. Follow the steps, betrothal and the whole nine, and the council can bless the wedding and counsel the trouble in the flesh. Say to hell with all of it, and you are saying you have nothing to do with us.

We say give the Lord no rest, make the time short, bring it on: when is he coming to get us out? We are trying to speed the Lord up. But the Lord has his timetable and a reason for the pace he is moving at, and when it is time for him to move, you can't stop it. Esau won't be able to stop it. “Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off.” When all the planets have lined up, it is time to send Christ and the destroying angels to bring his people home, and if you are not ready, he comes as a thief in the night.

Ezra shows the mind of the Most High, his vantage point: “Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together, Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys in Sion were hot” … “before they were sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure.”

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” The Most High made all of that, so we can't question that kind of understanding. We are not on the level to question how the Lord did things. Nobody did this but him, and by him alone it shall be ended.

So he sends Christ when he is ready to send Christ. We don't know the day or the hour, but we know we are in the season, and the enemies of the Lord include some of our own people siding with the oppressors by agreeing to be in sin and destroying their own people. That is not the agencies; that is negroes being wicked as hell, and negro is a mind state across all twelve tribes that was never supposed to be you. Knowing these things are coming, we need to get our minds and our spirits right.

God's vantage point is far beyond the vantage point we think we have. People try to tell the Lord what to do: you can't love Jacob, you can't hate Esau, you can't forgive this one. So the Lord clears the deck and lets everybody know where he stands, and everybody else needs to shut the hell up.

“Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?” Nobody. These are questions for us who are trying to push him. The dumb Christian talks about the way the Lord should be; shut up. “With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Who taught God knowledge? Nobody. God is the knowledge; how are you going to teach him?

Having asked questions we can't answer, he proclaims what it is: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket.” You walk with a pail of water and one drop falls out; you won't even notice it. All the nations put together are that one drop. They “are counted as the small dust of the balance”: not big dust, small dust on the scales, weighing nothing. “He taketh up the isles as a very little thing”: the Polynesian and Hawaiian islands, very little, nothing.

“And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” If they burnt up all the meat in Lebanon, it would not be sufficient for him to accept the Arabs, Ishmael, as his people. Only the Israelites are his people; that is why the first verse of the chapter says, comfort ye my people.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Less than nothing is spit, a bowel movement. That is how the nations are counted to God, while to us he says comfort ye my people. That is the difference, and nobody can say anything against it. 2 Esdras 6:55-56 parallels it and calls them spittle: Ezra was quoting Isaiah. The supreme power has it set up the way he wants it set up.

Ezra is still dealing with the mind of God. The Lord had said all things “were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” That is the smiting of the earth with a curse. We cannot move God's timetable; not a sparrow falls without the Father, and he has millions of things lined up that we are not even aware of. You are trying to move God with your hastiness, and yet you will not even keep the commandments.

Then Ezra asks for the sign: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall this wicked rule end? It is the same question the disciples asked in Matthew 24: when shall these things be?

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” That is the only clue given, and the people in the churches do not even know who Esau is, so they are completely lost. Bishop Nathanyel's class on the Achilles heel goes with this like cookies and milk.

“For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Once we find out who Esau is, see how he is acting on this earth and read about him in the Bible, we know the time is near, even at the doors. And Jacob is the beginning of what follows: Jacob is going to rule; that is the kingdom. Seeing all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought we to be? Our minds need to be on that level.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”. The other nations are in between, insignificant, affected by one or the other, and they will never rule.

“Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh”. Christ is saying, pay attention to the seasons. Watch the fig tree; when the branches are tender and the leaves come out, you know summer is near by how the trees are changing.

“So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” We do not know the day and we do not know the hour, but we know we are in the season. The prophets wrote down what was coming, and now we actually see it: the missiles sitting in the silos ready to rock, the mushroom cloud Isaiah 34 speaks of. They did not have that when Malachi brought this out, but it is here now, letting us know what time we are in. You are not going to get a bigger sign than that.

So that is where we are: the destruction is even at the doors, and here we are playing games. That is what Malachi was saying: “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” Smite the earth with destruction. So we had better remember the law of Moses, the laws and the commandments, and keep them, so that we are not caught off guard when that day comes. Knowing these things are coming, our minds and our spirits need to be right.

The same transition of time is written in Revelation. “And the great dragon was cast out”: that is Esau, the red dragon, the Romans. That was the Roman Empire that came into our heaven, meaning our kingdom, destroyed Jerusalem and cast us into captivity. The heaven Esau is going to fall from is his ruling kingdom right now. It is not a fight at creation where Satan got kicked out of heaven; that is a perversion of Isaiah 14.

Satan does what the Most High tells him. In Job the Lord asked Satan where he came from, and Satan could not touch Job because of the hedge around him, which is the hedge we want around us. In Kings, when Ahab was to be persuaded to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead, an evil spirit said he would be a lying spirit in the mouth of his prophets, and the Lord sent him. The Lord has control of everything. Here in Revelation 12 is when Christ destroys these demonic forces.

“That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: going all the way back to Cain, back to Eve. Devil means evil; Satan means adversary. That is the white man; he fits it to a tee. And he has never been white: not nasty white, not beige, not off-white. He is red. Stop lying when you look at him.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: he made everybody on the planet believe Christ looks like Charles Manson, when the Bible gives a full description of Christ as a black man with woolly hair and feet like brass burned in a furnace. That is great deception.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his missionaries, his black preachers and ministers, imps of Satan to destroy our people. Christianity is the perfection of slavery. In chains, being whipped, we still wanted freedom; but Christianity is the greatest dope of all, and it put us so far to sleep we do not even want to be free. It destroyed us from within.

When the Lord casts this devil down and smashes all that Christian garbage and all those lies, then: “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down”. When these devils go down, we rule. That is Jacob, the beginning of the world that follows.

Christ says, “except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” We claim we want the days shortened, but we are not ready, because wicked brothers are trying to slide in. Brothers and sisters who come from the world with a world mentality would love nothing more than to seduce and defile you, men and women both, because they don't want to change. Negroes don't like change. They pretend they've changed and put on the fringes and the border of blue so you let your guard down, then work behind the scenes to allure you away from your protection.

Dinah shows how it happens, and she was not raped. “And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.” Was she snatched? No, she went out on her own. With a father and twelve mighty brothers, you know they brought her the wisdom that pertains to a woman, and tried to keep her in straitly, the way the scripture says to keep a shameless daughter. She did not want to hear it. She wandered away from her father and her brethren.

“And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” Something in her spirit let him know. He knew whose daughter she was, and he saw she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers or her brethren. That is how slick brothers hit sisters in the DMs: they read your spirit when you are not studying, and once they talk that talk, you feed right into it.

“And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” That is the part that tells you it was not rape: he spake kindly to her. You gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured: drawn away from her protection, from her fathers, from how she was raised, from the protections leadership put around her. Enticing is covetousness; she belonged to Jacob, and he drew her away. Then he asked to marry her, and her brothers said no, you already defiled her. She had to live with that stain for wandering out of her father’s care, and you read nothing of her after that.

Christ warns, “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect”: some of you men and women of the third slated to make it. Everybody with fringes and a border of blue is not right; do not look at his pretty beard. One who tells women marriage is not the goal and singleness is not the curse, while flaunting his own wife, is the devil in black flesh; he wants the women to stay in sin. A woman in the world turned down one of these street preachers when he broke character to ask for her number. A woman in the world knows more about the commandments than a negro with fringes and a Bible who is supposed to be keeping them, yet a sister in here will entertain the same kind in her DMs. Whoremongering brothers fake the funk, become soldiers, and look for spinsters, sisters anxious about getting older and not married yet, and gas them up, because all bread is sweet to a whoremonger. That is why, when you correctly come together, you exchange medical records and show each other; leadership does not need to see them. Give diligence and study, so you can recognize deception at your door, whatever it is wearing.

Visualize the scene of Revelation 7: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds. That wind is not the regular wind that blows every day; it is destruction. The four corners are where the militaries are, straining to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back. Bishop Nathanyel, who is an artist, once drew this scene.

2 Esdras 13 is the same scene. “There arose a wind from the sea, that it moved all the waves thereof. And I beheld, and, lo, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.” That is how Christ is coming back. “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you think he will not see your wicked thoughts and the things you thought you were hiding? You don’t want to be on the wrong side of that magnificent coming.

Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. Don't fall from your own stedfastness: Paul said none other things than Moses and the prophets.

When they appointed Paul a day, many came to his lodging, “to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” That is the other scriptures. His source material was the Old Testament.

Write this down: Paul's letters predate the gospels, with the exception of Mark. Mark, Luke and Matthew are the synoptic gospels, and it is said Matthew and Luke borrowed from Mark, because Mark was Peter's scribe. That is why Peter has no gospel: Mark is Peter's gospel, and it makes sense that it is the oldest, since Peter's and Paul's ministries were at the same time. Paul's letters range from the forties to the sixties AD. John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome besieged Jerusalem in 70 AD, and Revelation around 95 to 100 AD.

So Paul was not pulling from John 3:16, because when he wrote his letters there was no John 3:16. He was not quoting John, Matthew or Luke; his letters came before them. Luke was travelling with him, and Luke wrote both Luke and Acts: Acts is basically a second Luke, Luke's letter number two.

That is why you cannot understand Paul's letters, the things hard to be understood, without the law and the prophets. Paul persuaded men concerning Jesus out of Moses and the prophets from morning till evening, and the unlearned who don't know those scriptures wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

Paul keeps saying “among”: the gospel “which I preach among the Gentiles”, preaching him “among the heathen”. Why does he keep using that word? Because Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he is writing to the entire time. Then he says “the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter”. Christ wrought effectually in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, “the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles”.

Who are those Gentiles? John answers: “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews here are the circumcision, born and raised in the Mosaic law. They ask where Christ will go that they cannot find him. Will he go to the dispersed? The dispersed are the Israelites, the diaspora scattered among the Gentiles.

And what do the Jews call those dispersed Israelites? Gentiles: “and teach the Gentiles”. So now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to throughout the entire time. It should be a no-brainer now.

That is why James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision”: Paul to the Israelites scattered among the nations, the others to the Jews who were not scattered abroad. And it is why Paul withstood Peter at Antioch. Peter ate with these Gentiles, the scattered Israelites he was teaching who they are, then withdrew when certain came from James, fearing them of the circumcision. You cannot teach the scattered who they are and then act as if you are not with them; that is a bad example.

“And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.” The heathen are the Gentiles: the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, justified through faith. But Christians say, see, brother, all nations will be blessed. So what does it mean?

Peter answers: “Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.” They foretold, as Paul says the scripture foresaw. “Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers”. The ye are the Israelites. Abraham was a prophet, and the covenant passed from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob, “saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

“Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.” Unto you first, the Israelites. The blessing is Christ dying for the Israelites, for all of us scattered among all the nations. The earth is too big for us to reach all our people, but Christ's blood covers us wherever we are found. That is how all the kindreds of the earth are blessed: Israel scattered among those nations and blessed with the death of Christ.

And Esau? He already got his blessing: blood and death, slavery, weaponry, war, bloodshed, nukes and witchcraft. He is literally dropping those blessings on Iran right now. He does not need any more. The other nations' blessing is to work, to build up our kingdom, and to survive the destruction as servants. “So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

“foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith”. How do we know who is justified? You will not find anywhere in the law and the prophets that Christ was going to justify, atone for or reconcile all the heathen Gentile nations through his death. What you find is this: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

All the seed of Israel, all the families scattered abroad over the earth, justified by faith in Christ. Whether they are called Jews or called Gentiles, they shall be justified, because Christ died for them among the nations.

Now show me a precept where all the seed of Edom will be justified. All the seed of Moab justified. All the seed of Ishmael, all the seed of the Canaanites. Show me one place. It is nowhere in there.

So “they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham”: the Israelites who have faith in Christ are the children of Abraham, known for his strong faith. Abraham believed God first, and only afterward offered sacrifices, and his faith, not the animal, was counted for righteousness. That is how the seed of Israel is justified, and why “they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.”

“But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” Justified by the law here is the same law as the works of the law in verses 2, 5 and 10 and in Galatians 2:16: the law of sacrifice.

Paul preached the same thing in Acts 13: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, and all that believe in Christ's death are justified from all things, all sins.

Could you receive justification from all things under Moses? No, because animals do not atone for all things. Does Christ's death atone for all things, reconcile us from all things, justify us from all things? Yes. That is the difference.

And the law is not of faith because faith came first. “The man that doeth them shall live in them”: the man who does the sacrifices lives until he commits a sin worthy of death, and then he cannot live anymore. The just live by faith in the one whose death covers what no animal could.

“for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. That is written in Deuteronomy 21: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled.” Hanging was capital punishment among us.

So Christ took on the curses for us, the punishment and consequence of violating that covenant, when he was hung. Some say he wasn't hung, he was nailed to a cross. But if you are nailed to a wooden pole, you are hanging by your hands and feet. That is a lynching. He was hung for hours.

Peter calls it the same thing, twice: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” And again, “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.” They hung Christ on a tree, on wood, a cross. Christ died a black man's death.

Do you think the lynchings among our people were a coincidence, when the white man hung us from trees and lamps and bridges? People have been hung from time to time, but not to the capacity we have been hung; it was enforced all around among us. The curse of the tree came on our people, and Christ bore that same curse to redeem us from it, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”

“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse.” The works of the law, in Galatians 3:2, 3:5, 3:10 and 2:16, is sacrifice, as in Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. And “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them” is Paul quoting Deuteronomy 27.

What does that curse mean? “Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image”, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” Can he atone for it, reconcile with God, find justification? What animal can he use? None. Under the old covenant you get death. That is what cursed means.

So it goes all the way down. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”: disrespects, curses or strikes them. “Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark.” The so-called white man has removed the neighbor's landmark: America is a stolen landmark, Africa is a stolen landmark, Australia is a stolen landmark. How can he atone when the land is still in his possession? He can't; he sits on stolen land. “Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife”, his stepmother. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.” “Cursed be he that lieth with his sister”, “with his mother in law.” “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly”: kills his brother secretly and does not get caught. “Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person”: a hitman, a mercenary.

After each one, “all the people shall say, Amen”: we all agreed to it. Then “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them”, which is exactly what Paul quotes. None of these could be atoned for with an animal. It is death all throughout.

That is why those of the works of the law are under the curse. We confirmed to do everything under that covenant of sacrifices, and if you violate a law that no animal can cover, you get the curse, which is death.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.” Some people read right past that. What is the curse of the law? Death. But you need a scripture to back up what you say, and John 11 is it.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation, all twelve tribes, perishing: that is the curse of the law. All twelve tribes broke the first covenant, and by that default we were all worthy of death. When Christ died, he took that curse upon himself for us. That is “being made a curse for us”: dying for us.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only.” Not for Judah only, “but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Gather together in one is reconciliation, at-one-ment, atonement.

So Christ died for Judah and for Israel, all twelve tribes. Those scattered abroad are the ones Paul was going to among the heathen, among the Gentiles, while being called Gentiles themselves. That is how “the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”

How did Israelites become Greeks? “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest”. Jason was a wicked Israelite who changed his name to Jason, a Greek name. He sought underhandedly to be high priest against his brother Onias, a righteous man, using money to gain authority and leadership. When a man seeks leadership, he usually is not meant to be a leader at all.

“Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents”. He bribed the king of the Greeks, the white man, to force his brother out of position and put him in. “Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise”, a gym, “and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen”: training the Israelite youth in the culture of the Greeks.

“and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” He registered the Israelites of Jerusalem as citizens of Antioch, the Antioch in Turkey that Paul writes about. Becoming Antiochians was a betrayal of the ancestral laws and a shift to the Greek way of life, and that cultural tension triggered the Maccabean revolt. Antiochian and Greek are the same.

So when Paul says “There is neither Jew nor Greek”, he is writing to the descendants of those same people. Whether called Jew or Greek, “if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” The heirs are Israelites, to whom pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law and the promises.

“There is neither Jew nor Greek”. Christians read it like a soft effeminate man, neither Jew nor Greek, brother, and say it means anybody. The people of Christianity have no idea about history. Why does Paul reference Greeks?

“Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God”. Your law, your culture and your race go hand in hand with God. The Bible says love your neighbour as yourself; that is law. Deny your race and you deny your laws; deny your law and you deny your God.

“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” It was basically illegal under the order of the king to call yourself a Jew or keep Jewish customs. So over time we became Greeks, Gentiles.

That is who Paul is writing to. The ye that were kept under the law in verse 23 are the same ye called Jews and Greeks, bond and free, male and female. Do not escape that context. Whatever your title or status in that present world, Jew or Greek, free like Paul or bond like others, “ye are all one in Christ Jesus”: all God's chosen people.

“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” Who was kept under the law? “Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law”. We were locked into that covenant until Christ came, died, and granted us liberty.

What was it we were kept under? Hebrews gives an example of the works of the law: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrifices could not make him that did them perfect, because sin was already in us since Adam. So the animals had to be temporary.

“Which stood only in meats and drinks”: meat offerings and drink offerings. These are the works of the law read all through Galatians, in 2:16, 3:2, 3:5 and 3:10-11. “and divers washings”: baptisms. “and carnal ordinances”: the traditions of the Pharisees. “imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Forced upon them until the time of reformation, which is the faith that should afterwards be revealed, when Christ came and did away with all of it.

So “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”. The schoolmaster was sacrifice. The sacrificing of animals was a foreshadowing of Christ's death, preparing us for his body. It was temporary, because we grew weary and rebellious behind it and would all have been condemned through it. “But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”: no longer under the law of sacrifice.

Who was bewitching the Galatians back into bondage? “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” After the manner of Moses, sacrifice followed circumcision, on the eighth day. To be circumcised after the manner of Moses meant going back to sacrifice.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” These men came from Judea infiltrating and causing confusion, saying you have to sacrifice.

“But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees came in as believers, part of the church, and were imposing that you had to sacrifice according to the manner of Moses. These are the same false brethren brought in unawares that Galatians addresses, who came in privily to spy out our liberty and bring us into bondage.

As the movement grew, the Pharisees went into the churches to win them back to temple law. Paul said he profited in the Jews' religion; people bringing animals was their bread and butter. They were saying to hell with what Christ did, you need an animal for atonement. Paul's answer: if you do, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

Paul calls them “weak and beggarly elements”. Hebrews calls the same thing weak: “For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.” The disannulling is of animal sacrifice. What made it weak and unprofitable? “For the law made nothing perfect”, including the man's conscience, “but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.” That better hope is Christ.

Hebrews 10 says it again: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” It could not make those who offered them perfect.

So the weak and beggarly elements are the sacrificing of animals. They were unprofitable because we were too sinful to keep maintaining them.

That is why verse 10 says “Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years”. Ezekiel 45:17 shows that it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. Colossians 2:16 matches it: meat, drink, holyday, new moon and sabbath days: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and Christ is the body, the sacrifice for all of those things. The Galatians were turning back to observing those days by the weak and beggarly elements.

“But when the fulness of the time was come”, the time appointed of the Father, “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.” Who did Christ come to redeem? Them that were under the law. The we is the same we of chapter 3 that were kept under the law, and the adoption pertains to Israel.

Hebrews is the nail in the coffin: “And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Christ is the mediator of the new testament by means of his death, hanging on the cross. Redemption is the redeeming, and he died for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.

Who was under the first testament? Israel. So those Christ redeemed are those who were under the law, the called who receive the promise of eternal inheritance: the heirs.

“And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.” When Christ died we were no longer servants but sons of the Father, and heirs through his Son.

“And almost all things are by the law purged with blood”. Almost, not all. So be mindful of always saying blood sacrifice, because the heathen are going to come with that. Not every sin offering was blood, because some among us were poor and could not bring a blood sacrifice.

Leviticus shows it: “But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.” The priest took his handful of it as a memorial and burned it on the altar.

And the main example was obedience: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise. To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” A propitiation is reconciliation. When you depart from sin and keep God's commandments, that is sacrifice enough.

Israel never got there. Israel thought, I can sin all I want and sacrifice all I want, and I'm good. We were children under the schoolmaster, sacrificing and sinning again, going into slavery and out and back again. The Lord said enough of that, and sent his Son. That is why turning back to the weak and beggarly elements is turning back to bondage.

“But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage?” We know the true God now, not a pagan one, and we are known of God because Christ died for us. Verse 3 said we were in bondage under the elements of the world; verse 9 calls them weak and beggarly elements. It is the same bondage the false brethren of chapter 2 wanted to bring us back into. So what are they?

Some say we keep saying law of sacrifice and it does not say that. But it does call it weak. “For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh”. Weak through the flesh means weak through our sin, through us.

What could the law not do? Hebrews 9:9 says the gifts and sacrifices “could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrificing of animals could not make us perfect. That is what the law could not do, and that is the weak in the weak and beggarly elements.

So God sent his own Son to do what the animals could not, and to turn back to animal sacrifice after knowing God is to desire again to be in bondage.
