“All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.” John shows the power we must not come under: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

The world here is predominantly America. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed and created against us, in complete opposition to us, to cater to and test the flesh. It is either to make you or break you, to forge you or destroy you. Only the strong, spiritually, mentally and physically, are going to survive this kingdom.

Do not love the things catered to us in entertainment, catered to us when we are bored and idle. Scrolling is idle; that is love of the world. Porn is love of the world. Instagram models are love of the world. Clubbing is love of the world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Satan was given power over this world, and he is going to try to get you to operate outside of your purpose. What looks good to the eyes and caters to the appetite is not always good; look past the outside to the ingredients. The body is not for any of that; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

“Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats”: food is for nourishment. “Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord”. Paul moves from food to fornication because the two are correlated: both deal with self-control over your vessel, which was created as a vessel of righteousness to be used for the master's work.

Sirach says: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” You might think it is only talking about sex, but your appetite can be anything you overindulge in: food, sex, working out, TV and entertainment, sports, scrolling. We focus on food and sex because they are one and the same, and if we get control over those two we can get control of anything in our life and reprogram our vessel to do what the Lord commands.

There are wants and there are needs. You need sex, in marriage; when you do not need, study, pray, fast. You are hungry, you eat and nourish your body, then you choose the foods that give you the energy to think, function and be productive in this work. That is what food is for.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” You become a laughingstock. There are videos saying, I can't listen to a fat prophet. A brother is powerful in the street, cutting people up, bad to the bone, and people say, I can't listen to you because you don't even listen to you. That is why they say bring back fat-shaming: you are operating outside the realm of discipline.

Satan tells you that you are hungry; Satan tells you to eat that McDonald's, that Burger King, that candy. These things are pushed on us to keep us sickly so we cannot do the work, sick every Sabbath. Feed the body the vitamins, fiber and nutrients it needs, so you possess your vessel and it serves the Lord.

Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

“I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?” Job had to literally make a covenant: I'm not going to watch that, and if it gets within my eyesight, I got to turn away. I got to train my eyes to look away.

That is the three-second rule. The eyes are input. If you let yourself look at something for more than three seconds, it goes into your working memory, your short-term memory; keep looking at it and you are programming yourself into long-term memory. Turn away within three seconds and it doesn't have time to work within your memory. That is why TikTok gives you three seconds to capture somebody's attention, and why Netflix keeps it moving: once they have your attention through your eyes, they have you. Our eyes are the portal to take control over your vessel.

The algorithm is a reflection of you. Your searches and your scrolls tell who you are, what makes you sad, what makes you mad, what music you play when you're angry. So when you say the algorithm got you, it's not them getting you. It's you, manifested on a screen. The devil don't make you do anything you don't want to do.

David said the same: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes.” Train your eyes. If a show is full of action but something enticing comes on that goes against your values and your struggles, turn it off, click by. If you hear gossip or something negative, leave the conversation, because three seconds of listening will taint you, and three seconds of something negatively influencing you will control you.

“Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weepeth upon every occasion.” The eye is where it starts. It starts with the desire of what you see, and then the mind decides whether to feed the lust.

That is why it belongs with Matthew 15. The Pharisees were arguing about eating with unwashed hands, and Christ told them that what goes in at the mouth goes into the belly and “is cast out into the draught”, but “those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” What comes out of your mouth is the output value of what was put into your mind, and the eye is one of the ways it gets put in.

The brain stores everything you let in. A random song or thought from years ago comes out of you because it was saved in long-term memory, the same way your stuff on the internet never really leaves. What you put into your vessel determines what comes out, and a lot of times we don't even realize we are being controlled. You were made in a factory called America, and those are not your words. The only way to break that code is to reprogram and recode, and the wicked eye is where the guarding has to begin.

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.

“And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.”

The men who gathered to David were not the full package. They were in distress, in debt and discontented: men with problems and issues. David took them in and became a captain over them. That was the beginning of IUIC too: men with problems and issues, taken in and built with structure and discipline. The women are built the same way, through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2 and Daughters of Sarah.

Later those same men are spoken of differently. In 2 Samuel 17:8 Hushai says to Absalom, “thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.” They were not mighty at first. David put in the work, the same way the leadership put the work in us.

That is why it sits with “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Everyone comes in with negative impulses, and we expect it. Hard times create warriors against sinful impulses, and the men are the vanguards of righteousness, to ward off any semblance of sin. When evil communications come to men and women, you shut them down and do not entertain them. The ones who come in get tried and watched, and the demons get exercised out of them through the congregation, the brothers and sisters that are watching them. If you really want to get yourself right, you will thank them for the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. But if you refuse to change, you have to go, because we cannot let a bad example destroy the rest of the flock.

“What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” Can words save him? Because that is basically all you are giving. Some people don’t even understand what faith really is, because faith alone is just saying I believe in something. Paul defines it: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

So don’t tell me you have faith. Faith is the substance, and substance is what you can touch, what you can see, something materialized. You can have faith in your head all day long, underneath your skull; I can’t see it. The only way I will know what is in your mind is when I see action as a result of your thinking. As a man thinks, you are supposed to see the fruit of it.

Even if he or she has not achieved it yet, you can tell where they are going by how they carry themselves. On a college campus you see a student walking into the engineering building with his T-squares and architect tubes. He doesn’t have the degree yet, he is not an architect or engineer yet, but the works of his mind tell you where he is going. That is how faith is validated by action. Where there is no vision, the people perish; your mind has to manipulate the elements around you to form what you have in your head.

That is what the Lord did. The earth was without form and void, meaning it did not exist yet, but he still called it earth, because earth existed in God’s mind. Then the Spirit moved upon the face of the waters, the elements, and caused them to form the earth and the light. And he saw that the light was good: he compared what was formed to what he imagined and it agreed with the thought in his mind. Sisters do the same at the mirror; you don’t walk away until what you did with your hands matches the image in your mind, and then you say it is good. That is the power we have, but our elders were cut off from giving us basic understanding like that, and we fell asleep for centuries.

That is why the elders must set up organizational foundations, literal buildings where people can see the works of the teaching. A brother or sister naked and destitute of daily food told “Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled”, but given nothing, is still hungry. That is church, that is Christianity. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

Leviticus warns that if a daughter is prostituted, “the land become full of wickedness.” Hosea shows what full of wickedness looks like: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” Controversy means against: the Lord is against how we live. It speaks mainly of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now.

No truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Truth is the Bible, the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to “Do not prostitute thy daughter”; nobody is paying attention to it or bringing that precaution into the land. No mercy: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. No knowledge of God, meaning his commandments: the priest's lips should keep knowledge and the people should seek the law at his mouth, and they are not getting it at all.

“By swearing, and lying”. We heard complete lies two weeks ago: a man told everybody that nobody had told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look as if the leadership didn't know what was going on. Brothers had to stand up, bring him right back to his lying statement, and correct his wicked ass in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did. Then: “and killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos.

All of it because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover your ass. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that when the clothes come off, all kinds of things go on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all. Then: “and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. People get stabbed and shot up, all because she had her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection?

So “full of wickedness” means literally full of wickedness: that is what you get when God's laws are not taught, no Bible, no scruples, no laws. Having kids through backdoor marriages produces madness like this. That is done here. You're going to do it right or you ain't going to do it at all; nobody is holding a ceremony over fornication. It starts with the fathers and mothers, who must not prostitute the daughter, because the enemy goes after the women: mess them up and the children are done.

Paul told Timothy he was persuaded that Christ “is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.” Paul committed his soul, his life, to Christ. What day? Thessalonians explains it: “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That day is the second coming, and all twelve tribes can only gather unto Christ.

“That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” People were writing letters in Paul’s name saying the second coming had already happened and you missed it. Paul said, I don’t care if you got a letter signed by me, I didn’t write that; that day did not happen yet. Remember in the sixties the FBI would write letters to the Black Panthers and other black organizations in each other’s names. They were doing the same thing with Paul.

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” Christ is not going to return until all twelve tribes fall away into captivity. Christians break that down as people leaving Christianity; it is not talking about that crap. It is falling into captivity, as Luke 21:24 says: “they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” All twelve shall fall, and we are still living in the times of the Gentiles.

In Paul’s day, Judah, Benjamin and Levi had not fallen completely; they were still in the land. But 70 AD was soon approaching. So the day Paul committed his soul against has not come yet, and it could not come until all of us fell. And we all fell.

“That day” in Paul’s words to Timothy is the second coming, and Joel shows what kind of day it is: “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” This is a time of war and devastation. When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

Amos says the same: “Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.” We say we can’t wait for the day of the Lord because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen. You think it is going to be a bright day and Christ will take us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of a day; it is not that type of a party.

Zephaniah: “The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.” Don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. We are going to be running and weeping.

Christ said it in Matthew 24: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”, which is Jacob’s trouble, “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, because the sky will be black, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. The powers of the nations shall be shaken with war. “and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” You think you will be happy, stomping your feet and clapping; the Bible says all the tribes shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly. That is the day Paul was preparing Timothy for, and why he told him to stir up the gift, not fear, and not be ashamed of the afflictions of the gospel.

“For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world.” Demas traveled with Paul and warred with Paul, and he forsook Paul. He saw the looseness of the women: Paul, I’ve got to go, my man, I can’t roll with you no more, I got needs. He let that overcome him. Crescens left for Galatia, Titus for Dalmatia. Mark shows what happened to Paul’s companions, men who were strong in the Lord and in the power of his might. Those guys are some of you guys.

“And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness.” I’m an Israelite, we got history, oh I love it. “And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time.” No root: I don’t study, I don’t addict myself to the ministry, I like my sports, I like my porn, the Bible comes last. So you only endure this gospel for a time.

“afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.” Offended, and you leave. Affliction is things that happen to you; persecution is what happens to you for the word’s sake, because you stand strong in this Bible. That is why Paul told Timothy not to be ashamed of his affliction, to suffer in it with him and stir up the gift within him. Christ lets us know some of us are going to leave this truth because of affliction.

And Satan will test. He asks the Lord, can I test him? Can I test her? The brother with a proclivity for the male gender went to the gym at two in the morning, where the freaks come out at night, found two men in the shower, stood there five whole minutes, and they invited him to join in. If you are struggling, stay out of the gym; do calisthenics at your house. You are trying to fight a spirit; don’t go around spirits like that.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, a piece of the American pie, may not be your thing. But the lust of other things is anything in you that nobody else knows. You may hide it very well, but God knows it is there, Satan knows it is there, and you do too. Satan is not tempting you with a pork chop. He looks into your soul, sees what you are battling with, and asks to tempt you right there.

That is what took Demas, Crescens and Titus, and it is what Paul went through with Alexander the coppersmith, who was in the ministry and turned against it, “for he hath greatly withstood our words.” We have seen the same: men in the gospel who went online to try to tear this down. “At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me.” Christ already prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” In 2018 brothers were dropping like flies, brothers and sisters we broke bread with, who stayed in our homes and knew our families, offended at the gospel and betraying it. Some tried to start Israelite congregations and fell overnight. God is not going to bless your hands after you did so much evil to your brothers and sisters.

The prince of Tyrus has “gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”, and our people try to get involved in America's wealth, America's riches. They want a piece of the pie. But getting a piece of America's pie is dangerous. Christ asks the question: “For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”

In order to get the fame and fortune that many of our people so desperately want, because we want to take care of our friends and family, you have to sell your soul. You must give your soul to these people.

That is often called hush money. Someone as wealthy as LeBron James takes care of his friends, which is admirable, and his family, which is admirable. But in terms of helping his people on a major level, he is not allowed to do that. That is hush money: hush the F up, and just take care of your friends and family. Oprah, all these people; many of them have gone to Epstein's Island, and their names are on the list.

So the riches of the man who says “I am a God” are not a blessing to reach for. Whoever gains his world gets it by trading away his soul, and the Lord has already said he will bring the terrible of the nations upon that man and bring him down to the pit.

Ezekiel says the prince of Tyrus got his riches “By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick”. Traffic means trade. Revelation 6 shows the same man and how he runs the trade of the world: “And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third beast say, Come and see.” This third beast, this powerful angel, says to John, I am going to show you something.

“And I beheld, and lo a black horse”. The black horse represents the dark nations that Esau is over. This whole chapter deals with Esau's rulership, from the white horse to the red horse, and now the black horse. “and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand”: the white man sitting on the black horse, holding a pair of balances, a scale of right and wrong weight and measure.

“A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny”. Who dictates how much wheat should cost worldwide? It is America: their World Bank, their IMF. They control the economy of the world. They are the ones that say Jamaica's money is no good, Sierra Leone's money is no good, Haiti's money is garbage. Yet those countries have all the resources, and America doesn't. But might makes right: America has the military arsenal, so all nations have to shut the hell up. “and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine”: see thou, meaning do not deal unjustly.

So verses 5 and 6 are the IMF and the World Bank, the world economy. That is the “great wisdom” and “traffick” of Ezekiel 28 by which the prince increased his riches and lifted up his heart. And don't let America tell you it is broke: its debt is in its own money, and it prints its own money. How can you owe yourself?

Habakkuk describes the man who “transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man”. The wine he transgresses by is his Christianity and his democracy, which are virtually the same thing: his policies, his religions, his politics. Obadiah names the proud man: “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”.

“We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” Someone is going to rise up among the nations and say, let's go against America, let's go against Israel in battle. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.”

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”. Edom is the prideful man. They come from the Caucasus Mountains and dwelt in the clefts of the rock through the Middle Ages; in Obadiah's time it was the place called Petra today, and look at the architecture, just like Rome, just like Washington D.C. Their high habitation now is their skyscrapers. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say that you have to have power: they are saying nobody can beat us.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. Their symbol is the eagle: take out your dollar bill. Who is sending satellites and doing space travel? America. So Edom is not the Arabs: the Arabs are not doing space travel, and their symbol is not the eagle. Nor is it the American Indian, who uses the eagle, because if they had had power they would have blown the white man off the face of the earth. People throw these things out to confuse the new converts.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” That began when the truth started to come out in the 1960s. And Habakkuk shows how: he “neither keepeth at home”, a busybody in every nation, destabilising country after country by economic or conventional war and gathering the residue of those peoples to America and England. “Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee”: terrorism from within, slowly but surely, “Because thou hast spoiled many nations”.

“Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength.” Jehovah has three syllables, and there is no J in Hebrew, so what was there originally is Yah-ha-wah, three syllables: not Jehovah, and not Yahweh, which is two. Then Christ gives us a heavy secret about who that Lord is.

“Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” He is letting them know he is the I AM of Exodus: “And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” That is Christ. He is saying, that Yah you were praying to, that was me back then.

Philip said, “Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” And Christ answered, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” You want to see the Father that created you? I am the Father that created you. Isaiah calls the child that is born and the son that is given “The mighty God, The everlasting Father.” And John says, “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.”

Now we know Christ is not the Father. But the God that was dealing with us in the Old Testament was Christ; that is why he said he comes in the volume of the book, and it is written of him. He is the only begotten of the Father: the Father only created Christ, and then said, this is your world, you create it. Proverbs 8 speaks of it, how he was daily the Father's delight, brought up with him.

So the Lord Jehovah of Isaiah 26, who “bringeth down them that dwell on high” and lays the lofty city low even to the dust, is Christ. They get mad online and say stop misleading the people, but that is the God in whom is everlasting strength, the one we are to trust for ever.

“Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.” The only time we cry to the Lord is when we are chastised; as Hosea says, “in their affliction they will seek me early.” Isaiah 59 is that cry.

“Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness.” Obscurity is confusion. “We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes.” Black people and Latin people act as if we have no eyes. We see the evil, and then we say, some of them are good, they ain't all like that.

“We stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men”: we are like the walking dead. “We roar all like bears”: that is us crying and screaming in the streets, “and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us. For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us.”

“And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” The judgment we seek in this wicked kingdom is always turned backward, and the truth of God fails out here.

We are watching it on the screen. Young Black men found hanging from trees in Charlotte, Albany, Oakland, Albuquerque, Brookfield, Marietta, and on the campus of Delta State with the back of his head smashed in, every one ruled a suicide with no foul play. Keith Porter shot by an off-duty ICE agent on New Year's Eve; Dr. Linda Davis killed by a driver fleeing ICE. A sixteen-year-old boy in Houston shot on a porch while holding up a wallet he was trying to return, the shooter released, and the boy's family ordered to pay $20,000. No justice, no peace.

We had sixty years of a little liberty that Esau gave us, and we could have done astronomical things, but we dropped the ball. We wanted to sin and be like the other nations, twerking and dancing while the Bible warned us. Now the white man is undoing it, done pretending he is not the devil, and the hangings of the '40s and '50s are starting all over again. So be careful with your children. That is why we cry now: because of our sins.

Revelation 20 says whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. So who is written in the book of life? Is it the Chinese, the white man, or the Arabs? Daniel answers.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time.” That is the indignation of Isaiah 26, when God's people must “enter thou into thy chambers” and hide “until the indignation be overpast.” There will be so much devastation that we will be fearful.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” Who is written in the book of life? Israel, Daniel's people. Not everybody.

Jeremiah says the same, and they hate this one: “Fear thou not, O Jacob my servant, saith the Lord: for I am with thee; for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee: but I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure; yet will I not leave thee wholly unpunished.” God is correcting us in measure, but he will not destroy us.

And Ezra: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.” All the nations were born in vain; the Israelites are the grape and the plant that is kept. So when the Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, Israel written in the book is delivered, and all the nations go into the lake of fire.

“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.” Revelation 20 shows that day of judgment.

“And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them.” That is Christ, in full power, and nobody opens their damn mouth against him. We thought it was the Father judging us, but it is Christ: “we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.” And “the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son.”

“And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened”: this is everybody, and the books are the Bible. “And another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” As Ecclesiastes says, “God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” We are judged according to our works, whether we were in God's laws or against God's laws.

“And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them.” That is what Isaiah 26 said: the earth shall no more cover her slain. Hell is the grave; those that died in the graves were given up, “and they were judged every man according to their works.”

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.” Death is finished at that point. And what goes with death and hell? The nations: “whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” That includes all the nations. The Lord comes out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth, and this is where that punishment ends.

“And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. The merchants are the corporations that make major deals with countries. The gold, silver and precious stones come this way by ship in those big containers, and the majority of what is listed comes from the continent of Africa. Then: “and slaves”: that was you and me. “And souls of men”: you want a piece of the pie, you have to sell your soul. There are things you must do.

Ecclesiasticus says it: “Why is earth and ashes proud?” Earth and ashes represents man; why is man proud? “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man”. They covet what does not belong to them. blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-marriage:
“But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom's identity. It was synonymous with him: his hair, his physical perfection.

And what came behind that? Ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself and you start to believe certain things. Absalom rose up against his father, it came to civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the same thing that was vanity to him.

That is the same lesson as David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. David saw a woman “very beautiful to look upon”, he saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem with Dinah. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house the rest of his days. The Lord forgave him, but he left him with drama for moving that way. Then Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty, came to pride and rebellion.

Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows you that trouble comes behind it. Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage: she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that is the only thing you are moving on.

This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

Paul praises the brethren that they “keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.” Then he gives the summary of the order: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.”

This is the same order as Ephesians 5:23: “the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” The woman’s list of duties may look longer, but the man’s responsibilities carry much more weight, because he is the one that is accountable. A sister’s accountability is for herself; the husband is accountable for her, the house, the children and the nation. He is the saviour of the body. Does that not deserve honour?

When marriage is grounded in the order God established, love becomes stronger. The passion and the joy come, not romance, which is a new modern term, but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. Marriage mirrors Christ and the Israelites, and prophecy is not entertainment: it is a sign for us to correct ourselves and get things in order, individually and as a people.

Paul says plainly: “But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh.” Marriage is no sin, but there will be trouble in it. Every marriage meets conflict.

How a couple deals with that trouble depends on the expectations they carried into it. Scripture does not define marriage by feelings; it defines it by function. Marriage originated with God. Culture later added the ceremonies, made it a business, and put unrealistic expectations on it. The traditions may carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. That is the modern confusion: putting feelings in front of function.

So the trouble in the flesh is expected, and it is met with the order of Ephesians 5: the husband as the head who gives himself for the wife, the wife submitting “as unto the Lord.” Marriage is meant to function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

“A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.” The Bible calls for peace in the marriage: not war, not strife, not enmity, not division, not variance.

This is how the trouble in the flesh of 1 Corinthians 7:28 is handled. The wife focuses on rejoicing her husband through reverence, and then he stands in his integrity, because there is peace in the household. Peace, not passion. Peace, not feelings.

That reverence is what Ephesians 5:33 asks: “the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Reverence is beyond respect. It is a profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, that manifests as obedience and submission. It cannot be done as a job description; it has to come from the heart, and if a sister does not have that spirit she has to pray for it. When it comes from genuine respect and a desire to please the Lord, she will not be derelict in her duties, and the house has peace.

“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

Christ said “ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled”, and “the end is not yet”. Ezra shows what the end involves, and it is not here yet.

“Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” That is the Arabs, Ishmael, the wild men.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”: the Carmanians are Iran. “And with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”: join battle with the Arab nations. “And shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians”, over on that side of the earth.

When it says waste a portion, it is dealing with nukes, and it is dealing with unity: Iran and the Arab nations together. Right now neither of those things is present. So what you are seeing is contractions. It is extremely significant and we should not sleep on it, but it is the beginning of sorrows.

That is why we are not troubled. We do not sleep as others do; like a team moving ten yards at a time down the field, we see ourselves moving toward the goal every time these things happen. It should only trouble you if you are not in the right spirit to move with urgency and repent.

“And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” Things are going to get so crazy in the earth that the Lord has to move events forward. Shortened means events will accelerate.

That is what the similitude of a woman in travail goes into: there are times of contraction, then a time of relief from it. But never forget that every contraction means you are being inched closer, moved another ten yards down the field. It is an acceleration of events, just as the prophets described.

So what we are actually witnessing is the stage being set. Do not think what is happening over there is insignificant by any measure. For Iran and the Arabs to be united the way the prophecy says, certain steps have to happen, and it may seem far off; but the Lord can put spirit on men to move things along quicker, shortening the days and increasing the speed of those events.

Christ did not give dates and times, because much depends on when we are sealed, when the 144,000 and the other pieces are in place. Prophecy is not meant to entertain us; it is meant to correct us. The more signs we see, the more urgently we should be repenting, correcting our lives and strengthening our households to prepare for those days. “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you”: Jacob's trouble is not here yet, but it can escalate quickly on the Lord's timeline.

“The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.” Why are they blessed? Because he raised a stable, sound household. The other purpose of marriage is “Be fruitful, and multiply”: marriage is nation building, and that implies children if you are able. Psalms 127 explains why.

“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.” The house is the house of marriage, the foundation of it, and by extension Israel as a people. That is why it is so important to handle this right: if you let the world build the house, you are going to get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people.

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Why put yourself in a situation and then say woe is me, I am miserable in my marriage, full of sorrows, as if you had no control, power or authority, and as if God were not on your side to fix it?

He did not randomly decide to talk about children; he started with building a house. “Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” That is how we carry on. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.” If the just man walks in his integrity, his children are in good condition.

“Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed.” They are not ashamed because you raised them godly, and it is not only what you tell them but what they see and experience in you as an example. “but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate”: that is the purpose. They follow behind you and fill your shoes, to point out the evils of our oppressors, to point out the evils of our people, and to give them the hope of salvation that they know not.

So the children of the just man are blessed after him because of Psalms 127: the Lord built the house, and the man kept his integrity in it.

Sirach praises “A shamefaced and faithful woman”, “the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house”, and “the fair feet with a constant heart.” Beauty is functional, not sexualized. Order equals beauty, sisters. Wives who neglect the home for other things are out of order and out of alignment with God’s will. The home is your first priority above all things, starting with your husband and then your children.

Titus spells out that order: “That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.” Keepers at home is what the ordering of her house goes into. It teaches them to love their husbands, and sums it up: obedient to their own husbands.

“That the word of God be not blasphemed.” If y’all are not applying this, sisters, you are blasphemous. And you think God will look past it, and at the judgment seat you will say, but my husband did this, my husband did that? He will say, that is blasphemy; that was the man I gave you.

If submission depends on how he treats you, it is not submission; it is manipulation. God told you to submit to your husband in everything, with no caveat. Proverbs 31 without genuine submission is decoration on a house with a weak foundation. Be soft, respectful and quiet; it is not your job to fix his issues but to make sure you are right.

This is the biblical model: complementary responsibilities. The woman’s list seems longer, but the man’s carries more weight. He is the head of the wife as Christ is head of the church, the savior of the body, accountable for you, the house, the children and the nation. Your accountability is only for yourself. Does that not deserve honor?

Tobias prayed, “mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” To age together is the long, intertwined journey of partners growing old side by side: shared history, mutual support through life's changes, companionship, and facing life's challenges as a team. Aged means refined, like wine or cheese.

Then Solomon: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity”. There's your romance. Live joyfully: that's part of the aging. “all the days of the life of thy vanity”, because we are here just for a fleeting moment, seventy or eighty years at best. All the days God gives you, you should live joyfully with your wife. That's a commandment.

“for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” This is how things are supposed to be set up. If you want to navigate this world the right way, you have to navigate your marriage this way.

So the joy is not the foundation; it grows out of it. Everything else has to be established first, or the romance will be fleeting and break the foundation of the scriptures. Tobias took his wife uprightly, and the living joyfully comes in the aging together.

You want passion in the relationship? Here it is: “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.”

Ravished is not a regular word: it means to fill someone with intense delight and rapture. Delight, charm, enthral, captivate, spellbind, bewitch, fascinate. That goes into the power a woman has in her voice and her conversation. There's your passion, there's your romance, after the foundation of your marriage is set up correctly and you age together.

But that can't exist if the other, divine parts of the marriage are not set up correctly; it's not going to happen. You don't seek this first. It's like looking for furniture, things for the walls, carpet and rugs, when you haven't even bought the house yet and don't know if the walls will hold or the foundation is strong. That's how we treat marriage nowadays.

Tobias did it in the right order: “I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly”. The being ravished always with her love comes after that foundation, as the fruit of it.

Tobias prayed, and Sara “said with him, Amen.” She agreed, because her mind was on her lord; she didn't say, wait, what about the house, what about the gifts. Sirach gives more insight into the character that strengthens marriage: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

A man and a wife that agree together. The agreement is not that you both like the same music, the same colors, the same food; that's part of the aging stuff. The agreement is this: she agrees to follow the scriptures that pertain to her as a wife, whether or not there are contingencies, because the Bible gives no contingencies for a wife's behavior. You do or you don't. And he agrees to do the same as a husband.

You agree in God that you are going to follow his order of marriage, running it with your responsibilities as a wife and yours as a husband the way the Bible says. That is what is beautiful in God's eyes, because it will work the way he intended when you do those things.

“Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.” Virtuous deals with her character. Look how everything gets better in the marriage when the wife moves in that spirit; a virtuous wife brings peace. Tobias asked God that he and his wife might become aged together, and a virtuous wife doubles those days.

“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” She honors him by agreeing to follow what the Lord says; that's the honor. A woman that honors her husband equals wisdom for the woman. But not how you think: you measure it against the scripture and ask, am I fulfilling all of these things? Pride is what breaks the submission.

When Titus says to teach the women to love their husbands, we have taken it for years as surface emotions. A man experiences love through respect; that is the chief love language of a man. Why does he like being around the brothers so much? Because he's respected among his peers. If the wife reverences him, he'll feel the love, and everything else falls into place behind it.

And not forced respect. It has to come from a sincere place. If you have to remember and remind yourself to respect your husband, you're not in submission. If you really desire your husband and see him as he is, not through a warped worldly view, it will come out of you innately, and watch what will come out of him innately.

Tobias prayed, “Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay”, and “let us make unto him an aid like unto himself.” Sirach says the same: “He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession, a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest.”

Marriage describes partnership and support, plain and simple. Not a rom-com romantic movie, not a novella or a soap opera. A help like unto himself, a pillar of rest.

What do you see in those words? Stability and wisdom over emotional intensity. We have to stop emphasizing the wrong thing. The emotional intensity comes as a byproduct of those things.

The Bible shows men taking wives: he took a wife, he got a possession. That is the foundation Tobias laid in his prayer, a helper and stay from whom came mankind, a nation, and it is what we must get back to.
