This kingdom will go down. It will pass away just like everything else. “And they that use this world, as not abusing it: for the fashion of this world passeth away.” You can use the things of this world, but do not get caught up. Do not hit the snooze button, do not abuse it, and do not lean on the things of this world over Christ.

If we really believe this Bible, we know the things of this world are going to pass away, and that fear should kick in on its own. Someone should not always have to check you. You read the Bible just like the next man. We understand young spirits, but eventually, as you walk, you check yourself.

You should become skilful in the word of God. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.” If wisdom is walking with you, if Christ is in you, by default you become skilful in the word and in how to apply wisdom in certain situations. You embody Christ, and everybody can see wisdom walking with you.

So the things seen are temporal and the fashion of this world passes away, while the things not seen are eternal. Use the world lightly and hold fast to wisdom.

“for the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary. They are not going to last forever, so there is no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. The United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall, thus saith the Lord. Now we have to put our focus on overcoming the beast.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. Anybody in this war against evil does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Who chose us? Our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ. He chose us to be soldiers in his military.

When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold. Who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? It is not to boast; it is just the reality.

So a soldier keeps his eyes on what is not seen. We do not see the kingdom right now, but the Lord lets us know it will last forever. The Lord is doing his job; it is time for us to do ours.

“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God. That is exactly what sin does. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthly tabernacle is our flesh. We were born and shapen in iniquity, so understand the condition of the battle: we will fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people think that when they come into the truth, things will just go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, not wearing fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness do not go away. You learn how to cope with them, and you have to prove yourself to the Lord that you are able to keep that Negro in check, that Latino in check.

“and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”. We do not have a lot of time left. Now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here. We are not worried about the war in Iran; God already has that. We need to worry about the war on the day-to-day.

That is looking at the things which are not seen: running the race with patience toward the eternal, not weighed down by the temporal.

“the things which are not seen are eternal” We do not see the kingdom yet, but it will last forever. So we have to stack our bricks, and we cannot be situational Israelites. We have to be in the spirit and move in the spirit, knowing our eternal home awaits us. It is a spiritual battle, a spiritual war.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We have to change by the renewing of our minds, because we are now new creatures in Christ. The mindset has to change.

Those things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world, in this day and age, cannot keep doing it. If you feel Satan raising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that.

That is what it means to look not at the things which are seen. The world presses its pop culture and pleasures on us, but a mind renewed stays fixed on the eternal kingdom rather than conforming to a power that is about to fall.

The Lord says, “I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction. For wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth”. How did wickedness come to pollute the whole earth? Esau. Malachi calls Edom the border of wickedness, and since the time of the Greeks that wickedness has grown and grown.

After Alexander the Greek died, “they all put crowns upon themselves; so did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.” That is the spread of it: from the Greeks all the way up until today. Do not forget the Romans, Spain, France, Germany, Great Britain, Russia and the United States of America. Each put crowns on themselves, their sons after them, and evils were multiplied.

That is why “their hurtful works are fulfilled”, and why the plagues are coming on the world. Every nation on the face of the earth has been affected by that line of kingdoms, now by America, by Edom. The whole world is defiled because of it.

The earth is under much wickedness, in gross darkness. Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise: awake to righteousness; it is time to wake up out of that deep sleep. Shine: that is going out to teach, letting your light shine, teaching God's commandments. Our light is Christ.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. The darkness covering the earth is the nations: every nation is affected by the United States of America, by Edom, and the whole world is defiled because of this nation. And because of that, the Israelites have been affected: gross darkness the people, God's people.

Then: “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The Lord is still going to arise upon us, because he is still going to choose Israel and have mercy on his people: the ones who want to stop sinning, not the ones who take advantage of God's grace and mercy. His glory shall be seen upon his people.

The earth is polluted with wickedness, and Babylon is at the center of it. “How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.”

America really thinks it will never have to pay for its crimes. So if you are sitting in your sins thinking, as Amos 9:10 says, that no harm is going to come to you, you have a characteristic of Edom, the same characteristic as Esau. If we want deliverance, why would we have that mentality? We cannot get salvation unless she is destroyed. So if you want to remain in your sins, you want America to continue.

This is for the brothers and sisters you barely ever see, because they always have something more important than the truth; the ones who fade, and nobody hears from them. This is a gut check, so you can get your mind right. Some of you have embodied the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off.

A lot of us look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman and are mesmerized. But she is the mother of harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute does not mean you are not out there dealing with harlots. She lives deliciously and thinks she will see no sorrow, but so much torment and sorrow will be given her. Come out of her.

The first author of beauty is our God, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.”

Comely means beautiful, handsome. That is how the Lord looks at his people: the daughter of Zion is a comely and delicate woman in his eyes.

That is why he says in 2 Esdras that “the innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me”, that “my people is led as a flock to the slaughter”, and that he will surely avenge them. All the murders and injustice done to God's children here in spiritual Egypt are done to the daughter he likened to a comely and delicate woman, and he will not suffer them to dwell in that Egypt any more.

The Lord likened the daughter of Zion to a comely woman, yet Jeremiah laments: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!”

The Lord cast the beauty of Israel down from heaven, from rulership, to the earth, to servitude. Why would he do that? Because we went off. We went away from the author who created us. That is why you would look to another nation for its beauty.

But God is letting you know he is the author, the creator of beauty. And America, that you think is beautiful, really is not beautiful. Under the skirt she is a worn-out harlot: you think she is beautiful, then you realize she has been with everyone on the block.

You went against your God. So now, knowing that, we have to return. We have to return back to the author of our beauty, so that he will avenge us and bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

The beauty of Israel was cast down because we left our God, so now we have to return. David shows how: “Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” We have to love righteousness and hate iniquity.

“All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces”, and “upon thy right hand did stand the queen in gold of Ophir.”

“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. The Lord says listen up. Just like a marriage, sisters, you have to focus on your lord. The Lord does not want to share us with anybody else; he wants us to focus on him and him only.

“So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.” When we get ourselves right, turn back to the Lord, love righteousness and hate iniquity, he will desire our beauty, the way he created it. And we worship him and him only, not the beauty of Egypt.

Ezra says the Lord will not suffer his people “now to dwell in the land of Egypt”, but will “smite Egypt with plagues, as before”. As before means this is not ancient Egypt; it is a coming Egypt, the United States of America. When it comes, we don't want to go down with it. So why would our people love this Egypt? Because of her beauty.

Wisdom answers: “With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.”

The first author of beauty is our God. Real beauty is not the Statue of Liberty; that is not real beauty. Only virgins are really beautiful. God is the creator of beauty, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman, as Jeremiah 6:2 shows.

So in this Passover season, get your mind right and remove the leaven. Do not be delighted with the beauty of Egypt and take her for a god. Know how much better the Lord is, who made the beauty.

Amos says, “All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” That is what God said is going to happen, and there is nothing you can do to delay or undo it. So we have to come out of the beast; we have to come out of that mentality. Jeremiah says, “Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul”.

Flee out of Babylon can be physical. That day may come when we have to go to different lands: some of us will be exiles, some will be deported, and sometimes you may have to go to the next city or somewhere else to keep this gospel moving. But it is also spiritual: we have to flee out of the ways of the beast now.

“Deliver every man his soul”: the soul is the real you, underneath this sinful flesh, and the Lord is telling us to deliver it. That means letting go of the things we are accustomed to here. We cannot be like Lot's wife, who looked back and became a part of the Lord's sacrifice.

The Lord is giving us the place, the time and the opportunity to get ourselves right, but the day of the Lord is approaching regardless. Some carry the spirit of those who say the evil shall not overtake them: I am an Israelite, I don't have to worry, the Lord will give me mercy. We cannot roll in that mentality. If you fall, get back up immediately, because that mindset has this future. We are in the midst of a spiritual war, and we have to meditate on these things constantly, get our minds right and stay steadfast until the end.

Christ likens the kingdom to leaven hid in three measures of meal “till the whole was leavened.” Leaven grows. Paul shows the other side of that same truth: “Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if you allow it to remain amongst other Israelites, that leaven is going to spread and defile others.

So the command is “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge out the leaven within our own spirits and within our various congregations. God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming, if you don't keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly.

“For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ was sacrificed for us, so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness and stop it.

“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out. And people who have been with us, who saw it happen before, still fall for it. We have to fight. Don't play into Satan's devices.

He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters, not doing anything right. Satan has you right where he wants you.

We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, and the reason is that they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught. That is how the leaven gets in and spreads.

“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day”. How often? Daily. Exhortation can't take place if you're not around nobody. The Bible is telling us what to do: stay around each other, stay around the righteous daily.

“lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin”. Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver, because you think you can get that feeling constantly. You can't; it's temporal, only for a certain amount of time. If we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

2 Thessalonians 2 shows it. “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the workings of Satan, making you think God is with them, and it's time to come up out of the beast and separate. “And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They loved their pleasures more than God, deceived by the pleasures of sin. “And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion”. You can be deceived by sin so bad you may never recover your soul: still alive, still living, but a dead soul and a dead spirit. Be very mindful.

“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven. Christ was the leader, and when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen. He knew what he was talking about.

The disciples “reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about bread. He reminded them of “the five loaves of the five thousand” and “the seven loaves of the four thousand”: it's not about the bread, pay attention. They couldn't receive it at that time, until “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The leaven is their doctrine and their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in the things they do: they say and do not, they are hypocrites.

And the Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but when you see a spirit on someone who can influence you negatively, beware. It's up to you to listen, but the best thing is to follow, listen and consider the end of their conversation. Be very, very mindful.

This tends to happen every year around the Passover, and this is a call to wake some up so they can get their mind right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”. When you notice that your study habits have changed, when you notice that you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has now set in. You are regressing, going backwards.

“and his heart is turned away from his Maker”. That sin, that leaven, is now blinding you, so that you can no longer see clearly. That is the leaven spreading through the whole lump: it starts small, with a pulling back, and grows until the heart is turned away from the Most High.

Some don't want to be taught, and Sirach says why: “He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you; you will not be taught, you will not retain it, it's not going to work for you.

“but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”. That wisdom is seeing it your own way, doing your own thing, and you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

Sirach 3:26 shows that bitterness: “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”. You're stubborn and don't want to learn; when wise words come out you're in the back, or you've got that hatred, something against somebody, so you don't want to hear nothing from them. And “he that loveth danger shall perish therein”. People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, because they are unwise and not taught, because fools despise knowledge.

“Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” That escape from corruption is the purging of iniquity in Proverbs 16:6, and it has to be kept up.

“And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.” We have to be diligent. We cannot just come in here knowing that Christ is black, God is black and the angels are black. When we come through these doors we have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just be in you, but be in you and grow. “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Meaning you do not have to be purged out. If you can do that, you do not have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you are constantly growing and doing the Lord’s will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind.” Sin has blinded you. You cannot think straight, you cannot do what is common sense, you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people and you love that pleasure more than God. He “cannot see afar off”: you cannot see that America is going to be destroyed and that salvation is coming. You are a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

He “hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you do not keep trimming, if you do not keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

The beast has “upon his heads the name of blasphemy”, and “he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven”: the Most High, Christ and the angels. That is what they do: they lie against God’s people and God himself. “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.”

Look at the Tomahawk missile that hit the elementary school in Minab, Iran, killing 175 people, mostly children. First they blamed Iran; then they said it was a mistake from outdated targeting data; then Trump said, I don’t know about it. Don’t listen for one second to these liars.

Ezekiel 28:3 answers them: “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee”. What was Daniel able to do? Interpret dreams. America is able to interpret your next move, because they have that kind of surveillance and technological capability. The Bible prophesied it.

So if there is no secret that can be hid from America, according to God, how did they mistakenly hit a school and think it was part of a base? It was no mistake. It shows you they are crooks and liars, the beast with a mouth speaking blasphemies. And to our people still asleep and following behind the beast, even a ranking man among us who re-enlisted in the army in the middle of Bible prophecy, knowing he will be deployed: come up out of this foolishness.

The beast of Revelation 13 rises out of the sea “having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns”. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets, the EU, and on the military side NATO, now over thirty nations.

Revelation 12:3 shows the same creature: “And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” This heaven is rulership: who would be leading the earth, the world superpower, in the latter days. So the beast is also the red dragon, and red is the key indicator of who this is.

Genesis 25:25 tells you: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Then “after that came his brother out”, with no description at all. Why? Because Jacob looked just like everybody else; everybody at that time had dark pigmentation. Esau was different, so he had to be described.

So the great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns is Esau, and the beast in power in the latter days is America, of the seven because the Americans came over here from Great Britain, with the ten horns giving their power and strength to it.

Zephaniah speaks of the decree; Peter shows it will not fail: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”. What the Lord said is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord does not want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he will not put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. How is that possible? By nuclear fire: the same burning with fire the ten horns bring on the whore.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? That goes to Deacon Yashua’s point. Should we sit with the popcorn just watching? Eating popcorn is not a sin, with a little butter and salt. But if that is all you are doing and you are not applying, that is when it becomes an issue.

This is not the time to kick our feet up or bug out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before and to increase in righteousness.

The ten horns “have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” That is NATO, formed in 1949, with America at the front. But things are changing. France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for oil through the Strait of Hormuz; Canada says it will never take part in the offensive; Germany warns against an endless war; Spain has withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. They agreed to give their power to the beast, and now they are looking out for themselves.

So as Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not only here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand our salvation is getting closer. “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us do not recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies and us being saved from their hands. How fitting that the high holy day comes in a time like this. So we have to increase our focus and buckle down; we are in the midst of war, and our minds should not be in other places.

As Deacon Yashua in Phoenix said last Sabbath: prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

“And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” Over time something will cause these kings to hate the whore, the United States of America. Trump badmouths NATO for not paying their fees and threatens to end the alliance, and now they don’t want to be drawn into a long war. They will make her desolate and naked with intercontinental ballistic missiles.

But before that comes, we have to achieve abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity. Zephaniah says: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The nation not desired is us. They call us minorities and put labels on us, blacks, Hispanics, derogatory terms wherever we are: the Dalits in India, the Afro-Iranians, the Afro-Palestinians. Wherever we are scattered we are hated and despised. But the Bible says gather together. It is all about Israelite unity, and that is what they have always feared, because if the Israelites unify, that is the end of this wicked regime.

They even lie about Amalek. Bibi Netanyahu and his crew are the Amalekites according to the Bible, so to deflect that history they call the Iranians, the Persians, present-day Amalek.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”. The decree is already made; it is prophesied, and destruction is coming. So take heed, acknowledge it, and get yourselves right.

“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.” Many of you look at America as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you are mesmerized. In America you can have every kind of pleasure. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you are not picking up a prostitute doesn’t mean you aren’t out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots. And remember, sin is pleasurable.

Paul describes the last days: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection”: some like young minors, some like people of the same sex. “Trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good.” I don’t like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he is doing something. What, teaching the word of God? We have spirits like that sitting among us, worried about petty things while this truth is trying to get us out of here.

“Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That is a big issue. If you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord’s work as much. Everybody asks, what’s wrong with that brother’s spirit? He loves his lust more than God.

That is what it means to stumble at the beauty of the woman and desire her for pleasure: to love America’s pleasures more than God. The brothers and sisters who fade away, this is your gut check.

“Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations.” Contextually this is spoken to the king of Tyrus, who was said to be wiser than Daniel. But when you read the scriptures, a passage may speak contextually of one nation and prophetically of another, because the Lord shows “the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” Prophetically, this is Babylon the Great, America.

Who are the strangers, the terrible of the nations? The Allahu Akbar type strangers. Another word for it would be terrorists. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom.” A lot of people thought America could never be touched. The Lord is showing you otherwise. When she begins to fall, she will be destroyed from the inside out, decaying, and then comes the great finale with the ten horns.

“And they shall defile thy brightness.” America likes to put on as if she is righteous, playing the moral world police, while she goes into countries, steals presidents and bombs everybody. That brightness will be defiled.

So don’t stumble at her beauty. The beauty of her wisdom and her brightness are exactly what the Lord has marked for the sword.

Don’t stumble at the beauty of the woman, America, or desire her for pleasure. Moses shows the way: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.” He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God had chosen him for a mighty work, to deliver his people out of captivity.

Some of y’all say, it’s not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions. Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some of you have nice jobs and status in America. So you can’t say it’s because of that. Moses gave it all up; why can’t you?

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” For a season means it is temporary. It is only here for so long, and then destruction and salvation. That is the mindset we have to have.

We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings get you killed. Choose affliction with the people of God over the passing pleasures of Babylon.

The class is The Beauty and the Beast, and this is the beauty. When sin takes over, you can’t see clearly. Isaiah says: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency.” That is how they perceive her, and how many of our people see America.

But you shouldn’t look at America like that. When you see the Statue of Liberty, you shouldn’t say, God bless America. Some of y’all feel real proud seeing things like that. When I first looked at it, I saw seven crowns on her head and ten toes, and I said, wow, the Bible is a true book. Not, Lady Liberty, I love you. The Bible is spot on.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” This place is going to be destroyed. You shouldn’t be sitting there gazing at her and mesmerized by her pleasures. You know this place is coming to an end. Wake up. Don’t stumble at her beauty.

Sirach warns not to stumble at the beauty of a woman, and the Lord calls this nation a harlot. Nahum says: “Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts.” The well-favoured harlot: some of you are caught up with her. I hope it isn’t a lot of you.

“That selleth nations through her whoredoms.” She sells nations. They sold us; that is how we got over here. “And families through her witchcrafts.”

Meaning what? If you are down with America, you are down with the devil. That is what the Bible is telling us. Nahum saw the same thing John the Revelator saw: the judgment of the great harlot that sits upon many waters, and upon her forehead “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” An abomination is something the Lord hates and despises.

So her beauty is the beauty of a harlot and a witch that sold us. Desire her not for pleasure.

She says in her heart, “I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.” Some of y’all have taken on the characteristics of America, and it is time to shake that off. She is “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH”, and an abomination is what the Lord hates and despises. So it is time to come up out of her.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

That ye receive not of her plagues, because the Lord is still sending plagues. Y’all remember the pandemic. Stay with the Lord and come up out of her spiritually, so that her condemnation is not your condemnation.

That is what it means not to stumble at the beauty of the woman: don’t be mesmerized by her or desire her for pleasure, but come out of her, because her judgment is coming.

The lion is Christ, roaring on his prey and coming up from his thicket as the destroyer of the Gentiles. Ezra saw the same lion: “And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”.

This eagle is America. The roaring lion sending his voice unto the eagle is Christ roaring against America, bringing destruction.

So when the destruction that wasteth at noonday comes on America, the Lord is the mighty protection of them that love him, a defence from heat and a cover from the sun at noon, while he roars against the eagle and fights for mount Zion.

Christ is returning with clouds, with his chariots and the multitude of angels. Habakkuk saw it: “When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself”. Why did he tremble? Because Habakkuk was put in it. He felt it; he saw it.

He trembled “that I might rest in the day of trouble: when he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” When Christ comes up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops, the angels.

That is the day of trouble in which the Lord is the mighty protection and strong stay of them that love him. The prophet trembled at what he saw, but those who fear the Lord will rest in that day.

“For thus hath the Lord spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. What is this talking about? The Lion of the tribe of Judah in Revelation 5:5: Christ.

And “when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.” The Lord is going to fight for his people.

“As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem”. As birds flying is Christ and the angels. And “defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.” Passing over: this is the Passover season, and just as he passed over us in Egypt, he will pass over and preserve his people.

That is what it means that his eyes are upon them that love him and he is their mighty protection. He comes down as a roaring lion to fight for mount Zion and defend Jerusalem.

The lion that roars on his prey is Christ, and Jeremiah shows him coming: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”. This is twofold. It was talking about Nebuchadnezzar contextually, but prophetically it is talking about Jesus the Christ. He's coming.

And “he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.” He comes forth from his place to make the land of the Gentiles desolate, their cities laid waste without inhabitants.

So while the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, and he is their defence from the heat of that destruction.

“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon”. God's eyes are on them that love him, and he is our mighty protection if we love him. A defence from what heat? Nuclear heat. And why a cover from the sun at noon? Because the destruction comes at noonday.

David shows it: “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The destruction wastes at noonday.

So all we have to do is be faithful and fear him, and he will protect us from the destruction to come. Sirach says the same of wisdom: “By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.” By wisdom we shall be covered from the heat.

The nations will be amazed at the strangeness of the salvation of the righteous, “so far beyond all that they looked for”, when those chariots come. John shows those chariots: “Behold, he cometh with clouds”. He is coming with clouds, and those clouds are his chariots.

And “every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.” Christ is returning with the multitude of angels, and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.

That is the day the Lord is “a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon” for them that love him: when every eye sees him coming, the righteous stand in boldness while the kindreds of the earth wail.

Isaiah says the Lord will come down to fight for mount Zion “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. Who is that lion? John shows it: “And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

That lion is Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David. He is the one roaring on his prey, not afraid of the voice of the multitude of shepherds called against him, coming down with his angels as birds flying to defend Jerusalem. He is the mighty protection of them that love him.

The Lord is a defence from heat for them that love him, and in that day they will stand. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” Why does he stand in boldness? Because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. When the nations see it they will be troubled, saying, what the hell is this? They “shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They cannot imagine it; they will not be able to fathom what is taking place when those chariots come.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints!”

The ones who mocked and afflicted the righteous will see him numbered among the children of God, protected while they are not.

“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Who is this wisdom we are to seek? Christ is also known as wisdom: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

So when Sirach speaks of wisdom exalting her children, and when Proverbs has wisdom saying “By me princes rule”, it is Christ speaking. The Lord is the one who sets up all the kings and all the princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God by whom they rule.

To seek wisdom is to seek Christ. Those who seek him are the ones wisdom lays hold of, and the children she exalts are the ones he calls: the called, both Jews and Greeks.

We have to be like Solomon: we have to pray for wisdom so that we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”, and at Gibeon “the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.”

Solomon answered, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, set in the midst of “a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.” “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”. As a youth, Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom.

“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” Because he “hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies”, God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.” And more: “I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave Solomon things he did not ask for because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek ye first the kingdom of heaven and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of Solomon’s book: wisdom exalted him because he sought her.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If we lack wisdom, go to the source: go to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.

Sirach shows how wisdom deals with the one who seeks her: “For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” When we come into this truth we are not right, so wisdom walks with us in our crooked ways, and the Lord will jack us up because we are not doing it right; but wisdom will still be there. “Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There is no cap on wisdom.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That is the key: you have to believe. “But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we must build our faith. And “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” We have to increase our study as we see the days approaching, and continue to converse in the scriptures.

How do we seek wisdom? Wisdom answers in Proverbs: “By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.” The Lord sets up all the kings and princes on the earth, and Christ is the wisdom of God.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you are not seeking him, he does not love you. “and those that seek me early shall find me.” We have a chance right now, in the midst of these wars and rumours of wars: we have to seek the Lord early, right now.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” Riches and honour are with Christ. Durable riches are not temporal, not temporary; they last a long time, forever, eternal. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”

That is how wisdom exalts her children and lays hold of them that seek her: she loves those who love her, she is found by those who seek her early, and she gives them lasting riches and righteousness.

“Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him. They are wisdom’s children.

Isaiah shows what that pity does: “for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children.” The Lord will fight those who fought against us, and he will save our children, because wisdom exalts her children.

He does it through Christ: “behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH”, and “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That is what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

And the end of it is in Revelation: “the accuser of our brethren is cast down”, and “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome by the blood of the Lamb; we must have faith and continue to be faithful, loving righteousness more than iniquity. The Father pities his children who fear him, and exalts them.

Solomon tells it himself: “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out. Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.”

“I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” So the question is: do you prefer God’s wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires? “all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” Solomon did not care about anything else except wisdom.

“All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”. Wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He did not hide his wisdom. Sirach says the same: “refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Just as Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures. Searching after wisdom is a good thing; that is what we are supposed to do. That is how we should talk, it should be on our minds at all times, and everything should always go back to the scriptures.
blog/2026/2026-03-14-2026-03-14-the-stor:
God held Moses by him a long season and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Ezra was not the only one; God showed Solomon the same. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”.

God showed Solomon how the world was created, from the beginning, when he said let there be light. He showed him how the elements operate: water, air, fire. You breathe the air but do not know where it comes from; ask Solomon. There is a spirit in fire: a little fire can consume a whole place; ask Solomon how. Everything runs to the ocean, yet the ocean never overflows; ask Solomon why. Christ said you cannot even count the hairs on your head. Those things are too heavy for us, but God showed them to Solomon.

The scripture says Solomon had more knowledge than any king before him or after him, the greatest king who ever walked this planet. He knew so much that at the end the knowledge almost consumed him. And he saw the beginning, the middle and the end of time, just as Moses did.

So if a young man says, I know everything in the Bible and there is nothing anybody can teach me, you are a fool. You can spend your lifetime in this book and still not master it. Bishop Nathanyel was not teaching back then the way he teaches today; as time goes by, more of the spiritual world opens to the Bishops. We have not been shown even ten percent of what was shown to Solomon. The waters are rising; just be patient.

David was down but not out, and he did not hide it from God: “I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.” To roar is to utter or express in a loud tone: to cry, shout, yell. David says, I'm feeble, I'm broken, and I cried out because of the disquietness of my heart.

“Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.” He laid it all before the Lord.

Some of you, when you pray, do not pray for yourself, because you think you are perfect. You need to pray for yourself and ask for help to overcome certain things. Some of you are fighting lust; when you fast, pray that Messiah helps you overcome that lust. We all have lust. Our lust might be different things, but we all have it. Some of you are fighting a covetous spirit; pray that Messiah helps you overcome it.

You are not going to walk into the kingdom of heaven thinking you're perfect and your stuff don't stink. Put your desire and your groaning before the Lord, so that when the storm comes, fear does not overtake you.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”. When fear or trouble tries to put you down, David shows how to talk to your own soul: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.”

David is speaking to himself, to his soul. Put plain: I might be down, but I'm not broken. I might be down, but I'm not out yet. Satan tried to take me out, but I'm still fighting. My hope is in the Lord, and I still have some fight in me.

Some of you are quick to give up. As soon as something happens, you run out: why did they have to put correction? Correction is a good thing. It keeps you on your toes, it makes you better and stronger. What doesn't break you makes you stronger; that is correction, that is the word of God. You can use a brother's correction to build yourself up: in my mind I was going to do what this brother got corrected for, so let me move from it. Moses said some you correct openly, so that others fear. Some of you never were corrected in your life until you came to IUIC, and you are too prideful to take it.

Brothers, never keep a yes-man around you. If you have a man in your circle who cannot say, bro, I don't think you should do this, that man hates you and is waiting for your downfall. You want men who tell you, don't talk evil of leadership; if you have a problem with a brother, go to him. Sisters are the same: the sister who won't tell you what you want to hear is not your enemy, she is the one you want around you, because she has no respect of persons. Men like that help you get the kingdom of heaven.

You won't walk into the kingdom thinking you are perfect. This is what Christ said: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”.

The word is overcome. Brothers, you must overcome the lust of America, and you must also overcome the personal thing you struggle with. We all struggle with things. Some of you struggle with lust, with porn, with prostitution, with drugs. Some of you are crackheads, weed heads; some of you it's cigarettes, Black and Milds, women. And yes, it is said to shame you. This is not my word; don't get mad at me. Read what Christ says you have to do.

The words “keepeth my works” mean keep my commandments, keep my laws. My works is this book: keep it. If you keep it, that means you have overcome. You must overcome, or else you are not going to make it to the kingdom.

So when you watch all these prophecies happen, don't include yourself if you won't let the lust go. Some of you need to let things go. That is how you keep from the spirit of fear: you prepare your mind in the scriptures and overcome, so that Esau has nothing to hold over you and you don't betray your brother to hide what you were watching.

“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” You are that gold. We are that gold. How do you purify gold? By putting it in the fire. Some of you need to go into the fire. You have stuff on you that has to be purged out, but you want to keep it and still have the kingdom of heaven. If you don't want to be purged, you cannot get the kingdom. Some of you want to be iron, some of you want to be silver; you have to be that gold.

What is the purpose of going through all that and not getting the kingdom? Esau has been putting you through hell all your life, and you end up missing the kingdom because you hold on to things and don't want God to take the unclean out of you.

Some of you hold on to things that happened fifty years ago, twenty years ago, five years ago. That's like a woman in an argument: you're talking about the orange and she says, yeah, but the pineapple happened five years ago. There's no pineapple here; we're talking about the orange. Some sisters got notes, waiting to bring them out. Men should not be emotional like that.

And “acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: it takes a strong man to take correction. Weak men cannot. When correction comes, the strong man gets up, repents and keeps moving, and you can tell he is still in the fight. When you get correction, that's when you push harder. Don't lay back. Prove to Messiah, not to leadership, that you are still in the fight.

God is “declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done.” Only the God of Israel can do that, and he shows the end to the prophets. Look at the videos of the missiles coming down at night: don't they look like stars falling from heaven? The prophets had never seen a missile, an Iron Dome, a supersonic missile or a nuclear weapon. They described what they saw to the best of their ability, and it is our job to put it together. Put yourself in the prophet's shoes, because you are the prophets; you just don't remember.

Habakkuk describes how it hurts when these missiles hit, because when they hit they bring destruction. You don't want to be around when a missile hits the ground; you don't even want to be ten feet away.

“When I heard, my belly trembled.” That kind of fear is an anxiety sitting inside you, in your chest. He cannot believe what he is watching, but the Lord had to show it to him. “My lips quivered at the voice”: he was shaking, he couldn't even talk straight. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself.” He could not believe the damage this thing was doing, the number of people it killed when it hit.

“That I might rest in the day of trouble.” He is saying, I don't want to be alive to see this. It is so bad I don't want to be around to see it. That is what Psalms 91 means by a thousand falling at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand: he saw the bomb drop and ten thousand people die right there.

That is the end God declared from the beginning, and “My counsel shall stand.” The media say Hamas is finished, Hezbollah has no weapons, Iran is weak; yet Hezbollah fired a hundred missiles into Israel the other day, and Israel cannot destroy Hamas under its nose while Iran is seven times bigger than Israel. We are going with the Bible. If you want the kingdom of heaven, you must accept what comes with it: war, tribulation and death.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” The same God who foreknew us and predestinated us to be conformed to the image of his Son predestinated us unto the adoption of children, by Jesus Christ, to himself.

That calling is what the class carried straight into Paul: “For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Paul understood he was a servant, sent to serve the people and deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” You have to do it willingly, not because somebody forced you; a brother forced to do something has no spirit in it. Yet some of you get up at four in the morning and willingly give the white man eight or twelve hours without complaining, while coming here on the Sabbath is a burden.

So being predestinated as children by Jesus Christ is not a reason to sit and wait. God did not call you here just to sit and listen. It is a call to be the true witness that delivers souls, and in the fear of the Lord is the strong confidence to do it.

“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

“A true witness delivereth souls”: a true prophet, a true servant, delivers souls. Paul shows how a true witness does it: “This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”

It is our job, brothers, to rebuke our people sharply. Why? That they may be sound in the faith; that they may repent. That is how souls are delivered.

So whose soul have you been delivering? You have been sitting here five years, seven years, ten years; some of you cannot even deliver your own soul, because you forgot the mission. Who are you working for, spiritually: Messiah or Satan? Some of you are agents working for Esau.

“but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.” Our people love lies, and the deceitful witness feeds them lies. That is why you see ten thousand, twenty thousand in the Christian churches: they do not want the truth. They say Christ cannot be black, Christ cannot come only for the Israelite. The truth to us is a foreign language. That is why the true witness has to rebuke sharply: sharp rebuke is what brings a people who love lies to repentance.

“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.
blog/2026/2026-03-15-2026-03-15-prophesy:
Alexander “parted his kingdom among them, while he was yet alive”, and “his servants bare rule every one in his place.” His generals divided it up: Ptolemy took Egypt, Lysimachus took Thrace and Asia Minor, Seleucus took Syria, and Cassander took Macedonia. Alexander had everything united as one; they could not unite, so they divided the kingdom.

Daniel shows the pattern: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory”. Back then, in the time of the Greeks, the strange gods were Zeus, Aphrodite and the like. The strange god today is Caesar Borgia.

It goes on, “and he shall cause them to rule over many”: he causes his people to rule over many nations, many countries. He “shall divide the land for gain.” That is what Alexander's generals did.

Many of these scriptures have levels to them. It started with the Greeks, but Esau kept that same energy at the Berlin Conference in the late 1800s. No Africans, no Negroes and no Latinos were in that meeting; it was about white supremacy, and they divided up the entire continent of Africa for gain, and the land of Israel with it. That is what the Balfour Declaration was about: some of these so-called Khazars wanted that land.

The Greeks and then the Europeans divided the land for gain. David shows how they got in: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

When the white man comes, his words are smoother than butter. He will talk about Jesus, about love, about honour and respect, and you will fall in love with what he says. But his intent all along was war and to destroy you.

They did not come into Africa talking war. They came with missionaries who talked the love of white Jesus: we love you, dusty Africans. In Africa you have Hamites and Shemites; the Shemites are the Bantus, and the Nilotes are the Hamites, who were their mercenaries. They brought their religions, spoke words of peace, learned our strengths and our weaknesses, and then devastated us with colonialism and slavery. That is how they divided Africa for financial gain, and why Africa is not united today.

Kwame Nkrumah wanted to unite the entire continent with one visa and one financial system backed by gold. The CIA said, we got to get rid of this dude, and he was run out of Ghana to Guinea.

They taught us to read but not to reason. That is why people get confused over Romans 9:13 and John 3:16: they can read, but they cannot reason. Softer than oil, yet drawn swords: behind every smooth word, the intent was war.

Paul says, “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.” Peace and safety is what Trump keeps saying, the peace president who bombed Yemen, Somalia, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Nigeria and Venezuela. Some of you love it when the president talks about peace, stomping your feet because you think nothing is going to happen in this country. Ezra shows what travail upon a woman with child means.

“As when a woman with child in the ninth month bringeth forth her son, with two or three hours of her birth great pains compass her womb, which pains, when the child cometh forth, they slack not a moment.” Within two or three hours: in the time of nations that is two or three years, or months. When a woman is having a baby, her contractions come ten minutes apart, then five, six, five, four, closer and closer.

“Even so shall not the plagues be slack to come upon the earth, and the world shall mourn, and sorrows shall come upon it on every side.” A pain comes one month, then things calm down; another comes two or three months later, and things calm down again. That is how it is going to be in this world.

But when things calm down, Israelites say nothing is going to happen and go back to business as usual. That is why Paul says “of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.” We read the prophecies every week, and if you are not paying attention you will be caught off guard. The real brothers and the real sisters will not need to be warned; they are aware of what is about to happen.

The great multitude “shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle, with things offered unto idols.” What does that mean? It is talking about Christianity. If you are idle, they are going to feed you Christianity. How do we know? Paul prophesied it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

We already know some of you are going to depart from this faith. Why? Because persecution is coming, and when you cannot pay your bills and cannot get food, you will leave. America wants to bring in digital currency so they can control us. In China, if you jaywalk, they take money out of your account; imagine being told you may not teach the gospel or gather on the seventh day, and when we do it anyway, your digital bank account is hit.

What is the doctrine of devils? Paul explains it: “Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats”. What religion forbids men to marry? Catholicism, Christianity. Commanding to abstain from meats: that is Lent, no meat for 40 days. That is the food offered to idols: Christianity, Roman Catholicism.
