Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. Israel is the elect. The elect gathered from the four winds are the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered to the ends of the earth.

And notice when it happens. He comes in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory after the tribulation and the war. There is no thought that he might come tomorrow; the tribulation has not come yet, and World War III is already in process. First the war and the shaking of Idumea, the powers of the heavens; then the sign of the Son of man, all the tribes of the earth mourning, and the gathering of Jacob's seed, Israel his elect, out of every nation where they were scattered.

Revelation 7 shows four angels holding back the four winds of the earth. What is the wind? Ezra gives the precept: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

A multitude of men out of number, coming from the four winds of heaven. The winds are the armies of the nations gathering, and the destruction they bring. They come “to subdue the man that came out of the sea”: to subdue Christ. They want to fight Christ, the Son of God.

That goes back to Daniel 8:25, where they stand up against the Prince of princes, but he is broken without hand. It is saying the same thing.

So when the angels hold the four winds so that they blow not on the earth, the sea or any tree, they are holding back the armies of the nations, on land, on sea and in the air, until the servants of God are sealed. Then the winds are let loose, the nations gather to fight Christ at his coming, and the end comes.

In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and he cries to the four angels, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

Isaiah answers: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal is the law, the commandments. That is what the angel is looking for, and that is what he is doing: sealing the law among the disciples, the servants of God, in their foreheads, meaning in their minds.

The ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed with the law, the destruction is let loose and the end comes.

So the gospel of the kingdom preached in all the world for a witness is the law and the testimony going out to our people scattered among the nations, sealing them before the end. He that endures to the end, keeping it, the same shall be saved.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Some say that contradicts Isaiah 66, where the Lord gathers his people out of the nations. It does not. The world Christ speaks of here goes into the 144,000, and Revelation 7 shows it.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.” The four winds are destruction. The earth is the armies on land; the sea is the navy and the marines; any tree is the air force, which comes down above the trees.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is what the angel is looking for.

Verse three is the point that ties in with Matthew 24: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” Do not let the destruction come until the servants of God are sealed. “And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

Once the 144,000 are sealed, then shall the end come: destruction upon destruction upon destruction. And because the 144,000 are scattered among the nations, the gospel must be preached among all the nations. That is why we must go out and prophesy and teach among all these different nations: our people are there.

“Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished.” The hands joined together are the black pastors holding hands with Amalek, encouraging the African-American churches to defend Israel, and even naming the Hebrew Israelites in their articles. The white man is not worried about them; they do not know the Bible and they teach heresies.

Maccabees shows this is nothing new: “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.” And “So this device pleased them well.”

Amongst our people there are wicked men, and they persuaded many. Let us make a covenant with the Greeks, with the white man. We have always had certain men among us who are wicked, who made covenants and agreements with the white man.

We are built upon Christ and the holy apostles.

That is the difference between the two sides of Proverbs 11:21. The black pastors and politicians built on lies, their refuge of lies that the hail will sweep away. The seed of the righteous is built on the tried stone, and “he that believeth shall not make haste”: he will not be confounded and will not leave this truth. That is why the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

The wicked join hand in hand by covenant, and Isaiah names that covenant: “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” That is the black pastors and politicians.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation.” This is Christ. “he that believeth shall not make haste”: you will not be confounded; you will not leave this truth.

“Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies.” The Lord is bringing judgment. The hail, the destruction, shall sweep away the refuge of Christianity and all its lies, and Islam as well. “And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand.” All the blacks that made a covenant with the white man, with these fake Israelis, shall have it disannulled; the agreement with hell is this low condition our people are in. “when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it”: those black pastors shall be trodden down.

“From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you”: from the time the teaching goes forth. “for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.” Morning by morning, day and night, you are going to hear the proper teaching, and it vexes you, because you already made that agreement for the financial gain.

“For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.” Whether you are in Christianity or politics, you are trying to get comfortable after hearing the vexing report. That is why the wicked, hand in hand, shall not be unpunished.

Latino and black pastors join hands to support Babylon and not God, not the Most High. Zechariah shows what those they join with have done to us: “Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.”

The ones that possess us now are the white man, and he slays us: Rasheem Carter, Kendrick Johnson, Breonna Taylor, Philando Castile, Sandra Bland, George Floyd. We found out they were hunting us on Epstein’s island. And they hold themselves not guilty.

“and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich.” They got rich from selling us into slavery. The majority of the wealth America has came from four hundred years of free chattel slavery.

“and their own shepherds pity them not.” Our own shepherds are our pastors and our congressmen and women. They pity us not because they are getting a piece of the American pie. They do not give a damn about our brothers and sisters being shot down in the street, about Rasheem Carter, about Kendrick Johnson, whose case was dismissed again though he had taser marks and cut marks and the school footage disappeared.

Those shepherds are the wicked joined hand in hand with our possessors, and they shall not be unpunished.

Daniel saw it too: “I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake”. Write this down: the horn is America. The voice is their media today, and it goes worldwide; even in Cuba there was American news on certain channels.

“I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.” Now he calls the horn the beast, and it is destined to be destroyed. Revelation 18:8 is the precept: “Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her.” That is the body given to the burning flame.

“And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning”. They will cry for this horn, this America.

So the mouth that casts out the flood after the woman is the same voice of great words that brings the beast to the burning flame.

“And he shall speak great words against the most High”: through their media, the same blasphemies we read in Revelation 13.

“And shall wear out the saints of the most High”. How did they wear us out? In slavery: shackles on our necks, our hands and our ankles; buck breaking; working seven days a week from sunup to sundown. That is what wearing out the saints means.

“And think to change times and laws”: the daylight saving time we just entered; laws like same-sex marriage; our Sabbath changed to Sunday.

“And they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time”: 250 years. What we need to see in this verse is that he speaks great words against the Most High, and that is their media, the mouth of the serpent casting its flood of lies after the woman.

Jeremiah 51:55 says “when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”. The waves that roar are the nations, and Isaiah 17 is the precept that proves it.

“Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” The nations are the waters, making a noise like the seas.

“The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.”

So the waters in these prophecies are peoples and nations. The waves roaring within Babylon are the nations inside her, and however they rush, God will rebuke them and chase them like chaff before the wind.

“A sound of a cry cometh from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans”. Babylon here is America, and the Chaldeans are modern Israel today. The Chaldeans were always an ally to Babylon: ancient Babylon were Kushites and the Chaldeans Semites, so brought up to today, America is Babylon and the Israelis are the Chaldeans.

“Because the Lord hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice”. What is the great voice? Their media, which goes worldwide and captivates and hypnotizes people everywhere. “When her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”: the waves are the nations within her.

“Because the spoiler is come upon her, even upon Babylon”, as we read in Habakkuk, “and her mighty men are taken”, as prisoners of war, “every one of their bows is broken: for the Lord God of recompences shall surely requite.”

“And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her captains”, the admirals and generals, “and her rulers”, the governors and mayors, “and her mighty men”, the soldiers: “and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake”. That perpetual sleep is the lake of fire; they are never waking up again. So the serpent’s mouth, the great voice, will be destroyed out of her.

“And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”. His mouth is the media, America’s media, and every single aspect of it is so-called Jewish owned; Amalek controls all the media, and Trump wants to control the whole of it. The water out of the serpent’s mouth is lies. The woman is our people, and the flood is to draw as many of the twelve tribes of Israel as they can into their Christian or democratic lies. That is their agenda.

Revelation 13 describes that mouth: “And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months. And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.”

In the time of Rome they had written media, pamphlets they sent out everywhere. It started with Rome; the Americans have it top-notch today, and their messages go out worldwide. That mouth speaking great things and blasphemies is the same mouth casting out the flood after the woman.

Revelation 17 ends with the woman: “the waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” Put up the Statue of Liberty: Lady Liberty sits upon many waters; she is everywhere. The ten horns, Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland, “shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” It will be an ambush; the entire country will be destroyed. “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” We call it a country; God calls it a great city. Nobody dominates America; America reigns over everybody.

Then chapter 18 opens right after: “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.” Why does it say fallen twice? Because Israel is the little Babylon.

“For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication”: her policies, the same thing Daniel 8 says, that through his policy he shall cause craft to prosper. All nations follow their policies. “And the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her”: the nations got in bed with her. “And the merchants of the earth”, the corporations and companies, “are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies.”

“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” That lets you know where the Israelites are: in Babylon. They say Babylon is Iraq. No, no, no: it is letting you know the twelve tribes are here.

“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. Christ knows the works of the Israelites in the church of Smyrna, a colony of Israelites, and the hell they caught there, hunted by Herod for Rome. They were impoverished, but he reminded them they are rich, because all the promises in the Bible pertain only to the Israelites.

“And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” That is why you have people like Herod, who said he was Jewish, and Agrippa and Bernice in Acts. You want to call it hate speech; we are reading from the Bible. Then: “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. That is Herod and Rome, and he calls them the devil.

Revelation 3:9 gives the end of it: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.”

That is a future prophecy that has not occurred yet. Today the synagogue of Satan sits in the land calling itself Jewish; the day is coming when they will worship before the feet of the real Jews and know that God loved us. Until then, “be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.”

Wisdom of Solomon 2 lets you hear the synagogue of Satan think. “For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.” This ungodly is Esau.

Now watch what Esau says about us. “He was made to reprove our thoughts.” The Israelite man, the prophet, was made to reprove their thoughts. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: just looking at us grieves them, because we are a constant reminder that we are the sons of God and they are not. “For his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion”, because we keep the commandments of God.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”. That goes to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9: they are counterfeits, fakes, frauds; they are not the real Jews. The Bible calls them counterfeits; those are not my words, those are the words of God. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”.

The table the Lord prepares before us in the presence of our enemies is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

The Lord told the prophet Habakkuk: since you want to get out of captivity, write the vision down, and make it plain upon the tables. That is what we are supposed to be reading.

Make it plain “that he may run that readeth it”: when we bring this out, everybody is going to be running, and we are going to run to teach it. The Bible is going to turn this whole system upside down: these are they which have turned the world upside down. But we have to be in it like that, not reading about overseas like entertainment while our own spirit is rotten.

Paul says what happened to our fathers is “written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” Isaiah shows why it was written: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

This is to the wicked Israelites, us, our people. Go write it before them in a table, and put a note in the book about their wickedness, our wickedness, “that it may be for the time to come”: for today.

And it goes on: “That this is a rebellious people”. That is what is going on with our people; our people are rebellious. But the Bible is here to correct you and straighten you out. If you want it, there is a way for you to get it.

Those who refuse to learn from the past by reading it are doomed to repeat it. You will repeat it because you refuse to learn, and the same spirits will follow you and attach themselves to you, the way people move to a new town, a new job or a new congregation and the same problem follows. The Lord sends those spirits as a mirror to show you what is wrong in you. Learn it from the book, and you won't have to learn it again.

Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.

God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Some of our people can't wait: they want to be part of the war in the streets, casting out demons, getting their names on the Saturday night specials: brother, get a good angle of me, I want my video to go up Saturday. But here's the stipulation: when your obedience is fulfilled. That means there is no impediment left in your spirit to commit sin; you are walking straight in your spirit, your household, with your children, blameless. Then you can go out and correct your people.

That is what the Apocrypha says: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. First set your house in order. Your physical house can't be set in order if your spiritual house, meaning your damn head, is not in order. You haven't even checked your own wicked thoughts, your own actions, your own temptations, and you are trying to correct your wife, your son and your daughter.

Set your head in order; then you can set your house in order; then you can reprove your people. That is when your obedience is fulfilled, and you can revenge all disobedience, because you checked it first within yourself. We want to play warrior, to look good, while there are demons all up in us that we have not corrected yet.

The weapons of our warfare are the commandments. You are supposed to answer your impulses, your sinful temptations, with the commandments of God, and that is supposed to turn you from the door of temptation. If you understood that death is around the corner, you would listen to these laws.

But the wicked man thinks judgment is far off: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Because the judgment is not immediate, his sick, evil mind is emboldened to commit evil and sin, and he leaves the commandments to the side. You had better recognize where you are.

That is the war inside you. The Lord isn't asking you to pick up a gun and go do something out there; he is asking you to get your mind right and set this mark in your head to change your behavior. We don't advocate anyone initiating aggression; if someone comes at you with a rope or a knife, you defend yourself. But the gung-ho brothers who can't wait for war can't even discipline their food. The war to win first is against the heart that sin makes bold.

“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. You are at war right now in your spirit, with evil temptations pushed on every front: family members, school, work, even your own thoughts as you sit here. The weapons are not guns; the weapons are the commandments of God, and they are mighty.

Mighty to pull down what? Lies. That is what the Bible does; that is how we tear the lies down. We open up the Bible and swallow up the lies, like it says in the Psalms: “Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.” We open this Bible, and the lies are swallowed up.

So “Casting down imaginations” is casting down lies, “and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”, and the knowledge of God is the law, the Bible. When you open this Bible and apply the commandments, you get rid of those impulsive, sinful thoughts and bring every thought “into captivity” under the obedience of Christ. That is how you walk straight past your temptation.

Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.

“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition”. It was in John’s vision but not in his time. When it came, it came out of Europe, Great Britain to be exact. And it shall go into perdition, destruction. That is where we are now; that is what this war is signifying.

The weapons to do it are already here. You don’t have to wonder where the fire is going to come from. The Lord will come with fire because he is coming with those weapons; he is going to be literally riding on the weapons being fired, and coming with something like two hundred million angels. That is what Isaiah 13:5 says: the Lord and the weapons of his indignation come from a far country, “to destroy the whole land”, the whole land, singular.

That fire is the perdition of Babylon the Great; that is what the beast is going to get. And “they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life”. They have no clue that this is Babylon the Great, and they are not getting the kingdom, no matter how many churches they set up.

Every time you pray the Lord’s prayer, thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth, you are advocating for the destruction of this kingdom. Christ is not setting his kingdom beside this one. The King of kings is coming to topple it with the weapons of his indignation.

“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”. The woman is Babylon the Great, America, and the martyrs of Jesus are the Israelites: those who stand up for this truth all the way up to the threat of death and beyond it. Many of us are going to get killed. They drank our blood by putting us in captivity and dealing evil with us.

Obadiah explains that drinking: “For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” The reward of what the nations did to us is coming back on them. “For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain”: what did they drink upon us? Captivity, slavery, rape, robbery, murder, lies, rigged juries, castrations, lynchings, railroading; the Rasheem Carters, the Kendrick Johnsons.

“So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down”. All the nations that did this to God’s people will drink the captivity, the slavery, the whipped backs, the lynchings, and digest it. “And they shall be as though they had not been.” They dehumanized us until we do not even recognize we were once a great people, reduced us to nothing, when we are the jewels of God. So they will be reduced to nothing, as Isaiah 14:21 cuts off their name.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.” Deliverance is for the ones of us that repent and stop BSing. The ones who do not repent and keep up the BS, the Most High is going to wipe out along with our enemies.

“Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.” That is why we deal with prophecy first. What we are watching in the news lines up with the scriptures: the fourth kingdom of Daniel 2, partly strong as iron and partly broken, mingling itself with the seed of men; and the ten horns of Revelation 17, NATO, that gave their power and strength unto the beast, America, since 1945, now turning on her, twenty-eight nations signing in the middle of the night to stand without the United States.

All the prophets saw the same thing. Habakkuk: “For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie”. What we read in Revelation is for an appointed time, and it shall not lie; it is guaranteed. What we read in Isaiah, in Habakkuk, in Revelation will happen.

“though it tarry, wait for it”. We hear the Bishop bring out the revelations and the breakdowns, and it is taking its time, while the Christians do not have it at all; it is oblivious to their minds, distracted with prosperity doctrine. Wait for it: that is the counsel given to the elect. Be patient and get yourself right, because the vision will come to pass, and the nations will turn on each other.

“because it will surely come, it will not tarry”. Just as the Most High hardened Pharaoh's heart, he has a proud man in power who will say and do anything and take everybody's stuff; that is how it is going to happen. God put it in their hearts to fulfill his will, so we do not have to worry: we know what is going to happen before it happens.

“Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans”. The virgin daughter of Babylon is America. People try to say Babylon is somewhere else, but when has America been touched? The one thing that ever happened, they blew up themselves: 9/11 was the biggest controlled demolition anybody has ever witnessed. The virgin means she has not been touched, defiled or destroyed, until these prophecies are fulfilled. She is going to be touched.

“for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”. She thought she was tender and delicate, but that is coming to an end. As Daniel 2 showed, all manner of nations are within her, including her enemies: sleeper cells.

“Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers.” A virgin would be covered, but here her locks, leg and thigh are uncovered: the wickedness of Babylon, America, is being revealed.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” What shame? How she allies herself with the little Satan and helps them bomb other countries, backing a demolition project to wipe out Gaza and its people, even renaming a whole body of water the Gulf of America. That is why the nations that benefited from her will grow to hate her, and prophecy lets us see it coming.

“but rather that ye may prophesy”. The purpose of prophecy is to build your spirit up and prepare you for temptation and destruction. Prophecy is warning: thus saith the Lord. When you see these things come to pass, know that Esau, Edom, America, is the enemy the Bible speaks of.

Revelation 18 gives the warning plainly. Babylon the great is fallen and has become the habitation of devils, and the call goes out: “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.”

Come out of religion. Come out of these doctrines. Come out of Christianity. Come out of the lies and philosophies and deceit, and repent. The Christian church has you clapping on a tambourine while the prophecy is fulfilled before your eyes; they say the book of Revelation is sealed and cannot explain any of this.

That is why we covet to prophesy: so our people can see who Babylon is, come out of her, and not receive her plagues when the fire comes on her.

Solomon’s mind was on the people. He did not ask for four hundred women or chariots, or to be a king of 4,000; he asked for “an understanding heart to judge thy people”, “for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?” Because he had a mind for the people, the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he even desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people, the Lord will bless that thing beyond measure.

Sirach says it plainly: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing this for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning, driving, so they could be here to help teach the class. A captain drove down and got here at five in the morning to check the congregation, to check on the saints of the Most High. The bishops travel all over the world; the deacons travel. This is not for ourselves; this is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom that is at hand.

“but for all them”: this is a nation. You must be nation-minded. A lot of times we are not like that: me, me, me, me, me, and that is all you are concerned with. But all through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and how to move the nation further ahead.

That is the mindset of a leader and the action of a king: like Solomon, labour not for yourself only, but for all the people, and the Lord gives more than you asked.

Mattathias would not do what everybody else was doing. He cried, “Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.” Somebody had to stand up, and that is the mark of a true leader. Acts shows what the leaders of the church were doing: “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Assembled with one accord: bishops on one accord, deacons on one accord, captains on one accord. And they send chosen men, not just anybody. You could say they send out Bishop Nathanyel and Deacon Isaac, as they sent Barnabas and Paul.

“Men that have hazarded their lives”: a real leader risks his life for Christ. They call Michael Jordan a leader, football coaches leaders of men; Michael Jordan is not risking anything. Wyclef, what are you doing? The men of this camp have been to Haiti, to Africa, to the barrios of Puerto Rico. They are not going to the suburbs; they are going to the hood, all over IUIC, putting their lives on the line for the name of Christ.

And leaders build leaders. That is an attribute of a father: a father wants his son to be better than him. The bishops are building leadership, sending men to countries and corners that could not be touched before, and now others have been raised up to touch them. But if your mindset is job security, sitting in the high seat, and not building brothers to be better than yourself, forget about it: the Lord will remove you.

Peter calls us “a peculiar people”. What makes us peculiar? Wisdom answers: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them”. The peculiar commandments, the same thing Deuteronomy 4 said, are what separate us. They see the fringes on your garment. They see a beard on your face. They ask why y'all never come out with us on Saturday, and you say I have to keep the Sabbath. The Sabbath, what's that? I thought you said you was Christian. That is what separates you from everybody else.

The commandments “that were given unto them”: all these things were given only to us. That is why 1 Peter 2:9 is talking about the Israelites, not the white man. It is not white Grecians in togas, and the Galatians are not the white man in Turkmenistan. It is talking about you. So many of our brothers and sisters have been destroyed and don't see themselves as a prince, a ruler, a judge, but God says you are all of those things. All the leadership books go back to the Bible, which was given only to us, yet they make billions off leadership conferences while we sit at the bottom.

We must magnify the law: “The Lord is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law”. That is each and every one of our jobs, to put the laws of God on a pedestal and stand firm for them. When you do, it automatically puts you in a different position, different from everybody else on the face of the earth, because nobody else is standing firm for the commandments. The way you do anything is the way you do everything; nine times out of ten the cracker over you on the job is no better than you, but you are not doing things according to the commandments.

That separation shows. Our sisters dress modestly while the women in Houston dressed so out of order a dress code had to be put in place. Fifty men reading the Bible on a cruise become the disturbance. They make a man an offender for the word. But we were called out of darkness to show forth his praise. Nobody takes a light and puts it under a bushel, and you don't shine from the back. It is time for all of us to take our places.

“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

Job 33:23 speaks of “a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”. You are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. When you are one among a thousand, that makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset shouldn't be to fit in; you should be figuring out how to make it better. Joseph didn't go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how we are going to solve the problem. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

The first thing in the mindset of a leader is that he believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else. When an issue arises, you don't run. You raise your hand, you volunteer, you figure out a solution to the problem.

Isaiah shows it: “Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That's the mindset of a leader.

That is the same thing David did. Everybody kept crying about the situation, and David said, where is Goliath at? Show me. The first thing you have to have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart. That is what the Lord has put in your spirit to do: not an unsure mind that says maybe I can, but send me.

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” When you get the flattering title, your maker soon takes you away. What does that mean? You want the flattering title, you get the test, you fail the test. Bam. Thought I was worthy. Nope.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, and it don't work like that; this is the Lord's business, and he is the one giving it out. Brothers that ask for rank, that say give me the 50's test, never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. When brothers ask for the test, nine times out of ten they fail it, because spiritually you are not ready if you are asking. Nobody asks to be a leader. The Lord raised all these men up. The Bishop didn't ask to be a bishop; he became a bishop. If you are asking for it, you are in the wrong place.

When the student is ready, the teacher will be there. The Lord will place you where you are supposed to be; promotion comes from the Lord, and there is a reason you are in the position you are in. Once you fulfill that office, the Lord will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down and never made it back, while others who were down came back on fire. The work determines where you are supposed to be. Brothers get jealous when another brother gets position, but if you love the Lord you work for the Lord, not for position. In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

That is what Judith 8:24 asks of a leader: not a title, but “let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us”. The higher up you go, the more people you serve. If you don't have the mindset to build up those beneath you and to support and push up the leader above you, forget it; the Lord can't use you.

Christ walked by the sea of Galilee and said to Peter and Andrew, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Baruch shows where that invitation comes from.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not to the other nations. So there is no reason for you to sit on that wisdom and do nothing.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is speaking of Christ. We are the only ones that have a God; the other nations do not. Our God saw us as so special that he showed himself on the earth. Our God, Emmanuel, walked with us and conversed with us. That goes back to Matthew 4 when he said “Follow me”: that was our leader telling us to follow him.

So we are not supposed to just sit here and do absolutely nothing. Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same thing: teach our brothers and sisters and wake them up. The invitation is there, and like Peter and Andrew, who “straightway left their nets, and followed him”, we have to accept it.

This is our job. “And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him”. You were made to be the servant of God. You were made to do this work. You were not born to be a basketball player or a rapper. You were born to be a servant of God; that is our duty and our calling. “To bring Jacob again to him”: that is your commission.

“Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

“And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. Think about that: it is a light thing. It is the least you can do. The Lord sacrificed himself for you; our God came down and walked with us. It is a light thing to do the work of the Lord and go wake up your people.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That is the same thing read in Matthew 4: Galilee of the Gentiles, the people that sat in darkness, saw great light. It is talking about Israel; we are to go to our brothers of the Northern Kingdom and be the light to the Gentiles, carrying on the mission God gave us.

“So built we the wall”: all through our history, the forefathers were building. What we are doing today is nothing different from what they always did, and Ezekiel shows the kind of building the Lord gives us while we are scattered.

“Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” Israel was cast far off and scattered, and the Lord still gave them little sanctuaries in the lands where they came.

When Paul went to Galatia, to Colossae, to Corinth and to Thessalonica, those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today. The schools are those little sanctuaries in the countries, and each and every one of us put a hand into building each and every one of them.

So the wall of Nehemiah and the little sanctuary of Ezekiel are the same work. The people built because they had a mind to work, and that mind to work is what leadership has to put into the people now.

The people built the wall because they “had a mind to work.” This is how a leader’s mindset must be, and Christ shows it: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

A single eye is being locked in, what they call laser focus. Whatever you are locked in on, that is what you are going to see. That is all you are going to see, and that is all that matters.

And when the leader is like that, guess who else is going to be like that? Everybody underneath him. The single eye of the one at the head fills the whole body with light, so the whole camp takes on his focus.

That is why the wall got built. The mind to work in the people starts with the mind of the one leading them.

“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him are going to be.

So when you see these other camps that look disorganized, that are talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders, and that is what you will see. When you see us traveling all over the world, building institutions, organizations within the organization, look at our leaders. We are the representation of our leadership.

When we go to Chicago we are not on film eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight. How is that a leader of a congregation? You will never see a bishop or a deacon put out a video like that. When we went to Chicago, we went to O’Block teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. There are cities where the leader was changed and the camp took off, and other places where the leader left and everything fell apart. You are who your leader is. That is why everybody wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but what they do not understand is that Christ is at the head and we are all following Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders, sealed with the law of God, and nothing they try can stop it.

That is why the people of Nehemiah had a mind to work: the wall reflects the ones leading the building.

Sirach praises the “Leaders of the people”, plural, and First Maccabees shows how they worked: “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” They said it one to another. Nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets, he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. The Bishop has said for years that this work is too big for one man.

We are in that decayed estate now. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: our women thinking they can wear tights outside and nothing is wrong, grown men going outside in a crop top with the belly out, our young women on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is the urgency you see in the brothers teaching loud in the streets, and that is why the Bishop and the deacons teach the way they teach.

Restoring the decayed estate of our people is what is happening at IUSC: our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“Let us fight for our people”, and for the sanctuary. You will go way further for somebody else than you will for yourself, and sacrifice way more for someone else than for yourself. That is why selfish people only go so far: they are satisfied at some point. A leader’s mind is on the whole people, like the leaders Sirach praises, who left a name behind them.

Sirach says “Let us now praise famous men” and names them as “Leaders of the people”, leaders, not one. Second Maccabees shows what those leaders do. Judas Maccabeus was preparing the men for war, and we are at war too, brothers: against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

First a leader has to know the condition of the battle. “And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” If the first time you hear there is a war going on is weeks after it started, you are sleep. If you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife and your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not ready for the famine the Lord said is coming, when your stomach touches your back and your kids are looking at you.

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” That is why the class keeps showing that Esau is the devil, lying and breaking every treaty and oath. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell, or wears the Frozen wig because she thinks Esau is still a princess, she does not see his breach of oaths. As a mother and a father you have to rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers. Keep the body, take the mind: that was the slave master’s method, and the leader’s work is to take back the mind.

“And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish. Onias was “a virtuous and a good man”; virtue is moral excellence, and our moral compass is God’s commandments that make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation”, eloquent in speech; “gentle in condition”, keeping his composure, not hot-headed; “well spoken also”; and “exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Nobody wakes up leading people. We are born leaders, but we become that in time. And “holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

Jeremias gave Judas a sword of gold: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” Then “Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas’s own mindset but the words of God, which comfort a people with a spirit of fear on them and stir them up “to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men.” They determined “courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader.

That is why the nations destroy the leaders first, because the leaders are in many cases the lifeline of the people. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.
