The horrible star is the ICBM, and the flying swords are the missiles. “And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.”

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. And “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, just as Revelation 18 says the kings and merchants of the earth will bewail her. That is the time of trouble in which Daniel's people, every one written in the book, shall be delivered.

Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

Daniel says “there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon, and Psalm 91 shows how Israel is delivered in the midst of it.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” And “he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.”

That is the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon: thy people delivered, every one found written in the book, not all nations. It is the same psalm Satan twisted when he told Christ to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

Daniel says “at that time thy people shall be delivered”. John shows the order of it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That standing up is now.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” Between the standing up and the deliverance, John left out the tribulation, World War III and Armageddon; the precepts supply it. Tribulation has to come, then World War III, then Armageddon, when Christ comes in the midst of World War III.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.” A great destruction.

The Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats to get out do not believe the angels are coming. Come up hither is the deliverance: the angels bear us up, as Psalm 91 says.

Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

“We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.” We are coming up on that moment now. And yet our people cheer the movies on Martin Luther King and Malcolm X. You may not agree with Martin's method, but how many of us would walk down the street knowing we would be beaten, jailed and have dogs sicced on us? Their stand ended Jim Crow, and in sixty years of that liberty, how have we used it? We shoot each other, besmirch one another and hate each other.

Jeremiah said, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” He wanted to leave black people. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men. And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Black people love to use their lips for lies.

“but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth”. They are valiant in the movie theatre. They cheer on Nat Turner in Birth of a Nation, cheer on Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, cheer the resistance in The Hunger Games and Star Wars, but they do not have that spirit and do not have the balls to do what those men did. They would never have joined Malcolm or Martin, and many will not join us out of fear. Two young boys got shot in the face in Georgia, instigated by a gaggle of other black men who scattered like cockroaches and played innocent when the cops came. So-called revolutionary brothers on podcasts call us a cult while including homosexuality and transgenderism; they have never left the couch.

“for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” That is why, in the time of Jacob's trouble, there is a voice of trembling and fear and not of peace.

“Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today. Then pay attention: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel 3:1 confuses some brothers: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read that alone and you think it means he is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Go back to Jeremiah 30:3. Notice the same words, except Jeremiah explains them: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” When he says he will bring again the captivity, he is speaking of bringing us back from captivity, not into captivity. Jeremiah explains Joel.

How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn't wake up one day as kids searching for the Lord of heaven and earth. The word was introduced to us and woke us up.

“I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.” We are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans. That is a nation not called by his name.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. We are that rebellious people, walking in Christianity and Islam, our people following their own thoughts in these religions. “A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and mosques. Then: “which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”. You know that's the church: there was always a swine fest at the end, pig feet and all of that; possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites on the street preaching: stand by yourself, I don't need no black Jesus, I'm washed in the blood of Jesus, I'm water baptized, I'm holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can't stand them.

That is the people Jeremiah calls an Outcast, “This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Those who think they are whole push away the physician; the sick who admit it are the ones he heals.

What Isaiah and Jeremiah say of the nation is the same thing Job went through. People read Job and think that was only him, but Job's real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. This was the fifth judgment on Job: “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” Didn't we just read that in Isaiah 1? “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”.

Job's life is Deuteronomy 28. He lost his businesses, his family, everything. And “There is none to plead thy cause”: Job had friends who would not stand up on his behalf. They were always telling him he was wrong, evil, the devil. There was no cure; God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel.

Even Job's wife turned on him in his darkest moment, when he had lost everything. That is how these black women do with us: in this state, the black woman turned on us.

But at the end of Job's life he was blessed. That is what is going to happen to us if we endure to the end: the incurable wound of Jeremiah 30 ends with “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”.

“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ right there.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

“In that day”, “I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”: that's Christ's return. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Uh-oh. Did you notice? David is alive.

Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

Christ says, “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Not at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. Read in context, it is tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don't believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me.

Paul testified what denying looks like from the persecutor's side: “Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.”

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ was talking about: deny me under torture, persecution, tribulation, hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Paul was not the only persecutor. What Paul did, they were all doing: the Pharisees, and later the inquisitors under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in the time of Spain and Portugal, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, to Africa, to Mexico, to South and North America.

And “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

Everybody in here says they love God, but some of us are liars. Some are not valiant for the truth; you are a professional student, a hireling. The hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. Think about being compelled to blaspheme, as in the film Unthinkable, where they brought in a man's wife and kids to make him confess. You think that could never happen to you; the devil is a liar. What Paul was doing is what Christ said is going to happen.

Christ says, “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”. They can't kill the real you, brothers and sisters. You think that body is the real you, but it is just a shell that corrodes in time. So why is our people so afraid to die? David shows it: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.”

Slavery, miseducation and religion are all part of that crafty counsel. Their religions make you think this is all there is, like the Sam Cooke song: I don't know what's up there beyond the sky. It puts a spirit of fear on you: if you die, you're going to hell and you're going to burn down there. So everybody is afraid to die.

But when you read the Bible, how come our foremothers and forefathers did not have the spirit we have today? They knew something we don't. The woman with the seven sons said, kill me now, cut my arms off, cut my tongue. We say, what the hell is this? Because the crafty counsel taught us lie after lie about reality: that after this you're done.

The Bible calls death sleep, many times. That's all it is, and you wake up before the Lord. Paul said to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. But do we believe that, or what the white man says on his television screens?

Christ goes on, “but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”: that is the lake of fire, which is not now. When you die now, everybody is at rest, even the wicked. When the Lord returns he takes the keys of hell and death and opens it all up, and that is when the lake of fire comes. So don't fear them that kill the body, because the things we teach will get us killed, and you will not deny Christ if you have not swallowed their crafty counsel.

“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: the churches argue about a seven-year dispensation, pre-trib and post-trib, and say the church is not going through tribulation. “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect? Not everybody.

Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. We are the elect. Israel is the elect. Not the Baptist church, and not all races on the planet.

And it is from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other, because Isaiah 66 already showed there are Israelites scattered in the isles afar off who have not heard his fame nor seen his glory, and we have to go get them.

Before that gathering, “then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”. It is going to be a happy day, but we will be crying and fearful too. And it comes only after the tribulation. “For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” All flesh. The slain of the Lord shall be many, and that is not just Esau. The wicked Israelites too.

That is why Christ is not coming tomorrow to rapture a comfortable church out of trouble. He comes with fire and sword against the nations of Idumea, and against every wicked one, including our own people who keep smoking, clubbing, and defiling the Sabbath. The powers of the heavens are shaken, his sword is bathed in heaven, and only his elect, Jacob and Israel who repented and endured, are gathered from the four winds.

Luke tells the same coming, and shows where we are in it. “And there shall be signs in the sun”, like a solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, blood moons and lunar eclipses, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we are seeing that now. “With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: the nations roaring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That is war. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top part of verse 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass”: the signs in the sun, the moon and the stars, the distress of nations with perplexity. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” We are supposed to be looking up and lifting up our heads, knowing redemption is soon to come.

But we know the order of what is going to happen: tribulation, war, then Christ. So this is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because the time is drawing close.

Revelation 7 has four angels holding the four winds of the earth. Let the Bible say what the wind is. Write it down: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

Where did the multitude come from? From the four winds of heaven. And what did they come for? To subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are their armies coming against the Son of God, coming against the master.

That is why the four angels hold the winds so they do not blow on the earth, the sea or any tree: the armies on land, the navies and marines on the sea, and the air force above the trees. The destruction is held back until the servants of God are sealed. When the 144,000 are sealed, the winds are let go, the nations gather for war, and after that tribulation the Son of man comes in the clouds of heaven.

“And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Why is iniquity going to abound? Because of the false prophets: the false Christians and these foolish Abrahamic religions teaching lie after lie. They glorify sin; sin is being glorified. And the love of many waxing cold means we are going to start to hate one another.

Ezra was told the same thing: “But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” The angel was telling Ezra that iniquity would go way beyond anything he had known or seen.

And look at it now. Men are cutting their privates off and having a vagina cut in there. That was unheard of. Women are getting penises sewn on. You cannot make this stuff up. Magic Johnson's son says he is only attracted to straight men; if he is attracted to you, he is not straight.

That is iniquity increased above anything heard of long ago, exactly as the angel said. So repent. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved”: we have to endure the hardships, the tribulation and the persecution Christ said would come, and not let our love wax cold.

Remember, the 144,000 have to be sealed, and then the end comes. Isaiah shows what they do: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000. He sends them “to Tarshish”, Spain; “Pul”, Libya; “and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey; “and Javan”, the Grecian islands; “to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”.

There will be people who have not heard the fame of the Lord and have not seen his glory: Israelites who have not heard or seen anything, and we have to go get them. “And they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” That is “this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”.

You might think that is talking about now. The next verse clears it up: “And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. Jerusalem is already established as holy. Is Jerusalem holy today? No, there are bombs and missiles going off there. So this is not now; the kingdom is already set up.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make them priests and Levites. With that, Matthew 24:14 gives a deeper understanding: the gospel preached in all the world is the work of the 144,000, and once they are sealed, the end comes.

In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and the destruction is held back “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

It is not the hexagram. Many of us thought so years ago when we were young. Isaiah says what it is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal of the living God is the law, bound up and sealed among his disciples. Pay attention, because if you blink you might miss it.

So the servants sealed in their foreheads are the ones with the law of God in their minds: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed, the four winds are loosed and the end comes. That is why this gospel, the law and the testimony, has to be preached in all the world for a witness: to seal the 144,000 before the end.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Earlier Christ said in Matthew 10, “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” So we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Then what does “all the world” mean, and when does the end come? Revelation 7 answers.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. That is the fighting, the wars. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies. “Nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies. “Nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. It is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” He cried to the four angels “to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”, hurt it with destruction: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

“And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” So the end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. The world Christ is talking about in Matthew 24 is the 144,000: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

Revelation 7:4 gives “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, and then verse 9 gives the great multitude. They say, see, we are all included. Ezra explains it crystal clear.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”. That is Revelation 7:4, the 144,000. “Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord”: new bodies. “Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord. Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

Then the part about time: he shall “think to change times and laws”. To see what he changed, go to what God set. “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.”

God himself appointed the first month of the year for Israel, at the time he brought them out of Egypt. The new year is not a date man picks. It is an ordinance of God, and it is one of the times the fourth beast thought to change.

Which month did God make the beginning of months? “This day came ye out in the month Abib.” Abib is the name of the first month of the ancient Hebrew calendar, generally corresponding to parts of March and April in the modern Gregorian calendar: the end of March into the beginning of April, the spring season.

The word comes from Hebrew and literally means ear of grain, young green ears, sprouting. It refers to the stage when barley is ripe but still soft, marking the start of the spring harvest. God's new year begins in spring, when the barley comes in.

So when you see Israelites celebrating Passover in the winter, they don't know what the hell they are talking about. The new year was changed from spring to the dead of winter. That is what God warns us about in Daniel 7:25: he shall “think to change times and laws”.

“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The lights in the heavens were set by God to mark the times.

“And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.” The first beast was Rome. You may think nobody worships Rome today. Really?

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

“Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not”. Very few understand that this is not their show. It is about the house of her husband. A wife after your mind is a woman who understands that she is in subjection to you and that you are the head of the home, so what you want is what she wants. She makes your desires her desires. Your aspirations become her aspirations. How you want things to be becomes how she wants things to be, because she understands her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself.

If her husband wants the environment this way, she makes the environment that way. If he wants the household this way, she makes the household this way. That is her job as the manager of the house: to make sure the CEO is happy. That is what a woman is supposed to do. But the world told her, no, it's yours, sis, you do what you want to do.

That is the last of the ten signs that she does not respect the Christ in you: she does not follow your lead spiritually, does not align with your direction in this truth, and picks and chooses what to follow. A wife after your mind is the opposite, and that is the wife Peter speaks of. By being in subjection to her own husband, her chaste conversation can win even a man that obeys not the word. The one who used to be loud and argue now does what he asks without challenging his authority, and he says, the word did that? Let me go see what those brothers in purple and gold are talking about.

Through submission you can move mountains with a man. When she knows she is right and still stands down because he is the head and has the final say, he is left with hot coals on his head, knowing she is more righteous than he is. It changes a man. That is a wife not to forsake.

Paul fears “lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted”. Satan is able to see what is within you, and that is what he attacks: not the stuff you are strong in, but the stuff you are weak in. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The temptation comes from something already within you.

So if you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, wanting to be over your husband, wanting to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home. Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That little bit of power feels good: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. Then you start overstepping your bounds and do not even know it was Satan who set you up with the curtains. Sisters, when you start to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan, you almost got me.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset: birthdays, baby showers, Mother's Day and Father's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger, rules God did not make that we think are how life is supposed to be. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. A father who told his son, get your money, the hoes are going to come, and left a condom on his dresser for him, normalized it. That residue has to be let go completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

It is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. And some brothers take themselves out of that role and want to be a mama's boy in the marriage, wanting her to mother them instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child and that is how she speaks to you. Both are drawn away by their own lust, and Satan works subtly on what is already within.

When a man takes a wife and says, “I took this woman, and when I came to her, I found her not a maid”, who is the accusation against? The father. It is his household. He brought his daughter forth saying, this is my daughter, she is a virgin, I have taken care of her, I have watched over her.

That is why Sirach speaks to fathers: “Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.” You are not supposed to be your children's friend. You are their parent, over them, the head of the household, losing sleep watching over your children. A daughter learns order from the household in the beginning, and her father is the first form of respect she has: honouring her father and her mother. Show yourself cheerful and you begin to blur the lines, and once the lines are blurred, so is her perception of authority. So when she gets older, how is she going to deal with her husband?

“Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter”. It is weighty because the man now has the power you had over your beloved daughter: the little girl you brought into this world, watched after and lost sleep over. Her clothes, her food, her home, where she lays her head: he is in charge now. If I marry my daughter to a crazy negro, I failed; I did not vet him. So if I am going to give that power to somebody, I am damn sure going to make sure he is going to do right by her. That is the father's job, to make sure he is the one.

That is what stands behind Deuteronomy 22: the father who kept his daughter brings forth “the tokens of the damsel’s virginity unto the elders of the city in the gate”, the proof that he performed his charge, and the elders “shall take that man and chastise him” for bringing up an evil name upon her.

When Ephesians 5 is read, some think there's wiggle room: that doesn't really mean that. This makes complete sense on the brothers' side of the room: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

Provide means her food, her raiment, her clothing. Lord, I didn't eat pork, I didn't eat shrimp or lobster, I stopped dealing with the prostitutes, I kept the Sabbath day holy. But you didn't take care of your wife or your kids. You were a deadbeat; you did nothing for her; you left the house, living among everybody else doing what you wanted, saying, I'm not dealing with that woman no more. That was your wife. That man has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church”. Is that an option? If I don't do that, will I see the kingdom? The natural thing for the evil man on this side of the earth is to be promiscuous, to roam, with nothing holding him down. Is that love? No.

So what makes you think it's any different when a wife doesn't submit? Your level of faith is shown by the level of respect you have for your husband, because that is the level of respect you have for God. The same goes for the man: the way you love and care for your wife is the level of love you have for Christ. If you don't love, protect and provide for her, you're an infidel; if you don't respect your husband and do what he says, you're an infidel. Fringes and every Sabbath don't matter.

Paul addresses it in almost all of his writings: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.” What is fit in the Lord? As the Lord has designed. Can you truly say you are in the truth and not respect that man? You can't, no matter how long you have been sitting here.

We understand that, just as we men have residue from the world to beat, our wives do too; they are the weaker vessel, and Satan often comes through the woman to destroy the house. So we have to dwell with them according to knowledge and cast down every imagination with the scriptures. Sisters, your toughest plight in this truth is going to be honoring your husband. You tolerate all those folks at the job and listen to the boss; your husband is supposed to get many times more respect than him, and you never clock out. Even your anatomy tells you that you are to be submissive; it's the world telling you that you have options.

Reverence is deep respect for someone or something. Respect is deep admiration: esteem, regard, admiration, veneration, awe. That is what you are to have for your husband, even if he snores or limps when he walks, because you chose him. Imagine arguing with Christ: you can't even put that together in your mind. If he says park the car in that spot, it's law.

And if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The Deacon's daughter Mimi comes running to the door, Daddy!, and she can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you've got to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel he is everything he's supposed to be, and watch what happens. Get your spirit right, and you'll see that Ephesians 5 man you want.

“let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” There is no room for options there. Nowhere does the scripture say you can respect him as long as he does this or that. If that's in your mind, you're led by the damn devil. Nobody says, I won't eat pork unless; I'll keep the Sabbath day if. No.

Your whole duty in life: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” There is no excuse for not observing a commandment.

Now, if you are being beaten in a relationship, are we telling you to stay, sister? No. If he's beating you to a pulp, get away from him. Don't die, sister. He obviously isn't keeping the commandments if he's harming you. But if he is not asking you to sin, you do not have a reason. You show him through your chaste conversation and your actions that you are going to serve the Lord no matter what; you heap hot coals on his head.

Disrespect should never be an option. Only Satan gives you that option. If submission depends on his behavior, it isn't submission; it's manipulation. God told you to submit without a caveat, because it is a commandment, and keeping the commandments is the whole duty.

“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” The same respect you would show to Christ is the respect you should show your husband. There are going to be sisters who find out they are not going to get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husband. Some sisters said, damn, so we're going to go to hell because we're disrespectful? Yes. You didn't realize that?

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?” They are going to have the audacity: Lord, I taught classes, I was out in the streets handing out flyers, I didn't eat pork, I left the shrimp alone, I wore fringes every day. “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

What could keep them from knowing the Lord? Iniquity: sin. Sister, every command your husband gives you is law. It is like getting orders from God for you. As long as your husband is not asking you to sin, if he asks you to do something, it is sin if you don't do it.

In the westernized mindset that doesn't compute: he has that much power? You malfunction because you don't believe he is a god; you don't see the Christ in him. You had better read your Bible. He absolutely has that much authority over you, and all the wonderful works in the world will not cover the iniquity of disrespecting him.

Moses repeats the commandment: “Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

It was so important for them to honour their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged, so they would not die, and so it would go well with them in the land. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation.

When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, there are going to be problems, and it affects the whole nation. Certain households affect other households. If your house is out of order and you are best friends with so-and-so, your kids play together and learn the same bad behaviours. If a sister is a gossiper running from home to home and she is your wife's best friend, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too. Same with you: kick it with the murmurers and you will murmur.

You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, always has been. A child raised in a household where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God is more likely to carry that legacy on. Everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

Respect is taught in childhood, and it starts with “Honour thy father and thy mother.” Leviticus says it the same way: “Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.”

The Lord understands the importance of structure, and it has always been there. You are to fear every man his mother and his father, and that goes on into old age. Don't think that once you turn 20 you don't have to listen. That power is always there: you honour your father and your mother.

And wives, once you become someone's wife, you also have your husband to deal with. The same power a father has over his daughter is handed over to her husband when he gives her away, so the respect a child learns for father and mother is the first line of the respect a wife owes her husband. That is how honouring father and mother connects to a wife respecting her husband.

Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.
