The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

“He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity”: that is the judgment of God. He that led the children of Israel into captivity shall go into captivity. I don’t want any freaking reparation; I want vengeance. The people that enslaved us, I want them enslaved and paying for what they did to our people. “He that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword.” Weren’t we killed in Africa and over here with the sword? God says they must be killed with the sword.

What is this judgment for? It is the judgment for verse 7: “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.” What you have to understand is that slavery was war. Colonization was war. The white man made war with us, and he overcame us by enslaving us. Verses 9 and 10 answer that war with the same measure.

“Here is the patience and the faith of the saints”: this is what you have to believe. Psalm 149: “To execute vengeance upon the heathen, and punishments upon the people; To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron; To execute upon them the judgment written: this honour have all his saints.” Their kings, Prince Harry and his little sons, made slaves the same way they made us and our people slaves; their nobles in chains.

The judgment written is: as thou hast done, it shall be done to you. And all the gold the nations stole, they will bring to us when Christ returns: that is the restitution. To hell with your reparations: judgment.

Deuteronomy 11:12 says the land God gives is “A land which the Lord thy God careth for: the eyes of the Lord thy God are always upon it”. God has his eyes upon a specific place for us. But there is another land his eyes are upon for a different reason.

“Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. America is a sinful kingdom, and God is looking at America to destroy it. “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord.” Jacob is the father of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” We were scattered into all nations in slavery and captivity, so he will sift us out of every place we went. The sifting is a teaching process: our people have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, their oppressors and enslavers, and now they must be trained in the word of God to establish the house of Israel.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Those are our people who are rebellious to what God has to say and want to do things their own way. That is what America, aka Egypt, has convinced you to believe: nothing can happen to you here. You hear Donald Trump saying we have the strongest military, no one can stop us, open the Strait of Hormuz or I will blow you back to kingdom come. Stop believing you cannot be touched because this man talks tough and proud. America's kingdom is temporary; the strength that lasts comes from keeping God's commandments.

Amos 9:9 says, “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations”. Christians read Matthew 28:19 and think it means make everyone disciples: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”.

This is what it means: because we were scattered into all nations, we have to be taught in all nations. It is the same sifting Amos speaks of. Christ himself, when he started his ministry, told the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles”, but “go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Teaching all nations is going into all the nations where the lost sheep were scattered.

That is why the bishop gives the order: look historically at where our people were slaves, and go there and train them how to behave for God, to establish the kingdom. They have been trained after the ways of their colonizers, so we must train them in the word of God. The brothers who travel find the hardest thing is telling oppressed people that Jesus Christ is not a white man, because that white Jesus, made up in the Renaissance, is how the colonizers modified their behavior. But the charge stands: tell our people, you are not black, not Hispanic, not West Indian, not African; you are the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

“Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” When the Bishop says separate that brother for the work, he is not talking about Atlanta. He is not talking about Miami or California. Did Israel only scatter in Atlanta? Did Israel only scatter in America? Separate them for the work means no matter where the work is, you have to go there.

The prophecy shows where the work is: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”. Not in America, not in Florida: among the nations. “and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” You know what that scripture is saying? No matter where you go, you are going to see Israelites. That is why a judge must be able to travel. Captain Joham just came from Trinidad and Suriname keeping Passover with the brothers there.

So the work Barnabas and Saul were separated for is the same work now: going to the nations where the Lord scattered Israel. It was the Most High God who called you, not the bishop, deacon or captain, and once hands are laid on you, you are sent away. When the phone call comes to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you but yes. Paul travelled, departing unto Seleucia and sailing to Cyprus, and we continue the Acts of the Apostles, bringing the good news all over the world, whatever hate we get for it.

Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

We were warned: “in the last days perilous times shall come”, and among the men of those days are “false accusers.” Sirach gives the law against it: “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.”

You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. How many people run their mouth without understanding, without knowing? How many gossip without the full understanding of what is going on, yet have so many opinions and thoughts on how this should be, on what so-and-so is doing and shouldn’t be doing? You look foolish when you do this without understanding what is going on.

If your opinion lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information needed to explain what is going on, but you still feel it necessary to give it, something is wrong with you. You have been put in many situations that showed you that you jumped the gun, that you didn’t know what was going on. Yet and still you feel your opinion matters. It doesn’t. Understand first, and then rebuke.

That goes with the pride Paul names. The prideful spirit won’t allow you to take any correction or accept what is being said; it has you thinking it is everybody but you. And it goes with the “despisers of those that are good”: people who hate that you are doing what you are supposed to do, that you are above them in rank and active in the body. Every time you turn around they have a suggestion nobody asked for, and they don’t say it to you; they tell everybody underneath you, so all your peers know how they feel. You never know them for exhorting anybody, only for bringing problems about everything they see.

The law says “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.” The talebearer with the tea, who somehow knows before leadership knows, is the fuel that keeps reputations scarred and people at odds. And when you tell a story as if you know what is going on, without the whole story, and it is not true, that is a lie: “he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” That is why you must examine the truth before you blame.

Peter says, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. That phrase “another nation” might throw you off, because Christians use it to say Peter was going to other races. Ezekiel shows what that other nation is: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The kingdom of Judah was called a nation, and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was called a nation. Two nations, two separate kingdoms, but one people. So when Peter the Jew, of Judah, speaks of coming unto one of another nation, that other nation is the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom. That is what the vision of the sheet was about: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean”, speaking of Cornelius and his family.

Then Peter says God “is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” A Christian will stop you right there, but read the next verse: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”. That tells you who Cornelius and his kinfolk were: the children of Israel, scattered in every nation.

Acts 15 looks back on this and quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. The regathering of the twelve tribes, the two kingdoms coming back together, is what Acts 10 is about. God is bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back into one nation, just as Ezekiel said.

Paul and Barnabas tell Judah, “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”, but the scribes and them were rejecting it, so “lo, we turn to the Gentiles.” Before that, those scattered abroad after the persecution about Stephen were “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only”: only to the tribe of Judah. So who are the Gentiles they turned to?

Matthew answers it: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls them Gentiles. When Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles, they turned to the northern kingdom Israelites.

That is what the vision of Peter in Acts 10 was about. Peter said “it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation”. Christians use that to say other races, but Ezekiel shows the two kingdoms were two nations: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” Judah was a nation and the kingdom of Israel, Ephraim and the rest, was a nation. And Peter’s own words about Cornelius and his kin folk are “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ”.

Acts 15 looks back on Acts 10: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. The kingdom was split, Judah, Benjamin and Levi on one side, Ephraim and the rest on the other. Turning to the Gentiles is God bringing the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom back together, the regathering of the twelve tribes.

Sirach says the man whose whole occupation is his worldly job shall not “understand the sentence of judgment”. Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? Proverbs answers: “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

That is the brother who is always confused. When leadership makes a judgment, he doesn't agree, even if he disagrees in silence. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job, not the word of God, so you are always confused. And the Bible says you are evil.

So that brother “shall not be sought for in publick counsel”. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your work, your job. He will not “sit high in the congregation” or have rank, and he will not “be found where parables are spoken”, because he could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

But they that seek the Lord understand all things. Chapter 39 shows the flip side: the one that “giveth his mind to the law of the most High”. He seeks out the wisdom of the ancients, is found where the subtle parables are, and he shall serve among great men and appear before princes.

The Lord tells Jacob, “Fear not”, and promises, “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty.” Thirsty for what? Thirsty for the truth. Paul shows what that water is: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” The water represents the word of God.

Read Isaiah with that in mind. “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”: I will pour the word of God upon them that are thirsty for the truth. “and floods upon the dry ground”: the floods also represent the word of God, poured out on the dry ground, these places wherein we dwell. “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring”: his spirit upon his people and his blessing upon their children.

God only chose Israel, and this washing is for his chosen, Jacob and Jesurun, “whom I have chosen.” The Lord made us and formed us from the womb, and he will help us.

When the word is poured out, “they shall spring up as among the grass.” That is what we are looking at now: the Israelites are waking up and springing up worldwide like grass. And verse 5 shows three kinds of Israelites waking up: one says “I am the Lord’s”, acknowledging we are the children of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; another takes on a new name and calls himself “by the name of Jacob”; another changes his surname and will “surname himself by the name of Israel.” It is the word of God, the water, that cleanses them and brings them back.

The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, “shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Why would we need to remember the things Christ said? Because we would be made to forget. Through slavery the nations annihilated our twelve tribes, burned our records and beat us into submission, and we forgot what Christ said.

What did he say? That he would gather his elect from the four corners of the earth. That he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

The Holy Spirit causes us to remember these things. If you don't remember them, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you. Keeping the commandments is the love Christ asks for, and the Spirit brings back to our remembrance who we are and what he said.

That is what is happening now: brothers and sisters waking up worldwide. Isaiah 44 promised it to Jacob, whom the Lord chose: “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”, the word upon those thirsty for the truth, and “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: And they shall spring up as among the grass”. The Israelites are springing up worldwide like grass.

“Go not into the way of the Gentiles”: in this verse that includes the other eleven tribes. “And into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not”: that is the Northern Kingdom. Why? Because it was not their time yet. The Lord said he would raise the tents of Judah first. “But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that starts with Judah first.

Some are confused and think this is new. It is not; it has always been taught. Acts shows the order being followed after Christ: “Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.”

To none but the Jews only: only to Judah. They were primarily dealing with Judah first.

That does not mean the rest were never to be reached. Christ himself went to Samaria in John 4 and taught the Samaritans for a few days, because he knew the time was coming to deal with them. Judah first, and then the other tribes.

The disciples went first to Judah, “preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” Then watch what Paul says: “Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?”

“Even us”: the tribe of Benjamin and all the other tribes. “Whom he hath called, not of the Jews only”: not of Judah only. “But also of the Gentiles”: the other eleven tribes.

Some were perverting Zechariah 12:7, where the Lord raises the tents of Judah first, as if it meant only Judah. Judah first is the order, not the whole. So go back to Matthew 10 with a better understanding: “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” In the beginning it was Judah first; afterward the call went to the rest of the tribes. There is no contradiction once you know the order.

People say the people in the land of Israel today are the Jews. That is not what the Bible says. After the tribulation, when the stars fall (the missiles) and the powers of the heavens are shaken (nations warring against each other), “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Notice the angels do not go to one land to gather this people. Christ is letting us know the Israelites would not be in a land; they would be scattered worldwide.

Who is the elect? Some say anybody who worships. Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. That is the elect: Israel, scattered in the four winds from one end of heaven to the other.

Before the angels come for them, the Lord calls to the heavens and to the earth: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” The saints are “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”, and only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. The call to the heavens is to the angels; the call to the earth is to us.

So the message for us on earth is the same as the angels' commandment: gather the saints. We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel, scattered worldwide, which is why the gospel has to go out to every land.

Christ said he would send his angels to gather the elect from the four winds, and Isaiah names the elect: “Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.” The Israelites would not be in one land; they would be scattered worldwide. Before the angels come for them, the Lord says, “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” So who are the saints?

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

Now read Psalms 50 again with that. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels he is calling to. “and to the earth”: the earth is you and I. And the message to both is the same, “Gather my saints together unto me.” That is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect, and it is the commandment to the prophets on earth too.

“those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. So we are not supposed to be looking for other races and other nationalities. The work of gathering is for the twelve tribes of Israel, the saints, scattered to the four corners of the earth.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?” How can our people call on the Almighty God that loves them when they have not believed in that God? Our people have believed in a strange god, a Eurocentric god. We are the only race that has a god that does not look like us. The God we serve is not the same God as the white man.

Daniel shows it: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory”. That white Jesus is a strange god. “And he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” The white man divided Africa for gain. That is what the Bible says he did.

Why is that god strange? Because he does not look like you. He has no laws, statutes or commandments. And he whooped you in slavery. We know that was the white man, yet we run on Sunday morning and pray faithfully to the same white man that shot us down in the streets and raped our mothers and fathers. Strange god.

“And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Because we have been following a strange god all our lives, someone must be sent. That is why we send brothers out, only brothers with a good name: “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” The glad tidings are that you are the Israelites, Christ died for you and your race, and he is coming back to save our race.

Zechariah says Zion, Judah, “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The key is who the daughter of Babylon is. The psalm names her: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” The word rase means destroy it: destroy it even to the foundation.

Then the very next words: “O daughter of Babylon.” Notice what it is calling them now. It is calling Edom, the so-called white folks, the daughter of Babylon.

So the scripture lets you know Judah would live among Edom, and where? In the land of the north. That is why the Lord cries, “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north.” The group of Judah in North America is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon, the children of Edom who wanted Jerusalem razed to the ground.

And the Lord's word to that people is: “he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” We are God's favorite, and the nations which spoiled us will answer for it.

Zechariah says, “come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: flee from North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: all Israel scattered, like we read in Matthew 24 and James 1. Then he singles out one group: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.”

Many scriptures tell us that Zion represents the twelve tribes. But in this context, which Zion is it? Asaph answers: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is the Zion right there.

So “Deliver thyself, O Zion” is talking about Judah: deliver yourself, Judah. That does not mean all the Judahites are in the land of the north; Judah was dispersed like all the other tribes. But God is pinpointing a particular group of Judah that would be in the land of the north, dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.

That fits the rest of the prophecy. In these last days the Lord raises up Judah first: the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”, and the blessing of Judah is, “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” The voice of Judah is the teaching of Judah, carried to the other eleven tribes.

Zephaniah says, “for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride”. Who rejoices in our pride? Sirach proves what pride is: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”.

Pride is departing from God, going against his commandments; it is our sin. So those that rejoice in our pride are the ones that rejoice in us going against God's commandments: the pastors, the Christians, the churches, the Democrats and the Republicans. They rejoice in us not keeping God's commandments. The Lord says, I am going to take them out of you, take them away from you, “and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain”, the land of Israel.

What he leaves is “an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the Lord.” The elect beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, the daughter of his dispersed, a large portion of them on the continent of Africa, are afflicted and very poor, as we saw going throughout Africa keeping Passover and the feast of unleavened bread. They must be taught to trust in the name of the Lord.

“The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies”, because they are being taught the commandments, and that is what we go out there for. No, Jesus is not white; no, he was not born December 25th; no, we are not to pray to Mary or to the ancestors. Sin has always been the problem, and breaking God's commandments is a sign of unbelief. When the ones who rejoice in our departing from God are taken away, the remnant shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
blog/2026/2026-05-02-2026-05-02-the-retu:
“Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin.” Our people take counsel, but not of God. The covering they cover themselves with is not his spirit: it is Christianity and it is politics, Democrat and Republican, and with it they add sin to sin.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” Literally, our people went down into ancient Egypt for help against Babylon, after God told Jeremiah to warn them not to go. But there is a double meaning. A shadow is not the real thing. The shadow of Egypt is America, the great city that Revelation 11:8 says is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

Peter laid out the instructions for marriages, because hard times are coming. We see marriage troubles where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor and she calls him lazy; or a sister gives up the faith and wants to go back to the damn world and be a h-o-e to negro Tyrone instead of a wife to the husband the Lord gave her; or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming, when you will be worried about surviving. How much more in a household where a man and woman are striving and going back and forth with each other?

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.” Sisters, your tone, how you speak toward your husband, especially in hard times, means a lot. How you respect your lord, your king in your household, and how you carry yourself toward him shows the level of your faith. You sisters have to increase your faith and learn how to be correct with the man God gave you. And not just husband and wife: all you sisters must honor the men of your nation.

In hard times Satan attacks marriage. He did not attack the government Adam set up first; he attacked the foundation, the marriage, which shows how powerful marriage is. And he did it by going through the woman first, which is why you sisters have to build yourselves up.

The Bible says marriage is honorable and the bed undefiled: righteous marriage, husband and wife, as with Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Joseph and Mary, not man and man or woman and woman. Keeping that honorable is part of suffering for righteousness' sake and being happy in it.

Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

The believers in Acts 4 “were of one heart and of one soul” and “had all things common”. To keep from losing ourselves, selling ourselves out and losing our souls, we have to grow the same way. Paul shows what pulls us away: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

The seducing spirits are money and wealth, the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the blitz last week, kids said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that actually build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. And there are men and women in the faith who want to leave this and go to the world and stream.

The “doctrines of devils” are religion, man-made religion. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy” is politics: a lie that makes you feel assimilated into a government that is kicking you out of it. If you are Israel, what they call black, you cannot be in their government. There is one black governor in this whole country, and all the black generals have been taken out as not qualified. They are making their country great again in their eyes.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.” Religion, politics and the gifts of this world sear the conscience. Money, riches and comfort should not be your god; the American dream is a lie. Having all things in common, in faith and understanding, is what keeps us from departing from the faith.

“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come.” In perilous times we have to start having all things in common, like the believers of Acts 4, and build our faith.

“For men shall be lovers of their own selves”: going for likes, not worried about being an aid to your society or your community. It is me, me, me: how many likes and followers do I have? It is not about you, negro. It is about your people. “Covetous, boasters”: boasting of vanity, money, drugs, houses, cars, women. “Proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful”: not appreciative of God and what he has done for you. “Unholy, Without natural affection”.

This is the nature of them that go after the world, that go after the gift that destroys the heart. The one who is a lover of himself holds on to what he has; the believers in Acts 4 said none of the things they possessed was their own.

So we have to stop living beyond our means and be content with our wages and content in life. A family of seven may need a house with a little room, but if you are a single brother, why are you buying a mansion and expensive cars? Do you know the times we are living in? There is coming a time when you will not be worrying about maintaining your BMW. Riches and comfort, keeping up with the Joneses and the American lie of a dream, should not be your god.

The same chapter shows what having all things common looked like: “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

That is the point. We have to begin to live below our means, not beyond them. This nation of ours is a big nation, and there are millions of our people that lack. When you sacrifice your much, it is much to them that have little.

The only way to experience that, to let what you have help those who have little, is to travel. We must go and spread this gospel abroad, and that is part of why we go out into the nations.

The believers of Acts 4 had prayed, the place was shaken, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost and spake the word with boldness. Out of that came one heart and one soul, and out of one heart and one soul came a people among whom no one lacked. That is the same order we need now: faith first, and then a nation that looks after its own.

Amos shows an Israel that hates the righteous: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” They tread upon the poor, build houses of hewn stone and plant pleasant vineyards, “but ye shall not dwell in them”. Don't be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying. A few verses on he tells them what to hate instead: “Hate the evil, and love the good”.

David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God's commandments: sin. We are supposed to hate sin, hate the fact that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We are not supposed to tolerate evil amongst our people.

Love the good is love God's commandments. That is your purpose, it is what increases your faith, and it is why you are called to magnify God's law.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Then “it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.” You receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good. That is the turn Amos calls for: stop hating the one who rebukes in the gate, and hate the sin instead. We separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor, and we strive for perfection.

Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

Job 36:10 says the Lord “openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity”: he commanded, requested and called you to return from iniquity back to your heritage. Verse 15 shows where he opens those ears: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The poor here are our people. It was through the oppression of the oppressor, and through the religion he gave us, that our ears were opened. Esau is not poor. They are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We are a people robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42 says, and it is being played out in real time.

Just because you are not in the prison system doesn't mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28:15-68 applies to us: the Lord gave us the warning, we didn't take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment was supposed to end slavery, but its clause, except as punishment for crime, made the loophole that fills the prisons with our people for free labor. Slavery was never abolished; it evolved. They framed mischief and made it law, like the throne of iniquity that “frameth mischief by a law.” A warden speaks of a young man's sweat equity instead of the death penalty, the same spirit as the Willie Lynch letter: don't kill him, it's not good economics.

This is still the land of our captivity, and the enemy got crafty with us. But in that oppression the Lord opened our ears. We were deaf and now we hear discipline; we were blind and now we see. We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” What are we coming out of? What this society promotes: adultery, the music, murder, sodomy, homosexuality, drunkenness, drug abuse, idolatry, wicked entertainment and corruption. All the things God hates, against his laws, statutes and commandments, and all of it deceives us. We must expose this evil so you can learn how to save your own soul. Look at what they call the YNs: our people smoking, toting guns, women with guns bigger than they are, little kids holding bullets. And then they call us a hate group when we are trying to stop the evil within our own community first.

Sin is deceitful, and America has blurred the line. Your president even asks, what do you have to lose? Choose the worst of both evils. Isaiah 5:20: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Woe is destruction unto them. That is how they blur the line between good and evil.

Who does that? Your pastor. Many a black church on every corner facilitates the continuance of your oppression. So you have to choose a side: righteousness, your heritage, your nation, keeping God’s commandments.

That is the second step: study, pray, apply, see yourself in the scriptures, and then show your faith by separating yourself from evil. Our purpose is Acts 26:18: “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God”. That is coming out of her.

The first step is study, pray and apply: do your research, and then turn from sin. Then we have to learn how to turn all of this evil and mischief into righteousness, from the power of Satan to God, from darkness unto light. Romans 12 lays out the steps: “Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.” Come home, family.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: looking out for each other and honoring one another within our marriages, our relationships and our nation. “Not slothful in business”: our business is that we are called by God to magnify the law and increase our faith. “Fervent in spirit; serving the Lord”: doing the work and helping your people. “Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints”. What better life to live than to help your people?

And the chapter ends with the sum of it: “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” Do not let this world destroy your faith.

How do we overcome? With the good of these commandments and the faith of Christ, and knowing who you are. You overcome that evil with the good of this Bible. Love without dissimulation, brotherly love, fervency, patience and prayer are the good that overcomes the evil around us.

Read Ecclesiastes 1:9 again with that: “and that which is done is that which shall be done”. The same thing man did in the past, he is going to come back and do again. “there is no new thing under the sun.” If you were wicked in the past, you are going to be wicked again when you come back on the earth. That is why the scripture says he that is righteous, let him be righteous still, and he that is evil, let him be evil still. If you are righteous, you will gravitate to righteous brothers and sisters; if you are wicked, to wicked people.

Why is this important? Because what was done to us in slavery is a circle coming back around. God's judgment is as a ring. Slavery isn't over; the white man put a fake smile on his face, and now he is showing his real face. It is the same people coming back to do the same thing. Antiochus died long ago under the Greeks, yet the scripture says he shall stand up against the Prince of princes, because the same spirit that came against the holy people is going to do it again.

The proverb was, “The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”: the present generation punished for the offences of their forefathers. The people were prone to plead their innocence: listen, I am this way because my father was this way. But the Lord said, “ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.” I am not letting you use the fact that you have been through intergenerational trauma, or that your fathers weren't right.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on out, you are not going to say, well, my daddy was wicked, so I am just going to be wicked by default. No, you are going to change it.

Verse 14 shows the son who does: “Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”. The son sees everything his father did, considers it, and does not do the same. A son can see it and change.

So the proverb is broken by a son who looks at his father's ways with open eyes. The iniquity we were shapen in is real, but it is not a sentence we have to serve; the son who considers and does not do such like is the proof that it can be changed.

The people still asked, “Yet say ye, Why? doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father?” That is the sour grapes proverb again. The Lord answers: “When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father”.

In other words, yes, intergenerational trauma is real. But do you just sit in it, or do you change? This son changed. If there is a son who changes and does what is right according to the Lord, he is not going to die, although his father will. Just because our fathers were wicked, just because our mothers didn't know God's laws and taught us evil, that is not an excuse to stay in this. That trauma is real; you must recognise it and move on from it.

“neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.” Each soul answers for itself.

And the Lord still has mercy on the sick. Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick”, and “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” That is every last one of us. Although we have been through trauma and traumatic experiences, we cannot use the excuse of what we have been through anymore. Christ has given us a clean slate, and the way to walk in it is to keep his statutes and do them.

Ezekiel 36:24-28 is the Lord changing us: gathered out of all countries, sprinkled with clean water, which is the commandments of God, given a new heart, a new mind, a new body, a new nervous system, with the stony, sinful heart that Adam had taken away. Then verse 33 shows what comes next: “Thus saith the Lord God; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded.”

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. First the Lord changes you; now he changes the land to conform to you. The Lord made it for us; the world was made for us. But he can't give us Jerusalem the way it is supposed to be right now, because we are in the midst of sin.

So he says: let me remove the sin, let me cleanse you, let me give you a new heart, let me remove that weak, brittle body and give you immortality. Then he will command the land to transform into the garden of Eden. We are going right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we are going to be with our father Adam again: his name is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, in the same place.

“and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.” The nations will say, God is with these people. He has spoken it, and he will do it.

Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us elite, the top people on the planet earth, holy and right. “how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, wow, y'all degenerate.

How did we become that degenerate plant? Verse 19 tells us: “Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee”. That is how we became degenerate: our own wickedness. “know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Are we feeling it now, brothers and sisters? Look at our conditions: the trauma, poverty, fatherlessness and broken families, the curse of Deuteronomy 28 passed from one generation to the next. That is the bitterness of having forsaken the Lord.

So our mission is the one in Maccabees: “Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” We have to restore the decayed state of our people: learn the word of God, apply it to our lives, and go out and teach our people, so the degenerate plant becomes the noble vine again.

Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.

“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Some who are older have parents who are not in this truth, and they might think that because their parent is not in the truth they do not have to give them the respect of a parent. That is not what the Lord said. It is no glory that your father or mother is not in this truth, and nothing to glory in because the Lord called you.

“For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.”

“My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth.” You are to be an aid to your parent when they reach a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. “And if his understanding fail, have patience with him”. We are the only nation of people that does not take care of our elders. Where do you think nursing homes come from? The children do not want to deal with their parents at a certain age, so they pay somebody else to watch after them. That is how we honour our parents.

The Deacon has a real disdain for children who do not honour their parents, because his died when he was young and he went through the system with no mother and father, though his grandparents took him in. To have your parents, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that is a problem.

“And despise him not when thou art in thy full strength.” Be patient, because the example we set is what the young men see; we are their goalpost.

Christ sent Paul, “Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light”. To open our eyes, and turn us from darkness to light: from sin to righteousness.

So “that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.”

That is the other side of Jude. Some are bound in chains of darkness, loving darkness rather than light, ordained of old to that condemnation. But the ones Paul was sent to are turned from darkness to light and from Satan unto God, sanctified by faith in Christ. That is the faith once delivered unto the saints that we are earnestly contending for, casting down Esau's lies about fallen angels and Nephilim.

Jude says the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved “in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” Has that great day come yet, brothers? No. Those sons of God who went in unto the daughters of men were destroyed in the flood, and those spirits came right back, by way of the three sons, Ham, Shem and Japheth. They are still here today.

John shows what that darkness is: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men loving darkness rather than light is sin: you hate God's laws, you hate this truth, you hate the Bible.

There are people like that who were ordained of old to stay like that, the “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. Remember 2 Thessalonians: God gave them up to strong delusion, that they should believe a lie and not repent and come into the light. Some people are bound in that darkness, and there is nothing you can do for them. That is the chains of darkness, reserved unto the judgment of the great day.

The three unclean spirits like frogs come “out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet.” Those three unclean spirits are politics, religion and finance. To see the first of them, go to the beast of Revelation 13.

John says, “I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.” Those two horns like a lamb are the two political parties, the Democrats and the Republicans: two political systems that look gentle like a lamb. But he speaks as a dragon.

That is the politics, the frog that comes out of the mouth of the dragon. And what comes out of a mouth? Communication, and that communication is propaganda, persuasion and lies. These are “the spirits of devils”, and they do not stay at home: they “go forth unto the kings of the earth and of the whole world”, gathering them “to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.”

The second frog comes “out of the mouth of the beast.” Go back to Revelation 13: “he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.”

That no man might buy or sell: that is the finance, one of the three unclean spirits like frogs, alongside the politics and the religion.

It is coming to a time where, if you are not in cahoots with, in support of, or in allegiance with what America pushes, you will not be able to buy or sell. On a large scale that is trade between nations, but it is also the regular buying and selling of everyday life. That is why they are trying to do away with the currency as it is now and bring everything into a digital system: to monitor God's people who speak up against this society.

The third frog, out of the mouth of the false prophet, is Christianity, their religion and their religious systems. Politics, finance and religion together are the spirits of devils working miracles, going out to the kings of the whole world, not only here at home.

John says it twice. In Revelation 19 he fell at the angel's feet, and here again: “I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.”

And the angel says the same thing again: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” He will not take worship, because he is not God. He is a fellowservant, one of the brethren.

That is who the angels are: our brothers. They are not demons. They ate with Lot because they have mouths just like us, and they were going to lie down because they look like us. Esau calls them humanoids, and to Esau they are going to be some demons, but those are our brothers. The angels have tribes too, and in Revelation 21, do not be surprised if the angels standing at the twelve gates are each standing at the gate of their own tribe.

Now Raphael makes himself known: “I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” The one Tobit called brother, Azarias of his brethren, was the angel all along.

Why do the angels present the prayers of the saints? Because they minister unto us. They are ministering spirits working on our behalf, because those are our brothers.

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. The world is being taught to call what comes out of the heavens demons and fallen angels, so that it will gather to fight against Christ and his army. But the angels are our brethren, fellowservants who keep the testimony of Jesus, and we worship God alone.

Here Raphael, before he makes himself known, presents himself to Tobit another way: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” An angel of God naming himself as one of the brethren, just as the angel told John, “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.”

Tobit answers, “Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock.” Tobit asks after his tribe and his family, and receives him as a brother.

He knows his people: “I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brethren: my brother, thou art of a good stock.”

So the angel who walked with Tobit's son was taken for an Israelite brother, of a tribe and a family. That is how close the angels are to us: they look like us, they have tribes too, and they are our brethren.

Revelation says the armies were gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse and against his army. Ezra saw that same war. “there arose a wind from the sea”, and “that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled.” The man that came out of the sea is Christ, with the thousands of heaven, the armies that follow him.

And “whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” He speaks the laws out of his mouth, and the people just disintegrate, because they are guilty of that law. That is the sharp sword out of his mouth in Revelation, the laws of God.

Then “there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. They will have one consent, because the Most High is going to harden them like he did Pharaoh. And the popular persuasion is already laying the groundwork: let's all come together and fight the demons coming from space.

After this, “all they which were gathered together to subdue him were sore afraid, and yet durst fight.” Scared to death, but the Most High moves them. As Romans 9 shows, he built them up, just like ancient Egypt: Babylon the Great, this white man, this Edomite, built up just to be destroyed, made to fight against him.

And “he neither lifted up his hand, nor held sword, nor any instrument of war”, but sent out of his mouth “a blast of fire”, “a flaming breath”, and “sparks and tempests”, and “burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.” Ashes to ashes, and dust to dust.

The armies in heaven follow Christ “upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” That fine linen, white and clean, is the immortal body. To prove it, go to Isaiah, speaking to Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.”

Christ said he is going to take vengeance, and he will not meet Babylon as a man. Christ is coming back with that immortal body. You will not be able to nail him back to the cross like you did in Jerusalem.

That is what the white horse and the fine linen, white and clean, make reference to. And he comes to make war, because God is a man of war: “in righteousness he doth judge and make war.” His vesture is dipped in blood, because there is going to be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of killing. On his head are many crowns, because he is going to take everyone's crowns and be the one King, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

Revelation says the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies were gathered together to make war against him that sits on the horse. Wisdom shows what happens when they see him: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” That is us, the Israelites, standing before Esau and the nations, who made no account of our labours here.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” The strangeness of his salvation is the chariots, us being taken up. That is going to be strange and foreign to them. They will no longer talk about the deliverance out of Egypt, but about the new deliverance from the land of the north. A black God, a black Christ, coming to redeem his black people: that is going to be the new talk of the town.

“And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach.” Christ is going to put it in their mind: these are the people you afflicted, raped, robbed, murdered and enslaved. These are my people.

“We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! Therefore have we erred from the way of truth.”
blog/2026/2026-05-16-2026-05-16-the-bold:
Saul finally confessed in verse 24: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, or you don’t want them to be mad at you, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

Then verse 28: “And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Damn.

That is what the bashful spirit costs. Verse 23 already said it: “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” When you are in that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. Leadership may see something in you and put you in a position, and then when we question you on certain things you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you, and you are keeping the brothers under you hostage.

The Lord had made Saul king “When thou wast little in thine own sight”, when he thought he was a nobody. And because he feared the people and would not obey, the kingdom was torn from him and given to his neighbour, David, who was better than he.

What is going on in 1 Samuel 15? The Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy all the Amalekites and everything they have, every last one of them. The Lord told Saul, wipe these devils out. And he didn’t do it.

The commandment was total: “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All that they have. All means everything.

Now hold that against Saul’s answer in verse 20: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” Wait a minute: the king is still alive. What do you mean you followed the commandment of the Lord? Saul is playing the defensive, justifying himself, making excuses.

Then verse 21: “But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault; I couldn’t do nothing about it. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability. The commandment said spare the sheep and oxen not, and Saul brought them back and blamed the people.

So Samuel answered, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” To do what you were told is better than coming back saying, my bad, I thought I understood what you wanted, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him?
