Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

So we have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord. That fear is “the root of wisdom”, and where it is present it drives away sin and “turneth away wrath.”

The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

Job's three friends heard of all the evil that came upon him, came every one from his own place “to mourn with him and to comfort him”, and “sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.” Now you see the type of men you are around. That is true friendship, and Galatians shows what it is supposed to do.

“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” When a brother falls, you have to build and restore this man back to life. Speak life into that brother to get him back on track, in meekness, remembering you could be tempted too.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” If we were in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it.

Job held fast his integrity when he lost his kids, lost everything he had, and had boils all over his body. Satan came in through his wife, “curse God, and die”, but Job answered, “shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” A man going through that needs brothers who will sit with him, carry his burden with him and restore him, not tear him down.

Judas is the character we are not to have. “This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag.” He walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the savior and everybody around him. Money was his root and his god: greed. That is how they infiltrate organizations: they come in and offer money, and a people lacking integrity gives up the organization and lets money dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

Israel is to give the nations the opposite: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Keeping the law is our wisdom, and it is seen.

When your coworkers wonder why this brother doesn't murmur with them and never works the Sabbath, that is the nations seeing the statutes kept. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, a Judas who can be bought. We give them this right here: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom.

When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the people answered him: “According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They hearkened to Moses because they believed he was the man of the Lord. Moses led the people with integrity and character, even while judging Israel in the wilderness, and he kept that integrity all the way.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing, and they learned integrity and good character by being under a man the Lord was with. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

“But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”. When you turn against the Lord in this, you turn against your neighbor too, because you are taking foreign women. We know it will turn your heart away from following the Lord, but what does it do to your brother? It says you hate your brother. Tobit shows it.

“Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. He calls interracial marriage whoredom. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”

“Now therefore, my son, love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them”. Don’t despise your brethren. Passing over the daughters of your own people for strange women is despising your brethren in your heart. “for in pride is destruction and much trouble, and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.”

That is exactly where Solomon went. The Lord had said of those nations, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and Solomon clave unto them in love. His wives turned away his heart after Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh and Molech, and he built high places for them and for all his strange wives. That is how syncretism enters: through the strange wife, and it begins by despising your own people.

Solomon offered “according to the commandment of Moses”, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the solemn feasts, “three times in the year”: the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles. It is the same law given in Deuteronomy 16:16: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God”, and “they shall not appear before the Lord empty.” So we are supposed to gather and give an offering three times a year. We come together.

But do we give a physical offering today? No. So what do we offer? We offer ourselves; we offer obedience. Sirach puts it plainly: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

Keeping the law is the offering. The one who takes heed to the commandment is not coming before the Lord empty; his obedience is his peace offering. That is how Israel keeps these feasts now, the feast of weeks, which is Pentecost, among them: by gathering together and bringing a life that keeps the commandments.

The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.” To see what that means, go to Proverbs.

“Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.”

Lest I be full and deny thee: that is one way of taking his name in vain. Lest I be poor and steal: that is sin, and sinning while bearing his name is taking the name of my God in vain. We are called by his name; he says we are a holy people, and he put his spirit in us.

So when they say you cannot keep the commandments, why can’t we? That does not mean we have never sinned. All men have sinned, and if anybody says they have not sinned, they lie. But when they say you cannot keep the commandments, it is because they want to remain in their sins.

This sits inside the first four commandments, which go into loving the Lord thy God. All of this blending of religions is meant to take you away from serving him and to keep you in sin.

When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

“Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” A man is wise in his own eyes; take heed, walk circumspectly. “but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. The Lord gives you a way to escape: this book, where you behold your face in the glass, and the people he sends into your life to instruct you and show you change.

But some hear it and say, I know the Lord is giving me a way to escape, but I don't want to escape. I want to stay in this same place, and still say I believe in God. Does that work? No.

Paul answers it a few verses later: “Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table, and of the table of devils.” You cannot do both. “I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.” Judge it by what we just read: you cannot have it both ways. You have to choose one.

If you are doing both, you are lukewarm, and the Lord said he would rather you were hot or cold. Don't play the middle ground. If you are cold you are not getting the kingdom, and if you are lukewarm you are not getting the kingdom either, so why be lukewarm? “Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”: whatever your god is, flee from it and take the way of escape he gives.

Sirach says “Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman”, and it begins with the eyes. Your eyes are directly correlated with your mind; they work in sync, and what you see makes your mind react a certain way. When you see something inappropriate online, not even porn, which is obvious, but something you know is not right, and you find yourself clicking and looking, you are not in control. You are down that rabbit hole looking for that feel good, because sin feels good. It is enjoyable.

That is why Moses is set before us in Hebrews: “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. The pleasure of sin is only for a season, and you are going to pay the price for it. There is a price that is going to be paid.

That little season we deem as pleasure is only pleasure because your mind has convinced you it is, and that is because you have made an agreement with your eyes to keep looking. That is what got David caught up. He did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came along with it.

So the best thing to do is turn away. Turning your head is proof you have control of your members; that is called self-control. If you cannot turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is driving. “For many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, deceived because they looked and did not turn away, when a simple motion of the head could have saved them a world of problems. Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasure; that is the choice set before us.

At the golden calf “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” What was that rose up to play? You think it was hopscotch? Paul explains it.

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” He is quoting the very verse, and before it he says: “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” When they lusted after evil things, that is the rose up to play.

The verse before that: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” Why were they overthrown in the wilderness? Because they lusted after evil things.

Then verse 8: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” So we understand the rose up to play was fornication. They lusted after evil things, and it destroyed us.

The nations understood this. When we are in sin, they know what will happen, they can destroy us. So when they took their crafty counsel they said, how do we keep these people in error? They like to rap, so give them murder music and lascivious music. That is why they give our sisters these songs, so vulgar. Their whole plan is to keep us in sin. Pleasure now, regret later: you are going to pay.

Ezra speaks of God “being judge”, and of those “that are cured with his word.” Cured with his word: that is why Christ said, I didn't come for the righteous, I came for the sick, and I am going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.

Read on and Ezra shows what would happen if God did not forgive those who are cured by his word and put out the multitude of contentions: “There should be very few left peradventure in an innumerable multitude.” Out of all the multitude, hardly any would be left.

So the word of God will cure you; it will heal you. When James says, confess your faults one to another and pray for one another that you may be healed, we have to apply the word of God. That is the cure the physician gives to sinners.

And that is the meaning of “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” We used to give sacrifices to absolve us for the sins we committed, but that is not how it was supposed to be from the beginning. The Lord said, I want to see you change rather than keep on sacrificing. His mercy is for those who are cured with his word and actually change.

The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Why is Christ sitting and communicating with ungodly people? To bring them to repentance. That was the whole purpose: “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” So if you think you're right, then he's not here for you. The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

James shows that first step: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” You have to confess your faults so that we can pray for you and you can be healed. There is no healing without confession.

You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God and Christ. Christ said, I came for the sick, those that need healing. But the sick have to own that they are sick. Many people are right in their own eyes; we don't want to see ourselves in a negative light and we act like the parts of us that aren't right will be all right with God. We will fall short of the kingdom if we keep that mindset of not changing.

So confession is where the physician's work begins. The one who acknowledges his faults can be prayed for and healed; the one who hides them, looking the part with fringes and a beard, stays sick.

Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” He came for the sick, those that need healing. So what do we use to heal ourselves? The psalm answers: “He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.”

He sent his word down to heal them. Write that down. The word of God is the medicine the physician brings.

So, men, do you know what the will of God is? Then you are ahead of the whole world, because people out here are crazy. People think you can still eat pork, or whatever you do, vote for Trump, whatever people are doing in this world. But you know his word, and his word is what is going to heal.

That is how the sinners at Christ's table were to be made whole: not by sacrifices, but by receiving the word he sent and letting it deliver them from their destructions. We all come in here sick, and we need to get cured.

“the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” “And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.” What would cause us to bow down to their gods? It just says they committed whoredom. It was sex that got the people to worship another god, and “Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

Jump to the end of the chapter: “For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor”. They vex you with their wiles, their seduction, and beguiled you into worshipping their gods. They knew: we have to get these people to sin against their God. So they used this tricknology, this stratagem, to move them away from God. That was the popular plan. “and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake.”

“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world”. It was Moab then, and it is all the nations now. Today the majority of the pornography is controlled by Amalek and Edom. They understood: we are going to destroy the minds of the people. We are not the only race having sex, but all our music is derogatory and evil, every video is a twerk video, and even somebody’s grandmother is twerking online. Everything is over-sexualized to destroy the minds of our young people, along with the drugs, the whoring and the music.

These are the wiles of the devil. The Lord would not let Balaam curse Israel, so the counsel was to make Israel fall through whoredom. As long as we continue in whoredom we will not build healthy marriages, we will not produce spiritually healthy children, and the generational curses keep going. Our strength is to come back to the laws of God.

“Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.” A man keeps rehearsing the same sin over and over, and in his own eyes he thinks he is walking right. When you keep doing the same thing over and over, you are getting further away from God. Watch what the same chapter says: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

You are wandering away from God. You keep doing the same thing over and over and over and wonder why life is not working out for you. This is what spiritual men and women are supposed to examine: things aren't working right right now; could it be that you have a secret life?

They thought sacrifice was going to absolve them, but “To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.” We repent to the Lord, Lord, we're sorry, then go back and do the same thing again: we're not really sorry. We set up prayers and fasts and return to the same behavior, because we don't really understand the fear of God. To know right and still do wrong is presumptuous sin, and we've all been guilty of it. But there has to be a day we stop, or we won't receive the kingdom.

So we all want the kingdom? Then we have to change on this end. We can't wait and think we'll become somebody different in the kingdom. Bring forth fruits meet for repentance, or remain with the congregation of the dead.

“Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way”: guard your heart and your mind in these commandments and these laws. Jump down the same chapter and see what happens to the heart that is not guided: “Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.”

Your eyes behold an evil woman, and your heart begins to utter. Does your heart utter anything? You utter from your mouth. So your eye is connected to your mind, and your mind is connected to your mouth. You see, you entertain, and then you begin to talk: hey, let me get your number, what's going on? Now you're talking, and you have no self-control over your members. Eye, mind, mouth. Out of the abundance of your heart your mouth speaks. No control, and then you're caught up.

It is the same road envy travels in verse 17, “Let not thine heart envy sinners”. Young people see the rapper's house, the girls, the car; the eyes instruct the mind, and the mind begins to envy: I want that, I want to be part of that. When you entertain it, you're telling God, that's what I choose, and this book isn't important. That is why we went into captivity: we did not serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart for the abundance of all things.

So guide thine heart in the way. Turn the eyes away before the mind takes hold and the mouth follows; that is self-control, and it keeps you in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

The psalm says of the nations, “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Who are God's people? We are God's people. And Judith shows one of their crafty counsels from the beginning: “Therefore the king of Egypt rose up against them, and dealt subtilly with them, and brought them low with labouring in brick, and made them slaves.”

That is one of their crafty counsels: we are going to work them to death. Today many of our people are working two big jobs, living paycheck to paycheck, too poor to stop working. It is happening even more with Trump in office. There is no middle class; that thing is gone. You can't work for a living wage and survive out here.

There was a time, and some of you older people understand, when you could have a job delivering milk or eggs, or work in a post office, and buy a home on one salary. Not no more. People with full-time jobs making $50,000 a year in LA are homeless, living in storage units.

They said, we have to find ways to keep the children of Israel under our foot. If we can't get them in religion, we will get them in the workforce. If not the workforce, gangs; if not gangs, porn; we will turn them into criminals. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, confederate with one consent, to cut Israel off from being a nation. In this world, all we have got is us.

“Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.” That is the part of us that groans to God because we are expecting the kingdom, if we are sincere. We are asking God to deal with us: I want the kingdom, I don't want to come up short, Lord, please preserve me, help me. Then let the word be engrafted in your mind; he is telling you what to do.

“And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.”

“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God”. If you love God, you are keeping the commandments. It works for good to those keeping the commandments, those that have the word engrafted in them, “the called according to his purpose.”

“For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Those that followed him before will follow him again; they are predestinated. You are going to be conformed to that image and measure to the fulness of the stature of Christ in this mortal body, because sin cannot reign in this mortal body. Stop thinking it is going to happen on the other side. Whoever could not figure out that you cannot live a life of sin and go to the kingdom is not going; they are going to be in the lake.

A hard word goes with it. Sisters that are married: if you refuse to serve your husband, look at him as your lord and obey him, down to the little things he tells you to do, you are not going, no matter how many head covers you wear or what offices you hold. If Jesus told you, you would do it. And husbands, if you are not guiding your wives in these scriptures and showing them how to be that woman, that is your fault; you are no wise master builder, having expectations while not molding them. Then the children are cursed. When a twelve-year-old in the house is deep in gay porn, something is wrong in that house, something is wrong with those parents.

“For the wages of sin is death”. The payment for sin is death. “but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord”. Through Christ is eternal life, and that is what we are looking for. If we keep the commandments, God says he is going to give us the kingdom, so we are expecting the kingdom.

Romans 8 shows that expectation: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” The creature “was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”, “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” That is what our expectation is to be: delivered out of bondage into the liberty of the children of God.

Then if we know the wages of sin is death, why sin? If you live in sin you are not expecting this; you know what you are going to get. In that day you will be saying Lord, Lord, and he will say, I don't know you; you didn't do what I said to do. How do you expect something you did not do?

So if your expectation is to be called a son of God in the kingdom, do not let sin reign in this mortal body. The one living a life of sin and thinking he will go to the kingdom is not going; he will be in the lake.

Pharaoh’s crafty counsel had a plan behind it, and here it is: “When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.”

What they were hoping for was to run into Hebrew women who hated themselves and hated their people, so their plan could be executed. They were doing it by proxy of the midwives, hoping the midwives felt the way the rebellious Israelites felt coming out of Egypt: we miss the garlics, we miss the leeks, take us back, we like being a slave. They were hoping they loved their enemy and hated themselves.

“But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.” That means the midwives loved their people. They feared God, and the way they showed it was that they loved their people.

The enemies of Israel have always capitalized off of our hatred of ourselves. What was commanded in Egypt is what abortion has evolved into: make the babies that come out of Israelite wombs vanish. Now the black mind has been so twisted and perverted that they do not even have to put out an edict that says kill the children. The black woman will do it herself, and she is already doing it by the millions. That is a genocide in itself.

That is why we must be the ones to correct this, to highlight it, illuminate it, and set the nation back in order: restore the love of ourselves and the fear of God, and show that the enemy hates us.

Isaiah says the kings and queens of the nations “shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet.” Christ says the same thing in Revelation: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

Those that say they are Jews and are not, but do lie, will be made to come and worship before the feet of the true Israel. That is the bowing down. Before thy feet in Revelation is with their face toward the earth, licking up the dust of thy feet, in Isaiah. The two scriptures say the same thing.

We can hardly fathom these words right now. Who is going to bow down in front of the black man? People will look at it and say you are dreaming. But guess what? That is what the scripture says. Let God be true, and every man a liar.

So don’t worry about the hatred, and don’t worry about what we are going through here. Christ is coming to save us from the hand of all that hate us, and what we have coming is greater: the Lord lifts up his hand to the Gentiles, they bring Israel’s sons in their arms and carry her daughters upon their shoulders, and “thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.”

Jeremiah says the Lord will gather us from all the nations whither he has driven us, and in all those nations we are hated. Christ said so himself: “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”. If Christ, the black Messiah himself, said I am going to be hated of all men, why am I surprised when they hate me? That shows the Christians are not reading this Bible. “but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.”

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We are not going to be able to cover the whole earth. We will not wake up every single Israelite before Christ comes back; that is what he is saying.

But the Lord will “bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive”: Israel, Jerusalem, our land. Everything you see here is temporary. It is a movie, and you already know the end: you win. So why are you bugging out? Some of us turn to liquor and alcohol to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred. The problem is you are dying to be loved by people who are never going to love you.

“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations”. Why does it say from all nations? This is for the Israelite who says there is no Israelite in Africa. No matter where you go on the planet, you are going to find some Israelite; that is why he says all nations, “and from all the places whither I have driven you”.

That is why Christ said, “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Teach the Israelites, because we were scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy. And no matter where we are, we are going to be hated.

That is why IUIC travels to all these countries: to bring our people back to who they are and tell them they are the Israelites. That is why we just had one of the biggest worldwide blitzes, because we understand the scripture and we follow it. As John saw, Christ redeemed us to God by his blood out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, and the Lord will bring us again into the place whence he caused us to be carried away captive.

Zechariah's flying roll is “the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth”, and the Lord says, “it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name”. America is the house of the thief; this place was stolen. Second Maccabees names what that thief has done and what waits for him: “And thou, that hast been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews, shalt not escape the hands of God.”

They have been the author of all mischief against God's people. They even put out the story that they have ruled the earth since Genesis, with no mention of slavery, of Egypt, of Babylon or Persia, as if they were all of them, and some of our people believe it. Josephus records it: the Greeks became the authors of such mutations, and when they grew potent they claimed to themselves the glory of antiquity, as if the nations were derived from themselves. They say they are the first founders of everything, the first man, the Egyptians, everybody.

They do that because a lot of our people don't read, so we won't know our true history. It is all a plot against our people. But they are not going to escape the hands of God.

That is the curse that “shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof”: the judgment coming on America. Ezekiel says why: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword”. America is a bloody land, full of the blood of our forefathers and foremothers, with churches built on top. “Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee”.

Zephaniah says, “The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy”. Luke shows how he does it: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. That horn of salvation is Christ, the black Messiah.

“As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. Our people ask, what did we do to you? Why do you hate us so much? You want to know the answer? Christ is coming back to save you from the hand of all that hate you.

Why are you worried that your enemies hate you? Your enemies are not supposed to love you; they were created to hate you. The problem is you think you have no enemies. It is a good thing they hate us, and they should continue: they hate us when we are in our righteousness, not when we are in the streets. So don't worry about those that hate you. Rejoice.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant”. The mercy promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is that the kingdom is ours. That is why Zephaniah says, “Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart”. Rejoice in the law, rejoice on the Sabbath, rejoice to be among the brothers and sisters. Our judgment is almost ended, and we have a short time here, so why are you bugging out? “The king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.”
