When God accepted Cornelius and his kinsmen in Acts 10, the apostles came together in Acts 15, and James said, “to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”.

What does that mean? Bring back the twelve tribes of Israel. Bring back the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. Christians do not realize it; ask them what happened to the northern kingdom and they say, I don’t know.

“And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: they are going to seek him in slavery. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian.

So the accepting of Cornelius was the beginning of that building again. The tabernacle of David fell when the kingdom split, and bringing Cornelius, a northern kingdom man out of Manasseh’s land, into the fold is God starting to put the two kingdoms back together.

James in Acts 15 was quoting the prophet Amos. This is what James and Peter were quoting: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. He is going to bring back the southern kingdom with the northern kingdom.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: as in the days of old, when the twelve tribes were one.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. The heathen called by his name are those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian. Christian is a Greek word that means anointed ones. They are not the anointed ones. We are.

So Cornelius and his house being accepted was the word of Amos coming to pass: the breach between the kingdoms being closed up, the tabernacle of David raised, and Israel set to possess the remnant of Edom, “saith the Lord that doeth this.”

Revelation 7 names the tribe of Joseph but not Ephraim. How do we know Joseph there is Ephraim? Write the precept down: “Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim”. See that? Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim. That is how you know Joseph stands for Ephraim.

And God does not leave that stick by itself: “and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.”

Ephraim and the tribes of Israel his fellows are the northern kingdom; the stick of Judah is the southern kingdom. God puts them together and makes them one stick in his hand.

That is the same work James spoke of in Acts 15 and Amos prophesied, the tabernacle of David built again, and it is why Cornelius, a man of the northern kingdom, was received. Joseph and Judah are made one.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls their land Galilee of the Gentiles. That is what they called the northern kingdom: the Gentiles. Christians have not figured that out yet.

So when Cornelius is brought in, he is not a Gentile of the nations. Look at where he was from: “a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius”. On the map of the Holy Land, Caesarea sits right above Samaria on the left. That is Manasseh’s land. That is where Cornelius was from.

This is more proof that Cornelius was northern kingdom. You can jump up and call him a goy all you want to; we don’t give a damn. Do some research. Do some study.

Cornelius was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house”, an Israelite of the northern kingdom, a Gentile in the way the scripture uses the word, and his prayers and alms came up for a memorial before God.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” All the tribes, the northern kingdom along with the southern, are sealed. The two kingdoms that God said he would bring back together are there together in the end.

Look at the bottom of verse 6: “Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand.” Manasseh is mentioned by name, the same tribe whose land Caesarea sat in, where Cornelius came from.

Then verse 8: “Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand.” Highlight that. Joseph is mentioned, and Ephraim is not. Joseph here is Ephraim.

So the northern kingdom that Christians say disappeared is sealed in Revelation 7, Manasseh by his own name and Ephraim under the name of Joseph. That is the tabernacle of David built again: all twelve tribes counted and sealed.

When Joseph’s brothers sat down to eat bread, they saw “a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.” Judah said, “What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites.” Then the verse changes names: “Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.”

There are always questions about the Midianites and the Ishmaelites. Genesis 25 shows who the Midianites were: “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah. And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.” Keturah had six sons by Abraham, and Midian is one of them. The chapter goes on to his sons: “And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.”

So the Midianites are Abraham’s children through Keturah, just as the Ishmaelites are Abraham’s children through Hagar. They were working together and roaming the land together, all Abraham’s kids, and they looked very similar. That is why the story says Ishmaelites, then Midianites, then “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar,” and then in Genesis 39 Potiphar “bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” It is not a contradiction; these groups were together.

Genesis 37 names both groups in the sale of Joseph: the Midianites drew him out of the pit and “sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver,” and later “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar.” Genesis 25:12 shows who the Ishmaelites were: “Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham.”

Abraham had Ishmael from Hagar, and Ishmael had sons as well: Nebajoth the firstborn, “and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.” “These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.”

Abraham’s children from Keturah and Abraham’s children from Hagar always lived together and worked together. So when a company of Ishmaelites comes by carrying spices down to Egypt and Midianite merchantmen are among them, it is one caravan of Abraham’s other children traveling side by side.

Meanwhile the brothers, so envious of Joseph, dipped his coat of many colours in the blood of a kid of the goats and let Jacob believe “an evil beast hath devoured him.” Reuben had suggested the pit so he could come back and save him, and when he returned, “Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.” Envy will have you do evil things. Remember Reuben’s character; it plays a part later.

Joseph was seventeen, a teenager, sold into Egypt: “Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” Yet “the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master “saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand,” and made him overseer over his house, putting all that he had into his hand.

Luke 16:10 explains why: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” Joseph was in slavery, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up.

It speaks to us today. Many brothers and sisters have jobs, and the Most High is observing us in whatever we do. The least that we are faithful in is these little jobs out here. Just as Joseph was in captivity, we are in captivity, but that does not mean we can steal, lie or rob. When you are on your jobs, do not steal; deal right. God is watching each and every one of us.

And look what faithfulness brought: “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.” The theme is the same as when Jacob worked for Laban all those years and Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake. Faithful in little, Joseph was trusted with much, until his master “knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat.”

When Potiphar’s wife could not get her way, she lied. She called the men of her house and said, “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.” Then “she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home”: she kept his clothes as false evidence, and told her husband the same lie.

Sirach shows what that kind of tongue does: “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction. Joseph was the greatest man in Potiphar's house, trusted with everything, and a lying tongue brought him down to the king's prison.

It is the same today. Many brothers have been locked up because a woman lied on them: an ex-wife or ex-girlfriend who wants his life to go down the tubes, who calls him over, is refused, and then threatens to tell the police he hurt her. Others are in jail because a woman started a fight and expected him to defend her. Don't deal with a woman like that; that is the kind of woman Joseph had over him.

And this same spirit met our people in slavery. A lot of us were put to death because of it. Emmett Till was put to death for the lying woman, and there are a lot of cases like that. What Potiphar's wife did to Joseph, a backbiting tongue has done to Israel again and again.

Sirach goes on: “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” The tongue does a lot of evil, and that is exactly what Potiphar’s wife did to Joseph. She never lifted a sword against him; she only spoke, and her words did the work.

She told her husband, “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me,” and “when his master heard the words of his wife,” “his wrath was kindled.” On nothing but her word, “Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember how old Joseph is here: 17.

That is how our people have fallen too: brothers in prison on a lie, and in slavery times men like Emmett Till put to death because of a lying woman's words. More have fallen by the tongue than by the sword. Guard yourself from the kind of company that can destroy you with a word.

Joseph was 17, falsely accused, and thrown into the king's prison. Sirach tells you why this should not shock a servant of God: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Joseph understood this, because his father Jacob taught him.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Make not haste means don't leave this truth in your time of trouble. Satan will tell you, if you weren't in that Bible you wouldn't be going through half of what you're going through; you had it better when you served me. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Joseph's family was rich; Jacob was a wealthy man. Joseph was taken from all that, sold as a slave, and now he is in the midst of poverty, in prison, for a crime he refused to commit. That is a low estate, and he bore it without leaving God.

Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph. Israel today has been brought down to a low estate, and the tests and trials come because we serve the Lord. Endure them, cleave unto him, and you will be increased at your last end, as Joseph was.

Even in prison, “the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.” The keeper “committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison,” and “looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.”

Solomon gives the reason: “When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Joseph. He was a Hebrew slave, accused of attacking his master's wife, locked in the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and his very jailer became favourable to him and handed him the whole prison.

It is the same pattern all through Joseph's life: in Potiphar's house the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house “for Joseph’s sake,” just as Laban was blessed for Jacob's sake when Jacob worked for him. Joseph's ways pleased the Lord; he refused sin even when it cost him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it to prosper. Keep your ways pleasing to God, and he will make even those set over you in captivity to be at peace with you.

Potiphar’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” Joseph refused, and he did not refuse half-heartedly: “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Notice he was not blaming God that he was a slave in a strange land. His master had kept nothing back from him “but thee, because thou art his wife,” and Joseph would not touch her.

This was not a single moment. “she spake to Joseph day by day”; she was trying to wear him down day by day. And the Egyptians loved beautiful women; remember when Abraham went down into Egypt, Sarah was in danger because of her beauty. Potiphar’s wife was no ugly woman; she was good on the eyes, and Joseph, at 17 years old, still said no. When she finally “caught him by his garment,” “he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.”

Sirach gives the precept for what Joseph did: “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” Joseph saw sin like a snake, and he ran like a rabbit. If a snake fell into the room right now, everybody would be out of there. That snake is your sin. “All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.”

Everybody's demon is not the same. For some it is food; for most of the brothers it is sexual demons, and those demons will get you. Put yourself in Joseph's place and be honest about it: many have been put out for adultery two and three times. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did: don't stand there and reason with it, don't come near it. Flee.

The butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord and were put in ward “the place where Joseph was bound.” “they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night,” and in the morning they were sad, because “there is no interpreter of it.” Joseph answered, “Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.”

Sirach speaks to dreams: “The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.” “Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.” Don't chase dreams; a man who lives by every dream is grasping at shadows.

But verse 3 gives a clue to understanding the dreams that come from God: “The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” You may dream about somebody you know, say a man named Joe, and see Joe's face; but it is not Joe. It is someone similar to Joe, maybe in age or in what they do for a living. It could be Bob. You just have to know the people in your circle.

That is how the dreams in Genesis 40 work. The butler's vine with “three branches” and the baker's “three white baskets” were resemblances of one thing to another: the three branches and the three baskets were three days. The interpretation belonged to God, and Joseph gave it.

Jeremiah says the same thing Job said: “Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.” Two prophets, and neither one blessed the day of his birth. Put that together with Pharaoh's birthday in Genesis 40, where the baker was hanged at the feast.

We never celebrated birthdays. They are days of narcissism, days to put ourselves up above God. The custom came from the nations; it came through the white man, who got it from what they dug up in their archaeological digs, and then taught that we should be celebrating birthdays.

So stop celebrating that foolishness, even with the excuse that it's for the children. Shut up, you narcissist. It is not of God. It's of the devil. And after that birthday feast, “Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.”

Joseph's interpretations came to pass “the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants.” On that birthday “he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again,” “But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.”

Wherever you read of a birthday in scripture, Pharaoh's birthday, Herod's birthday, the birthday of one of the Greek kings, something bad happens. Here a man is hanged at a birthday feast. A birthday is a day of narcissism, a day of proclaiming yourself to be God.

Job shows how the Hebrews felt about the day of their birth: “Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.” A righteous man did not exalt the day he was born; he wished it would perish. That is why we never celebrated birthdays.

After interpreting the butler's dream, Joseph asked him, “think on me when it shall be well with thee,” and “make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:” “For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.” He wanted out of that dungeon.

Notice the prison is called a dungeon. Lamentations uses the same word: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” To cast a stone upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity.

That goes with our political prisoners, who have been in there for a long time, cut off in the dungeon with a stone cast over them. Joseph, stolen away and imprisoned though he had done nothing, is a picture of his people in captivity.

“at the end of two full years” Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat kine eaten up by seven lean kine, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears “blasted with the east wind.” None of the magicians could interpret it, until the chief butler remembered his faults and told Pharaoh of the young Hebrew. “Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.”

Solomon wrote the precept: “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.” The business is God's business. Joseph was diligent in it in Potiphar's house and in the prison, and now a slave out of the dungeon stands before the king of Egypt. Even there he gave God the glory: “It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

And he did not come to Pharaoh with only a problem. He told him the dream is one, seven years of plenty and seven of famine, “because the thing is established by God,” and then he told him exactly what to do: appoint officers, take up the fifth part in the plenteous years, and lay up corn against the famine. To every problem, brothers, we must have a solution. Some spirits among us have a problem for every solution; stay away from brothers and sisters like that.

So Pharaoh said, “Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?” He put his ring upon Joseph's hand, arrayed him in fine linen, made him ride in the second chariot, “and they cried before him, Bow the knee.” We are going to tell the nations that too: bow the knee. “Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh”; he went in at 17 and spent 13 years in servitude and prison before he stood before the king.

This is why you see Israel today meeting dignitaries across the world: because we have been diligent in God's business. Mean men are obscure men, bums on the internet with a handful of followers who want to debate you for clout, whose numbers go up as soon as they see the shirt. They are not worth your time. A man diligent in God's business stands before kings.

Proverbs says “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings,” and Paul shows which business that is: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” That is the proof. The business is God's business, serving the Lord, and you must not be slothful when it comes to it.

That is the business Joseph was about. He served faithfully in Potiphar's house and in the prison, he gave God the credit before Pharaoh, and he was fervent, not asleep, when the answer was needed. He is the diligent man who stood before kings.

So don't be over there asleep in the things of God. Be fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, and God will set you before kings and not before mean men, as he did Joseph.

Ezra explains why famines come: “Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be always mindful of the scourges.”

Scourges come, like what happened with George Floyd among us, and 9/11. But our people tend to forget. Civil rights came around 1964 and 1965, 62 years ago, and people said it could never happen again, the same way people in South Africa act like apartheid never happened. The evils are growing behind the scenes.

That is said for a reason. We are telling our people famine is coming, and some are preparing while some are not. The word does not fail just because it does not happen the next day. In Genesis 43 the corn from Egypt was eaten up, and Jacob had to send his sons back, Benjamin with them, with Judah saying, “that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.” The famine came, as Joseph said it would.

Isaiah gives the rule for what belongs in the word of God: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate.” No prophecy shall fail, and every scripture has its mate. You cannot mate another book with the Bible.

Esau is now loading the Bible apps with additional books. Not the Apocrypha, which we read, but books like Enoch and Jasher. When Joseph saw Benjamin, “his bowels did yearn upon his brother,” and he went into his chamber and wept. Then he washed his face and said, “Set on bread.” They set on for Joseph by himself, for his brethren by themselves, and for the Egyptians by themselves, “because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

That is here as evidence that America is Egypt. “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” God speaks in similitudes. What happened in Egypt under Joseph is not just a nice story; it is a likeness of what is coming.

The Egyptians, when money failed, gave up their cattle, then their bodies and their lands, and became servants unto Pharaoh. “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” That is civil war. To prove that Hosea's “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people” speaks of intermarriage, Ezra gives the precept: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.”

The holy seed is mixed: that is the word. Israel married the daughters of the strange people of the land, and the scripture calls it iniquity. There is the precept for the mixing.

So when Hosea says Ephraim is “a cake not turned,” it is describing what that mixing produced: part of Ephraim very light from mixing with Esau, and part very dark because they did not mix.

Ezra explains how Ephraim and Manasseh pushed the people “to the ends of the earth”: “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.”

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,” “That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” “And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river.” “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.”

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth.” It took a year and a half to travel, and that region called Arsareth is the land now called America. “And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath.” That is Jacob's “blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lieth under”: good climate and good weather, and the fish and treasures beneath the waters. “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”: there are things on Cuba and Puerto Rico that only come forth by the moon, like the coquí frog that comes out in the time of the moon.

“and for the good will of him that dwelt in the bush”: that is Christ, whose spirit was in the bush. “let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the top of the head of him that was separated from his brethren,” just as Jacob said the blessings “shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.”

“His glory is like the firstling of his bullock”: that is Ephraim. “and his horns are like the horns of unicorns,” meaning the rhinoceros: “with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.” That is very important. Ephraim and Manasseh were used instrumentally by God to push the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere.

Hosea said Ephraim “shall eat unclean things in Assyria,” and Ezekiel shows it is not Ephraim alone: “And the Lord said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.”

Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes. Wherever God drove the children of Israel among the Gentiles, they would eat defiled bread there. That is the condition of the twelve tribes scattered in the lands of their captivity today, the spiritual Egypt.

“They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The children of Israel are in the west when the Lord roars.

How did they get to the west? Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13 just told you. Ephraim and Manasseh, with the horns of the unicorn, pushed the people together to the ends of the earth, and the ten tribes went a year and a half's journey into the region called Arsareth.

So the blessing of Joseph in Genesis 49, “in the last days,” is a blessing on a people in the western hemisphere, by the waters, on the islands. It is from the west that the children will tremble and come when the Lord roars.

“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Some like to say that is not talking about mixing with other races. It is, and 1 Esdras 8:70 is the precept for it.

Ephraim today is like that: some are very light, extremely light, some able to pass for Esau, because they mixed with Esau; others who did not mix are very dark.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not”: the white man has devoured Ephraim's strength, and Ephraim does not realize it. “yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not”: Ephraim grows old and does not know his own history. The fruitful bough of Genesis 49, blessed above his brethren, has been mixed and devoured and has forgotten who he is.

“As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.” “Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them.”

“Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place”: that pleasant place is what Moses and Jacob spoke of, the islands, the fruitful bough by a well. “but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” Ephraim would willingly give their children over to improve the race, as the doctrine of la raza taught: wanting children with straight hair, light skin and lighter eyes, not the nappy hair. “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink”. Wait: who was going around judging people? Christ tells us: “The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. They sat in Moses’ seat, meaning they were the judges.

“All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.” Hypocrites. “For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.”

Imagine you are a poor brother with a sin you want forgiveness for, and they tell you that you have to get a bull. You say, I cannot afford a bull; I have two sheep over here. Well, that is too damn bad. That is how these dudes rolled, because they wanted that money.

So the men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:16 are these judges, the ones laying the burden of the sacrifices on the people after Christ had come.

This is how you esteemed the day, and this is what the Pharisees were judging the people on. “And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof:” “This is the burnt offering of every sabbath”. Two lambs that are one year old: that is how you esteemed the sabbath.

Now watch the new moon: “in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot”. Two young bulls, one ram and seven lambs on a new moon, one year old, without blemish. The meat offering was flour “mingled with oil”, measured for each bullock, each ram and each lamb, “for a burnt offering of a sweet savour, a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.”

“And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb”. There was a measuring instrument you had to use to measure the wine; the drink offerings were men pouring out wine. “this is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year.” “And one kid of the goats for a sin offering”.

So “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days” is meat offerings and drink offerings: on certain high holy days so many lambs or goats, on the new moon the bullocks, ram and seven lambs, on the sabbath the meat and drink offerings. Do not let a Christian use that verse to say it is talking about pork and getting drunk. That is why Paul said bring the books and the parchments: everything he wrote was based on what the scriptures said. And they “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

“And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.”

There were some who doubted that Christ’s blood was able to absolve them of their sins, and they ate of the sacrifices. Some ate, but they were not fully persuaded at this point. That is the doubt Paul is talking about.

People say fully persuaded means, I am not fully clear that eating pork is wrong, because of the New Testament. That is not what it is talking about. It is being persuaded that Christ’s blood would absolve them from sin. So the eating in Romans 14, like the meat of Colossians 2:16, is the eating of the sacrifices, not the eating of unclean meat.

Here is another precept about them judging people: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” Remember who the master is: the master is Christ.

“One man esteemeth one day above another”. How did they esteem it? Through sacrifice: on the sabbath day you had to offer two lambs of the first year. The Jews that were following Moses esteemed one day above another through sacrifice. “another esteemeth every day alike”: the Israelites that followed Christ were not doing the sacrifices. They said, we are just going to accept what Christ did; we are not doing burnt offerings. Like today: here is the sabbath day, and we are not esteeming it with animal sacrifice.

“Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.” Fully persuaded in Christ: that his sacrifice, his dying for you, forgives your sins. There was a dispensation of time from the time he was crucified until the temple fell, when people went back to the temple and were still struggling to accept that Christ coming to die would absolve them of sin, and they were given time to be fully persuaded. It is not being fully persuaded about keeping the laws of God, like adultery. No.

“He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord”: regarding it through sacrifice. “and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it”, because he accepted Christ and did not need the goats and the bulls. “He that eateth, eateth to the Lord”: eating the animal sacrifice, you eat to the Lord and give God thanks, and he that eats not gives God thanks as well. “For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.” “For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.”

Colossians says the meats, drinks, holy days, new moons and sabbaths the people were being judged by “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” All those sacrifices were a shadow of things to come. Hebrews says it the same way: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

The law of sacrifice was a shadow of things to come, which was Christ. It was not the very image. Those sacrifices offered year after year could never make the people perfect. It was temporary.

That is why the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling the people when they said, go back to the lamb, go back to the goat. The Sabbath had once been esteemed with two lambs of the first year; Christ came and fulfilled that. The shadow pointed to him, and the body is of Christ.

The priests under the law were those “Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

Everything Moses did was symbolic of what he saw in the heavens. The tabernacle, the service and the sacrifices were made after a pattern shown to him in the mount; they were an example and a shadow, not the heavenly things themselves.

That is what Colossians means: “Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.” The service Moses set up was a pattern pointing to the real thing, and the real thing is Christ. So no man should judge you or beguile you back into the shadow when the body has come.

“And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so was all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.”

That is how speaking with Ahithophel was regarded: as if you enquired at an angel of God, like the word of God came from heaven. Ahithophel was a man, but his counsel was received like an oracle, both by David and by Absalom.

That is the sense of the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18. You thought Michael and Uriel came from the heavens to talk to you? That is not what it means. It is the worshipping of men that speak so well, with enticing words, with the wisdom of this world. Paul spoke of “the wisdom of this world” and “the princes of this world, that come to nought”. It goes into the same thing.

So “a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels” is you voluntarily humbling yourself in the worshipping of man: receiving a man's word as if it were an oracle of God, the way they did with Ahithophel. Let no man beguile you of your reward that way.

“intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,” “And not holding the Head”. Who's the head? Christ. What were they intruding into? Acts 15 is an example.

“And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” If you ain't circumcised, you don't get salvation. “When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.”

Then here it comes: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” Which believed: they said they accepted Christ. That is intruding into those things not seen, vainly puffed up by a fleshly mind, and not holding the Head.

The apostles answered those Pharisees: “Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law”. Troubled you with words, subverting your souls: getting you away from Christ. Keep the law here is the law of animal sacrifice.

“to whom we gave no such commandment”. Hear what the apostles said: we didn't give that order; that didn't come from us. “It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,” “Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

So you see the problem. Christ was dealing with the apostles, and Christ never told the apostles they had to get circumcised and deal with animal sacrifice. But these Pharisees that believed looked in the scriptures and put their bright ideas to them.

That is “vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind” in Colossians 2:18: I'm the priest, I understand it, not you apostles. And it is “not holding the Head”. The men who came from Judea went out from the apostles without their commandment, and the believers were beguiled by words the apostles never gave.

How do you go about not being beguiled? Paul answered it in the first chapter: “For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding”.

“That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;” “Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness”.

That's how you are not beguiled: filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, increasing in the knowledge of God. If you study, you don't willingly give yourself over to men that will deceive you by handling the word of God deceitfully. The “voluntary humility” of Colossians 2:18 is people giving themselves over willingly. The cure is knowledge. A believer filled with the knowledge of God's will is not left to humble himself to a man with enticing words.

“And not holding the Head”: who is the Head? “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ”. Christ is the head.

These men were not holding Christ as the head. They were putting Moses over Christ, animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ.

Then Colossians 2:19 goes on: “from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered”. We are the body of Christ; we get our understanding, we are nourished through Christ. So to hold the Head is to grow up into Christ in all things. Letting a man beguile you back to the ordinances is letting go of the Head the whole body is nourished from.

“Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels”. What does he mean by worshipping of angels? Paul shows it: “And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.”

The Galatians received Paul, a man, as an angel of God. You see how men are considered like angels. So the worshipping of angels in Colossians 2:18 is the worshipping of men: following man, voluntarily humbling yourself to men.

And he is not changing the subject. It goes back to verse 4, “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words”, and verse 8, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” He is on the same train of thought, repeating it again.

So when you read verse 18, it is not Michael and Uriel coming down from the heavens to talk to you. It is men that speak so well, with enticing words and the wisdom of this world, received as if they were angels of God, and people giving themselves over to them.

The reward of Colossians 2:18 is for those who come to God by faith: “But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.”

God is a rewarder, and he rewards those that diligently seek him. Christ said his reward is with him “to give every man according as his work shall be”, and here we see it is faith that pleases him and diligent seeking that he rewards.

So when Paul says “Let no man beguile you of your reward”, this is what is at stake. The men beguiling the believers were turning them away from faith in Christ, back to the carnal ordinances, putting Moses over Christ and animal sacrifice over the sacrifice of Christ. Without faith it is impossible to please God, so a man who talks you out of your faith in Christ is talking you out of your reward.

Here is another example of the evil of these people: “Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.” They saw Christ raise Lazarus from the dead.

Them people back then, those same evil spirits are around today. That is the voluntary humility and worshipping of men in Colossians 2:18: giving yourself over to men who are enemies of God, and being beguiled of your reward.

“Let no man beguile you of your reward”. What reward? Christ says: “And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.”

Christ comes quickly, and his reward is with him, to give every man of the children of Israel according as his work shall be. That is the reward Paul is guarding in Colossians 2:18.

To beguile is to deceive, to trick. So “Let no man beguile you of your reward” means: don't let nobody trick you out of getting your reward in Christ. The men with enticing words and bright ideas are not only leading you astray in doctrine; they are robbing you of what Christ is bringing with him when he comes. Your work is what the reward answers to, so don't let a man turn your work away from Christ.

Paul writes of the great conflict he has “for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Laodicea is in Asia Minor. When you read the book of Acts, it is not written specifically that Paul went to Laodicea. He did go to Asia Minor, but it does not say he went to Laodicea. They had not seen his face in the flesh. One of his companions did go.

“Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” His companion in the truth and the gospel, his fellow soldier Epaphras, was of that region, going back and forth, and he was the one dealing with Laodicea directly.

On the map of Asia Minor you see Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Smyrna, Philadelphia, Ephesus and Laodicea, with a river that splits between Ephesus, Philadelphia and Laodicea. Paul had a group of fellow soldiers like Epaphras who were about the work without being pressured. They were about God’s business, labouring fervently in prayer that the brethren would stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.

“For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me”. Peter is getting this from Deuteronomy 18:15 to 19, and that prophet is Christ.

This is what Paul was warning the Colossians about. The men beguiling them were trying to trick and deceive the followers of Christ into going back to the carnal ordinances of animal sacrifice: get that lamb, get that ram, get that goat, get that ox. Christ taught that his sacrifice is supreme, and every soul that will not hear him on it shall be destroyed from among the people.

Paul already said how serious it is to bring another doctrine: “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.” They were coming with a different doctrine than Christ, so let him be accursed.

Then he repeats himself so nobody misses it: “As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.”

That is the weight behind Colossians 2:22. The men teaching the believers to go back to animal sacrifice after Christ were preaching another gospel than the one they had received, and whether it is a man or an angel from heaven, the one who brings it is accursed.

Paul asks, “why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances, (Touch not; taste not; handle not”. Why are you going back to those ordinances? He has not changed the subject since verse 14, “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us”, and those ordinances are the “carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation” of Hebrews 9:10: until the time of Christ.

Leviticus shows what touch, taste and handle belong to: “the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten the same day that it is offered; he shall not leave any of it until the morning. But if the sacrifice of his offering be a vow, or a voluntary offering, it shall be eaten the same day that he offereth his sacrifice: and on the morrow also the remainder of it shall be eaten”. You had to eat these offerings. Eating, eating: that is the touching, tasting and handling of the sacrifice.

So when Colossians 2:21 says “Touch not; taste not; handle not”, it is saying leave it alone. The men beguiling the believers were rejecting Christ, saying the animal is above Christ: you need that goat, you need that lamb, that ram, that ox, that bull. Paul was saying no, Christ is above all. He taught us that those animal sacrifices were temporary, and his sacrifice is supreme.

Colossians 2:22 says the ordinances “Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men” Christ said the same of the scribes and Pharisees: “But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

That is why Paul calls the call back to the sacrifices the commandments and doctrines of men. Christ had come and taught the perfect way. Anyone still pushing the believers back under those carnal ordinances was teaching men’s commandments as doctrine, and that worship is in vain.

So stop following man. The ordinances of touch not, taste not, handle not were temporary and perish with the using; going back to them after Christ is worshipping in vain.

The end of Colossians 2:23, “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh”, seems like hard wording. Other translations read it, but are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh. Leviticus shows the fast: “Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.” The tenth day of the seventh month is the day of atonement. In the Father and in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul explains that hidden wisdom to the Corinthians: “That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.” Do not let your faith stand in the wisdom of men, the ones who speak very well with six syllable words, quoting poets and philosophers. Many of the things Paul is saying he is getting from the scriptures, the Old Testament. He is not pulling things out of thin air; he is speaking from a scriptural context. Then he goes on: “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit.”

So the hidden wisdom Paul preached, the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hid in Christ, is the same thing the prophets wrote. What God has prepared no one but God has seen, and He reveals it to His people who wait for Him.

Paul says the princes of this world did not know the hidden wisdom, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” John shows why: “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

If they left him alone, everybody was going to believe on him. But they feared Rome. The princes of the world feared Rome, and that was their god. They could see the miracles and still chose their place and their nation under Rome over the Son of God.

That is why the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hid from such men. The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome; had they followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right. But they said, no, we follow Rome, and so they crucified the Lord of glory.

This is what Christ said to the Pharisees who followed Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The devil he was talking about was Rome. All the desires of Satan, their father Rome, they would do; they obeyed Rome.

“He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him.” That goes back to Cain, that hateful spirit. Cain did not abide in the truth, and the Pharisees followed that same spirit. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.”

So the princes of this world could not know the hidden wisdom of God that is in Christ. They were of their father the devil, with no truth in them, and that is why they did not know the Lord of glory and crucified him.

Paul warns “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.” To beguile is to charm, enchant or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or cunning way; the word bridges a line between friendly charm and sneaky manipulation.

What are those enticing words? They go back to the wisdom of this world. Paul says of himself: “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”. Why? Because man's wisdom can beguile you and deceive you.

Paul was not pulling things out of thin air. What he taught he got from the scriptures, the Old Testament, and “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. So the preaching that does not beguile is the word revealed by the spirit, not the enticing words of man's wisdom.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers”. Why? Because they will seduce you to serving Satan once again. But you'll say, no, he's so fine, so divine, I could win him; or, she's so lovely, I could win her over to this truth.

“for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?” What agreement has righteousness with unrighteousness? “and what communion hath light with darkness?” There is no agreement there. “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?”

An infidel is an idol worshipper, an unbeliever. You think you've got the Midas touch and can win them over; you are fooling yourself. Being yoked to the unbeliever is how the enticing words get to you, which is exactly what Colossians warns against.

Family members and preachers who say come out of that Bible will seduce you right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and Pharisees were doing and what the Christian preachers do. Paul says: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”.

Why does it say which is not another? Because the Pharisees were using the same scriptures to manipulate the followers of Christ to go back to animal sacrifice; they said salvation comes through sacrifice. That was the context Paul was dealing with. These Christians use the same scriptures to manipulate people into believing Jesus is white and it is okay to celebrate Christmas. Same text, but lying with deceitful words.

“but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” That is what the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian church does today. They pervert the gospel of Christ; that is their livelihood.

We don't break up families. If your family has no issue with you in the scriptures and isn't trying to manipulate your children, fine. But if your family says, to hell with that Bible, let's smoke some weed and do what we used to do, you had better separate from them. All we can do is warn you.

When we are warned not to be beguiled, and to avoid them that cause division, it is so that you and I don't get seduced: but he or she was my friend, I think I can win them back. No. Stop it. Christ laid out the order: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is for major things. It's not about stupidity like somebody moving your pencil from the right side of the table to the left, or a sister wanting people thrown out of the school because nobody likes her unleavened bread. You can't cook? Learn. We aren't throwing anybody out over your bread.

“And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not like them and did not talk with them. The heathen were the other nations. So deal with him like that. You don't know better than Christ.

Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you. They always keep a little way to get back into your life, a little hot pocket, to win you over to Satan with fair speeches and kind words: I always liked you, you were my favorite deacon, come over for dinner tonight, you're different than the rest of them. All that is to seduce you.

Who beguiles whom? Proverbs says: “The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.” Although the righteous is more excellent than his neighbor, the wicked seduce them.

You will not find scriptures where the righteous seduce, because seduce is a word with a negative meaning. The wicked always seduce the righteous, not the other way around.

This is why brothers and sisters meet somebody in the world and convince themselves, because he or she is so good-looking: I can win them over. I think I can win him; I think I can win her. That never happens; it is not what the Bible says. Just give it time, and you'll be out. Enticing words flow from the wicked to the righteous, never back.

Paul was warning, lest any man beguile you, deceive you, trick you. So he says in Romans: “Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.”

“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly”: their own personal gain. They feed their own belly, their own mind.

Here is how they do it: “and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and lovely, beautiful speeches. If you ain't studying, especially you sisters, you are going to get deceived very easily: all nations can be saved, God loves everybody, and he's white. The scripture is warning you about fair speeches that deceive the hearts of the simple. Mark them and avoid them.

The order Moses set in the camp continues in the church: “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.”

The first leadership in the church is apostles, then prophets, then teachers. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy 1, because all men have different gifts. The wise and known men set over the tribes, and the apostles, prophets and teachers set in the church, are the same God's order.

“helps, governments, diversities of tongues”: that goes back to the stewardship program. It all falls into place. Every man has his gift and his place, and that structure is the order Paul rejoiced to behold in Colossians 2:5.

Paul was not there in Laodicea, yet he was with them in spirit, “joying and beholding your order”. God loves order, and the order of Israel is written: “Take you wise men, and understanding, and known among your tribes, and I will make them rulers over you.”

We always skip that part: “known among your tribes.” Some captains and officers are not known; nobody knows them except their local school. That is not something done to them; they decided to hide and be known only locally, and made themselves a nobody. How will we know you are wise and understanding? No brother has been held back from teaching the morning daily bread. Once your wisdom kicks in, people are going to know you are wise: this brother is good, I listen to his classes, he travels, he's here one week and there another month.

“And ye answered me, and said, The thing which thou hast spoken is good for us to do. So I took the chief of your tribes, wise men, and known, and made them heads over you, captains over thousands, and captains over hundreds, and captains over fifties, and captains over tens, and officers among your tribes.” So we are not making this structure up. The captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens are in the law.

That is why IUIC is restructuring. Some men have positions and don't fit the bill: authority without wisdom, no knowledge, not knowing how to build men. The scripture calls for wise men, understanding, and known.

Part of assessing a man for order is integrity: his actions in private compared to his words. “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” He teaches many, but when difficult situations come, he does not apply anything he has been teaching.

That is called a hypocrite. And you can only find it out when he or she is in a difficult situation, whether it is covetousness, stealing, adultery or hatred. That is why the assessment looks at how a man lives, not only how he talks: his honesty, his responsibility, his family, his finances, how he handles conflict.

A man set in authority has to profit himself with what he teaches. Paul joyed in beholding their order and the stedfastness of their faith; a teacher who is unprofitable to himself does not fit the bill, however much he knows.

“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” Accepting a man's person is partiality. In some IUIC sanctuaries, brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them and like them. That is not scriptural. A man with wisdom in the scriptures, with skills, who knows how to deal with the people, gets passed over for the guy who kisses your behind.

A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom, made a captain or a high ranking officer: that's just a flattering title. He don't fit the bill. Officers of fifty, sixty, ten and twenty were asked to paraphrase Genesis on Abraham, father of many nations, and none of them could break it down. How did they get these titles?

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say: I like this friend better than the one that fits the bill, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting me. You want men like that around you. No dummies, no yes-men. If I say or do something wrong, I expect the men around me to say, Bishop, don't say that, don't do that.

When everything you say is right, you're a fool, setting yourself up for a fall. If you're the smartest one in the room, you better get out of the room and surround yourself with brothers that got some sense. That is order: men placed by what the scriptures say, not by flattery.

Paul left Titus with a charge: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.” Set in order the things that are lacking.

Those elders go back to Deuteronomy 1:13-15 and to 1 Corinthians 12:28: known men, wise amongst the people, ordained in every city. Paul beheld order in Colossae and commanded order in Crete.

So when you hear people say rank ain't nothing: rank is important for structure's sake. The elders were appointed and set in order, and the body of Christ runs on that structure.

To be “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith,” you have to study, and Paul is the example. “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.”

The parchments are the writing papers he wrote his epistles on; he was going to be writing a lot of letters. The books are the books of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel. Even in prison, Paul wanted his books.

Paul was always studying. He was a man of study, and he did not stop. We do four chapters a day; that is low level, but we have to start low level so we can get to a big level. Being rooted in Christ means never putting the books down.

Colossians says, “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught.” We must be rooted in Christ, and to be rooted you have to be studying; and if you are studying, you had better be applying, because you will be tested. A brother tells another brother to do what the scriptures say, and that brother gets mad and leaves because he is being pressured to do God’s work. That is simple.

“As ye have been taught”: the faith comes by being taught. Acts shows it: “And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.”

The eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah and could not understand it without a man to guide him. There are people who say, just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them. Being established in the faith comes by being taught, as the eunuch was taught by Philip.

Colossians says to be stablished in the faith “as ye have been taught.” Hebrews says to remember those who taught you: “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.”

Those who have the rule over you are the ones who have taught you the word of God. Follow their faith, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, which is soon to come.

That also speaks to what happened with the old school. Some of the leadership went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs and throw it in the garbage? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Shake that dumb black mentality. Men make mistakes and men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby out with the bath water.

Colossians says “Rooted and built up in him.” Jude says who does the building: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.”

The key is yourselves. We can go over scriptures until we are blue in the face, but it is up to you to build yourself up, to study and apply. Study, pray, apply. That is upon every man and every woman; we cannot do it for you.

It is like going to the gym. Deacon Abiel goes twice a day, but if he just sat there and ate a sandwich he would not be building himself up; he would come back a Teletubby all over again. The weights are there; put them to use. Likewise with the word of God. Everybody has a Bible, everybody has the app. Study it, pray on it and apply it, and you will be rooted and built up in him and stablished in the faith.

When Christ said “He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”, he was quoting the law. Here is where he was getting it from: “And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.”

You curse your father and mother, you shall surely be put to death. But I’m mad at my father and mother, I’m going to curse him? Okay. Well, you are going to have a short life.

This is the commandment of God that the Pharisees made of none effect with their tradition of “It is a gift”. The law was plain, and the Son of God stood on it. That is what Colossians 2:8 means by beware of the tradition of men: the tradition of the elders set the child free from his parents, but the commandment of God says the one that curses them shall surely die.

“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men”. To see what the tradition of men does, go to the scribes and Pharisees.

“Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” The tradition of the elders means oral traditions passed down. They had a tradition that you had to wash your hands from the tip of the finger up to the elbow before you would eat.

Here is his answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” That is the fifth commandment, honour thy father and mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could declare himself a gift and be free from obeying his parents. It is what they call emancipation today: America has the same thing, get to sixteen and get away from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees were following traditions that contradicted God’s laws. That is the tradition of men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:8: whatever sets aside the commandment and is not after Christ.

Was Paul saying to ignore the things we need on earth when he said “not on things on the earth”? No. Paul was not running around contradicting the Bible; that is what the elders in these Israelite camps are doing.

“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.” You need that to survive. “Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.” It is better to have your own place, brothers, no matter how messed up it is, because it is yours, than to live sumptuously in somebody else’s house.

“Be it little or much, hold thee contented, that thou hear not the reproach of thy house.” Whether you have a little or a lot, be content. “For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where thou art a stranger, thou darest not open thy mouth.”

So setting your affection on things above does not mean neglecting the needs of this life. It means not living to satisfy the flesh.

Was Paul saying to reject the things on the earth, to hell with education, to hell with getting work? No. Jeremiah shows what the Lord told His people in captivity: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon; Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.”

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters”: get married and have children. “And take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters”: pick good wives and good husbands for your children. “That ye may be increased there, and not diminished”: increased even there in Babylon.

So Paul was not contradicting the Bible. Seeking “those things which are above” does not mean rejecting work, education, marriage or building. It means putting to death the sins of the flesh, while still building houses, planting gardens and raising families even in captivity.

“Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.” Is Paul saying don’t get a job, don’t become an entrepreneur, don’t get married? No. He is talking about sexuality. The thought continues from the end of Colossians 2:23: “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.”

Philippians shows what minding the things on the earth looks like: “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When the flesh is your focus, your aim and your goal, you are minding earthly things.

That is how it is with many Israelite camps today: to hell with the godly things of the Lord, I want sex, sex and more sex, give it to me now. Men in those camps talk of two, three, four wives, and it becomes sexual immorality all over the place; those wicked spirits are back today. That is why Paul says to mortify the members upon the earth, “fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”: when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.
blog/2026/2026-06-06-2026-06-06-member-s:
Every member was set in the body for a reason, so Peter says: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”

Shame on you if you come in here and sit on your hands, sit on the talent God has given you, and put forth no effort. If you have a craft or something to offer and you don't come in trying to show it and help, shame on you. You have been given that for a reason.

Your job is to utilize that gift and benefit your nation. Nobody should be bogging down your talents or making you stagnant; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching them to others where possible. That is being a good steward: the gift is ministered one to another, so the whole body is built up.

“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord is not the author of confusion; he is of order. When he brings in these different talents, gifts and members, he brings them for a purpose that serves one thing, with different functions. Paul shows it: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”.

All of it was for one goal: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for the perfecting of the saints.

You see it in the teachers today. Not all of them focus on the same things: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage, and you can see, that's his specialty. Learning from the deacons as the first internet member, you could see, he's good at this, I need some of that, and you learn where to go and what to glean.

What office can we say we don't need? If you think like that, you're not nation building; you haven't been given the vision. Back in the day some camps said, don't do anything with the videos, just play them. But the video needs music, an intro, something alluring, so someone outside the scriptures says, let me look at this, and once the scriptures start hitting: oh snap, I know who I am now. That effort is a member doing its part.

We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

One body, many members, so “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”

That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some of you security brothers, be careful. Because you're able to say move over here, move over there, you get ahead of yourself playing musical chairs: get up, go over here, no, sit right here, don't say nothing, hop on one leg, Simon says shut up. That's your brother; that's your sister. Deal with somebody the way you want to be dealt with.

Yes, some folks are hard-headed and act a straight fool, and sometimes you have to speak a certain way to let them know you're serious, because some don't understand organization. But no member is better than the next. We are all the same, working toward the same goal: we want the kingdom.

If we have this mind frame, esteeming each other better than ourselves, we are going to move mountains. That is what it means that the many members are yet but one body.

“A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.” When you have a talent, when you're able to do something for the nation, at least come in and say, hey, I'm able to do this. We may say, all right brother, we'll utilize that gift a little later, or, we need you right here right now.

When the building in OKC was first acquired around 2017, it was trash. Out of nowhere brothers started coming out of the woodwork: I heard y'all teaching, I want to join. One saw them working on the building and said, I'm a carpenter, I build. It was dangerous in there, with downed wires, mold, asbestos and fiberglass floating; some brothers probably have lung damage to this day. He looked around and said, that's a fire hazard, you're going to die if you mess with that wire.

They were in there on the strength of the Lord, tearing down to build. The Lord brought those people in so they could build up the school. And right after completion that same brother disappeared: he served his purpose.

So a gift is not for hiding. It makes room for the man and brings him where the Lord wants him, and the body is built because every member brings what God gave him.

God has given us different gifts and different offices but the same mission. So Paul says, “to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We are all expendable; we can all be replaced if we don't put something into this truth.

What happens when someone thinks more highly than he ought? Just because you're the knuckle, the one who keeps us safe, you think you're better than everybody else. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices as less important.

Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters who clean the toilets, the kitchen and the floors? Infested with roaches and mice. Without the kitchen? Hungry as hell; some single brothers look forward to the Sabbath because they get a real meal and not the peanut butter and jelly they're used to.
