The Lord brought all these administrations together so we can function. Not one is more important; they all play a part.

Even leadership. A deacon is not better than you; he could die tomorrow and be the devil. He has to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. At the gas company nobody says, oh, that's Deacon; they say, nigga, I had to come shut your stuff off for you to come see me. No one cares. If you start to think you're better because of your office, this body will suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into the earth, and it may have been you who got one.

“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” A body has many parts that all work together: the heart that pumps blood, the brain that thinks, the arms and legs that move. We at Israel United in Christ are not many bodies. IUIC Austin, OKC, Atlanta and Arkansas are many members, but not different bodies. We are one body, in the same mind and the same spirit, so wherever you travel it should have the same feel and the same teachings.

Ephesians says it: “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

There are not multiple ways, no matter what Oprah said. There are not different types or different forms of God and how to worship God. There is only one way, one truth, and to be in alignment with it you must do exactly what the body is supposed to do: keep the commandments and have faith in his Son.

That is what brought us together. If fellowship, friendships and relationships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. We are brothers and sisters who decided to do what God said against all odds and all the influences of the world; we don't care if you look at us funny.

We keep coming back to that soundness, that unity, that oneness in Christ. Anybody teaching anything other than that does not belong here. There is no separatism in the nation and no separatism in the body of Christ. We are all one.

God set the members in the body “as it hath pleased him”, and Paul says: “Let all things be done decently and in order.” The Lord is about order. He is not going to keep bringing the same member into the body, just hands and more hands; that is not how this works.

Understand how the scriptures use the body: it goes into functions. Can everybody be a teacher? Then who is going to read? Can everybody be the one for camp? Change is coming, because we have grown into a nation, and there are many talents and gifts, especially among the sisters, that have not even been tapped into yet.

We have looked at this from a war perspective, and it is all-out war outside; we need brothers prepared to spread this gospel. But in the functioning of this body, the Lord is showing that there are many more things we have to prepare ourselves for. If we don't, we will stay stagnant like others have. The camps that taught their people not to go to school, because Christ is coming soon, cannot open one building to this day, because they taught their people not to achieve greatness.

God brings the different members in for a purpose that all serves the same thing, with different functions. Back in 2016 the vision was set forth: Original Royalty, the kitchen, the school with the kids, security, video, music, all components of a society, the body of Israel under Christ working together for the common good of the whole nation. What was vision then is old news now; that is what order and vision do for a nation.

“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” God organizes the body, and God is who made us great. We are at the forefront, considered the vanguard, because God appointed us to be; if we move any differently than that, God will remove us and put somebody else there. Each of us was gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation.

Romans says the same: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. Why do the members not have the same office? The heart and the brain function in different ways, but they come together to make the body function as one. The mind does not have the same function as the hand, and the hand does not have the same function as the foot. Every member functions, but they all need each other.

The body could not function with all hands or all elbows. If everybody comes in trying to be the hands, or everybody trying to be the feet, what will happen? Disorder. Everybody cannot be the head; everybody cannot be the shoulders. Everybody has their function.

So for those who think you are insignificant, just a regular Joe: God called you in here, and you have a mission and a purpose. You had better apply your gifts and your talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God. And preparing as a nation means more than food and water: we need lawyers, doctors, nurses, farmers. Go to school; master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation.

“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Christ tells us how to build on him: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock”.

These sayings of mine are Christ's words. What did Christ say? If you love me, keep my commandments. What else did he say? That anybody teaching against keeping the commandments is going to be least in the kingdom of heaven.

This is what we have done here. We have built this house, this congregation, this organization on Christ, on the laws of God and faith in him. We surrounded ourselves with those who decided to build on the proper foundation, and that is why this house stands.

“Where there is no vision, the people perish”. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps. In 2006 one of the biggest things taught was that 9/11 was an inside job. Israelites were doing hour-long videos on the back of the dollar bill: connect the words, it says Mason on it. There was FEMA camp doctrine, that we were all going to get killed and put in plastic coffins at Walmart. People were scared to go to Walmart. Their focus wasn't on the right thing.

Some brothers said, we're going to take to the streets and talk crazy to white folks and at the women as they walk by. Where has that gotten them today? Who grew a congregation by hating the black woman, the white man and all the other nations? Whose congregation is thriving with that as the basis of its teaching?

The Nathaniel 7 page separated many so-called teachers from those who actually feared God and understood the mission. Having a vision, a plan for our people and for the kingdom, is part of the foundation laid on Christ. Without it, the work burns and the people perish.

“Every man’s work shall be made manifest”. What made Israel United in Christ different from the other organizations, some of which started building before us with far more members and resources, yet show no growth, no expansion, no change? The foundation. “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments”.

That was learned very early in this truth: if they weren't keeping the commandments, they couldn't teach me nothing. You would see different camps outside teaching on the Lord's Sabbath with a beanie on, scarves and head wraps, coffee steaming off the cup, telling you the white man is the damn devil and you need to join a school.

Meanwhile, how do you get to the kingdom? How do I make my marriage better, deal with my wife, deal with my kids? How can I be a better brother? What's the plan, what's the vision? None of that was being taught.

Back in 2006, when everybody was doing YouTube videos, the Bishop's videos weren't getting the hits, because they weren't the conspiracy stuff. But the good understanding belongs to them that do his commandments, and that is the foundation this body was built on.

Build any other way and it is going to fall. “Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.”

Go ahead and try to do it another way. A lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord. Some built their whole congregation on fear. They ran to Egypt because they thought the judgment was coming in 2012. Brothers got their passports, not to go teach but to try to deliver themselves; they left Babylon and literally led their people into a civil war, talking about safety and security. We are not built like that; this foundation is built on the rock.

Black people have the attitude that we can't build anything for ourselves and that the other nations, especially the white man, have to get involved for us to succeed. We have a totally different mindset. The Bishop always taught: make sure we have our own and never depend on anybody, because the enemy can shut you down any minute. Nobody is backing us up, and we don't need anybody to. We need each other. Together we can move mountains.

That is why we have had the success we've had: the Lord built the house. And this is just the beginning; you have not seen anything yet.

Look at the back of your shirts, brothers. We have built this congregation, this body, on the faith in Christ and the commandments of God: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Is there any other way to build? Can you be successful any other way? No.

That is the foundation Paul says no man can lay other than Christ. For those in the Israelite camps who want to know the secret, the secret is keeping the laws, from the beginning. As long as we stand in the spirit, the Most High God is going to bless us and you'll see the growth. When another camp asked how we set up schools in different states and countries all over the world, the answer was: we keep the commandments and faith in Christ. The Lord is not going to bring the believers to you if you haven't been sent.

Rather than roll with those that had no vision, the choice was to stand with those that decided to turn against the ways of the world: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”

It was clear this was the right place when surrounded by men and women who decided to put everything else behind them and not be conformed to this present world, who decided, we are going to do what God said.

It may not be fashionable. At one point fringes weren't fashionable; now everybody's mama wants fringes. At one point it wasn't fashionable for women to be in a dress, fully covered in modest apparel. They said, y'all are oppressing them women. No, we are not oppressing them; we are giving them what God said.

That is building on the right foundation. Those who do his commandments have a good understanding, and that is why you are here as well.

“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

Christ warned of his departure, when he would no longer be with them in the body: “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.” What does it mean? Christ does what his Father tells him to do, Christ comes and tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments.

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.” What commandments? The Father's commandments, all of them. We ain't Christians up in here picking and choosing and cherry picking, hopping and skipping around. Everything the Father told us to do: those are the commandments. The one who has them and keeps them is the man or woman that loves Christ, that loves the Lord.

“and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.” He is explaining the manifestation, how you receive the Holy Spirit. In order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High God and his Son.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is the oneness of Deuteronomy 6:4. Being one is not everybody doing their own will; it is every member doing the will of the one who is over him. That is how Christ is one with the Father, and how the body is one with Christ.

“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Our people are the remnant, scattered to the four corners of the world.

How are these people going to be able to rise out of these places if they were never told? That is why this gospel has to have a global standard, preached to the whole world. If your leadership ain't talking about covering the earth, they're not the guys. Don't waste your time.

They ridicule us now: y'all going over there to Africa, y'all in India, you went to Australia, you went to Papua New Guinea. We don't give a damn how anybody feels about it. Negro, you do lack the understanding of this Bible; you do err, not knowing the scriptures. The people have been scattered to the four corners. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street, if you want to be known for Times Square or a street corner?

Where would we be today if this truth had stayed in Harlem, if it never left the streets of Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are. Being the light of the world means going where the remnant was scattered, to the islands of the sea, and telling them who they are.

“Ye are the light of the world.” Not the light of Brooklyn, not the light of one city: of the world. When the Lord sent us out, he sent us out as a light to the whole world, and Matthew 24 shows how far that light has to go.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” How is it going to be preached in all of the world if you have no plans, no plan of action, no implementation to do anything worldwide? How are you the guys if you ain't got global goals and you ain't touching the ends of the earth?

The Lord sent his prophets with vision, with goals, with aspirations to take it to the ends of the earth. That is why leadership puts things in place: “Where there is no vision, the people perish.” This is a global mission, and our aspirations and goals have to be set to a global standard, not a local one.

So the light of the world is a people carrying the gospel of the kingdom to all nations, and the end does not come until that witness has gone out.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.
blog/2026/2026-06-06-2026-06-06-members-:
You have one job on this earth, and you have been given a mind to do that job. Solomon gives it: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” One duty.

You have a brain to understand how to fear God. You have a brain to understand what the commandments of God are. You have a brain to apply the laws of God in your life. That is why you have a mind. Congratulations: you know the meaning of life now.

If you are doing anything else with your mind, you missed. You are on that broad road to destruction. You cannot fill your mind with kill moves on Mortal Kombat, the moves on the PlayStation, the stats of Kobe and whether the NBA finals are over. We don't give a damn about none of that. Fill your mind with thus saith the Lord. Apply it to what is necessary in life: How do I deal with my wife? How do I deal with my kids? What can I do to become stronger, a better asset in this truth, so the Lord can use me? That is what we are supposed to be concerned with. If you are concerned with something else, maybe this ain't you.

Paul opens, “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.” Sirach says the same: “Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.” You have to learn this and understand it, in the great matters as well as the small.

Do not be ignorant in the functionings of this body. It is essential to understand how the body works: you have to realize what every individual is worth. Nobody is above this. You are special because you are part of the body, but do not think you are more than another part. We are all one, working towards the same goal, and we have to do exactly what the Lord told us to do to get where we need to get.

It is easy to come in, sit down, and think everybody is just doing what they do. But understand how intricate this thing is, how many different offices there are in this body. Some came in, got patted down, dropped the kids off, and did not think twice about how much goes into dealing with those children. Some will get a plate of food brought to them and have no idea how many hands were involved to make that plate possible. There are people with gifts to deal with things you do not even have to think about. Be not ignorant of that.

Following what the Deacon brought out, Christ says: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied.

If your mind is filled with Mortal Kombat moves and the stats of the greatest to ever play any sport, that is where your focus is and that is where you are building up your treasures. “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. All of those carnal things are going to be destroyed, so that should not be where your focus is.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt”. When you occupy your mind in the laws of God, that is where you are laying up your treasure: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is where our minds should be: on treasure that cannot be corrupted, that no rust or moth can touch.

What is the will of the Lord? David answers: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God, and they are within the heart.

That is what a renewed mind does with them: it moves by them, processes, understands, knows, sees clearly. You have understanding now, and you are bouncing things off of the scriptures.

So you no longer conform to this world. You do not move like everybody else anymore. You are using your mind for what it is for: to delight in doing the will of God, with his law written within your heart. That is the opposite of the ignorance Paul warned the Corinthians about when he wrote, “I would not have you ignorant.”

To be not ignorant, Paul tells the Romans: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think. The scriptures are supposed to be inside you now, and you have to apply them.

And why? “that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” To prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now, and you will not be ignorant in anything any longer.

You were ignorant in the church. You were dumb as hell, stupid, knowing nothing, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: it is Christmas time, it is somebody's birthday, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, and never asking why. But now you are different. Now it has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible? That is proving what is acceptable unto the Most High God, his perfect will.

“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Precepts were called for from the brothers, and the first was Paul's own plea to the same Corinthians: “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”.

That fits the body. The members are many, but they speak the same thing, and there are no divisions among them. Diversity does not mean division: a different administration, dealing with something you don't deal with, is not separate from you. And different roles do not mean inequality; no function or operation in the body is unneeded.

That is why, wherever you travel among us, it should carry the same teachings: we are one body, in one mind, speaking the same thing. It all goes back to endeavouring to keep the unity, until we all come “unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”.

Christ is the head of the body. Colossians: “And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.”

Christ is before all things, and by him all things consist; everything holds together in him. He is the head of the body, the church, which is us. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead.

“that in all things he might have the preeminence”. The many members, with their different gifts, administrations and operations, are one body because they all come under one head, and he has the first place in everything. Make sure those precepts are written down: the body of 1 Corinthians 12 is the church, and Christ is its head.

The body is one and has many members, “so also is Christ.” Another brother brought Colossians: “And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” It takes some explaining, but it speaks to the same thing.

The body is held together from the Head, Christ. From him the whole body, joined and banded together, has nourishment ministered to it and is knit together, and so it increases with the increase of God. The members do not hold themselves together; they are knit together by holding the Head.

That is the unity of the body: every joint and band ministering what it has been given, all fastened to the Head. Not holding the Head is how a body falls apart, and holding him is how it grows. That is why the next scriptures read go straight to Christ as the head of the body, the church.

The body has many members, and the different administrations in it are all to endeavour to keep the unity. So when we have these different administrations, we should not hide or neglect them. Sirach: “Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?”

That goes into wisdom, but also into the gift, because the wisdom God gives you comes through those gifts and through the spirit God puts on you. What profit is there in hiding wisdom or hoarding treasure? None. There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration God has set you in and given you.

“Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.” A man who hides his folly is better than one who hides his wisdom, who hoards up the understanding God has given him. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to keep pushing the truth and growing the unity God has called us to, because we are all one body and it all goes to the same Spirit.

“so also is Christ”. How is the body Christ? Ephesians: “And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

God put all things under Christ's feet and gave him to be the head over all things to the church. Who is the head? Christ. Who is the body? The church. And who is the church? Us.

So when Paul says the many members are one body, “so also is Christ”, he means that we, the members, are his body, and he is the head over all of it. That is why there can be no division in the body: every member belongs to the same head, and the body is “the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

Luke says the same thing, just in case anybody relapsed and wants to jump in the pickle juice: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire”. This is not talking about water.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.” That is talking about judgment.

So you want the baptism of the Spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else, and that is what Christ is coming with. The one Spirit that baptizes us into one body is the cleansing that gathers the wheat into his garner; the chaff that refuses it will be burned with fire unquenchable.

“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body”. How many of us were dunked in water, the Baptist way? A church baptism in a green, filthy pond was shown, the brothers joking that it was pickle juice, but this verse is not talking about that. Baptized means cleanse. Write that down and look it up yourself: baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water, which is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

John says: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance”. If baptism always meant water, why would he need to say, I baptize you with water? It means, I cleanse you with water unto repentance. That was John's administration, water baptism, a tool to show forth repentance. It was never a requirement for the kingdom of heaven.

“but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear”. Somebody far mightier is coming, whose shoes John is not even worthy to hold. “he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Did you hear anything about water? No. The baptism we must come under is through Christ: by one Spirit we are all cleansed into one body.

Paul reminds the Corinthians where they came from: “Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” John gives the charge that goes with it: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Stay the heck away from them. Stay away from it.

This was us. Esau's successful mission was to make our nation forget the laws of God and change the ordinances, to take away our heritage and make us become something we are not. They created that mind frame here, and you see it amongst our people.

Once you come into the truth you are supposed to go ten times harder and repent, not go back to the idols you were carried away to. Habakkuk showed where the idol worshipper ends up: destruction, speaking to wood and dumb stone that cannot teach.

So Paul clears away the old idol mindset before he teaches the diversities of gifts, administrations and operations in the one body. Keep yourselves from idols, renew your mind, and you can learn the godly order the Most High set in his body.

“Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” Why does Paul bring this up before he goes over the order of the body? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols wanted instead of what the Most High God wanted. He tells the Ephesians the same: “remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”. That was us too: Hellenized, living like heathens.

Think about the mind frame of a person that follows idols. Habakkuk: “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?” Somebody created this thing, formed it, and then turned around and said this is God, this is what brought you out of Egypt. You know how dumb you have to be? You stupid.

“Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach!” Woe is destruction: destruction to him that says to the wooden idol, wake up, and to the dumb stone, arise. You are on a highway to hell, a fast track to destruction, following dumb idols.

That is why Paul reminds them of the mindset they came from: to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult. You have to let them know, that is not us anymore. As Romans 12 says, you have to renew your mind. We do not conduct ourselves like that any longer; now we learn the order of the body of Christ.

“But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” Everyone has a gift, but it goes toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you. However the manifestation comes, there are different gifts given so that you can profit with all the nation.

Peter: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” Where does the gift come from? The Lord. And what is it used for? To minister one to another.

You have not been given a gift just for you. If you have been given a gift and you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord; it is not of the Lord. You are supposed to use that gift to benefit your nation and your people. That is why you were given it. If your gift only glorifies you, it is not about Christ; it is about you.

“as good stewards”: now you understand the stewardship program. These gifts are to be used for the building of the body, so that we can do what we need to do as a nation. The word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, all given “to every man to profit withal.”

When you have these gifts, what do you do with them? Paul: “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” How can I apply this gift to help somebody? How can I use what I know to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? What little brick can I put in that is going to bring us to where we need to be? That is the mind frame we must have when we function as a body.

Take the gift of reaching people. Some brothers can get a flyer into anybody's hand, even people who do not want one. The man walks off from one brother and tells him to go screw himself, and then another brother walks up the same way and the man leaves with a flyer in his hand saying, all right brothers, y'all take care. People have different gifts.

You might have used that gift in the world to hustle and get over on people, but that is not why you were given it. When you come into this truth and your mind is renewed, you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out, relate to people, and show them thus saith the Lord.

If you are not using that gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you; Satan gave it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose, “to profit withal”: every man looking on the things of others.

“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”. These are the different gifts, administrations and operations. Whatever gift you have been given, if it is prophecy, prophesy with everything you have; whatever the Lord gave you, that is what you give.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching”. Everybody stays in their lane. You work within the gift and skill set you have been given, and you do not try to force things that are not you. Size is not everything, but at camp you cannot put the brother who is 105 pounds at the front sentry. He might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but if the wind blows it will carry him away and we will not have a front sentry.

When you are outside of your character, things get messy. If you pretend to be something you are not, you may be put in that position, and the person who should be there cannot operate the way the body needs, and we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off at the school. We learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.

“Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.” Everyone in their office, in their proper position. That is what Paul means when he says the one Spirit is “dividing to every man severally as he will.”

In the days of the Maccabees, “many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” They consented to the religion of the Greeks, idolatry: they gave up what God told them to do and said, we are going to do what they want us to do. That is Hellenization. They profaned the sabbath and left the feast days, sacrificed swine's flesh and unclean beasts, left their children uncircumcised, and made their souls abominable, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.”

Paul reminds the Ephesians of exactly that: “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. Remember, back in the day, you were Gentiles. What is another word for Gentile? Hellenized Jews, Greeks.

Why were they called Uncircumcision? Because it was their fathers, back in the time of the Maccabees, who decided they were not going to circumcise their children. The Circumcision in the flesh were those whose fathers decided to stay, who did not give up, who did not allow their children to become Hellenized. Paul is telling them, remember: you were living like heathens. To the Corinthians he says the same: “ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.”

The racial slur this country put on our people is another form of that same Hellenization. The devil called us that. It is one of the most hateful epithets in the English language, and we took it up, changed the ending, and called it friendly and empowering. There is nothing empowering about it. Your oppressor named you that to demean you; you did not call yourself that. If you call someone that, you are telling them they are unrepentant, that they have fully learned the customs of the heathen, and that the Hellenization worked.

That was Esau's mission: to take away our heritage and make us something we are not, so that we forget the law. Brothers and sisters, we are not that word. We never have been, and Lord's will, we will never be again. When we come out of that mind frame, we do not refer to each other that way.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” It is just a part of being in this truth. All of you went through it; you don’t even have to be asked. You caught hell coming into this truth. That is just how it works.

Satan didn’t want to let you go. He didn’t want to give you up. You had family, you had old hoes contacting you from years ago: how did you get my number? Satan. Satan wanted you. He doesn’t want a single one of us to wake up. But we are here.

That is why Paul says “all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” It is going to happen; you are going to go through things; it is inevitable. “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” There are going to be schisms and divisions and things happening amongst us, all to find out who is built for the battle and who is going to make it through. Is a confrontation with a sister you keep bumping heads with going to take you out? Your marijuana addiction, your addiction to women, your addiction to porn? Or are you going to fight the fight and keep throwing blows back while you are getting hit? As long as you are fighting you are all right; the moment you stop fighting, it is over.

Pressure either bursts pipes or it doesn’t. Pressure exposes the weak points, and then you see where the repairs need to be made. And some go through heavy things, a husband who did this and that, and they are still here, strong as hell. Christ said “It is impossible but that offences will come.” Somebody is going to disappoint you, misunderstand you, correct you, overlook you, frustrate you. You didn’t run away from home over a fight with your sibling; you stayed, and you didn’t stop loving them. We are in the trenches, and we are not leaving. Prepare your soul for it, because the temptation is part of coming to serve the Lord.

Isaiah shows what the “middle wall of partition” of Ephesians 2:14 looks like: the hatred, the enmity, the envy and the vexation between the two kingdoms.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Has this happened yet? No. We are waiting on this second coming, waiting to be delivered again. That is why unification is so important: we have to go back to all these places, because our people are there. The Bible says they are in Assyria, in Egypt, in Pathros, in Cush, in Elam, and in the islands of the sea. We have a lot of work to do.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts are those who were kept afar off, living amongst the other nations as heathens, like Hellenized Jews. These are the ones Paul calls those “who sometimes were far off” and are now “made nigh by the blood of Christ.”

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” The envy of Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the wall of partition, and it is going to be gone. No more division: light skinned against dark skinned, look at your hair, look at my hair; the northern kingdom looking at us and us looking at them. Yes, Esau touched the northern kingdom; the southern kingdom has been through changes too. We look different today, but we are all the same people.

That wall is what Christ tore down. “He is our peace, who hath made both one”: the two sticks, Judah and Ephraim, made one, and right now in the congregation northern and southern kingdom are back together again.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.
blog/2026/2026-06-06-2026-06-06-seeking-:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron”. It began with Rome, and America and Europe are the extension of Rome, the iron of the feet. Now Sirach: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Who is that iron? The fourth kingdom that rules the earth today, Europe and America, the white man.

Who is your enemy? In the 1950s you understood who your enemy was. In the 1800s you understood. Forty or fifty years ago you understood. God says never trust him. As iron rusts, the rust will always appear again, and that is his wickedness. Even though he said, we changed, we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you anymore, you see the wickedness coming back now, and they are taking it all back. His kingdom is made of iron, and that wickedness will always return.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He acts like he loves black people and cares about them. Beware of that iron. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” If you are righteous and have wisdom, you see all his wickedness as in a looking glass: look at their history. They are a genocidal race of people, and you cannot get justice from them. Look at Palestine, Lebanon and the Congo, hundreds of thousands dead, while the ones running the courts don't stop it. This whole system is unjust.

That is why Daniel says the iron shall “mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”. After 1945 Britain opened itself to the people of its colonies, and after civil rights everybody started coming to America. The white man said he changed, and brought the same people he colonized and destroyed to live among him. Decades later they say they should never have let any of them in. The white man did not change; he is the same person, his rust has not been wiped away, and white people and everybody else are not going to get along.
blog/2026/2026-06-13-2026-06-13-daily-br:
“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”. Everybody says the Corinthians were Gentiles. If they were Gentiles, how is it that all their fathers were under the cloud in the wilderness? Reading is fundamental; sometimes it is as simple as that.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. When they try to tell you what baptized means, go to Sirach: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Moses being given the commandments in the cloud.

The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ; do not leave that part out, because the whole Bible is about Christ. Moses did not dip the six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers. Where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock. It all goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.

Then “did all eat the same spiritual meat”: the manna, and the law of life and knowledge. “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Everything in the wilderness was the foreshadowing, the setup, to show the dependency we would need on Christ. Many were overthrown in the wilderness, not by an enemy but by their own lusts, and the way to avoid lusting after those things is to feed yourself on the word of God daily.

Christ said, “If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.” There is that daily again. Paul says it of himself: “I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.” How do you do it? By feeding. You deny the carnal man and feed the spiritual man. Not that you stop eating; you starve the carnal and feed the spiritual.

Paul shows it in chapter 9: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”. That is the dying daily. “lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway”. Paul preached to others, but he knew he would drift if he did not die daily and give life to the spiritual man daily as well.

Romans says the same: “if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” You cannot do that without constant connection to the scriptures. Many say they are battling depression or sin, but they do not open their Bible every day; they are not battling anything. When somebody with good works and a good reputation moves to the left or the right, it is because they stopped feeding themselves daily. That is scary; we all have to check ourselves.

There is no excuse anymore: you have a Bible with you all the time, on your phone. The pattern runs through the whole book: daily bread, daily mercy, take up your cross daily, daily death, daily renewal. “though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day”. The outward man dies; the inward man must be fed. That is daily bread for a dying man.

Christ says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” This goes into the bread of life: everything that happened with the manna was always symbolic of Christ, a shadow foreshadowing him. And the first thing he calls himself is the way.

John tells us what it means for Christ to be the way: “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” We have to walk as he walked.

Christ is not a way you only talk about or feel; he is a path you walk. Whoever says he abides in Christ has to walk the same way Christ walked, in the same commandments, day by day. That is what it means to feed on him as the bread from heaven: to take in his word every day and live the way he lived.

“He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.” Christians stop and say this record is exclusively the New Testament. No. The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament.

At the time these letters were written, maybe they had the gospels at best, but a lot of the New Testament was not there. So where do you find the record God gave? In the Old Testament: the manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so that they could live. It physically happened so that we could have that today.

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” That is the daily bread, the daily nourishment. “He that hath the Son hath life”: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven, the Holy Spirit. “and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.”

So it is not just, oh, I accept Christ, and that's all. It is everything we have read up to this point and everything in the Bible in its totality. That is the life Christ means when he says, I am the life.

Christ says, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Paul says the same: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

He is the life. There is one God and one mediator between God and men, and that mediator is the man Christ Jesus. Nobody else stands between us and the Father: not a priest, not a saint, not anybody else.

That is why he is the way, the truth and the life, the manna from heaven and the door. The flesh is dying, the mind forgets, and the inward man has to be renewed daily by the word. The only way that renewing reaches us from the Father is through the one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.

The last part of John 14:6 is “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” By Christ we know the Father. He says it another way: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.”

He is that door. You want to get to the Most High? You have to enter in through Christ, and whoever enters by him shall be saved.

“and shall go in and out, and find pasture.” He shall go in and out and find pasture, and find that rest. The door is the only way in to the Father, and on the other side of it is the pasture and the rest the sheep are fed with. That is how the bread from heaven feeds a dying man: by coming through Christ.

Christ says he is “the life.” He tells the woman at the well: “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

He is that sustenance again. Just as he said, “he that believeth on me shall never thirst”, he is the water as well as the bread. Remember in 1 Corinthians 10 it says they all ate the same spiritual meat and all drank of that same spiritual drink, from the spiritual rock in the wilderness.

The water out of the rock physically happened so that they could live, and so that we could have its meaning today. The water Christ gives becomes a well inside you, springing up into everlasting life. That is why he is the life.

Christ says he is also “the truth.” The psalm says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and Christ is the embodiment of all these things. He fulfilled, and will fulfil, all the prophecies: he came in the volume of the book, as it was written of him.

So when Christ says, I am the truth, he is saying he is the law of God walking in the flesh. Everything from beginning to end has Christ in it, which is why the Old Testament established everything else, and why we need here a little and there a little to unlock the scriptures. To come to the Father by Christ is to come by the truth, his everlasting righteousness and his law.

Christ “took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it”, and said, “This is my body which is given for you”. Paul shows what that breaking of bread is: “The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?”

“For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.” We are all partakers of that manna. Christ is the true manna, the bread from heaven, and we feed upon Christ through his words.

So when we break bread together we are not only eating a piece of bread. We are showing that we are one body, all of us feeding on the same bread, which is Christ and the word of God. That is the fuller sense of “this do in remembrance of me.”

We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously. Paul received it of the Lord: “the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.” Then “This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

The broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice: he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? Breaking bread once a week and thinking that is all right is not enough. The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day, day and night.

Revelation 2:17 promises it: “To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”. The body is dying; you are born and on a path to death. The flesh fights, the mind forgets, and the soul is weighed down by this tabernacle, so the inward man has to be renewed and kept alive by the word daily. The manna showed it, the prophets lived it, David meditated on it, Paul explained it, and Christ revealed himself to be that true bread from heaven. “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.”

In the wilderness Israel sacrificed daily, twice daily. Psalm 51: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it”, but “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If we really considered our ways, our thoughts and our behaviors, we would understand why we need to seek him daily and continually to forgive our sins; feeding yourself so sparingly, you won't understand this.

To be spiritually minded is life and peace, and Isaiah shows where that peace comes from: “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.” This is part of the meditation, the daily feeding. If we are not feeding ourselves, we are being pulled away from God.

When we meditate day and night on the Lord, our mind is stayed on him and we build up our trust in him. That is what the second generation had to do in the wilderness that the first generation did not.

It is heavy, because it says to trust in him. People say, it doesn't work for me; that shows they do not trust in God. It is unbelievable how much goes back to your faith. If you are weak in spirit, your faith is weak too. If your faith is only strong when things are going your way, that is not faith at all; if it is only when things benefit you that you feel confident trusting God, then you do not trust in God.

The peace of God overcomes anything you are dealing with or struggling with. If it does not seem to work for you, you are still not applying it: keep your mind stayed on him and trust him, and he keeps you in perfect peace.

“For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh”. Where your heart is, there will your treasure be: if you are after the flesh, you are going to mind the things of the flesh. “For to be carnally minded is death”. If you stay in that carnal mind, that is death.

Romans 6 goes with it: “What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed?” That is the fruit of the things you now realize were sinful behavior. “for the end of those things is death”. The end of the things you should be ashamed of is death. Paul is dealing with the carnality.

So the death of Romans 8:6 is not a mystery: it is the fruit of minding the flesh. The things we once did in the flesh bore nothing but shame, and their end is death.

Then read Romans 8:5 again with that in mind: “but to be spiritually minded is life and peace”. Notice it is not just life; it is peace. Some of us still have so much drama in our lives because we are not applying this, seeking peace in things that are not God.
blog/2026/2026-06-13-2026-06-13-traitors:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”. It is not another because it is found in the law of Moses. “but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” They are the same men of Acts 15, who went out from us and troubled the churches. Paul says, if any man preach any other gospel, “let him be accursed”. Those men were running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Chapter 2 names them: “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”. The liberty we have is that we no longer offer up animals. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. The bondage they wanted to bring us into was sacrificing animals again to be saved, like Acts 15.

So Galatians 5 says “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” If animal sacrifice saves you, Christ died for nothing and you are fallen from grace. Yet “ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: do not use this freedom to do what you want and sin.

Likewise today, Christians will come in here and do the same thing: accept the identity, but not the theology, using the same book and the same Bible to push Christianity. That is the same infiltration in reverse. As John says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and those who trouble you shall bear their judgment.

Isaiah prophesies against the elders and rulers of his time: “they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine.” People read that and think these men were getting drunk. That is not what it is talking about. Micah shows what the wine is.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” The wine and strong drink are the falsehoods and the lies. It is not the priests and prophets actually getting drunk and teaching; it is them pushing doctrines.

Read Isaiah again with that: they have erred through doctrine, lies and falsehoods, and are out of the way of the Lord. “they err in vision, they stumble in judgment”: they do not teach correctly; it is their erroneous doctrine. “For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.”

So if the priests and prophets are that wicked, whom will God teach knowledge? “them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts”: those raised on the word of God, the Old and New Testament, who learn it “precept must be upon precept”, “line upon line”, “here a little, and there a little”, not by commentary and the doctrine of the oppressor.

And that same strong drink is the refuge of the rulers in verse 15: “we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” I teach everybody can be saved, I teach he is not Esau, the white man will protect me, the scourge will pass me by. Micah’s prophet of wine and strong drink is exactly the prophet this people wants.
blog/2026/2026-06-20-2026-06-20-blasphem:
Kings tells the same account in its own way. It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

Babylon, “given to pleasures”, that “dwellest carelessly”, says in her heart, “I am, and none else beside me.” Where does she get that from? Isaiah 46 shows it: “Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me.”

That is what God says of himself, and Babylon says the exact same thing. America puts herself in the seat of God. You are a man, but if you want I will make you a woman; I can fix that, I made that happen. America is the land of entitlement and privilege. She does what she wants to others and to her own people: passes laws secretly, changes laws, raises prices and brings them down, puts people in office who do not belong there. She dwells carelessly, and she makes her citizens care less, read less, think less and do less.

That is blasphemy from Babylon’s mouth and actions. And our people share in it, because they cannot see a world without the white man ruling the planet. They say he has to be saved, because they cannot see Negroes ever ruling the earth; we can’t rule over ourselves without him. That is blasphemy, an insult to God: saying what God made cannot rule over its own people. You are in hell trying to give your oppressor a heaven.

But God alone is God, and the one who says “I am” in his place is brought down: “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne.” The loss of children and widowhood come upon her “in a moment in one day”, “in their perfection”, every missile hitting its target as God intends, and her astrologers and prognosticators “shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them.”

Luke gives the same word Christ spoke in Matthew 12: “And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.” It shall not be forgiven. A word against Christ himself can be forgiven; a word against the Holy Ghost, the power of Christ, what he was doing, cannot.

Why did he say it? Because of what they said earlier in the chapter: he casteth out devils by devils. Christ answered, No, I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, and if I do that, the kingdom is here with you, meaning himself. Christ was healing the people with the Spirit of God, and they said the spirit he was using to heal was the devil. They were speaking evil of his power. That is blaspheming the Holy Spirit itself.

Mark, Peter's scribe, gives the same account in more detail. “He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.” Christ asked them, “How can Satan cast out Satan?” Why would Satan cast himself out? That makes no sense. “And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand”; that is why we fell. “And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.” That is happening right now, America and Israel turning against each other, America burning bridges and going against NATO. Esau has an end.

Then Mark makes it plain: “he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.” Ghost, spirit: same thing, don't let the words fool you. That's the difference. They said the power Christ used to heal the people did not come from God but from the devil, and if they kept that mindset to death, that was it for them.

Brought to now: those who were once enlightened, who “were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, and then fall away and call this truth a cult, blaspheme that same Spirit. Die in that without repenting and you're finished, a dead man or a dead woman walking.

“Judge not, that ye be not judged” is Christianity's favorite scripture, so go to Luke to see what it means: “Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned.” Luke explains Matthew. To judge here means to condemn someone. Judge not, condemn not: that is the precept of it.

So you cannot say someone is damned. You cannot say someone blasphemed the Holy Ghost. That ain't your call to make and that ain't your place. Vengeance and judgment belong to the Lord. “Judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come”, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness; in that day we will all know who made it and who didn't, and who was doing right or only pretending to.

And look at the one making the call. I'm going to say he blasphemed the Holy Ghost, but I'm out here messing with these hoes, endorsing gang culture, going to the bars and getting drunk every other week, robbing women and robbing my congregation and spending their hard-earned money on my clothes and debauchery. But he's condemned? Get out of here, man. Judge not before the time, because your behind might go to the same place their behind is going.

That is Matthew 7 read with Luke 6: “For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged”; with what condemning you condemn, you'll be condemned too. You say your brother blasphemed while a beam is in your own eye and you are blaspheming more. Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye. We are all a work in progress, and the same mercy God had on David and Manasseh can be extended to you.

The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

Further down Asaph says it again: “Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, primarily, and in some instances our own people too.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.
blog/2026/2026-06-20-2026-06-20-from-bro:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” This is about self-examination, and it goes for all of us. “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”, so what was read about those men in Maccabees pertains to us even today, because there are men and women with those same hateful attributes.

The wise man says the same: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.” Examine yourself now, before judgment comes, and you will find mercy when the Lord visits.

What were those men's problems? Not sexual lust; nothing read that day was about a woman. It was covetousness: covetousness of power and authority, men wanting certain seats. From that came hatred, betrayal, a traitor, lies, theft, stealing from the temple, and murder. Everybody's demon is not the same. Covetousness is number ten of the commandments, but it is where all the others start, because it is internal, within you and me. Those are the sins to examine ourselves for.

One brother just left saying Captain Abiel kept putting too much pressure on him. What pressure? He is forcing me to go out and teach and do God's work, forcing me to be accountable. Are you kidding me? A spirit like that that will not examine itself, just leave. Nobody is going to cry over spilled milk. The one who examines himself before judgment finds mercy in the day of visitation.

Simon fell out with Onias, and “when he could not overcome Onias”, he went to Apollonius, the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, and “told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money.” They were working together on the temple; they had one dispute; Onias as high priest had the last say, and Simon did not agree. So he ran to the other nations against him. You can't make this stuff up.

Sirach describes that man: “Every friend saith, I am his friend also: but there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is it not a grief unto death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy? O wicked imagination, whence camest thou in to cover the earth with deceit? There is a companion, which rejoiceth in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him.”

That is Simon: a friend only in name, a companion turned into an enemy. Because of one argument, he told the heathen about all the money in Jerusalem.

And that money was not his to give away. The treasury held what the law set aside: the tithe for the Levites, who had no inheritance, and for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord might bless the work of their hands. So he was ready to see the Greeks take what belonged to the widows and orphans rather than let Onias have the last word. This is a no good dude: from brother to betrayer.

Simon of the tribe of Benjamin was the governor of the temple, working alongside Onias. When he “fell out with the high priest” and “could not overcome Onias”, he turned back and ran to the nations. Christ says of that: “No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.”

You put your hand to the plow to do the work. Then you get frustrated with brothers always correcting you because you are doing stupid stuff, and now you are mad, you are going to separate yourself and do your own thing. Simple.

Brothers and sisters, when you turn back, regardless of your great speech, we're still keeping the commandments, you have looked back. You have taken your hand off the plow, and Christ said you are not fit for the kingdom of God. You can try to manipulate his words all you want to justify it, but that is what Christ said.

Onias was known for “his hatred of wickedness.” David shows what that hatred looks like: “I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.”

The work of them that turn aside is brothers and sisters that leave the truth. When they leave, they always say, we're still serving God, we keep the commandments, I've been in ministry for 35 years. Everybody says that. But when you see them a year from now, or two years, they are not serving the Lord. They are back with Easter, back with Thanksgiving, back beating piñatas.

God says, I hate the work of them that turn aside, and it shall not cleave to me. That is what Simon of the tribe of Benjamin did: he was the governor of the temple, working with the high priest, and he turned aside. Hating that work, and not letting it cling to you, is part of hating wickedness the way Onias did.

Jerusalem was at peace and “the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness.” That is the mentality we all must have. David says it: “Ye that love the Lord, hate evil: he preserveth the souls of his saints; he delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.”

In order for the Lord to deliver us out of the hands of the wicked, we must begin to train ourselves to hate evil. A lot of you say you hate evil, but as long as you watch pornography, you don't hate evil. As long as you watch the black woman twerking up and down, you don't hate evil. You might go on the street and say you hate evil, but at home you don't.

Onias hated wickedness, and the whole city benefited. His faith, his strength and his love for God's laws inspired everybody else, so that even the kings honored the place and magnified the temple with their best gifts, and Seleucus paid for the sacrifices out of his own revenues. Your faith helps other people's faith.

That is the promise in the psalm: the Lord preserves the souls of the saints who hate evil and delivers them from the wicked. A city led by a man who truly hates evil is kept in peace.

The apostles said, look out “seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom”, to take care of the widows. You may ask, what did they base choosing these men on? Timothy shows how they gauged it.

“Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.”

Then: “Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.” You didn’t just look at the man; you looked at his wife too. Sometimes you find a brother who appears decent, but his wife is ratchet, low down, no damn good. That’s a reflection on you, brother. If your wife is low down and no good, you ain’t guiding her right.

So they looked at the man, then they looked at the wife, and said, he has wisdom, he is of honest report, and they chose seven. The ones trusted with what belongs to the widows and the fatherless had to be proved and blameless, the very opposite of a man like Simon, a betrayer of the money.

The money in the temple was “laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children.” What is a widow? You may say, a sister whose husband died. But Paul says, “Honour widows that are widows indeed.”

First, “if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents.” Then: “Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.” A widow had a duty. “But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth”, because the widows made a kind of vow to dedicate themselves to the Lord and pray night and day for the benefit of Israel. And “if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”: the family looks after her first and foremost.

“Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man.” There was a widowhood of sisters whose job was to pray for Israel, fasting and praying night and day. She didn’t just sit around and say, my husband died, I’m a widow. She had an obligation. She had to be sixty, married to one man in her life, “Well reported of for good works”: she raised children, lodged strangers, the brothers who came to the city, washed the saints’ feet, relieved the afflicted.

“But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry.” Wanton means lustful. She gave up the vow to pray and fast night and day because she wanted a man. “Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.” That widowhood was not taken lightly. And they learn to be idle, “wandering about from house to house”, tattlers and busybodies. So “I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house”: get a husband, sister.
