“The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste.” Ar and Kir are cities of Moab. This took place under Nebuchadnezzar, when Babylon came in smiting Moab. But there is more to it, and we go to Revelation to see it.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” The dead bodies are the spiritually dead bodies of the Israelites. And the great city is Babylon the great. That is the point to hold: Revelation speaks of a great city, a Babylon, in the last days, where our people lie spiritually dead in the street.

So Babylon is not only the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar. There is a Babylon of the last days as well, and Revelation 14:8 names it: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city.” When Isaiah shows Babylon laying Moab waste in the night, bringing its cities to silence, and Moab howling over Nebo and Medeba with baldness on every head and every beard cut off, it carries a dual meaning. Moab, which today is China, the Vietnamese and the Mongolians, will be laid waste again, and the great city where our people lie spiritually dead is the Babylon of today.

Revelation 11:8 speaks of “the great city.” Revelation 14 proves which city that is: “And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”

The great city is Babylon, the one that made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication. This place, America, is a spiritual Babylon. It is not the actual Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar, but this place God calls Babylon the great.

That is why we went there from Isaiah 15. Isaiah’s burden of Moab took place when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab: Ar of Moab and Kir of Moab, cities of Moab, “laid waste, and brought to silence” in the night. Moab went up to the high places to weep and howled over Nebo and Medeba, and “on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off”, because Moab shaves off its hair in great sorrow and mourning, a custom that remains in their religions to this day, in the head shaving of the monks and nuns of Chinese religion.

So when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab, know that there is dual significance behind it. There is a Babylon the great today, and Moab today is China, who with the Vietnamese and the Mongolians will be laid waste once again.

“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David.” The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ, and Isaiah 9 shows it: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” The government shall be upon the shoulders of Christ.

“and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” A lot of people don’t understand why he is called the everlasting Father. It is because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. That is why there is a lot of confusion in the Israelite community.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Don’t just read by that word increase; the mustard seed of Matthew 13 shows it. We are at the mustard seed stage now, and this is the beginning of God’s government.

“upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” To order it and establish it with judgment and justice: that is law and order. That is why we establish law, order and rank, and teach brothers and sisters the laws, commandments and statutes of the Holy Bible.

Some don’t like law because they like adultery better; they don’t like order because they like disorder, chaos, a toxic marriage and a chaotic life, married today and divorced tomorrow. That is genetic encoding from slavery, and it is in all of us. But the Bible can break that spirit, only if you let it. Only God can cleanse that from you, and his throne, established in mercy, is judging and “hasting righteousness.”

Isaiah tells Moab, “hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth”, and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler.” The outcast is us, the Israelites; that is why verse 1 speaks of “the mount of the daughter of Zion.” During the time of Nebuchadnezzar many Israelites fled and hid amongst Moab, and the spoiler they hid from was Nebuchadnezzar.

Jeremiah is the proof of where our people fled: “Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.”

Where were they? In Moab, among the Ammonites, and in Edom. When the king of Babylon came through, Judah scattered into those lands and hid there, just as Isaiah told Moab to hide them. And “Sela” in verse 1 is Petra, which is Edom; they call Edom Petra today.

There is a dual meaning behind these scriptures. What happened with our people and Moab in the time of Nebuchadnezzar speaks again to the last days, when Moab is China and our people are outcasts among the nations, until “the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land” and the throne of Christ is established.

Isaiah 9:7 says, “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Why does it say the increase of his government? Christ answers in a parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.”

A mustard seed is one of the smallest of all seeds, and that is how the kingdom of heaven is on the earth now. “but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.” When it is grown is the increase. All nations are going to submit to it and follow what it says.

We are at that mustard seed stage now. A lot of people say that Israelite thing ain’t nothing. Oh no, it is something: it is the beginning of God’s government. And it is only going to increase. When you check the history from the time of Nat Turner, you might think it ended there. It did not. Look at the history of the Israelite schools; we here are part of that great history, part of that mustard seed that, when it is grown, is the greatest of all. You are not tricking us back into worshipping white Jesus.

So the throne of Isaiah 16:5, established in mercy in the tabernacle of David, starts small and grows until every nation lodges under it.

“And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.” Chemosh was their god; Moab always had a lot of gods, but Chemosh was the favorite. Notice it says the house of Israel, the northern kingdom, was ashamed of Bethel. What is it talking about?

“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Two calves, and our people were worshipping them. “And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

“And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.” Then “Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah”. Judah kept the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth day of the seventh month; Jeroboam and the northern kingdom said, we are going to do the eighth month, the fifteenth day, “even in the month which he had devised of his own heart”, sacrificing unto the calves in Bethel. That is the shame of Bethel: calves of gold, false priests and a feast made up in his own heart.

Moab will be ashamed of its gods the same way. Look at the gods in China today: horned gods, very similar to Baal, the calf god, carved in stone with the cow’s head and body. Israel had two calves; these gods have the same horns. More proof of who they are. And just as Israel was brought to shame for Bethel, Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh.

Jeremiah says Moab “shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.” Ezra shows the same judgment and why it comes: “Like as thou hast done unto my chosen, saith the Lord, even so shall God do unto thee, and shall deliver thee into mischief”. It goes into what they did to us. What was done to the chosen will be done back to them.

Remember who the subject is. Back in verse 46: “And thou, Asia, that art partaker of the hope of Babylon, and art the glory of her person”. This is Asia, East Asia in particular, the same Moab of Jeremiah 48 that burns incense to all kinds of gods and ancestors.

“Thy children shall die of hunger, and thou shalt fall through the sword: thy cities shall be broken down, and all thine shall perish with the sword in the field. They that be in the mountains shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drink their own blood”. That is cannibalism. They that be in the mountains are the ones in those bunkers, little bunkers, big bunkers, all kinds of bunkers. Everybody thinks they have a plan for when Armageddon takes place and all nations fight: we will go into the bunkers, we will survive there, we will live there for a century. No, that is not going to happen.

“And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of thy land, and consume part of thy glory, and shall return to Babylon that was destroyed.” The idle city is China. And it shows America is not finished yet. Although the country, Babylon the great, the United States of America, gets wiped out, her military is not finished. That is why America has over 800 military bases worldwide, and it is the only country that has that. Russia doesn't have that, China doesn't have that. Their home base is finished, but they have bases everywhere, and that is how they will successfully get China; then they return and see Babylon destroyed.

“Thy children shall they carry away captive, and, look, what thou hast, they shall spoil it, and mar the beauty of thy face.” Those are prisoners of war. It is the same as Jeremiah, where the mighty men’s hearts in Moab are “as the heart of a woman in her pangs”, very fearful, scared and afraid: “thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.” Whatever China says in its pride, God says it shall not be so. Nobody gets away with what they did to God's chosen people.

Jeremiah ends the judgment of Moab with “Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.” Although it happened with Nebuchadnezzar, God said it is going to happen again in the latter days. Ezra shows how God's judgment runs: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.”

There is no slackness of the last plagues and judgments, and no swiftness of the first. It is a steady flow, a steady flow of judgment upon all nations. What came on Moab in the days of Nebuchadnezzar comes round again on Moab today, and the fear, the pit and the snare will find them even in the hidden bunker city under Beijing.

So are we promoting harm to the Chinese? No. Some of you work for them, some of you go to school with them. Fine, that's fine. Our job is to tell you what God says is going to happen to these nations: not just the Chinese, but all nations. The judgment is God's, it comes in its time, and it comes on every nation.

“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan. “For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.

“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

“And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel”. Sirach tells what that does: “The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” You rule people with roughness and pride, you are going to lose your position.

That is what happened to Rehoboam. The ten tribes said “What portion have we in David?” “to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” When he sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him to death: you came to collect money? We are not giving you anything. Rehoboam made speed to get up to his chariot and flee to Jerusalem, thinking they would kill him next. “So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

We just had a case like that in Cali, and many cases in the states, New York and Texas, where brothers felt that in order to be the leader of the sanctuary they had to rule the people with roughness and pride, and they were taking advantage of the brothers and sisters. No: we had to remove you. Roughness and pride is the losing of authority.

Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

Cornelius was “a certain man in Cesarea”. Write this down: Caesarea is in the land of Israel. It is in the land of West Manasseh, right beside Samaria. It is not some foreign country; it is the land of the northern kingdom.

And Acts shows believers coming out of that very place: “There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.” You had some disciples that came from Caesarea as well, the same place Cornelius is from.

Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport there, and he sailed up north to visit Cornelius. Christ was raised further up, in Galilee, so he was raised around them in that area. And the place called Scythopolis means city of the Scythians, and the Scythians are northern kingdom also: that is who Paul wrote to in Colossians 3:11.

So Caesarea was a place of disciples in the land of Manasseh, and Cornelius and his kinsmen were northern kingdom Israelites living in their own land, not a Roman people God took in instead of Israel.

Cornelius is called “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” How do you become a devout man? People go, yeah, he was another nation, but he was devout. No, no, no.

Look at how the scripture uses the word: “And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. You see? A devout man according to the law. The other nations did not have the law.

So how was Cornelius a devout man according to the law? How did he fear God? How did he know how to pray to God? He had to know the law. He even kept the hours of prayer: the angel came to him “about the ninth hour of the day”, and he told Peter, “at the ninth hour I prayed in my house”.

So yes, Cornelius is an Israelite, northern kingdom. His devotion was devotion to the law of God, which was given to Israel and to no other nation.

The voice spake unto Peter the second time: “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” So what does God cleanse? Does he cleanse Esau? I never read that one. Ezekiel tells us who God cleanses.

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Then: “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” God says he is going to cleanse us, the twelve tribes.

So what God hath cleansed is Israel, the northern kingdom brought back to Judah. That is why Peter could go into Cornelius’ house. Christians read verses 34 and 35, “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, and say God accepts everybody, that Cornelius was a white man, an Italian, a Roman. That is supersessionism, replacement theology. The next verse explains it: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”.

In the dream Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. What is that vessel? Hosea says it: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel is the vessel. Swallowed up among the nations, a vessel no one has pleasure in: that is what came down to Peter in the sheet.

That is why the dream was never about eating unclean animals. Verse 28 is where Peter breaks the dream down: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man. It is not talking about roaches or ants or eating unclean pig. The dream was about man.

What man? The Israelites being cleansed, the northern kingdom being cleansed. The vessel full of fourfooted beasts and creeping things is Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and God was showing Peter it was time to bring them back in.

“But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.” The same thing that happened with Paul happened with Christ: “After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.”

Christ was not walking with the southern kingdom any more. He went to Galilee, and Matthew 4:15 shows you who was in Galilee: Zebulun and Naphtali, “Galilee of the Gentiles”. Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom.

So the same thing Paul and Barnabas met, the Jews rejecting salvation in Jesus Christ, is the same thing Christ had to deal with. And Paul did what Christ did: “seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”

The word had to be spoken to Judah “first”, as the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”. When Judah put it from them, Christ went into Galilee, and Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles: the northern kingdom. You cannot just assume that because it says Gentiles it means the other nations; there are times it refers to the Israelites in a Gentile state, cut off from being his people in Hosea chapter 1.

Obadiah shows Samaritans, Gentiles and Israel at the same time: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”.

The house of Jacob in verse 18 is Judah alone: the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The house of Joseph is Ephraim and the rest, the northern kingdom. That is who the Samaritans and Gentiles are in Matthew 10:5.

So when Christ tells his disciples not to go to the Samaritans or the Gentiles, the house of Joseph, but rather to the lost sheep, the house of Jacob, he is saying the exact same thing Paul says here: “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”. First to Judah, the southern kingdom; then “lo, we turn to the Gentiles”, the house of Joseph.

And both houses are brought together against Esau: “they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” Judah received the gospel first, and then the Lord showed the other tribes, and that order has always been the same.

“Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria”. At ease in Zion: that is the southern kingdom. Trust in the mountain of Samaria: that is the northern kingdom. How do we know Zion is Judah’s Jerusalem?

“Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.” The city of David, which is Zion. So Jerusalem was also called Zion.

So Amos is speaking a woe to both houses at once: Judah at ease in Zion, and the northern kingdom trusting in Samaria. And he tells them both what is coming: “I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces: therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.” All twelve tribes were going off, so the southern kingdom was going to get it, and the northern kingdom too.

Amos set Zion and the mountain of Samaria against each other, and Christ speaks to the same divide with the Samaritan woman. “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: that was Mount Gerizim. “and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship”: y’all Jews say that.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Why? Because 70 AD was coming; Rome was going to destroy all the remaining Israelites.

“Ye worship ye know not what”: you, northern kingdom, don’t understand what you are worshipping, because the northern kingdom went into idolatry. “we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” Salvation comes from Judah.

What was he letting her know? The temple was going to be destroyed, the Israelites would go into captivity, and you would have to deal with the Lord one on one, with no more priests intervening for you: “the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. Neither Samaria’s mountain nor Zion would stand; both houses would go captive, as Amos said.

“In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.” Christ told the Samaritan woman “salvation is of the Jews”, and the psalm agrees: in Judah is God known.

That is why Christ came out of Judah. Salvation comes from Judah. He is not tribe hopping.

So when Amos speaks against those at ease in Zion and those who trust in the mountain of Samaria, the difference between the two is not that one of them was righteous; all twelve went off and both would go captive. But God was known in Judah, and out of Judah the salvation of all Israel would come.

Amos says the tabernacle of David is fallen. Hosea tells how long it lies fallen: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.” Teraphim are the little images we made of family members. Many days with none of it: no king, no prince, no priesthood.

And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

Christ said “This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.” The same generation that was around during Christ's time, guess where they are now? Here. “Heaven and earth shall pass away”: with nuclear fire.

“But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.” The exact same people that were ruling during Noah's time will be ruling in this time. The same ignorance Noah faced back then, we are going to face now. The same word he was preaching back then, we are preaching now.

“For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away”. That is Peter's scoffers: in Noah's time they didn't believe. Noah is crazy, building a boat for no reason, him and his crazy sons and wives. Where's your rain at? Where's this judgment coming from? And today they say “all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation”: this is how the world is supposed to be; this ain't captivity, we free.

Peter says the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished, and the heavens and the earth which are now, “by the same word”, the word Noah preached, “are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech and Noah preached to the wicked of our people mingled among the other people, and the flood came and killed them. Here we are again, preaching to the same wicked sons of God mixed with the same people before the fire comes. It is the exact same thing.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people”: out of Babylon. Then, “that ye be not partakers of her sins”: whose sins do we not partake in? Edom's sins. The same way the sons of God should not have partaken in the sins of the daughters of men back then, when Noah was preaching to them. It is the exact same thing all over again.

And “that ye receive not of her plagues”: her plagues back then were water; her plagues now are going to be fire. That is Peter's warning, that the heavens and earth which are now are “reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.”

“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” The Lord remembered Cain's iniquities too. The scoffers say all things continue as they were, but God does not forget. As in the days of Noah, those who come out and do not partake of her sins will be saved, and those who stay will receive her plagues.

“For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood”: he is the cause. Whose evil was responsible for the earth being flooded? Cain's evil. The heavens that were of old in 2 Peter 3 are Cain's kingdom, the ruling class that was of old, and “the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished”.

The sons of God, Seth's line, went in with Cain's line, and God dealt with them: if you're all for Cain now, I'm going to kill all of you. Then “wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value”: the ark, the little boat the scoffers laughed at, carried Noah through.

Likewise today. Peter says “the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire”. God said, I promised you with the rainbow that I would not flood the earth again. I won't flood it, but I'll burn it. The same cause, the same wicked kingdom ruling, and the same judgment coming, this time by fire, while wisdom directs the course of the righteous who hear the word.

Solomon says it again in chapter 3: “That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.”

It is the same as “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. One generation comes and another goes; the old die and the young are born. The sun has its cycle, the wind has its circuits, and the rivers run into the sea and return again. Generations have their circuits and cycles the same way.

So what is to be has already been. Before our generation it was already in the past, only “There is no remembrance of former things”. That is why a man can stand in a moment and feel, I remember this.

What is the thing that hath been? Solomon names it: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man”. So he explains it himself: the thing that have been is man.

Just like the wind, the sun, the moon and the rivers have a flow, likewise man: we come and we go. You and I have been here before, in different cycles of life. That is why it is called deja vu, a French term that literally means already seen: the sensation of having already experienced a situation even though you know it is happening for the first time.

Already seen, because you are already meant to be there. The prophets saw things that came to pass. When the prophets saw us going on slave ships, we had to live out what they saw. So when John saw America in flames, we have to live out what John already saw. We are catching up to the prophecies, and what leads up to them is already set in motion. You can't change it.

“Who is as the wise man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?” The wise man knows the interpretation of the thing. And “a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine”.

The thing that hath been, in Ecclesiastes 1, is talking about man. Man has been around before, but “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” It takes wisdom to interpret that thing.

So the wise man understands the cycle: the generations pass and come again, and what the prophets already saw is what we are living out now. The wise man knows it is man that hath been, and that is why there is no new thing under the sun.

Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

Christ said to his own people, “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning”. Those same Jews wanted Christ dead; they were plotting to kill him. Did Satan murder anybody? No. Who killed in the beginning? Cain. Christ is calling him the devil. The Lord said to Cain he would hide his face from him, and Cain's father became the devil.

John says what Christ said in John 8:44: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was Satan's baby, spiritually obviously. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” And he killed Abel savagely; it wasn't like he just cut his throat, it was very bad.

So “the lusts of your father ye will do” means the same way Cain killed his brother, you are going to kill me: the same spirit that was in Cain is in you. “and abode not in the truth”: in process of time Cain offered up fruit, when he was supposed to offer up animals. It is not talking about Satan, who was always a liar; that's his job. It's talking about Cain. When the Lord asked for his brother, Cain said I don't know. Was he lying? Yes: “he is a liar, and the father of it.”

The commentaries on Genesis 4:7 all tap dance around this and don't want to be honest about it. Be very careful about modern scholarship, because they hide things; older scholars are more upfront, and there is a movement set up to censor any biblical truth that can be substantiated.

The evil man and the violent man of Psalms 140 has a name, and Malachi gives it. “I have loved you, saith the Lord.” Israel asks, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” And the answer: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” He loved Jacob just like he loved Abel, and he hated Esau. Laying his mountains and his heritage waste means God allowed him to be overthrown.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: we lost all, we are going back to being vagabonds. “but we will return and build the desolate places”: build themselves back up as an empire, just like Cain built that city. And the Lord answers, “They shall build, but I will throw down.”

“and they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: the beginning and the end of wickedness. “and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: no repentance, no salvation, no kingdom, ever. Not even the good ones, so some of you coons out there.

So when David prays “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man” and “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”, this is who he is praying against: Esau, Edom, the people the Lord hated and against whom he hath indignation for ever.

“And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven, that's Israel, and Israel suffereth violence. The violent that take it by force are the Romans, and Esau is the Romans.

That puts a name on the man of Psalms 140. The Bible calls the evil man, the violent man, the wicked, and Esau is the violent man, the wicked man. “They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips”: they are liars. And they “have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

So David's cry, “preserve me from the violent man”, is Israel's cry to be kept from the hands of Esau, the Romans, who have done violence to the kingdom of heaven from the days of John the Baptist until now.

The beast rising up out of the sea has “seven heads and ten horns”. John sees that same beast again: “I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.” The woman sits upon the beast, she being the eighth head.

“And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication.” Purple and scarlet, gold and precious stones: well off, wealthy, powerful.

“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” Why is this important? Because judgment is like a ring. Babylon was the first, and it ends with Babylon again. It comes full circle, just as a ring: Babylon reigned over us, and now Babylon reigns over us again. There is nothing new under the sun; this is a whole loop.

That is why the beast of Revelation 13 is made up of the empires before it: like a leopard, the Greek philosophy and democracy of America; the feet of a bear, Persia; the mouth of a lion, the Babylonian doctrines found in America. This empire took all the ancient dark civilizations, learned from their mistakes, and merged them into itself. It is the same fourth beast of Daniel, the eagle of Esdras, the dragon of Revelation, and upon it sits Babylon the Great.

Paul writes “To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse,” just as Ephesians is written to the saints at Ephesus. Same concept: these are Israelites in Asia. Then he says, “Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus.” What is Paul saying? He never went to Colosse. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that it spread all throughout Asia, and Paul heard there was another congregation over in Colosse that was fervent in spirit too, so he wrote to them.

Chapter 2 proves it: “For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Why had they not seen Paul’s face? Because he never went to Laodicea, and he never went to Colosse. For anyone who wondered why there is no precept in Acts of Paul going to Colosse, that is the precept.

On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it (the Laodicea you read about in Revelation), and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities of that region. The gospel spread through all those cities, “as it is in all the world.” Acts 19 says Paul turned away much people “not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia” from the goddess Diana, the woman all Asia worshipped, just as America worships the Virgin Mary. The spirit was so heavy on the apostle that places he never physically went to were getting touched.

Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon were written in the same period, around AD 60 to 67 while Paul was under house arrest in Rome, to the same region. That is why they overlap and speak of the same things, like this mystery.

“How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ) Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel.”

That is the mystery: the animal sacrifice is done away with, no longer in play, and the northern and southern kingdom now have a chance to come back into the fold with Christ. Partakers of his promise, the covenant: the promises were not made through animal sacrifice but through Christ. That is the same “mystery among the Gentiles” of Colossians 1:27, Christ in you, the hope of glory.

Colossians speaks of “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints,” once again using that term saints, and then of “the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” There is a Christian out there watching who will say, see, Gentiles means the other nations. Matthew shows who the Gentiles are.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom, and their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles.

So the mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom can come back into the fold: “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” We had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance and no reconciliation, except through Christ.

“And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” That is the Marcus of Colossians 4:10, Barnabas’ sister’s son.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God. And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.”

It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found; he came up missing. Paul said straight, I do not care if that is your nephew, he is not traveling with me any more. Barnabas said, that is my sister’s son, I am taking him with me. You can understand that dynamic. The faithful ministers like Epaphras are the ones who stay with the work.

The Colossians learned the truth “of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.” That is how they woke up: one brother heard it and said, I am going to teach all of you. Acts 18 shows the same concept at Corinth: “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.”

“And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house.” If you were in the synagogue, you were practicing the law of sacrifice. Crispus was the chief ruler of it, and he believed on Christ, just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity and then believed. “And many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.” It started with him and then the others took hold of it.

Paul was actually at Corinth, though. With Epaphras it was different: he was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He said, that is true, I believe it, I am going to go teach it. That is just like today when somebody sees IUIC on YouTube, prints out flyers and starts hitting the city, and then this school pops up and that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles, and when we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them, because we are doing the exact same thing.

Epaphras, the “faithful minister of Christ” the Colossians learned from, comes up again at the end of the letter: “Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.”

“For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” On the map you see Colosse, then Laodicea and Hierapolis, all in that same region. Epaphras was one of them, and he carried the work through all three cities.

Epaphras was putting in serious work. He heard the truth, believed it, taught it, and kept labouring fervently in prayer for the congregations he raised up, with great zeal for them. He is the example of the brother who takes the truth and gets the ground running in his own region.

“The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.” Then the subscript many Bibles carry: “Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.” Some people’s Bibles may not have that line, so it was put up on the screen for everyone to see.

This epistle was written from Rome, while Paul was under house arrest, which parallels Acts 28, and sent to the church at Colosse by Tychicus and Onesimus. Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, Philippians, 1 Timothy, Titus and 2 Timothy were written in that same time, which is why they overlap and speak of similar topics and the same people.

Paul never went to Colosse. He wrote to a congregation raised up by Epaphras, and sent the letter by brothers who were themselves of that city.

“All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord.” Tychicus carried the letter. “With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.” Onesimus was one of the Colossians.

“Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister’s son to Barnabas.” If Marcus is Barnabas’ sister’s son, that makes Marcus his nephew: John Mark.

That is the same John Mark that Paul and Barnabas had their dispute over at the end of Acts 15. Barnabas was sticking up for him because he was his nephew. So these closing names are not filler; they tie the letter to the history of the apostles and the men who carried the work.

“Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.”

Philemon was of Colosse, the same place Epaphras taught. So it started with Epaphras, and then others came: Philemon, a dearly beloved fellow labourer, Apphia, Archippus the fellow soldier, and a church meeting in Philemon’s house.

That is how the truth spreads. One brother, a faithful minister of Christ, wakes up and teaches, and then fellow labourers rise up around him and congregations meet in houses, the same way schools pop up one after another today.

“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Why would Paul write to Philemon on behalf of Onesimus? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

The prayer asks God to “send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” You wonder why you have no peace in your life right now, why you are all over the place? Because you are not serving him, not keeping his law and commandments in sincerity. Isaiah shows what keeps us from being one with God.

“Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” His hand is not so short that he can’t reach down and help you when you are afflicted or in trouble. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.” His ear is not so heavy that he can’t hear your prayers and your cries and come down and get you out of that situation.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is what separates you from your God: your sins, your iniquities. That is the only way he separates himself from you, if you are in the midst of sin.

But if you are doing what you are supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he is going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers. If you are sincere and honest with him, walking right in his sight, waking up and returning to him, he will never forsake you in time of trouble. He will help you through your hard times.

Baruch says, “Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God”, and “unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.” Here in America we have open shame, because we departed from our God and refuse to come back and repent. Lamentations shows what that open shame looks like.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are an afflicted people, and we haven’t realized it yet. We are being put through the wringer because we constantly break his law of commandments, because we departed from God, because we don’t know who we are, and because God has been calling us and we refuse to turn around and come back to him. And we are drunken, but not with wine. Drunken with what? Micah shows it.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” We are drunk with philosophy and doctrines, the lies we learned here in America. If you follow those doctrines, those laws, those philosophies, those lies, that man is going to be the prophet to you: a prophet to lead you right to hell.

A lot of these wicked and evil pastors are just chasing money, money, money, and don’t give a damn about the people’s souls or their spirits. They don’t care about healing the people, fixing the people and bringing them back to Christ. The people are crying, looking for Christ, and these men mislead them while chasing the dollar bill. Let those men be your prophet if you are going to believe that garbage.

That is why we have gangs in the street, prostitutes in the street, our sons fainted and lying “at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”: the dead Israelites in the churches are not teaching our people how to keep the Lord’s commandments or how to come back to Christ. But the Lord who “pleadeth the cause of his people” says he has taken the cup of trembling out of our hand, and “I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee.”

“And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”. Who is the eagle? The eagle was Rome at the time, and Rome is an extension of this place called America. Moses tells us about that eagle: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”. That's Rome, when they came in and attacked us in Luke 21, the abomination of desolation of Matthew 24:15, when they destroyed us and ran us out of Jerusalem. From the end of the earth: from Europe.

“a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: we did not understand their tongue when they landed here. Columbus found the Taino, a people who shared food, land and knowledge and fed him as an honored guest, and he wrote that they would make fine servants, and with fifty men he could make them do whatever he wanted. They knew what they came for. Within fifty years the Taino nation was virtually extinct. In Africa they sent explorers, missionaries with Bibles and the cross, and traders with gifts first; they ate at the tables of kings while mapping the gold and rubber, got treaties signed in crafty, ambiguous words, and at the Berlin conference of 1884 sat around a table and split up the continent. They came as swift as the eagle flieth. You can never trust that red man, that devil, that dragon.

“A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”: they didn't care about old or young; they put everybody to death and enslaved everybody. “And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, and leave neither “corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine”, kine being cattle, “until he have destroyed thee.”

Then the woman is nourished in her place, and that is America, where we've been nourished through their welfare system, their disability system, their politics, their religions, their educational and economic system. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Hungry, thirsty, needing clothing, a passport, a visa, a death certificate, anything we need, we have to go to them. “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The red man put a yoke of iron upon our necks, and we are destroyed today as a people. Even the ones speaking up for us say we love America: that is how destroyed we are.

The woman is nourished “from the face of the serpent.” Jump to verse 9 to see who the serpent is: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.”

That old serpent is the serpent from Genesis. He is called the Devil and Satan, and he deceived everybody; he deceived this whole world. He was cast out into the earth with his angels. That is who the face of the serpent is: the devil himself and his kids, the white man, the red man. They are the enemies Deuteronomy 28:48 says we serve, called the serpent in Revelation.

That is why verse 12 says “Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.” Woe means death and destruction; this earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He is mad right now, and that is why we are going through it.

And verse 15: “the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”. That flood is his media, his witchcraft, the same script read word for word on every station, the deceiving of the whole world coming out of the dragon's mouth. But “the earth helped the woman”: this Bible helps us understand what happened to us, what is happening now, and what is going to happen.
