The Lord told Ezekiel, “set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” Who or what is mount Seir? Genesis 36 answers: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” Esau's dwelling is Seir, so when the Bible prophesies against Seir, it is prophesying against Esau, the nation of Edom. Now there is context, and no one can say we are making it up. We don't need a cosigner; the Bible says what it says.

With that key, Ezekiel 35 opens up. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: a hatred that has gone on for centuries, from Esau their father to his children toward us. It is in their blood to hate us; their hatred is damn near biological, from the womb to the tomb. That is why they do such terrible things to us: eating us, hanging us, castrating us, raping us, mutilating us. A sister whose husband was murdered sought justice in court; they hung her from a tree, shot her full of holes, cut the unborn baby out of her, stepped on its head and set it on fire. Damn! That is a perfect hatred. There's no record of black folks ever doing that to white folks. What we did to the French in Haiti was retaliation, and they deserved it; she was innocent.

They shed our blood “in the time that their iniquity had an end”: after the Emancipation Proclamation came the KKK, Black Codes, Jim Crow, convict leasing and redlining. That envy goes back to the birthright. Esau was the firstborn and felt it was not fair that God chose Jacob, and the Lord says he will do “according to thine anger, and according to thine envy.”

Edom said, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it.” The two nations are Judah and Israel; the two countries were Judea and Samaria and later Israel and the Americas. They took one as Romans and later as Israelis, and the other as Christians, as conquistadors. “I have heard all thy blasphemies”: this is a direct precept to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, possessing the land and professing to be the people that belong there. They have said it to our faces: yes, you are the real Jews, but the land is ours now. They know; the world does not.

“When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” As long as that nation is on the earth, there can be no peace; when there is no more Edom, the earth rejoices. “thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it.” The judgment on Edom is complete, with no exceptions, and they shall know that he is the Lord.

Isaiah says the terrible one, Edom, is brought to nought: the one that does terrible things to the nations behind the cloak, behind the scenes, to maintain power and authority on the earth, destroyed as Ezekiel 35 said. The scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, those “That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate.” Who is the one that reproveth in the gate? Amos answers: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

They hate him that rebukes in the gate, in the streets. They abhor him that speaks uprightly. That is the one teaching in the streets, and that is who they lay the snares for, in the legal system, in their music and their media.

So they will pass laws to make those of us who reprove offenders for our words. Say certain things and you face jail time, imprisonment, exile, banishment; they are even trying to pass laws where you can be put to death, talking about bringing back beheadings and the guillotine. They will call it hate speech, terrorism, treason, being unpatriotic. You are anti-MAGA, against abortion, against same-sex, against white supremacy? Lock that brother up, lock that sister up. You say you are an Israelite, that they are fake Jews? Hate speech; five years; fire them from their job; fine them thousands; put a lien on their house.

They will do it because they can, and they will. But the most frightening one to them is the one they cannot kill, the righteous one they cannot pay off, bribe, drug, slander, poison or shoot. And Isaiah’s end is sure: the terrible one is brought to nought, and all that lay snares for him that reproveth in the gate are cut off.
blog/2026/2026-07-26-2026-07-26-living-y:
“Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” We are not judging Michael and Gabriel and them; that is not what it is talking about. Christ said: “Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” It is talking about our own people. We shall judge the leaders.

“If then ye have judgments of things pertaining to this life, set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church.” The least esteemed are the young men, the lower ranked men. Raise those men up and use them. Stop wasting your time on brothers who have been around ten years and are doing nothing; they lack the zeal and the fire, and you have to force them to do everything, like a fizzle of wind.

Around the table you can see the ones with zeal: they have questions, they want to know, and when you read the scripture the fire is in them. Then there are the ones who stay in the back; you have to call them into the war room and they say, oh, I didn't know I could come in. That is a lie. In California, brother after brother gave the most outrageous answers because they do not study, and it is not just Cali. On the quests, in the middle of the ocean with nothing else to do, those brothers are not around; for them it is a vacation. That is a hireling.

The ones who will sit on thrones judging the tribes are the ones who follow Christ now, so give the work to the young men who want to learn and grow.

“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?” The law here is not Rome; Rome was not listening to every little problem. The law is the Pharisees.

Christ shows it: “Then spake Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, Saying, The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat”. That is the law right there: they sat in Moses' seat, and they were the law. So the unjust were the Pharisees, and the saints were the followers of Christ.

“Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The Pharisees are not the ones who will judge; the saints that follow Christ shall judge the world. So judge the small matters among you. Stop going to the scribes and Pharisees and go to the saints among you who follow Christ; they know the scriptures.

“I speak to your shame. Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?” Paul is speaking to the leaders in Corinth who were not doing their job: all that rank, and not one able to judge between his brethren. Why does that happen? Because they are hirelings, leaven in the church, sitting amongst us but not about the work.

The man of God out of Judah was charged by the word of the Lord, “Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.” The Lord told him what not to do and what to do. He refused the king, even for half his house. Then an old prophet in Bethel came after him: “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.”

This dude was lying. God said the only one he speaks with mouth to mouth is Moses; everybody else he speaks to with dreams and visions, and this man said an angel came to him. The man of God went back, ate and drank, and “a lion met him by the way, and slew him”: “It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord”.

That is why the Lord said, “Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” That is why you have to be mindful with brothers. If God tells you something, follow it; don’t go to the left or right of what he says because a brother says so. Follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.

Some people are in your life for blessings, some are in your life for cursings; but ultimately it is to try us, each and every one of us.

“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”. God is telling us to separate from these nations, these unbelievers. “and touch not the unclean thing”: do not follow their customs, their religions, their holidays or their politics. Only then will God receive us: “and I will receive you”.

What Paul instructed in Corinthians is nothing new. This is where it came from: “And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.” God instructed the twelve tribes to separate from the other nations and stop following the customs and traditions of those nations, and when they returned to him they separated themselves and confessed their sins.

Your churches have just never taught you that. They want to integrate; all churches want to integrate. Remember Philip Anthony: this is not a black church. Was that so moving? No, you sound like the devil now. He did not have to dance with the devil.

So coming out and being separate is the old path of Israel. The seed of Israel separates from the strangers, confesses its sins and the iniquities of the fathers, and then the Lord will be a Father unto us, and we shall be his sons and daughters.

“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. And Luke shows feigning in action: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words.” They pretended to be just men so they could catch Christ in his words.

During the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, so we expect that to be true today. There is going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day. It's going to happen, because the scriptures say it.

But we have to be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. Ezra asks God not to think upon those, “but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

“And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this.

How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have the desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself, to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You're a hireling.

You could be in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out. The hireling walks feignedly; the one whose heart burns is the one who has known God's fear.

“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

Diotrephes is another kind of hireling: he “loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” And the strange thing is, the apostles set this man up. He was always around and made it appear like he was in the truth. But everybody's problem isn't always sex; some brothers want power, preeminence. I was never anything in the world; I'm going to come in and be somebody. Not by the word of God, but by being deceitful and slick and witty, disrespectful in a secretive way.

Paul settles who has the preeminence: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” There is only one preeminent, and that is Christ. He is the king; not you, not me. Christ has the preeminence, not Diotrephes. Diotrephes lost his mind, and you know why? He was a hireling.

We have seen it: a brother in the office of ten sees a congregation in Alaska with no senior man, asks no counsel, pops up, and shazam, he's over the congregation, and because he came from the States they love him and accept him. It happened in Ghana and many of the African countries. Another went out, and where were the congregation's donations? In his personal bank account. You can't make this up. These are hirelings; they don't believe, and there is no fear among them.

Diotrephes was “prating against us with malicious words”: always something smart to say, I know what he knows, I know more precepts than you. He would not receive the brethren, not even the ones that taught him, and cast out any who wanted to visit the apostles. But John says “if I come, I will remember his deeds”, and “Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.”

Who are the elect the angels gather in Matthew 24? Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name.” Israel is God's elect.

So there's no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the angels gather the elect, and the elect is Israel. Ezekiel's sheep, Matthew's elect and Isaiah's elect are the same people.

The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors, who tell the people it is everybody. The Lord said: “I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick.” That's our people: we were broken, we're the sick ones. “but I will destroy the fat and the strong”: he is going to destroy the nations. “I will feed them with judgment.”

“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” Who is that I? Christ. And Christ said who he came for: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

That is what Christ was doing, seeking out the lost sheep of Israel, and that is what Paul and the apostles were doing after him. That was the great commission in Matthew 28:19.

So when Ezekiel says “I will seek that which was lost”, that's our people. The lost sheep Christ was sent to are the same sheep God promised to search out and deliver “out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day”: all places, countries and lands.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” These are the angels of Psalms 50, called from the heavens to gather.

Did he say gather everybody, all people? No. They gather his elect, and his elect are Israel. It's the same gathering Ezekiel spoke of: “so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.” The four winds are all the places, countries and lands where our people were scattered.

The prophets gather on the earth, the angels gather from the heavens, and it is the elect, the sheep of the house of Israel, who are gathered.

“Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.” The saints are the twelve tribes God gathers.

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: because we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. “let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: for so long we've been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” He doesn't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people.

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That's the rest right there. It is what Ezekiel promised the gathered sheep: “there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.”

Ezekiel says God will search his sheep and gather them from the countries. Who does the gathering? “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.” He calls to the heavens from above: those are the angels he's calling to. And to the earth: the earth are the prophets, you and me on the earth.

“Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Those are the twelve tribes of Israel. So he's telling the prophets, gather the twelve tribes, and he's telling the angels, gather the twelve tribes.

That is the promise of Ezekiel 34: “I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel.” The good pasture is the kingdom.

Moses chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” What is the sin he refused? John defines it: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is breaking God’s law. The pleasures of sin are the pleasures of transgressing the law, and if anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie. It is very fun. But you have to perform abstinence, and choose affliction with the people of God over it, the way Moses did.

That is the difference between Moses and the hireling. A hireling has a temporary time in this truth. He or she doesn’t care about salvation, and is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood, everything they built up, just for their own sin. The love of sin. The hireling chooses the pleasure of transgressing the law for a season; the true servant chooses to suffer with the people of God.

The pleasures of sin last only “for a season”, and Paul shows where they end: “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

If anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie; it is very fun. That is exactly why it is dangerous. Those who have pleasure in unrighteousness instead of believing the truth are the ones who are damned. So you have to perform abstinence.

Moses saw it. He chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” The hireling does the opposite. He has a temporary time in this truth and does not care about salvation. He or she is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood and everything they built up, just for their own sin, for the love of sin. That love of sin is having pleasure in unrighteousness, and its end is damnation.

“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

Against the hirelings who scatter the flock, the Lord promises “I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them: and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking”. Jeremiah shows what they will feed us with: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Knowledge and understanding of what? God's laws. It isn't talking about feeding them with jumping up and down, screaming and foaming at the mouth.

Right now we are lacking as a race, as a people. We are lacking knowledge, wisdom and understanding; and when you break it down, we are lacking rulership, dominion of the earth, our own country, a fortified family, a nation. We are lacking everything. Pastors after God's heart, feeding us the laws, are the shepherds who end that lack.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was during the time of Adam. Ezra says “the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. Strait things is tribulation.

So all Israel is going to go through tribulation, the righteous and the unrighteous. “they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The false prophets say “No evil shall come upon you”, but “a whirlwind of the Lord is gone forth in fury”, and it will not return until he has performed the thoughts of his heart.

What we see on the news, death after death, is just the beginning. A young black girl tied to a tree with a ratchet strap, the kind trucks use to hold down wood, and they call it suicide. Tonya Miller, 27, and Juliana Enza, 16, found hanging from trees, ruled suicides; look at all these names. They can insult our intelligence with this because we are not unified and not connected to the Lord; there is no consequence. They don't do it to the Chinese or Japanese. And it is not only the men: all you independent women, get ready. I don't see color; well, color sees you. It's going to escalate. They won't ask what God you serve: you're in the image of God, and they will come for all the melanated brothers and sisters. The righteous suffer the strait things and hope for the wide.

“They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace”. They are speaking to people who really hate God. At the sit down, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, we're not going to be here; the church won't be here. Christians just lie and tell you there's going to be peace.

Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

Write this down: women were never designed to lead men. God made the woman “an help meet” for the man, and when that order is turned around, Isaiah 3:12 calls it what it is: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.”

That is a curse. It is not a good thing; it shows things out of order, not how God set it up. A woman's body alone shows she was not made to lead men into danger: her cycle comes, she is pregnant for nine months, and she is supposed to lead you somewhere?

Women ruling over you is a curse, brothers. Some of you are scared to lead your house and have let her lead. If you are passive, scared, afraid of confrontation, she is going to walk all over you. It is not a secret; everyone sees it, and other men see it in your demeanor. You have to change the way you think. Stand up and take your place back.

The women were designed to be a help to their husbands. When they step outside of that, and when the brothers allow it, chaos follows. That is why there is dysfunction in our nation right now: because the men do not want to lead.

“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

“A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself”. Knowing the time, we had better prepare ourselves. Ezra was told: “For the world is divided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it are gone already, and half of a tenth part: And there remaineth that which is after the half of the tenth part.”

That was during the time of Ezra. Understand that we are in the last days; the clock is ticking, brethren. We have leadership able to show us what is going to come to pass, and we just saw Daniel 3 come to life before our eyes. Babylon is going to burn. If you're smart, you'll get ready.

“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”. Knowing the time, we must set our houses in order. Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right and fix their stuff.

If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage; that is the first place. If the home front isn't right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people? How are we going to inherit what the Lord has prepared for us if we are not taking this Bible seriously? The simple take notes, say that's some good stuff, close the Bible, go home and proceed to be a demon. They saw the evil but they aren't hiding, and they pass on and are punished.

“She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is the kind of wife you want, brothers. There was no kindness or wisdom in the email that attacked leadership over the one instance of a leader put out for adultery, while ignoring the three bishops and the seven or eight deacons who were in the midst of no such thing. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems. That is not wife material; they are idolatrous women, some of them idolatrous evil black women, and they will try to destroy your life. Be mindful who you marry.

Now see what language God uses when Israel is in the midst of sin; he uses it in the female context: “She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her”. There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

Marriage was designed to happen when you are young: you meet a young woman, and this is the person you grow old with. “rejoice with the wife of thy youth.” Tobias prayed the same thing on his wedding night: “And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

Hands went up around the room for five, ten, fifteen, twenty and twenty-five years of marriage and more, and the Bishop has been married 36 years. These are the examples we have right here. Those married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at their wife or husband and see when they were young. That is why they can be content: both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember.

“let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” When you marry her young her breasts are at three o'clock; as you grow old together they will be at six. But they are yours, brother, no matter what time it is. You walk in the room and she is the only thing you see. That bond can't be broken if you are in the Lord.

So we pray we are able to see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some don't; let it be because of passing, not because you weren't applying the scriptures or listening in class. The prophecy classes are dope, but you have to have the same zeal for the classes on marriage and repentance and apply them in your everyday life. Otherwise your marriage falls apart, your kids go who knows where, and then you look at us like it was our fault.

Satan's stipulation is worship, and many of our people will pay it for money. Paul says, “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.”

“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

That is what Satan will have you do: pierce yourself through with many sorrows, because you covet to be rich in this world. If you covet fame and fortune in this world, you must worship Satan. You must; that is the only way. That is what the Bible is saying.

So the power and the seat and great authority that the dragon gave the beast in Revelation 13 is the same thing he offered Christ on the mountain, all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, and the price has always been the same: fall down and worship me. The ones who will be rich take that snare and err from the faith.

Revelation 13:2 says “the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” How do we know that is what it is talking about? Because you can be blessed by God or you can be blessed by Satan, and some people do not understand that.

Matthew shows it: “the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” What is the stipulation? “if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” Fall down and worship Satan, and he will give you all this power and authority.

That is exactly what we read at the bottom of Revelation 13:2: the dragon, which is Satan in this part, gave this last beast his power, his nuclear power and armaments, his seat, and great authority. The beast of seven heads and ten horns, the European powers with America as the eighth head, took the offer Christ refused.

And people are still taking it. On Venice Beach you have people who want to be blessed by Satan: women run through by every so-called movie or music producer who walks up and down that beach, still waiting to be discovered; a man about 90 years old playing the guitar, waiting to be seen by Rolling Stone magazine. People are delusional.

Solomon said, “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” Paul says the same thing in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”. Our learning today. There are no new incidents on this earth; everything that was done in the past is reoccurring.

Ezra shows it with a ring: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is like a circle. “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first”. Slackness means slow: there is no slowness of the last judgments and no swiftness of the first. His judgments on the earth are a continual event that reoccurs over and over; it is the same thing.

That is why Paul said to comfort ourselves through what is written in the testimonies of the past: what we are living is a reoccurring event. To deal with these reoccurring events we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We see it now. Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and gathered the rulers to its dedication, setting up a one world religion; today pastors gather to pray over and dedicate a towering gold statue of Donald Trump. What we read in Daniel 3 is coming to pass again, because the judgments go around like a ring.

The things written aforetime were written for our learning, and Hosea shows how they were written: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, even Hosea. God multiplied visions, and he used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.

That is how the scriptures teach us today. The past is a similitude of what is happening now, and by comparing one thing to another we can see our own time in what was written. The last beast of Revelation 13 is described with the leopard, the bear and the lion of Daniel 7: it carries the attributes of Greece, Persia and Media, and Babylon. The golden image of Daniel 3 stands again in our day.

So we read the prophets as similitudes, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, because the Most High already showed in the past what he will do in the future.

Wisdom says that “Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they honoured, to the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.” Verse 17 goes with Matthew 24.

“Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” In Liberia there were ten brethren out there teaching, and they said the many is you. So the many Christ was talking about is ten men with a Bible? You’re stupid as hell.

The white man took the counterfeit of this white man’s image from far, from Rome and Spain, under the conquistadors. Columbus came with a whole wooden cross of Jesus and images of Jesus, and there were thousands of conquistadors who went worldwide. That is the many that came in his name saying I am Christ. He is not talking about ten negroes with a Bible; he is talking about these folks. But our people in Africa do not want to admit that; they feel safer saying it is you than the white man.

The image kept spreading. “The singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition”: the artificer is the artist. Leonardo da Vinci made preliminary sketches in the 1400s of Cesare Borgia as the new Jesus. The Head of Christ, the Sallman Head, was painted by Warner Sallman in 1940; the Baptist bookstore popularized it through the southern United States, and the Salvation Army and the YMCA handed out pocket-sized versions to American servicemen heading overseas in World War II. That is how that image became famous.

“And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god”. Our people in Christianity truly believe those false images of the white man are Jesus, and the Bible calls them the ignorant. “And this was an occasion to deceive the world”: the idolatry itself is the deceiving of many that Christ warned of, and it started with Nimrod, Semiramis and Tammuz long before Cesare Borgia.

Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. “Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately.” He came crouching and speaking softly: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” And Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord: “Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.”

This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. That is the perpetual hatred we never learned.

Esther 2:5 gives Mordecai’s line: “a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Mordecai, and Esther with him, were of the tribe of Benjamin. Go back to 1 Samuel 9 and see who Kish is.

“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Kish was a mighty man of power.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.”

So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line, the line of Kish. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows, because the enemy Saul was sent against in his day, the Amalekites and their king Agag, shows up again in Mordecai’s day. The hatred is perpetual, and it runs down the same lines.

“Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” We are the temple, the spiritual house Peter speaks of. “If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” That is why we have to change the way we conduct ourselves. Our communications must change. The malice, guile, hypocrisies, envies and evil speakings of 1 Peter 2:1 defile the temple.

Paul goes on in 2 Timothy: “Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation. There are brothers and sisters who are gold and silver, applying 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are those of wood and earth, meaning no good: fringes and a border of blue, but they have not changed their lives in two or three years. Not the new people, but those who have been with us for years and are still grimy, still that secret adulterer, still that liar, complainer, murmurer.

The captains must be able to identify in their school who is honourable and who is dishonourable. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge means cut them off, like pruning a plant and taking away the bad elements. I knew which brothers always got me in trouble; I almost got arrested many a time with those grimy brothers, and I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership. Keep the temple holy.

Christ's body was the temple, and his temple today is us. Peter says “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house”, and Paul shows how that house grows: “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”. All the building is you and me. See that word growing: Peter just explained how we grow, by laying aside all malice, all guile, all hypocrisies, all evil speakings, and desiring the sincere milk of the word.

You know what fitly framed together means? Stones have to come together. Brothers, we must merge together. Whatever your position is, play that position. Don't try to change positions through deceit. A brother was demoted in New York for lying over a simple thing; when we ask, most of the time we already know the answer, and when the witnesses are called, the liar is put on front street and found not worthy of his rank. A stone full of guile does not fit in the frame.

“In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.” Wherever our congregation is, that is a spiritual house, the real temple, and God dwells in it through the Spirit. That is why Zerubbabel is our example: he got to his position not only for his fighting skills but because he was of noble character, understanding God's truth. We should not be deceitful, envious, hateful or filled with guile toward one another, but lively stones with zeal, passion and fire, built together into the house where God lives.

Paul says in a great house there are vessels “of gold and of silver” and also “of wood and of earth”, and “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour.” The next chapter names who those vessels of dishonour are: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Why does it say a form of godliness? That is the fringes everybody wears and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible, saying Most High, in Christ, blessed heartily. But you are not keeping the laws in your heart. You are really not keeping the commandments.

The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation of Israel. There are brothers and sisters of gold and silver, applying what we read in 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are brothers and sisters with fringes and a border of blue who are no damn good. They have not changed their lives; they are the same as they were two, three years ago. Not the new people who just came in, but people who have been with us for years and are still grimy: still that secret adulterer, that liar, complainer, murmurer. You are that wood and that earth. In every IUIC school there are men and women of honour and of dishonour, and the captains must be able to identify which is which. If you can’t do that, there is a problem.

“from such turn away.” That is what he said in the chapter before: purge yourself from these. Purge means cut them off, cut them loose. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. You know which brothers always get you in trouble. Rolling with grimy brothers, you can almost get arrested many a time; cut them off, say I’m not rolling with y’all no more, and hang out with leadership. That is how you become a vessel “sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.”

The hearings said the American Negro is the one who is going to lead all the others, the vanguard of the liberation movement on an international scale. The Bible said it first: “And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”.

Judah is going to be the one teaching and preaching, and he is the one who is going to know where the tribes are. “let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

That is why, as in Daniel, the captor chose the best of the children of Israel, the king's seed and the princes, and brought them into the land. Esau took the best stock and put them in North America, and the American Economic Association wrote that the Negro stock landed in America was physically superior to the average of that left behind, the soundest and strongest, who transmitted to their offspring their qualities. We didn't write that; the white man wrote that. Judah in America is the one the Lord brings unto his people and helps from his enemies.

Babylon chose children of Israel “in whom was no blemish”, and the white man's own books say the stock landed in America was the soundest and strongest. A lot of our women don't understand this. “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” Don't give your strength to other nations, or to wicked women.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed”: sow with thine own race. “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” That's some good stock right there, and some of you are ashamed of it.

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” You didn't know the word race was in the Bible, in terms of ethnicity, in terms of your nationality. This is what your sons and daughters have to know, instead of running around giving their seed to any old thing out there in the world.

And don't hold your breath for reparations. Esau is not stupid. After slavery we had no reparations and still built great, advanced societies without white folks, and they came up with a reason to drop dynamite on us and destroy them, even Seneca Village in Central Park. Trust in the goodness of your stock: we can build without them.

Nebuchadnezzar told Ashpenaz to bring “certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes; Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science”. That is what Deacon Malachi was talking about: Babylon didn't take any old body. Esau did the same thing. They said no, we need the best ones, and put them in North America. The ones they left behind were not the same, and that is why you see Africa the way it is.

The hearings they read say it: within the Negro population of the United States, the Negro working class is destined to be the vanguard of all liberation movements, and a strong Negro movement in the USA will be able to influence and direct the Negro movement in all those backward parts of the world. See what they called all the other places: backward parts of the earth. That is why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks. Canada and Europe have free healthcare and America does not, because they don't want the American blacks to get it; this group here is more dangerous than all the other groups.

That is why the Lord said: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. That is what the white man knows. It isn't Judah over in Africa; it isn't Judah in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here, and the Lord is going to raise them up first.

So be proud of this history. Don't be mad; be glad. Sisters, don't just let your boys run out: the white man has his eyes on your sons, because they know what stock they come from. Even if the father was no good, the son is still of good stock, and there is still hope for him.

When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: all the other nations sit between those two. They are like extras in the movie. Moab is an extra; Ishmael is an extra. The story is Jacob and Esau. Christians do not know what that means at all.

Rebekah bore twins, but they were not identical, because the Lord said “two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” They looked different. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau means wasted away: his melanin was wasted away. Look at them in a heat wave in France: when they are in the sun they get red. Down south they are called rednecks, but it is not just their necks. Don't call them white; they are Esau, and these are his children.

The scripture never mentions Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father. In fact, Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. Genesis 2:7 shows what that was: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” The dust of the ground is different shades of brown, and the deeper you dig, the darker it gets. That is what Adam looked like, and Eve, and everyone who came from them.

The only one who differed was Esau, and that is why the scribes had to write down his color: he was starkly different. In the old world, Cain's line was cursed with a lack of melanin. The flood came and killed them all off, and God brought them all back through Noah's three sons.

So when you move up the generations to Isaac and Rebekah, the two lines return in one womb. Esau is the return of Cain's lineage, and Jacob is the return of Seth. That is why the two boys were two manner of people from birth: Esau the cunning hunter, a man of the field who liked the rush of the hunt, and Jacob a plain man, dwelling in tents, herding the sheep and the goats.

Esau cried, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” Jacob had already received the major blessing. Rebekah sent him in, dressed in goats' hair so he would feel hairy like his brother, because she remembered what God told her at the birth: the elder shall serve the younger. When Jacob feared a curse, she said let it fall on her. The white man's the devil, and when you ask the Christians about those two boys, they say Jacob was the evil son and Esau the good one, and black people in church echo those same sentiments. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicator, the one who despised his birthright, and Rebekah was being obedient to God.

They want a white Jesus who teaches love for everybody: if it feels good, just do it. Remember they said we have no king but Caesar.
