The nation that reigns over the kings of the earth is the United States of America, not the Vatican. It is a mystery because the same place that destroyed us is the place that feeds us and gives us Medicaid, housing and education.

People will hear us teaching and say, oh, you're saying all Judah is in North America. No, that's not what we're saying, just like we know all Levi is not on the island of Haiti, and all Benjamin is not on the island of Jamaica or Trinidad. “And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Israel and Judah were scattered worldwide.

Zechariah is pointing out a remnant of Judah that is in North America. And what's so special about this group here? The house of David is here. You are going to find that thing out.

Why are they so hard on Judah here as opposed to Judah scattered elsewhere? The civil rights hearings of 1959 before the Senate, under the title American Negro problems, say it: the Negro question in the United States of America must be treated in its relation to the huge Negro masses oppressed and exploited by white imperialism in Africa and South America, and the Negroes of the United States are the most advanced section of the Negro population of the world and can play a decisive role in helping and leading the liberation movement of the Negro colonies. You have Negroes in Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Saudi Arabia; Judah is everywhere, the southern kingdom is everywhere. But the white man examined all the Negro populations and said the American Negro is the most advanced.

Deacon Malachi brought it out: when Nebuchadnezzar came against Judah, they took the best of the best, the most educated. Esau isn't stupid; he knows that history. At Elmina Castle in Ghana, the tour guide said it himself: you never ask why the American black is more advanced; when they came to Africa, they took the best of them. Look right after slavery, without even reparations, how the blacks here advanced, and how they came and dropped bombs and destroyed them. That's why Esau always has his eye on the American blacks: that group here is more dangerous than all the other groups where the blacks are. And that's why the Lord said, “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first.” It isn't Judah over in Africa or in Saudi Arabia. It's Judah here. This history you should be proud of.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the land of the north is North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Which Zion?

“But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” The Lord chose the tribe of Judah, mount Zion. So we know that the Zion dwelling with the daughter of Babylon is Judah: deliver thyself, O Judah.

Benjamin does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon; they are on a nice, pleasant island. Levi does not dwell with the daughter of Babylon. That's why all the tribes make fun of Judah: we have places to go back to when we want to run; y'all have no place to go. Why? Because Judah dwells with the daughter of Babylon, with Edom, in North America.

“For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: he that touches you touches my favorite. “For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”: Edom shall be a spoil to us, and we are the servants here. “and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.”

The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

In the sit-down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat argued there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.

Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

Zechariah asks, “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”. Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity, and Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So who is this great mountain? Jeremiah shows where the mountain is: “And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the Lord.”

Watch what he calls Babylon: “Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.” The great mountain is Babylon.

“And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the Lord.” That lets you know it is not Iraq. Are people still living in Iraq today? Yes. This says “thou shalt be desolate for ever”, so it is not talking about ancient Babylon.

So the great mountain before Zerubbabel is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Before him it becomes a plain, flattened and destroyed, and it is done “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Everything we do must be according to the spirit of the Most High God; it has nothing to do with our physical powers and our skills.

Zerubbabel is the branch in the line of Christ: Matthew's genealogy runs from Zerubbabel through Abiud, Eliakim, Azor, Sadoc, Achim, Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” So when the Lord speaks to Zerubbabel, he is speaking to the father of Christ's line.

“Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.” Zerubbabel was of the king's bodyguard, one of the top fighters. The Lord is telling him, no, this has nothing to do with your fighting skills; we know you can break bones, but that's not what is going to overcome everything. The spirit of the Lord is what's going to do it.

“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon the great, and it shall become a plain: flattened, destroyed. “and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it”: crying mercy, mercy unto it.

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is that? Christ. He is the headstone. Not only would Christ come from Zerubbabel's lineage; Zerubbabel shall bring forth the headstone.

“The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it.” His hands started the foundation of the temple, and he did finish the temple. But this goes deeper than that: because of verse 7, verses 6 through 9 are going into the last days as well, when the great mountain, Babylon the great, is brought down to a plain and the headstone, Christ, is brought forth.
blog/2026/2026-08-08-2026-08-08-from-bro:
“A wise son heareth his father’s instruction”. When you first come in as a brother, you are still attached to the life you are coming out of; somebody has to instruct you. Acts shows it. The eunuch “Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?”

We study and we get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up? When we give an instruction, do we follow up and ask, did you understand what I'm telling you to do? Or is it, boy, I said do it, do it, until the kid is intimidated and afraid to do it? Are we checking whether the person is actually ascertaining the instructions, or just repeating what they see and trying to make it?

Black people will buy something that has to be put together, dump all the pieces out, look at the picture on the box and put it together like that instead of reading the instructions. That is what we do with the scriptures. We read and study, but are we challenging ourselves on what we study? Are we asking the questions and going back to say, I'm reading this, but I don't understand any of it? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people?

“And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.” We all have to be guided in the instruction we are getting. You can't just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit, and that is how a son learns to hear his father's instruction instead of becoming the scorner who hears not rebuke.

“He that walketh with wise men shall be wise”: broaden your circle to wise men, men that keep the commandments, and you'll have righteous success. Speaking of that: “The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.” When the Lord blesses you, there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains.

Think of lifting weights. When you exercise, the muscles are being broken down; an acid releases in your body and breaks them down. But when it regroups, it builds more muscle and makes you look stronger, and when you look stronger you feel stronger and sit up a little more. Shout out to the Greensmen and the brothers that got necks: they were fat and their neck sat down in their shoulders, then they slimmed down and now you can see they've got a neck. People start praising you: bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed.

That is what being around wise men does. Everybody knew the men who walked with Christ: you sound like him, you talk like him, you've got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up and makes you feel and be somebody.

Evil success is different. Some kids think making money on OnlyFans or social media content is success; it's not, and it's nothing to glory in. It seems good and brings profit, so it is “abomination to fools to depart from evil”. That's why rappers and entertainers keep selling digital crack and the prostitute lifestyle to the community but not to their own kids. Evil success comes with sorrow; the blessing of the Lord adds none.

The Bible has given us all the instructions we need to fix ourselves, and the ultimate fix to all of our problems is remembering and keeping the laws of God. Mattathias told his sons: “Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

That is what a man in his truth is going to do: give his life. That is his time, his patience, his problems, his traumas. Sisters as well, you are going to give your lives for that. Everything should revolve around being an Israelite.

A brother asked how he could normalize the lifestyle of an Israelite, and the question itself was the answer: normalize it in your everyday life. When you wake up in the morning, you are an Israelite. You are not a black man in America; that is just what you have been labeled. The same way you grew up admonished by the media in being a negro in America, you have to reverse that and admonish yourself in what an Israelite is, the Israelite culture. Your thought process has to be an Israelite man, not a man in America.

“Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time”. That is Romans 15:4: the things written aforetime were written for our learning. Remembering the acts of our fathers is how you normalize what it is to be an Israelite, a person keeping God's commandments. We see where they overcame and where they were punished, and we say, I see the mistake they made, I am not going to make it; I am going to be better than the men before me.

“so shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name”. That is how we receive that name, and how we break the generational curses we have been stigmatized with.
blog/2026/2026-08-08-2026-08-08-stay-in-:
John writes “concerning them that seduce you”, and verse 27 shows how the seduction comes: “ye need not that any man teach you”. The antichrist is going to try to teach you something. He isn't floating in the air going boo; he's teaching. What do you think all these apologetics are? That is the spirit of antichrist. Does that mean the bishops and deacons can't teach us? No. It is the ones who fell away: “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and now all of a sudden they want to teach you.

Jude shows who they are: “These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” There will be those who separate themselves, sensual, not having the spirit of the Lord. How can we prove it? What does the Lord require of us on the holy Sabbath day? So when the spirit rises up in you to stay at home, to play Sabbath sick, to forsake the assembling of ourselves together, whose spirit are you moving in? You see how simple that is. The Lord is about unity; he has never been about separation.

When that spirit rises up in you, recognize it, say Satan is trying to get me, and force yourself past that point. Do you wake up every day on the right side of the bed, everything perfect? No, but you push past it. You don't call off work every day. You still go shuffle the white man's papers, stand by the coffee machine and the water cooler and act interested in the job when you don't want to be there. The hope is that once we are among each other, someone who has the spirit of the Lord can be so infectious that it jumps on me, and I get in the spirit of the Lord.

The gripes and unresolved issues, hatred and jealousy, are what Satan uses as a reason to send you back to Caesar Borgia: he spoke rough to me, he didn't say anything to me. Some brothers and sisters, no matter what you do, you can't make them happy; some are ordained to be that sensual brother or sister. That is why we have to stay in the spirit.

Paul sent to know the Thessalonians’ faith “lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain.” During afflictions we are mentally, physically and spiritually in a weakened state, as Christ was after forty days and forty nights of fasting, and the tempter comes. One of the ways he comes is through correction. When tribulation comes, brothers who do not want to address the elephant in the room leave and rebrand themselves, like the brother who was here in 2016 and 2017, never around long enough to be built up, now online as an apologist calling himself an ex black Hebrew Israelite. He could not get his wife to submit, and rather than take the counsel, he left.

“All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.” If you have ever dealt with us in a counsel setting, where are we going to read from? The scriptures. So your anger and your disdain is not with us; it is with God.

When you get that deep sinking feeling in your diaphragm, when you want to get upset and get mad, that is Satan stirring you up to be disobedient to what God has said, using your emotions to unravel you. Whether it is correction or instruction in righteousness, such as, brother, I do not think this move is good for you, do not go down this path, some brothers get in their feelings and do what they want anyway. Then the hands of the one who gave the instruction are clear.

Counsel is of the Lord, and the Lord is in the midst of it. But Satan is right there too, telling you it is not of the Lord. Stay in the spirit, so that the tempter does not make the labour in vain.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” How can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained, from the council Ezra speaks of, when he prepared the world “which was not yet made” and “no man spake against me.”

Think about it. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord says, when you grow up, you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth.

The same way with these young men. If I could go back and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth! But learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. If you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood the trials that came to many brothers and sisters then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. There was not every topic and every class online for you to watch and say, let me get my spirit right. When I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.

That is every single one of us. It is ordained by the Lord for you young ones to be here in 2026, when your parents can send you a class for the spirit you are dealing with, so you are able to abide in this time. Many fell out back then. You were known and set apart before you came out of the womb, called at the time the Lord chose.

Ezra says, “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed.” Before the world was made there was a council, and no one spoke against what was ordained. Christ said, these spirits over here, y’all are the twelve tribes of Israel; those spirits right there, y’all are the Jebusites. No one disagreed. When you are before the creator you are not going to say, no, I don’t want to be the Edomites.

It is like a screenplay writer and a director. You show up as the actor, they give you the script, and you say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Michael B. Jordan agreed to play Killmonger; they portrayed him as the bad guy, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. Chadwick Boseman agreed to his role. Everybody agreed to their role, then the movie was made and we cheered, Wakanda forever. The same way the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles and tasks.

Wisdom of Solomon proves he knew beforehand: “As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do.” The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt and all the plagues that came. What is very telling is that he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.

So what Paul said and Peter said, the prophet Ezra says the same: it was ordained before the world was made. Now “the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”, and the Lord already knew who would be ungodly and dealt with them accordingly.

“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.
blog/2026/2026-08-15-2026-08-15-destruct:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

“She is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You didn't learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself; you never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.
blog/2026/2026-08-15-2026-08-15-give-dil:
Paul declares that God “hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.” As it is also written. Acts 15 says the same thing when the apostles came together: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written”.

As it is written means they had to go back and search: wait, this was written here. What happened in that particular place of the book makes sense because the prophets wrote about it. The glad tidings Paul preached were not something new; they were the promise made unto the fathers, fulfilled unto their children, and the prophets had already written it.

That is precept upon precept. Christians call it Hebrew hopscotch and cherry-picking, but it is studying and understanding the word of God, understanding the history and what things must take place. The apostles themselves did it: they took what was happening and laid it beside what the prophets wrote.

Those who do not have the spirit of the Lord cannot do it, and they want to shame us for having understanding and being able to go from Genesis to Revelation and give the understanding thereof. We are going to keep on going precept upon precept, confounding you negroes, because that is how the apostles taught: as it is written.

Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

Christ “went and preached unto the spirits in prison”. We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. Christians ask, did he go under the ground? No. Being dominated by another race is a prison, and Christ came to us while Rome dominated us and preached to us.

“Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” The word covenant means agreement, and our people made one. See that? Wicked men went out of Israel saying, let us go and make a covenant, an agreement, with the heathen, meaning the other nations, the Greeks in this context. They told the people that since they had departed from the nations they had had much sorrow.

People often say the Bible has no relevance today. They join MAGA, the Republican party, the Democratic party.

Against the covenant with death, the Lord God lays something else: “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.” This stone is Christ, and Ephesians proves it: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.”

Christ himself is the chief corner stone. That means he is the leader; he is the commander. Only what is built on the corner stone, Christ, stands.

“for he was cut off out of the land of the living”: that is when he was crucified. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The people of the prince that shall come is Rome.

So the same Rome that dominated Israel when Christ was cut off came and destroyed the city and the sanctuary. Christ was cut off for the transgression of his people, and desolations were determined upon the city by the hand of Rome.

We might think that Christ doesn't understand what we are going through. Isaiah 53 shows that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, and verse 8 says: “He was taken from prison and from judgment.” How?

John shows it. “And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend.” Pilate “brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.”

“And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King! But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. “and who shall declare his generation?” David answers: “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.”

To declare means to teach. To declare means to preach. They shall come and shall declare his righteousness: that's us, you and me. Unto a people that shall be born: that's us too.

So the question Isaiah asks is answered by a seed that serves him and is accounted to the Lord for a generation. Christ was cut off out of the land of the living, but his generation is declared by those who come after, teaching and preaching his righteousness to our people that he hath done this.

Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. “For I knew that they would not hear me”: that is why he put us in captivity, because we are a stiffnecked people. He delivered us to the enemy, by ships, “unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. This land is the land of our enemy: our enemy conquered us and made this land his land. Far is here, far from Jerusalem; near is Africa or Madagascar, colonised just the same.

“but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In our captivity, in the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. That is what bethink means: remember, call to mind. Solomon saw in the spirit our people put on the ships and scattered all over the world, yokes put upon our necks, and destroyed so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. He saw that we would lose ourselves and our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, instead of in the image of God.

So first we must remember ourselves. We can only say “We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness” if we know who we are. And once you learn who you are, you learn who the enemy is by default. As long as you don’t know who you are, you will make your own people from the continent or the Caribbean your enemy, while the white man gets a pass.

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. The Lord will bring you into captivity again, because Egypt represents bondage. What does Egypt represent? The first commandment tells you.

“I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.”

Egypt is the house of bondage: the house of slavery, the house of captivity. Egypt and slavery are synonymous. So when the curse says into Egypt again, it means into slavery again.

And it says with ships. Not imaginary ships, not planes, not trains, not a blimp or a hot air balloon: with ships. Ships will be used during this Egypt. And the Lord says it is “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: that Egypt as a nation, the one we walked into the first time, we will never see again as slaves. That is done. This Egypt is by boats, and “there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”, slave men and slave women, sold from those ships to the same enemies who put a yoke of iron upon our neck in verse 48.

Last of all, “and no man shall buy you”. The first time, the Lord brought us out of the house of bondage by Moses, and before that we had Samson and Gideon save us. This slavery, nobody. The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

A quick precept on borrowing a little here and borrowing a little there: “Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt lie in wait for thine own life, and be talked on.” That is what was going on in Thessalonica. Some walked “disorderly, working not at all”, and they had become beggars by banqueting upon borrowing.

Paul had already commanded “that if any would not work, neither should he eat.” A man must labor. As a leader especially, you have to work and hold a job. How can you instruct the people and show them how to build a nation if the headman himself and the men under him are unemployed, refusing to work and take care of themselves?

“be talked on.” People are going to talk about your nasty bum self. Why are they talking? Because you are a bum. You don’t have a job. You are always borrowing from this one, borrowing from that one, here a little, there a little. That is why Paul says “note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed”: you are supposed to shame the man that refuses to work and is fleecing the people. Borrow here, borrow there, need this here, got this here.

We know brothers fall on hard times. Come to the leadership; we will help you. Very rarely will we not help a person in the body who holds a job, pays their bills, gives offerings and helps. That is not how we move. But when it becomes a pattern, and a side thing on the side, you lose the trust. When I hear that, what I think is: we are back in the world.

“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

Hosea ends with a promise: “he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” What is the analogy of the former and latter rain? It's going to be a blessing. When we harvested crops, we looked forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us. That's how he punished us.

We read that in Deuteronomy 28: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” That is what it looks like when the rain does not come: the heaven shut like brass, the ground hard as iron, and powder and dust in place of rain.

So when Hosea says the Lord will come unto us as the rain, it is the curse being lifted. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. We were torn by captivity and slavery, and he will heal us, meaning redeem us out of this situation. After two days, two thousand years, he revives us, and in the third day he raises us up to who we are, to our identity.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do, then shall we be bound up and healed. The rain the Lord withheld in the curses comes back as a blessing, and that blessing will be in the application of his laws.

Hosea prophesied: “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.” These are those days. We were out for a long time, without the understanding of who we were as a people or what the will of God was for us, and in the last days the Lord raised up the prophets on the earth again to teach the word of God and apply it, so we could be delivered out of here. Where in the New Testament do we read that the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord? Right here: “But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.” That's us, reviving in this time. What you are part of is the resurrection of God's Christ's kingdom, and in that kingdom righteousness must reign. The Father is going to try us to see if we will worship him according to spirit and truth.

And what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Worshipping in truth is the application of God's laws, the keeping of God's commandments.

“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” Emphasise one word: must. There's no other way to do it. Take one law that is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. We must congregate, it's a holy convocation; we cannot cook, clean, shop, buy or sell on the Lord's Sabbath. There's no deciding it's not important. It's those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us. If someone won't congregate with the body and goes to congregate with somebody put out of the body, that's sin: can two walk together except they be agreed? We rationalize in our mind what we think God will be all right with, but his thoughts are not our thoughts. Do what he told you to do.

Where the law is not applied, Hosea says the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” There is no knowledge of God because the laws of God are not being taught or enforced. “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” To break out is to break away from the law: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Blood touching blood is violence and hatred against each other. “Therefore shall the land mourn”: if those same sins abide in the body, the congregation won't grow or flourish. So leaders must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example themselves. What God asks is a small thing next to the sins we have committed: not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath holy. The truth is all we've got to get out of here. There is no plan B; outside of this is death.

John is the only one in the Bible who calls a system or a person the antichrist. The prophets spoke of that last kingdom that would fight against Christ at his return, but they did not call it antichrist. John says “as ye have heard that antichrist shall come”, which is future, “even now are there many antichrists”. Anti means against. Even in John's time many were against Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us”. These were men among the apostles who up and left the apostles and their teachings, which were the teachings of Christ, and went out teaching against them. They said the resurrection had taken place already. They taught that you have to be circumcised. That is an antichrist doctrine, one form of antichrist in the time of the apostles.

That goes back to the history in Acts 15: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.” The Pharisees were pushing first and foremost that they had to be circumcised after the manner of Moses, meaning the old covenant of animal sacrifice, and not Christ. It is not only circumcision of the foreskin, because that is a law we have to do; it is that they pushed that before they pushed Christ.

So from the beginning there were many antichrists: those who went out from the apostles and taught contrary to Christ. That is why John says “they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.”

“for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” What is the falling away? Slavery, captivity. And the precept for it is Luke: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

We fell by the edge of the sword, and we were led away as slaves into all nations. That is what happened to us. Before Christ returns, Israel had to fall away, and that falling away goes into a lot: it goes into us even forgetting our nationality and all of that.

The apostles asked Christ what they had to look for before his return and for the end, and Paul is explaining the same thing here. “Let no man deceive you by any means” is the same thing Christ said: don’t let anybody deceive you. All the prophets say the same thing in different words. Christ said Israel would be led captive until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled; Paul says the day of the Lord shall not come except there come a falling away first.

And while Israel is in that captivity, “that man of sin” must “be revealed, the son of perdition.” Instead of saying antichrist, Paul says the man of sin. It is not one person but a race, a people: Edom, the one Malachi says the prophets “shall call them, The border of wickedness.” That is the time we are living in now, with Israel fallen away into all nations and the prophets revealing the wicked, and that is why the day of the Lord has not yet come.

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

Christ said many would come in his name and deceive many by changing who he and his people are. So look at what the apostles and prophets were called: “Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene.”

They were called what? Niger means black. The white man uses that term as a derogatory word, but the prophets were called black right through history. So if the prophets were black, what does that mean Christ was? Black too.

And the same way they were called that then, we are called that today. Nothing has changed. The people of the Bible were black, which is why the false Christ of Christianity, the white Jesus, is a deception. Christianity is built on white supremacy, on murder and bloodshed, and those who come in Christ's name with a white image are against the Christ of the Bible.

Christ warned, “For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” John says the same beast “opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.”

To come in Christ's name saying I am Christ, I am Christian, I am the people of Christ, is blaspheming his name, because they are not the Christ of the Bible. That is Christianity. In the 1400s, during the Renaissance, they changed over the black icons all over Europe and set themselves up as the anointed ones, the people of God, the Jew. They came in the name of Christ and set up that false religion and deceived the whole world.

You heard it from their own mouths. Jake Lang, the one burning Qurans and causing riots this week, said Jesus was a white Jewish man just like him, and that God would not make himself not white. That is blasphemy against God. They call themselves Christians: that is blasphemy against his name. They call themselves the white angels: that is blasphemy, a lie told against the Bible. Christianity and Judaism cannot be separated; to set up Christianity they had to set themselves and their race up as the Jews and erase the history of the real Jews.

Do they love Jesus? They love him once he looks like them. Tell them Jesus Christ is a black man and you see the anger in their face. They hate black people and they hate Christ. That whole religious system is the antichrist system, against the true Christ, and the world calls us a hate group and black extremists for saying we are the Jews and the believers of Christ.

This explains the war in heaven: “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth. And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit.” The high ones that are on high are the people ruling. The Lord is going to punish Europe and America, and the kings of the earth too. The gathering into the pit goes into Revelation 20.

Isaiah 34 shows what heaven means. “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies”: in Revelation their armies are called his angels. “he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.” “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll.” “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Is this heaven paradise? No. This heaven is the governments of this world, and the sword comes down upon Idumea, Edom, the people of his curse.

So the dragon in Revelation 12 is Edom, the fourth beast, also called the Devil and Satan. That war in heaven is Christ fighting with the white man and his armies: Lucifer falling from heaven: how art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer. “neither was their place found any more in heaven”: they have no rulership any more on this earth. And the one “which deceiveth the whole world” is not just a spiritual demon; it's his children, the white man, Edom, Lucifer, that transformed himself into an angel of light.

Daniel said, “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered.” That time is Armageddon, when all nations rise up and fight, and Michael rises up to fight for us. Revelation 12 is the same thing: “And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon.” It's not talking about war in the sky, as Christians say, Lucifer fighting with God and his angels. It's all nations fighting with each other. This is the time of trouble.

“and the dragon fought and his angels.” Who is the dragon? Lucifer: America and Europe. His angels are his armies. Isaiah proves it: “In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.”

Leviathan, the piercing serpent, that crooked serpent, is the white man. And the dragon that is in the sea is America. The Lord will punish him with his great and strong sword in that day, the same day Michael stands up for Daniel's people and they are delivered.

“Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters.” Remember what we read: “the dragon fought and his angels.” That's what we are reading about here: Christ and Michael and the angels fighting against the white man and his army.

“Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness.” The heads of leviathan are all the heads: Europe, France, all of them; America, all of them. Christ is going to destroy that dragon, the whole government.

That is why Revelation says the dragon and his angels “prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven.” They don't win against Michael and the angels. When Christ returns, Michael and the angels fight against the white man and his army, and every head of leviathan is broken in pieces.

“We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. So you see who is referred to as the star, the bright morning star: Christ, the day star that arises in your hearts.

Then why is the king of Babylon, America, referred to as Lucifer? Because “such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.” “And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.” The white man came and taught another Christ and transformed himself into an apostle of Christ. America transformed itself in the 1950s into a God-loving Christian nation, and for the last seventy years has pushed that it is here to set up righteousness and justice on the earth, after murdering, stealing, colonizing and enslaving millions of people.

That is why Isaiah calls him “Lucifer, son of the morning”: he says he is Christian, righteous, the light, and makes himself look like the morning star. But Christ is the real morning star, “the true Light”, and the day star Peter speaks of arises in the hearts of those who take heed to the sure word of prophecy.

Christ says, “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” So who is the morning star? Christ is the morning star. Then why is Lucifer called “son of the morning”? The King James is the only version with Lucifer there, because the scholars who translated it understood something everybody else did not: there is a difference between that morning star and the morning star we read about all through the scriptures.

Balaam saw the true star: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob”. A star out of who? Out of Jacob. Did it say out of Esau? No: out of Jacob.

“and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel”: a ruler shall rise out of Israel. “and shall smite the corners of Moab”, the Moabites, the Chinese, “and destroy all the children of Sheth.”

So the star in the scriptures is Christ, the ruler rising out of Israel, the offspring of David. The star comes out of Jacob, not Esau, and that is how we know the one called Lucifer, the false morning star, is a different one.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”. “and the Ancient of days did sit”. The Ancient of days means he was here before days began; that is the Most High, and his judgment sat. Did sit: that tells you something. He had a body in order to sit. He had legs, he had a garment on, he sat down, and he had hair on his head. People say God doesn't have a body; he has a celestial body. I know the Most High is the Most High, but he had a form so we could describe him. He didn't say he was a lizard or some other creature; he sat down and judged, so he looked like a man type of figure, the way the Lord is called a man of war.

“whose garment was white as snow”: he wasn't like a ghost or a sheet flying in the wind; the garment was on his body. “and the hair of his head like the pure wool”: like pure negro hair, white and woolly, black men's hair. That is our king, that is our creator, and his Son looks just like him. That is what is coming to us.

So in the days of these kings, while they are in rulership and the decadence is setting in, the Most High is causing us to get ourselves together, and persecution is part of that. When the thrones are cast down and the Ancient of days sits in judgment, the God of heaven sets up the kingdom that “shall not be left to other people”, other races and nations, but is for the twelve tribes of Israel, and it “shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”. That is what Christ is going to do.

Jeremiah says to Babylon the Great, “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness”: the measure of her evils has come up to the Lord's nostrils. Samuel asked Saul, “Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the Lord?” King Saul had an issue with being obedient to the Lord, and God called that disobedience evil in his sight. Saul answered, “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord”, and then, “But the people took of the spoil.” Was that a sign of godly sorrow? No, there was none involved. Isaiah 58:9 names what Saul was doing.

“Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity.”

What is the putting forth of the finger? That is blaming. Saul blamed the people right after saying he had kept Agag alive. He blamed the people for keeping the sheep and the best of the flocks, but did not take accountability for keeping Agag the Amalekite alive. So what does the Lord say? He is not going to hear any of us until we stop playing the blame game. The Lord answers, “Here I am”, when the finger is taken away.

Stop blaming others. How are you dealing with that situation? I am bitter against this person because they did this to me; I have hatred towards this person because of this. The Lord does not care about your reasoning or your justification, because every one of us will be judged according to our ways. The Lord sees how that person is treating you, and the same way he sees how you are reacting to that treatment. If you trust in the Lord, you act according to how God commanded you to deal with that situation, and then let the Lord deal with that person.

That is a building block of bitterness. Disobedience, then justifying yourself, then blaming others: the bitterness is compounded on sins that were already there. As 1 Samuel 15:22 says, “to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

Mark 7:22 names “an evil eye” among the evil things that come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” 1 Samuel 18:9 says “Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” Was it with the looks of righteousness, or with an evil eye? An evil eye. And that evil eye defiled Saul even further, after the Lord had already rejected him. To see it, go back to where Saul’s trouble began, in chapter 16.

“But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” Saul was already battling some things. The Lord had rejected him, and an evil spirit from the Lord had taken him.

“And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee. Let our lord now command thy servants, which are before thee, to seek out a man, who is a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.” They told him: find someone who plays cunningly on a harp, and that spirit will leave you.

There are building blocks of bitterness. Bitterness doesn’t just come about; there are other things first. Saul rejected the word of the Lord, and the Spirit of the Lord departed from him. That was the ground the evil eye grew in. And don’t think, because you are not battling that spirit right now, that it won’t come. Satan says, hold my cup. Wait until you get the new job offer, the promotion, the demotion, the transfer to another school or another city, where you are dealing with different spirits and different circumstances, and you wonder why you are being troubled in the spirit. If it had not been for the Lord, we would all be as Sodom.

“And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.”

So David did a good thing by playing the music to have that spirit depart from King Saul. Saul did what the servants said, the spirit left him, and he was refreshed. He was like, man, I needed that. He was back in the spirit again. David was sent for Saul’s benefit, and Saul could not see it.

Now fast forward to chapter 18. Saul “eyed David from that day and forward”, and “it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul.” The very next day after he had an evil eye towards David, meaning he was ready to do harm to David, that evil spirit returned. “And David played with his hand, as at other times: and there was a javelin in Saul’s hand.” David had already done this for him, as at other times. “And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it.”

That is how quickly hatred can progress: the man whose playing made the evil spirit depart becomes the target of the javelin. That is Mark 7: “an evil eye” comes from within and defiles the man. The evil eye brought the evil spirit back, and the bitterness turned into an attempt to kill.
