Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

Ananias and Sapphira sold a possession and “kept back part of the price”. It was their property anyway; they did not have to lie. But Peter said, “Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?”

Nobody had to tell Peter that. He already knew. That was the spirit of God working those senses. When he saw him, he already knew something was not right with this man, something was not right with this spirit: you are dealing evil right now. That is what the scripture means: “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things”. A spiritual man discerns all things.

Sirach shows how that discerning works: “As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” When you eat, you do not have to see; you can tell the difference between chicken and beef, chicken and fish, without looking. So a heart of understanding can discern false speech. One way: a man who is talking too much. You do not have to convince anyone of the truth.

Peter told him, “thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” And “Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.” The fear came because Peter was able to discern lies and truth. We laugh about it because we know it is true: when you are not moving right and a brother in the spirit sees it, you wonder how he knew. That is clear knowing, the spiritual senses trained and at work.

Moses commanded: “thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing. “Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law”. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God: in hearing we process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life.

So we have to exercise these senses: in what we watch, as Job 31 was pulled up, and in our hearing, what we ingest and listen to. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.

That is why the law is read in the hearing of the whole house, even “their children, which have not known any thing”, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord. If the ear is filled with the law, it forms the mind in the law; if it is filled with evil communications, it corrupts the manners.

We exercise the physical senses, what we see and what we hear, so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have. Going from milk to meat means training the ear on the word of God and guarding it from everything that would corrupt it.

“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

Sirach names the senses the Most High gave man: “They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.” Cogitation is the act of thinking very carefully and deeply about a subject, or a carefully considered thought itself; meditation is a good word for it too, the capacity to think or reflect.

So the sixth is understanding and the seventh is speech, and speech is the interpretation of what your mind meditates on. That is why “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What you meditate on is what comes out of your mouth.

Thinking and reflecting do not work unless they are funnelled through the word of God; that is how your mind has to work. If you are not moving right, the thought that comes out is going to be off, and so will the speech that interprets it.

The list goes on: “Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand. Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.” The tongue is the instrument we use to form our words. Counsel is a man weighing options and determining what should be done, but he must be a godly man who surrounds himself with godly people. A mind fed on porn and then making decisions will make a mistake, and a mouth speaking out of that heart will show it. These senses are given so we can understand good and evil, and they have to be exercised in the word.

“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resist: resist the pleasure of sin. It is also in Hebrews, where the saints are striving against sin and resisting it. You are resisting sin.

James said it just before: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” If your eye is single, what are you resisting? All your appetites and all the lust you have. If your eye is single, you are on that path: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

The opposite is the double-minded man: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You are looking at the Lord and you are looking at Pornhub; you are looking at the Lord and you are in the midst of sin. “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

A brother who would not resist shows where it goes. It started with handing his phone to a woman at work while another brother stood a few feet away, no fear at all, and it spiralled into porn, the strip club and fornication. His heart was full of darkness: “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

That is why Peter says “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the fleshly lust comes from what you look at, “the lust of the eyes”. You are at war, brothers, and if you are not resisting you are losing, while Satan is in your head saying you got it under control. The one who resists the pleasure crowns his life.

“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

Sirach describes the man who grows: “If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.” If you die, you leave a greater name than a thousand men, and if you live, your name keeps growing. That is a man who is ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ. That measure is the goal the whole passage is climbing toward.

It comes in steps. First he serves “among great men” and appears “before princes”: studying four chapters a day, occupied in meditation and prophecies, keeping the sayings of the renowned men. Then he repents: he will “pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” Then, “When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding”: when the Lord has seen you making a conscious change, mortifying and disciplining yourself. Before that, the strong meat is not for you. You have to learn the simple things first: no whoremonger shall enter the kingdom of heaven, wear your fringes, remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy, know the twelve tribes.

“In his secrets shall he meditate.” That is the transition from milk to meat. “He shall shew forth that which he hath learned”: out of his mouth comes the wisdom gathered over years of studying, applying, and getting around renowned men. “His name shall live from generation to generation.” That is what you want in your name, still part of the conversation after you leave this earth, for the wisdom God moved in you.

So you have to level up. As a teacher you cannot keep regurgitating the same classes over and over; you have to grow in understanding and application to teach the people. Growing to the full stature of Christ is how a name increases while you live.

Solomon says “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just for us to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. That is Matthew 6:33: seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That’s what the Bible says.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” That does not mean you just pray, God, give me understanding so I can break down Revelation. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved and rightly divide the word. You have to choose this, and make him first.

“All gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” Why is wisdom better than gold and silver? Those things are corruptible: they can be stolen or destroyed, and when you sell them the money runs out quick. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more and to do this and that.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” I choose wisdom above all things; I prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it, but we have to make him first. Wisdom is “a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God”, and seeking that first is the beginning of the transition from milk to meat.

For the last sixty years a war has been waged on the black community, and Esau has been exploiting our weakness. What is the black man's weakness? The black woman. Peter calls her “the weaker vessel”: she is weaker than us. When Satan waged war against Adam, did he come and trick Adam? No. He went through Adam's weakness, the woman, to take Adam down. And the white man understands that too.

That is why God says of the 144 in Revelation 14, “These are they which were not defiled with women”. If our weakness is the woman, the 144's weakness will not be woman. They overcome the very place where Satan took Adam down.

And the woman's weakness is her emotions. She can be manipulated; the white man can trick her. Satan played with Eve's emotions, and she said the serpent beguiled me. Sisters, learn to control your emotions. In the house the sisters get in their feelings; that is their weakness, and our weakness is them.

We come down hard on the sisters because of the important role a woman plays in the nation. Y'all don't understand your importance, but our enemy does. He says, to destroy the black man I have to destroy the black woman first: make her a liberal, destroy the household, take the man out of it, make her think she doesn't need a man. The white man tricked you, sisters. So many problems in the black community come from no father in the house.

A strong woman and an independent woman are two different things. Our righteous foremothers were strong women: a strong woman builds her husband, keeps the family together, and uses her good job to help her family. An independent woman, the liberal woman, oppresses her husband, argues with him, won't listen to him, and ultimately leaves him seeking happiness. Your grandmother before the sixties was good, but the women from the 1960s until now, the majority of their minds are destroyed. The man who dwells with his wife according to knowledge must know where the weakness lies.

God commands the brothers: “set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them.” Sisters say, you're always getting on the sisters. We get on you because the white man has tricked you and you have been deceived, and because you play an important role in rebuilding the nation. For the last sixty years the white man has used you to destroy the black community. So God says, set your face against these liberal women, the free thinkers who want to do whatever they want.

They prophesy out of their own heart, their own emotions: I don't feel it's wrong to wear pants; I don't see anything wrong with a blonde wig; Jesus loves everybody. No. Do what God says: wear skirts, and don't wear what pertains to a man. We prophesy against you so that you will see your wrongs and change, and so that the damage the white man has done to our community through our sisters can be undone.

Look at the decayed state of the liberal woman. One says there's nothing wrong with being an angry black woman; if she is angry she will raise her voice, twist her face and snap her neck. No sister should come with that spirit. That is no way to speak to your husband, or to anyone. Another had a man paying all the bills and taking care of her and the children, and she left him because she needed clarity and to find herself. Another left her husband of more than ten years because they outgrew each other, because he wanted her home and she wanted her career. Some sisters did the same and have repented: they left their husband thinking there was something better out there, and the next man did the same thing the first one did.

Genesis 2:18 shows what God made the woman to be: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” When God created woman, he said she is a help meet unto Adam, a good help. That is scriptural. Brothers, you want a woman who will help you build the kingdom, who will help build your dreams and help establish the kingdom of heaven. The liberal woman wants the benefit of a king without the patience or the work of helping him build.

That is what the civil rights did to our people. When this happens across the whole community, sons grow up with no father in the house and baby mamas instead of wives, and these things help destroy a community. Many sisters don't want accountability or responsibility, and there is a lot of work to do.

“A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come”: giving birth you will be in sorrow and feel a lot of pain. “but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world”. For joy a man is born into the world.

Write down Luke 1:13-14: that is when Elisabeth bore John the Baptist, and there was much joy in the world at his birth. The birth of a child is meant to bring joy, not depression. God made the woman “to be a joyful mother of children.”

So sisters should not be having kids and talking about being depressed, or using the liberal word from social media, overstimulated. Overwhelmed can be understood, because when a baby comes you will sometimes be overwhelmed, and that is why it is good to be a family and around each other, so the kids can go by the grandparents. But naturally a woman is not supposed to be like that after she gives birth. Much of the depression during and after pregnancy comes from what Esau gives you: the pills and the prenatal vitamins with folic acid, and food without nutrients. The white man is the devil.

The sisters training as midwives, doulas, doctors and nurses need to bring that lost knowledge back and teach it: the right food after pregnancy, the vitamins from food, the herbs, the steam baths. Postpartum is Leviticus 12, the days of her purification, when a woman was put in a separate place and nursed back to health by her family and the midwives.

Leviticus 12:4 says “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.” Purification means being washed, cleansed, made holy; literally, removing what is foreign and contaminated to restore something to its natural clean state. So purification is not just staying away from the temple. The days of her separation are also her being nursed back to health, restored.

Esther shows purification too. Go there and read it for yourselves: Esther went through her days of purification with sweet odours and so forth, and everything else she needed, and she had maids to help her. It is a different purification, but it shows that purifying a woman is a lot of stuff: care, help, the right food, the things her body needs.

So it is with a woman after she gives birth. She was not just sent home and left alone. For those forty days, or eighty for a girl, she was kept in a special place, and midwives and family came, cooked the right food and nursed her back to health. That is postpartum in the Bible, and it is why a sister who has just given birth needs people around her and help with the baby, not the postpartum depression that Esau made up.

Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. There are no laws involved, no commandments involved.

The commentary on Peter says it: false teachers who sound impressive yet deliver nothing of substance. Homoousios, hypostatic, exegesis, ontological, hermeneutical, Christological: great swelling words. Their speech is grand, polished, well paced, even spiritual sounding, like Bible, but it is hollow, with no commandments, no responsibility, no accountability. Unlike Paul, who said “my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”. Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on style over truth, eloquence without gospel substance. In the Greek, great swelling words means great bulk: high sounding, but only words, vain and meaningless, with nothing but emptiness behind them.

Show me the scripture that says Christ is fully God and fully man. It isn't there. The word of God is plain and clear. Even their hermeneutics goes back to Schleiermacher, a German called the father of modern liberal theology, and Isaiah says “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”; the vile person will “utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry”. The word comes from Hermes, the Greek trickster god, so it is a trickster's interpretation, and the Jesuits carried it around the earth.

Peel back the swelling words and here is the premise: if Christ is fully God and fully man, only a two-essence being can keep God's laws, so we don't have to. But Christ said be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect, and Zacharias and Elisabeth walked “in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” It can be done. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments.

Isaiah said the people draw near with their mouth and honour God with their lips, “but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”. The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

Christ says the same thing and names who Isaiah was speaking of: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

The elders in Isaiah's day were teaching doctrines of men, and the Pharisees in Christ's time were doing the exact same thing. Those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time. The same spirit passed down.

So the doctrine of trinitarianism is exactly that: teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. It is not found plainly in the Bible; it comes from men. People draw near with their lips and argue about essence and substance while their heart is far from God and they forsake his laws, and in vain do they worship him.

The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. So are they all one entity? Do they form Voltron, do the fusion dance, become a Megazord? It's madness; it's ridiculous. One means one in spirit and speech, not one entity.

That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

Christ said to men, “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” The trinity doctrine says no: only God can keep the commandments, so Christ cannot be fully a man, because a full man can't keep those laws, but a full man and a full God can. The insidiousness behind it is to make it impossible for man to keep God's commandments.

Luke answers that with John the Baptist's parents, Zacharias and Elisabeth: “And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” Both righteous. Walking in all the commandments. Blameless: that's perfect. So human beings can keep God's commandments, perfect as the Father in heaven. It can be done.

The scripture also says we are gods but shall die like men, so we are the two anyway; for not keeping the commandments we die like men.

Peel back the layers of confusion and the doctrine is all about removing the humanity of Christ, or keeping some of it and making him a god too, so that man can't keep the commandments: Christ kept the laws so we don't have to do anything. That's the whole premise behind the great swelling words. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments. Where is Christmas, New Year, Halloween, carnival, Labor Day, the Fourth of July or birthdays in the Bible? Your three-in-one God has nothing to say about them.

“Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.” Don't waste your time talking to dumbass people; they'll turn against you and fight you. There is no magic scripture. You cannot save everyone. Some people are meant, predestined, to be stupid.

Luke gives the instruction Christ gave: “And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” Shake off the very dust. Wash your hands of them and leave them alone.

If you explain that the heavenly Father is the Most High God, that he has a son, and that his son has sons, the children of Israel, and they can't understand it and say no, they're all one, leave that negro alone. You're wasting your time; he is on medications or should be.

The proverbs read with it say the same: “If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.” There is no conclusion; it is a circular argument that goes nowhere. “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” Three is one, one is three, round and round. These are unreasonable people, so you shake off the dust and move on.

“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.
blog/2026/2026-09-27-2026-09-27-the-imag:
Ezra saw the city of the kingdom with its narrow entrance, “like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. That fire and deep water is the nations afflicting us. Judges makes the point about the nations: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”.

He didn't get rid of all the nations. He said, no, I'm going to leave something there, because I don't want you to just skate through. You have to learn some things. If we did not have to be buffeted by our enemies, our journey would be quite smooth; but God put it that way because we messed up, and now we have to serve them, and they are going to make it hell for us to get the kingdom.

“Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”. We didn't know about war before; now we know about war. We are getting the training now. When we get into the kingdom we are going to be experts in everything, bad upon bad, because we will have done it all and endured it all. That is what is going to make us perfect.

Captivity and persecution are hard and rough; nobody wants to go through these things. They can kill the body, but they cannot kill the spirit. They can do all kind of evil to my body physically, but when I come back, I'm going to hang your ass. That is the mindset you have to have: going for the kingdom regardless of what is thrown at you, to persevere between the fire on one side and the deep water on the other. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

Daniel 7:27 says “the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom”. That is why Daniel 2:44 says the same: “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed”.

The days of these kings are the same kings of Daniel 7, the thrones cast down in Armageddon when Christ comes back to smash and destroy and set his people up in rulership. The kingdom the God of heaven sets up is you, sisters and brothers, the nation of Israel, and it is starting now. A lot of people don't like that, but the Most High is building this kingdom right now, in the age of their decadence.

“and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”. The Most High's kingdom, the nation of Israel with Christ and the Most High and the angels leading us, shall break the nations and make them bend to the will of God, or death. Everybody is going to be made to follow the words of this Bible, its laws and commandments. Full stop.

“and it shall stand for ever.” That is the everlasting kingdom of Daniel 7:27. Remember these words: the kingdom the Lord is setting up shall stand for ever, and we are supposed to be in the image of understanding that, not the image of dysfunction. All the wealth of the nations under the whole heaven, the whole planet, has to be given back to Israel, including the nations themselves.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

The place where it was said, ye are not my people, is the place where we were made to be dysfunctional, where we were made a mess, where they called us coon and spear-chucker. They called us everything except the Israelites. In that very place the Most High is going to beautify the meek with salvation, and there it shall be said, ye are the sons of the living God. That is Daniel 7:27: the kingdom under the whole heaven given “to the people of the saints of the most High”.

The Lord is going to punish the nations for what they called us and did to us, because we are God's heritage. Those who put their nasty, mangy hands on us touched the apple of his eye, and they are going to pay for it. Our brothers and sisters were hung and suffered all kinds of evil, and the Most High has the chart on everything. The Lord allowed it to happen, and he is still going to make them pay for doing it.

The Lord allows the nations to afflict us and still makes them pay, and who can resist his will? That is the argument of Romans 9. “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.” The same purpose for which God raised up Pharaoh is the purpose for which he is raising up Esau: to show his power by channeling his destructive anger through him, and to get his glory by destroying the man everybody is worshipping, so they will all know the Most High is the real power.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.” He raised up Pharaoh to resist God, and he makes Esau do the same. He is fattening Esau up with weapons, technology, power and pride, the way you fatten a turkey before one of their wicked holidays, and then he will cut him down.

“Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?” How can he find fault with the man when he gave him all the weapons and made him resist? Esau cannot resist the will of God, and neither could Pharaoh. Pharaoh wanted to let the Israelites go, and the Lord hardened his heart.

“Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” Esau was formed as the fitting vessel for God's destruction; one vessel is for wine and one is for the bowels.

So you had better be glad you are the Israelites. After slavery, Jim Crow and the lynchings, to die with the same man who did it to you would be crazy. The kingdom goes to the saints of the Most High, and the vessel of dishonour is broken.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. The book of the Lord is no other book on this planet except the Bible. Solomon warns: “And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.”

Anything outside of the Bible that you try to live your life by is a weariness of the flesh. All you will profit from it is getting tired. You might get a good night's sleep, unless a demon flies out of the bag reading some book with some kind of skin on it. There is no end to these books: they are always writing some book about what God is going to do on this earth, about his plans and who his people are. No other book can answer that except the Bible. The much study of the rest of these books is a waste of time.

When books are brought in class, they are filtered through the Bible. If they contradict the Bible, if they go against the laws, the commandments and the prophecies, they are garbage. They are brought only to illuminate the reading, as in Nehemiah 8:8.

“Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter”: the conclusion of the whole matter is in the Bible. Daniel says the same: “Hitherto is the end of the matter”, the kingdom given to the people of the saints of the Most High. “Fear God, and keep his commandments”: his commandments are found in the book of the Lord, not in the Quran, not in the Egyptian book of the dead. That is how you know which is the book of the Lord.

“for this is the whole duty of man.” The image of God is doing what God said. The man spoken of is the Israelite man, because we are the ones who will make everybody else dance to the tune of this Bible, but it has to be done by us first. We are in training. That is why we are on this slave ship called America: because we broke God's laws and his commandments, and we must endure all of it to get back home.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. The Bible alone is the book of the Lord, so why are other books ever brought into the class? Because of Nehemiah: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.”

Whatever is brought before the brothers and sisters is brought by the commandments of God, to illuminate the reading and make sense of it: to give the sense and cause them to understand. Sometimes tangible things, relative to your understanding today, are grabbed to help you see what is written in the Bible better. That is the only reason books are referenced here and there.

But everything is filtered through the Bible. If a book contradicts the Bible, if it goes against the laws, the commandments and the prophecies, it is garbage and is not dealt with at all. None of these books can be mated to the Bible. The Bible stands alone, and the other books only serve to give the sense of it.

The Lord has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. Watchmen pay attention to the condition of the people and to the enemy coming to destroy the people. “ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Nehemiah shows how the enemy takes it when Israel speaks up: “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” They do not like it when we speak up for our people.

That is why our enemies want us silent, locked away with the key thrown away and our mouths zipped. They call us troublemakers. Yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. They want a quiet slave.

The squeaky wheel gets the oil. Quiet people are ignored, and noisy people force others to take action. So we will complain, judge, bring out the records and tell it like it is, and we will beg the Lord and give him no rest, like the widow before the unjust judge, until he kills our enemies and sets Jerusalem up on high.

“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.

“Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.” It is the same secret counsel of Psalms 83, taken against the people who, as Achior told Holofernes, can only be overcome when they sin against their God.

“Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.” Their bitter words: calling us anti-Semitic, when we are the Semites, from Shem, and their fathers came from Esau.

“That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not. They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them? They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search: both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.” They think deep on how to trap us into perpetuating our own destruction: making us image ourselves as nothing, so they no longer have to enforce it. Parading a simple brother in a dress, stripping our women, keeping us clowns on the court and on the stage who know nothing of their ancestors.

That is the image of dysfunction they laid as a snare, so that there would be error in this people and it would be their ruin. The answer is to get back into the commandments so there is no iniquity in the nation, and the Lord defends us. If we as men do not do this work, no other species will.

Achior runs Israel's whole history down to Holofernes, and in it is part of the key to getting out of this mess: “whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them.” So the objective of our enemies is to keep us from obeying God, to keep us in dysfunction so they can dominate us. They love that we're brilliant; they want the body and the mind, but they don't want us using that mind for ourselves. And the counsel he gives: “if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.” That is exactly what is happening to us now. “But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them.” That's where our power is: checking each other so there is no sin in the nation.

Add this to your prayers: “Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God. For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.” They are God's enemies, lifting up their heads against everything that is about the Most High.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” AIPAC counsel, The Israel Project counsel, ADL counsel, Canary Mission counsel: consultation, secret meetings against us. The nations are terrified that we are learning and teaching this Bible. An Israeli official came down to Atlanta, and in a meeting with AIPAC and the ADL they said the black man leading was the number one threat. Not Hamas, not Hezbollah: the blacks in this country, because they read the prophecy.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” In their meetings, the discussion is to cut us off from the Most High, from who we truly are, from the image of God, and morph us into the image of dysfunction. They did it through a slave system designed to destroy the manhood of the black male, and they do it in the schools, killing the confidence of our sons by the fourth grade. They didn't bring dummies here: we were warriors and family heads, kings, princes, judges, architects, engineers, doctors, mathematicians, an industrious and skillful people. So no, we're not niggas; that lie garbage was given to us to make us think we are a different image than what God made us. They are not doing it to those over there. They do it to us because we are the Israelites.
captains/2026/2026-08-25-2026-08-25-chri:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zebulun and Naphtali are tribes of Israel, part of the northern kingdom, and yet their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles. So the southern kingdom was calling the northern kingdom Gentiles and uncircumcised. Very simple.

How did Israelites come to be called Gentiles? In the days of the Maccabees, “according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”. They were enforcing it: you could not be circumcised; you had to be like the Gentiles. They were hanging babies. So what is the next generation going to be? Uncircumcised. And the next one, uncircumcised, not keeping the laws, profaning the Sabbath, calling themselves and being called Gentiles.

Zondervan's compact Bible dictionary says Gentiles usually means a non-Israelite people. Usually: meaning there are certain contexts, like this one, where it is not talking about the other nations at all, but about Israelites who were made to live like the heathen. That is how Ephesians 2 has to be understood.

“And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.” Who? The children of Israel. “And he said, The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints”. Of who? Of saints. When we were liberated out of Egypt, he called them the saints.

“from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” That is how you know it is not talking about the mixed multitude among them: the fiery law went to the children of Israel only. “Yea, he loved the people; all his saints are in thy hand”: all these saints, the children of Israel, are in his hand. “and they sat down at thy feet; every one shall receive of thy words.”

So the saints are the children of Israel, the ones who received the law from his right hand. When Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, he means the same people Moses blessed: Israel.

“Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus”. To the who? To the saints. So we must go into the Bible and figure out who the saints are.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people”: his people, the Israelites. “the praise of all his saints”: his saints. “even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” If you did not know, even means indeed. Indeed, of the children of Israel.

So the saints of God are the children of Israel, the people near unto him. When Paul writes to the saints which are at Ephesus, he is writing to Israelites living in Ephesus, not to everybody in the city. That is where the understanding of Ephesians has to start.

Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, so who are the saints? The Lord says: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”

So the only saints in the Bible are the ones that made a covenant with God by sacrifice. That is Israel, the people who made the covenant with him. It did not change. It did not go away. That is who the saints are.

So when Paul opens his letter to the saints, he is speaking to the covenant people, the ones God gathers unto himself. The letter to the Ephesians is written to Israel, and it has to be read that way.

Paul says “at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise”. Who were the strangers? Chronicles shows it: Asa “gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.”

The strangers out of Ephraim and Manasseh. That is the northern kingdom, and they were called strangers. Israelites, called strangers.

The literal definition of Gentiles is nation. How can you in time past be another nation? How can you in time past be another race? Go to sleep Japanese, wake up Arab? That does not make any sense. It only makes sense in Christianity. But when you read that Israelites of the northern kingdom were called strangers, Ephesians 2:12 makes sense: the strangers were Israel.

Paul says they were “having no hope, and without God in the world.” Who was without hope? Ezekiel shows it: “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.”

They said it themselves: no hope. So Israel was the one without hope. “we are cut off for our parts”: we were alienated from the commonwealth. The dry bones are the whole house of Israel, not another nation.

So every part of Ephesians 2:12 lines up with Israel. The ones cut off, the ones with their hope lost, the aliens from the commonwealth, were the house of Israel itself, and that is who the letter is speaking to.

Why were Ephraim and the northern kingdom called strangers? Hosea says it: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”

So at one point the northern kingdom was not a part of the commonwealth of Israel. Why? Ephraim joined himself to idols and was let alone. They became strangers; they became alienated from the commonwealth of Israel. That is what Paul means by “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”: not another race of people, but Israelites who were cut off for their idolatry.

It is very basic and simple. All you have to do is read. Blessed is he that readeth.

Paul says the same people were “strangers from the covenants of promise”. But to whom do the covenants belong? Romans says it: they “are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

“to whom pertaineth the adoption”: that means the coming back; they were brought back. “and the covenants”: the covenants, the old and the new, only belong to the Israelites. The promises belong to them too.

So you can only be a stranger from a covenant that was yours to begin with. You were strangers from the covenants of promise for a time, but it was always for you. Ephesians 2:12 is Israel cut off and then brought back through Christ, not the nations being added in.

Ephesians 2:13 says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was far off? Who was once close, and then got distant, pushed away, cut off? Daniel answers it in his prayer.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” That are where? That are far off. The far off are Israel, driven into all the countries because of their trespass against the Lord.

So the far off of Ephesians are not other nations. They are Israel, both near and far off. Israel said, we are cut off for our parts, we have no hope. But now they do have hope, through Christ: the ones who were far off are made nigh by his blood.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” He is the peace of the saints Paul writes to in Ephesians 1:1. You have to know history to understand this verse, because why does it say both? Is it only talking about Jews and Gentiles? What happened in the history?

Ezekiel shows it: “And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” One king: Christ. No more two nations.

That is the both that he made one: the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. Jew and Gentile, circumcision and uncircumcision, are those same two kingdoms. When those two kingdoms were against each other they were at odds, and that hatred was the middle wall of partition. But the Lord said there is going to be peace, and Christ is that peace, making the two into one again.

“Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.”

This is the same chapter where the Lord promises to make the two kingdoms one nation with one king. With that promise comes a covenant of peace. And Ephesians 2:14 says, “For he is our peace, who hath made both one.” The covenant of peace Ezekiel spoke of is Christ.

So in one chapter of Ezekiel we get all of the information and all of the understanding of Ephesians 2: the two kingdoms made one, one king over them all, and an everlasting covenant of peace. Paul is not speaking about the other nations joining Israel; he is speaking about the fulfilling of this prophecy for the house of Israel.

Ephesians says he made “of twain one new man, so making peace,” the same twain made one in Ezekiel 37, and the peace is the covenant of peace of Ezekiel 37:26. Then: “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross.” Words are important, Christians; the Bible is full of them. Reconcile is a verb that means to restore friendly relations. So when was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?

Ezra answers: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen. All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes.” He made the world for the Israelites’ sake.

“As for the other people, which also come of Adam, thou hast said that they are nothing, but be like unto spittle: and hast likened the abundance of them unto a drop that falleth from a vessel.” They are nothing. Does that sound like friendly relations? No, they never were. Isaiah 40:17 says the same thing, for anyone who does not think the Apocrypha is canon. So the reconciling of Ephesians 2 cannot be about the other nations.

“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Thy people are the Israelites, and thy holy city is Jerusalem. Within those seventy weeks the Lord would make an end of sins and “make reconciliation for iniquity.” That reconciliation was determined upon Daniel’s people, not upon the other nations.

So when Ephesians says Christ came to “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby,” it is the fulfilling of Daniel. Christ dying brought reconciliation to God’s people, Israel. It is very easy, very simple, very plain.

“Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting.” The Lord is Israel’s father and Israel’s redeemer, from everlasting.

Reconciled: reconciled who, to what? Married people get reconciled. They were together under a covenant, something happened and they broke apart, and in order to bring the marriage back together they must reconcile. That is what the word means.

The nation of Israel was once together under God, as the children of their father. Something happened: sin and the split of the kingdoms. Then Christ brought them back together. That is why Ephesians says he might “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”: both kingdoms brought back to the Father who was always theirs.

“We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name.” Israel says to the Lord, we are yours. And of the other nations: the Lord never bore rule over them, and they were not called by His name.

So how can anyone be reconciled to a God that never owned them, never knew them, and never had them? To reconcile is to restore friendly relations that were there before. Israel was the Lord’s, called by His name, and fell away; the other nations never were His.

That is why the reconciling of Ephesians 2:16, “that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross,” belongs to Israel. The both are the two houses of Israel, the ones called by His name, brought back to the God who bore rule over them.

Ephesians 2:14 speaks of “the middle wall of partition between us.” What is that wall? The next verse explains it: “Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances.” A Christian’s head just blew off. They do not know what that is talking about. What are those commandments contained in ordinances?

Hebrews tells us. The tabernacle service “was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

Carnal ordinances. These are the commandments contained in ordinances: the law of sacrifice. That was the enmity, and that was the wall of partition between the two kingdoms. It was imposed only until the time of reformation, and Christ abolished it in his flesh, so that there is no more fighting over where and how to sacrifice.
captains/2026/2026-08-31-2026-08-31-igni:
Baruch says the law “endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Since the beginning of time this law has been in place. Break it and judgments come upon you; keep it and blessings come upon you. Solomon shows what happens to those who leave it: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

Look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world. You look dead, spiritually dead. Run down and tired, twenty-one years old looking forty, when that was supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. We wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. That is why the law is called a spirit: the commandments are spirit, and without them there is no life in us.

They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday, what the Lord said would come on us for breaking his commandments: walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something, all confused in the spirit. Even with the sun at its apex we could not see. We were blinded. We were distracted.

So the law is the difference between the living and the dead. Those who keep it come to life, the way we did when we came into this truth; those who wander from it remain in the congregation of the dead.
captains/2026/2026-09-02-2026-09-02-sove:
Why is it that the Lord established David over his people, to establish the sovereign kingdom of Israel? If you want to be sovereign, there is one way to it: a one-way road with one victory at the end of it, the kingdom of heaven.

“And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis.” Even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish him. “And when he had removed him”: the Lord removed Saul from being king over Israel. So where does this power and authority come from? Only from God. Only God can make you sovereign and remove your sovereignty; not you, and not your piece of paper with weird words on it. “he raised up unto them David to be their king”: as righteous and powerful and mighty as David was, it was still the Lord that established him as king over Israel, a sovereign government.

“I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.” That is the caveat to being sovereign, to ruling over God's heritage: a man after God's own heart, exactly how the Lord wanted his servant and king to be. And he fulfils all the Lord's will, not his own personal will or desire.

What is the will of God? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. What pleased God in David, to the point that he established him as ruler over his people as a sovereign government? He kept God's commandments; he kept the testimonies. The Lord establishes his rulers by who is faithful to him, faithful to the commandments.
captains/2026/2026-09-04-2026-09-04-hono:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Oh, my dad, yeah man, he is broke, he is a bum now, my mom left him behind. That is no glory to you. You came from him. “For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father.” Solomon says the same: “Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.”

Children's children, the grandchildren, and the great-grandkids are the crown of old men. They want to see you have children and keep procreating. They see it and say, dang, you came from me, and now you are creating life again. Man, I would love to see that. Parents love seeing that.

And the glory of children are their fathers. So if your father is in dishonour, you are in dishonour too. There is no glory in that, and “a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.” The honour of the parents and the honour of the children are tied together, one generation to the next.

That is why we have got to let our light shine: so our fathers are honoured in us, and we become a crown to them.

Sirach warns that “he that angereth his mother is cursed: of God.” Does that mean you are in sin because your mom is mad you are not coming to the Christmas party, or because you did not come over for Mother’s Day with a bouquet of flowers? Jeremiah answers it.
