“Why trimmest thou thy way to seek love?” We cannot trim our ways in keeping the commandments to seek love, affection and acceptance from our family members.

“Therefore hast thou also taught the wicked ones thy ways.” When we do that, we teach our family members to be wicked. We say we are not going to do this or that, then they say, come do this with us, and we cave in. That shows them we are not really about the word of God.

So honouring your parents is helping your father in his age, having patience with him when his understanding fails, not despising him when you are in your full strength. It is not trimming the commandments to keep the peace at their holidays.

Sirach says “he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.” We are not talking about gold or diamonds or crypto or NFTs. Christ shows what kind of treasure it is.

“Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. The treasures on earth, crypto coins and Bitcoin, can go when the computers blow up; money is going to burn; gold can melt; somebody can steal it.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal”. The treasure in heaven is the eternal life we are all striving for. Nothing can take that away from us once we attain it, and no thief can break through and get what the Lord has prepared for us in paradise.

So honouring and respecting your mother is laying up that treasure in heaven. But we have got to get there.

Honouring your father and mother does not depend on whether they are a repentant Israelite or still in the world. You still have to respect and honour them either way.

We have to let our light shine and be the light to the Gentiles, the unrepentant of our people, because at one point you were unrepentant too. Paul says, “As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.” As much as the opportunity arises, we do good to all men, those in the truth and those out of the truth, and that includes the parents who raised us.

That goes back to Romans, where it says live peaceably with all men. So when Sirach says “Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, it is not only the father who is in the faith; doing good to your parents wherever they stand is the honour that brings that atonement.

“Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins”, and that goes for your mother too. When you honour your father, that wipes away your sins. Hebrews shows why.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence”. Another word for reverence is respect, honour. The fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them that honour.

“Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” So even more so we have to respect the Lord that created us. But that does not cancel the first part: we still have to have respect, honour and reverence for our earthly fathers. Thus saith the Lord. Honouring the father of your flesh is part of being in subjection to the Father of spirits, and that is why it makes an atonement.

“Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard.” Why does it say that? It means that when you are not honouring your father or your mother, your prayers are not going to be heard, which shows that honouring your parents is a commandment.

John makes it clear and plain: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners”. Everybody knows it. Dishonouring your parents is breaking a commandment, and a sinner is not heard.

So when we are in habitual, presumptuous sin, the Lord is not going to hear our prayers. The one who honours his father is keeping the commandment, and that is why, when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.

“He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.” The same respect you have for your boss, your employer, whoever gainfully employs you, the elders and the men over you, you should have for your parents and more, because they brought you into this world.

Hebrews says it plain and simple: “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls”. These people watch for our souls.

Your parents did that too. Even in the past, before they or you knew the truth, they watched out for your life, your safety and your well-being. They cared for you all the way up to the time you were able to repent and become a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them, and do service unto them as to your masters.

“Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them.” Both in word and deed means whatever you say, do it. The blessing comes from them, and “the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children.” How can the blessing of a father establish children? Solomon shows it: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.”

Children's children are grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family, with your mother and your parents, you never know: they could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect.

But you only get that blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do. If you are acting up and being disrespectful to them, and not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you, and you will never even see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things if you are not honouring and reverencing them.

That is how the father's blessing establishes the houses of children: honour him in word and deed, and his inheritance reaches down to your own children.
docs/study/1-chronicles/10.md|1 Chronicl:
The woman brought up Samuel. “And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice”, and she knew then who had come to her: “Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.” She said, “I saw gods ascending out of the earth”, and “An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle.” Saul “perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.”

Through Samuel the Most High told Saul he would join him the next day. Both men died, but the difference is that Samuel died righteously. Saul died for his transgression, for not keeping the word of the Lord, and for seeking that familiar spirit.

This is what drove Saul to the witch. “And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He enquired of the Most High, “the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.”

So Saul turned to the witch instead. Rather than inquiring of the Most High, he went to the left hand, and that is why Chronicles records that he “enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him”.

Here is the very thing Chronicles speaks of. Saul told his servants, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” They found one at Endor, and “Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment,” and came to her by night with two men.

He asked her, “divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.” The one he wanted brought up was Samuel. This is Saul “asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”, the last straw that cost him his life and his kingdom.

This is how Saul came to reign at all. Israel came to Samuel and said, “make us a king to judge us like all the nations.” “But the thing displeased Samuel”, and he prayed. The Most High answered, “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

Israel rejected the Most High as their king and demanded a king like the other nations, and Saul was that king. He ended by keeping not the word of the Lord and asking counsel of a familiar spirit, so the Most High slew him and “turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.”

The law is plain: “There shall not be found among you any one” that “useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch”, nor “a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.” Israel is forbidden to use divination, enchantment, or to consult with familiar spirits.

Saul died “for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”. That was the last straw for him. The left hand of the Most High is real, and people who meddle with it get entangled and get spirits put on them. It is not our custom.

“Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.” Witchcraft and consulting familiar spirits are not Israel's custom. The law does not even suffer the witch to live among the people.

That is what Saul turned to. The king who should have kept the word of the Lord went seeking counsel from a woman that the law says not to suffer to live, and he “enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.”
docs/study/1-chronicles/11.md|1 Chronicl:
“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”. The word must be gone over constantly.

Eleazar the son of Dodo, “one of the three mighties”, stood with David where the Philistines gathered in a parcel of ground full of barley, and “the people fled from before the Philistines.” But “they set themselves in the midst of that parcel, and delivered it, and slew the Philistines; and the Lord saved them by a great deliverance.” The Most High was working with these brothers to make them mighty.

When we go into the street it is not a physical war, but we are to stand against three hundred with the word. This is why we must study, and make our calling and election sure.
docs/study/1-chronicles/12.md|1 Chronicl:
The tribes of Israel sent through all Benjamin asking, “What wickedness is this that is done among you?” and told them to deliver up “the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel.” “But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel”. Instead they “gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children of Israel.”

Benjamin stood with its own against all Israel. Benjamin tended to stick with Benjamin, and that is the tribal loyalty David feared. So when “there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David”, he was leery because of the beef between him and Saul. He went out to meet them and said, “If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, mine heart shall be knit unto you: but if ye be come to betray me to mine enemies, seeing there is no wrong in mine hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it.”

Then the spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains: “Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse”. So “David received them, and made them captains of the band.”

Christ said, “The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.” Pray for more labourers, and keep working while He adds to you.

That is what happened to David. Captains of the thousands of Manasseh fell to him at Ziklag and helped him “against the band of the rovers: for they were all mighty men of valour”. “For at that time day by day there came to David to help him, until it was a great host, like the host of God.” When the Most High works with you, He sends help.

“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” The Most High breathed on the slain and they lived, and that is what He has made of Israel: an exceeding great army.

An army has to keep rank. Of Zebulun there were fifty thousand, “expert in war, with all instruments of war”, “which could keep rank: they were not of double heart.” To keep rank is to stay in proper order and play your role without jockeying for position. They were not double minded; they listened to orders and structure.

When we battle the wickedness of this world, we must keep our rank. It is imperative.

“Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.” Israel is to be of one accord.

That is what the tribes were at Hebron. The men of war “came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.” Even the tribes beyond Jordan were of one accord with the rest. That is why we must be of one accord, for Christ is going to sit on the throne of David his father.

They were with David three days, eating and drinking, and their brethren brought bread, figs, raisins, wine, oil and cattle abundantly, “for there was joy in Israel.” The joy came from being of one mind, which is why the feast days are to be kept with gladness.
docs/study/1-chronicles/13.md|1 Chronicl:
When the Philistines held the ark, “the hand of the Lord was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with emerods”. The men of Ashdod said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us: for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god.” They carried it about unto Gath, and there too “the hand of the Lord was against the city with a very great destruction”, and the men “had emerods in their secret parts.” The Philistines begged Israel to take it away.

The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it. After the breach upon Uzza, David was afraid and asked, “How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?” So he carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, “And the Lord blessed the house of Obed–edom, and all that he had.”

The lesson of Uzza stands: if the ark falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it.

“And when Jeremy came thither, he found an hollow cave, wherein he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.” Some that followed him “came to mark the way, but they could not find it.” Jeremiah blamed them, saying, “As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that God gather his people again together, and receive them unto mercy.”

In David's day the ark was with Israel, and David gathered all Israel to bring it up “from Kirjath–jearim”, the ark “of God the Lord, that dwelleth between the cherubims”. They carried it in a new cart and played before God with all their might, moving it to where David was so the priests could inquire.

But do not let anyone claim the ark is in Ethiopia. The prophet Jeremiah hid it in a cave with the tabernacle and the altar of incense, and it will not be found until the Most High gathers His people again. The ark is hidden until Christ returns.

When Aaron and his sons had covered the sanctuary and its vessels, “the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die.” The holy things were not to be handled; only the Levites bore the ark.

So when “the oxen stumbled”, and “Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark”, “the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” The ark was only to be touched by the Levites. The Most High does not play.
docs/study/1-chronicles/14.md|1 Chronicl:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” Their images are to be burned so they do not become a snare unto us.

David kept this. He smote the Philistines at Baal-perazim and said, “God hath broken in upon mine enemies by mine hand like the breaking forth of waters”, naming the place for it. “And when they had left their gods there, David gave a commandment, and they were burned with fire.”

“Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.”

Saul was told to overcome nations and did not. He was told not to go to his last battle, yet he went and died there. “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”

David is the other side of it: “David therefore did as God commanded him: and they smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gazer.” The lesson is precise obedience. If he says do not go up, do not go up; if he says go this way, do not go that way.

“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The Most High is a man of war, and He knows exactly how to handle the battle.

When the Philistines came up a second time, David did not presume on the first victory; he “enquired again of God”. This time the Most High told him, “Go not up after them; turn away from them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” He was to move only “when thou shalt hear a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees”, “for God is gone forth before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.” The man of war laid out the battle Himself and went before David.
docs/study/1-chronicles/15.md|1 Chronicl:
“Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.” Uzza handled the ark when he was not to, and he died for it.

That shows why this order matters. David had seen what happens when the ark is not carried the way the Most High commanded, so now he says, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites”.

“And I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel: that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary.” The Levites were given to Aaron to do the service of the tabernacle, set apart to this office.

That is why David declared, “None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath the Lord chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.” He prepared a place for the ark in the city of David and pitched a tent for it, and this time he set it in the hands of those the Most High had chosen.

“And thou shalt put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, that the ark may be borne with them. The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.” The staves are set in the rings so the ark is borne, and they are not to be taken out.

The first attempt failed, “for that we sought him not after the due order.” This time “the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord.” The due order is the order Moses was given.

“Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.” The priests could not deal with holy things while unclean, so they had to be clean before serving.

That is why David charged the chief of the fathers of the Levites, “sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel unto the place that I have prepared for it.” “So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord God of Israel.”
docs/study/1-chronicles/16.md|1 Chronicl:
The shorter account in Samuel records the same gifts: “he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.”

Chronicles says it the same way: when the ark was set in the midst of the tent and the burnt offerings and peace offerings were made, David “blessed the people in the name of the Lord. And he dealt to every one of Israel, both man and woman, to every one a loaf of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine.”

This is the covenant “which he made with Abraham”: “I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.”

The Most High makes of Abraham a great nation, and in him all families of the earth are blessed. That covenant was sworn to Isaac and confirmed to Jacob “for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant”, with the land of Canaan as Israel's inheritance.

“He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac; And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant”. It is the same song and the same everlasting covenant.

The Most High is mindful always of his covenant, and a thousand generations is to say forever. It was made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant, “Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance”.

Chronicles ends with “David returned to bless his house.” Samuel shows what met him there: “Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David”. She met him scornfully: “How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!”

David answered her, “It was before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord. And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight”. He played before the Most High who chose him over Saul.

“Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.”

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.”

That is the bitter woman whose heart is snares and nets. When David returned to bless his house, Michal met him with scorn for playing before the Most High. But David had pleased the Most High, and the man who pleases the Most High escapes her.
docs/study/1-chronicles/19.md|1 Chronicl:
“Ye shall not round the corners of your heads, neither shalt thou mar the corners of thy beard.” It was not the custom of Israel to cut the beard, and that is why the shaving was so shameful.

David meant to show kindness to Hanun, because Nahash his father had shown kindness to David. But the princes of Ammon poisoned Hanun's mind, telling him David's comforters were come “to search, and to overthrow, and to spy out the land”, though that was not the case. So Hanun took David's servants “and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the midst hard by their buttocks, and sent them away.”

The men “were greatly ashamed” because they knew how to carry themselves as men of the Most High. Our ancestors had far more respect for themselves than to be exposed this way. So the king said, “Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and then return.”

“Be of good courage, and let us behave ourselves valiantly for our people, and for the cities of our God: and let the Lord do that which is good in his sight.”

Joab spoke this with the battle set against him before and behind. The Ammonites had made themselves odious to David and hired thirty and two thousand chariots, with the king of Maachah and his people. So Joab divided the army: he took the choice of Israel against the Syrians and gave the rest to Abishai his brother against Ammon, saying, “If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will help thee.”

Be of good courage, behave valiantly for the people and the cities of our God, and let the Most High do what is good in His sight. And He did: the Syrians fled before Joab, and when Ammon saw the Syrians flee, “they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city.”
docs/study/1-chronicles/2.md|1 Chronicle:
“Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” It is a great love and an honor that we should be called the sons of God.

The world knows us not. The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us. But we are not a minority. We are “the sons of Israel”, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

“Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.” These are the same sons listed in Chronicles: “Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.”

These are the sons of Jacob that came into Egypt, and we carry their name, their lineage, and their descent from the twelve tribes of Israel.

“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. It matters whose son you are.

That is why the record sets down “the sons of Israel” by name. When we search out our fathers, we find these twelve, and we carry their name, their lineage and their descent.

“And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.” The Most High named the child Jezreel to declare His judgment.

Names in the line of Jerahmeel carry meaning the same way. The record names his sons through his wives, Ram, Onam, Shammai, Jada and the rest, and keeps account even of the branches that did not continue: “Seled died without children”, and “Jether died without children.”

“And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” The Most High named her Lo-ruhamah, for He would no more have mercy upon the house of Israel.

The name itself declares the judgment. That is how names carry meaning in scripture, and why the names in this line of Judah are set down one by one.

“And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name was Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her.” She bare him Er, Onan and Shelah, the three “born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess.” Pharez and Zerah he had of Tamar his daughter in law.

“Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the Lord; and he slew him.” Just as Cain was evil and is passed over in the genealogy of the sons of God, an evil son is not counted in the record. This is why the counsel is to desire not a multitude of unprofitable children.

“And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers”. Pedigrees are declared by the house of the fathers.

“Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters.” He gave his daughter “to Jarha his servant to wife”, an Egyptian, “and she bare him Attai.” The line is carried down from their child, and even here it is reckoned through the father: Attai begat Nathan, Nathan begat Zabad, and on down to Elishama.
docs/study/1-chronicles/21.md|1 Chronicl:
“Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the Lord my God of that which doth cost me nothing.” David would not offer to the Most High that which cost him nothing.

It is the same conviction in Chronicles. Ornan offered it all, the place, “the oxen also for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meat offering; I give it all.” But David said, “Nay; but I will verily buy it for the full price: for I will not take that which is thine for the Lord, nor offer burnt offerings without cost.” He paid six hundred shekels of gold, built the altar, and the Most High “answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering”, and the angel “put up his sword again into the sheath thereof.”

This is a pattern for Israel today: what is given to the Most High should cost the giver something.
docs/study/1-chronicles/22.md|1 Chronicl:
“And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.” Hiram helped supply the timber for the building of the temple.

That help was already coming in David's day. David gathered the strangers in the land of Israel and set masons to hew stones for the house of God, and prepared iron, brass and “cedar trees in abundance: for the Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.” The strangers were brought in to help build the temple, and Tyre, whose king loved David, kept on helping his son.
docs/study/1-chronicles/25.md|1 Chronicl:
“And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.” When Miriam came out, she led the women in prophecy, and it was with music. Music is a form of prophecy.

That is why David and the captains separated the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, “who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals”. The sons of Asaph “prophesied according to the order of the king”, and Jeduthun “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the Lord.” The sons of Heman were given by God to lift up the horn, for God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
docs/study/1-chronicles/4.md|1 Chronicle:
“And they had in their inheritance Beer–sheba, Sheba, and Moladah,” and the cities round about. These are Simeon's inheritance in Joshua, the same dwellings Chronicles names: “they dwelt at Beer–sheba, and Moladah”, and the rest. “These were their cities unto the reign of David.”

Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, “but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah.” Simeon kept its inheritance, but the blessing of increase rested on Judah.
docs/study/1-chronicles/5.md|1 Chronicle:
“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.” When the Most High is against a people, this is what happens to them.

Here the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falls on the enemy instead of on us. Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh made war with the Hagarites, “And they were helped against them”, “for they cried to God in the battle, and he was intreated of them; because they put their trust in him.” “And they took away their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses two thousand, and of men an hundred thousand.” “For there fell down many slain, because the war was of God.”

“Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue”. The fringes were given so that we would look upon them and remember the commandments, and do them, and not go a-whoring after our own eyes.

These tribes failed to do that. “And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.” Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity “unto this day.”
docs/study/1-chronicles/6.md|1 Chronicle:
“Fear the Lord with all thy soul, and reverence his priests.”

The men David set over the service of song were not regular men. They were set apart to minister before the house of the Most High, and they waited on their office according to their order, so they are to be held in reverence.

“And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”, and “to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” It is the prince's part, the Levites, to give the burnt offerings and make reconciliation for Israel.

The singers David set over the service of song were of that tribe. “And they ministered before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of the congregation with singing, until Solomon had built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem: and then they waited on their office according to their order.” The tribe was in right order at this time.

“By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.”

Even in Babylon our captors required of us a song of Zion. That is proof to the nations of how great our singers were then and are now.

So do not read “these are they whom David set over the service of song in the house of the Lord” as regular men. These were famous men, royalty, chosen singers with musical talent, set apart to minister before the house of the Most High.
docs/study/1-kings/1.md|1 Kings 1:1-4|Ec:
“Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.” “Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm alone?”

That is exactly what David's servants sought for him. King David “was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.” This is one of the things that happens with age, when the body no longer produces heat as it did in youth and strength. So they sought a young virgin, “and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.”

Abishag the Shunammite was found, and she “cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.” That means he did not have relations with her. She was there only to keep him warm.
docs/study/1-kings/1.md|1 Kings 1:30|1 C:
“Howbeit the Lord God of Israel chose me before all the house of my father to be king over Israel for ever: for he hath chosen Judah to be the ruler; and of the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he liked me to make me king over all Israel: And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The Most High chose Judah, then David's house, then Solomon among all David's sons. So when David says, “Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead”, he is repeating the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.
docs/study/1-kings/10.md|1 Kings 10:10-1:
When the way was too long to carry the tithe, Israel could turn it into money, “And thou shalt bestow that money for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul desireth: and thou shalt eat there before the Lord thy God, and thou shalt rejoice”. Whatsoever the soul lusteth after means oxen, sheep, wine and food, not sex. The word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think.

So when “king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked”, people assume it was sexual. But her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order.

Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing: “So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.”
docs/study/1-kings/10.md|1 Kings 10:14-2:
“Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.” The law forbids images set up to worship.

Solomon's throne had six steps, “and two lions stood beside the stays.” “And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.” These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to. They were not worshipped, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.
docs/study/1-kings/10.md|1 Kings 10:6-9|:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

Even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people. The queen of Sheba said it herself: “Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.”

She saw it in Solomon's servants too: “Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.” They were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people.

“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand”.

He set his love on Israel not because they were many, but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers. That is the love the queen of Sheba spoke of: “because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king”.
docs/study/1-kings/11.md|1 Kings 11:1-3|:
“Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away: neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.”

That is exactly what Solomon did. “And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.” The law told the king why not to multiply wives, “that his heart turn not away”, and it turned away just as it said.

“Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.

Solomon loved “women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites”, the very nations of which the Most High said, “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”. It was not a maybe but a will. “Solomon clave unto these in love”, and “his wives turned away his heart.” It happened exactly as the Most High said it would.

“And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.”

The law warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and Solomon is the proof. He had strange wives of the nations, and “his wives turned away his heart.” Their daughters went a whoring after their gods and made the king go a whoring after them too.
docs/study/1-kings/11.md|1 Kings 11:26-4:
David charged Solomon before he died: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. The promise hung on it: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

Solomon did not keep that charge. The kingdom was rent “Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways”, “as did David his father.”

The same charge was then set before Jeroboam: “if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David”. Solomon sought to kill him, and Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

“For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim”. So when Solomon, “seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph”, Jeroboam was set over two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh.

Jeroboam the son of Nebat was “a mighty man of valour”, and he lifted up his hand against the king. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him in the way, rent his new garment in twelve pieces, and said, “Take thee ten pieces”. The Most High would rend ten tribes out of Solomon's hand and give them to Jeroboam, leaving one tribe “for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake”. The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, and the ten tribes went to Jeroboam.
docs/study/1-kings/11.md|1 Kings 11:4-8|:
“Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.”

Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles. It is the same idol, the star of Molech that Solomon built a high place for, “figures which ye made to worship them”. What Solomon brought in for his strange wives, Israel carried on for generations, and the Most High answered it with captivity.

“But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, and that six-pointed star came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.

When Solomon was old, “his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and he built “an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab”, “and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.” The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol. It has nothing to do with righteousness.

David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin. That is why Solomon's heart “was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father”, for a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.
docs/study/1-kings/12.md|1 Kings 12:25-3:
“It was also contained in the same writing, that the prophet, being warned of God, commanded the tabernacle and the ark to go with him, as he went forth into the mountain, where Moses climbed up, and saw the heritage of God.” There Jeremy “found an hollow cave, wherein he laid the tabernacle, and the ark, and the altar of incense, and so stopped the door.” Those who followed “could not find it”, and he said, “As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that God gather his people again together, and receive them unto mercy.”

Jeremiah hid the ark in a cave, and it is lost until the Most High gathers his people. So it is not in Ethiopia, and no man has it.

Jeroboam turned Israel away from the house of the Lord at Jerusalem. He said, “It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt”, set golden calves in Bethel and Dan, made priests “of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi”, and ordained a feast “in the month which he had devised of his own heart”. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today. After forty years of peace under Solomon, the nation of Israel began to decline even more.
docs/study/1-kings/13.md|1 Kings 13:1-5|:
“But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.” And how shall we know? “When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken”. The test of a true prophet is that the thing he speaks in the name of the Most High comes to pass.

The man of God out of Judah passed that test. He cried against Jeroboam's altar in Bethel that a child of the house of David, “Josiah by name”, would offer the priests of the high places upon it, “and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.” He gave a sign the same day: “Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.”

When Jeroboam put forth his hand, saying, “Lay hold on him”, his hand “dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.” “The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.” It came to pass, so the word was from the Most High.
docs/study/1-kings/13.md|1 Kings 13:11-1:
“Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall.”

The man of God had his charge: “Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.” He repeated it to the old prophet of Bethel who rode after him and found him “sitting under an oak”. But the old prophet said, “I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water.” The scripture plainly states it: “But he lied unto him.”

The man of God gave reverence to the older prophet, and “he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.” He let the reverence of a man cause him to fall.
docs/study/1-kings/13.md|1 Kings 13:20-2:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” The old prophet who lied and the man of God who was lied to were both in the hand of the Most High.

That is why the word of the Lord could come through the very prophet who had deceived him, as they sat at the table: “thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.” The Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man of God would keep the charge he had been given, “Eat no bread, and drink no water.”

He did not keep it, and under that dispensation disobedience carried the penalty of death. A lion met him by the way and slew him, and his carcase was cast in the road with the ass and the lion standing by it, neither eaten nor torn. Deceiver and deceived were both his, and the judgment was his.
docs/study/1-kings/14.md|1 Kings 14:19-2:
The law is plain: “There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” The Most High forbids it in the land.

Yet under Rehoboam, “there were also sodomites in the land”. Judah did evil and provoked the Most High to jealousy above all their fathers, building high places, images and groves on every high hill, and doing according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel. The very thing the law said should not be among the sons of Israel was there.

“Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.”

The abominations Judah practiced were the very things the law commands Israel not to do. When the scripture says there were sodomites in the land, and that they did “according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel”, this is the abomination it means. The nations were cast out for these things, and Judah took them up.
docs/study/1-kings/14.md|1 Kings 14:7-11:
This is the heart of the charge against Jeroboam: “But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back.”

The Most High exalted him from among the people, “made thee prince over my people Israel”, and rent the kingdom away from the house of David to give it to him. Yet he did not walk as David, “who kept my commandments”. He made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back.

Therefore the judgment: evil upon the house of Jeroboam, every male cut off, “him that pisseth against the wall”, and the remnant swept away “as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.”
docs/study/1-kings/15.md|1 Kings 15:1-5|:
This is David’s repentance after Nathan came to him: “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.”

The matter of Uriah the Hittite was a real wrong, and it is the one exception the scripture names: David did right all the days of his life, “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.” But David pleaded for mercy and acknowledged his transgression. He repented.

That is why, for David’s sake, the Most High gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem, even though Abijam walked in all the sins of his father and his heart was not perfect as David’s was. The children did what they saw their fathers do; David’s heart was the standard, and his repentance is part of why.
docs/study/1-kings/16.md|1 Kings 16:29-3:
Ahab followed the same road Solomon went down: “when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods”, and “Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians”.

Ahab took to wife “Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.” The Zidonians again. Solomon’s heart was turned by his wives, and Ahab’s was turned by his, until he reared up an altar for Baal and made a grove, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger more than all the kings of Israel before him.

The law forbids it: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Israel is not to marry outside the people, lest their hearts be turned to other gods.

Ahab broke that law, and it did exactly what the law warned. As if walking in the sins of Jeroboam were a light thing, he married Jezebel, the daughter of the king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal. Solomon’s wives turned his heart after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Zidonians; Jezebel turned Ahab’s heart to Baal.

When Jericho fell, Joshua laid a curse on it: “Cursed be the man before the Lord, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.”

In Ahab’s days it came to pass word for word. Hiel the Beth–elite built Jericho, and “laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.” The word of the Most High by Joshua stood, generations later.
docs/study/1-kings/16.md|1 Kings 16:8-14:
Moses foretold it: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”. Israel grew fat, “then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” They “sacrificed unto devils, not to God”, to new gods their fathers never feared.

The Most High says, “they have provoked me to anger with their vanities”. That is the same word spoken over Baasha and Elah his son: all the house of Baasha was destroyed “For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son”, who made Israel to sin, “in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.”

So when Zimri, captain of half his chariots, slew Elah while he was drinking himself drunk in Tirzah, and then left not one male of the house of Baasha, it came “according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet”. It was the Most High answering the provoking of his people.
docs/study/1-kings/17.md|1 Kings 17:17-2:
“Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.”

The widow’s son fell sick, “and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.” A man’s life is short and full of trouble, and it can be cut down like a flower. The widow took it that the child was paying for her sins: “art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?”

But how long a man lives is not his own to decide, nor the grieving mother’s. That rests with the Most High, as the verses that follow show.

“Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass”. A man’s days are determined and appointed. When the appointed day comes, a man cannot pass it.

But this child’s day had not yet come. Elijah carried him up into the loft, laid him on his own bed, stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried, “O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again. And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.” Because it was not the child’s time, the Lord let his soul return.

All praises that Elijah was there to call upon the Lord. And the widow said, “Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.”
docs/study/1-kings/17.md|1 Kings 17:2-6|:
Christ said, “Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.” Instead, “Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

“Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God? But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.” That is how much power the Most High holds. Not one bird is forgotten before him, and he has command over them all.

So when the word of the Lord sent Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, he could say, “I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.” And “the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening”. The Most High has power over the animals, and he can command the ravens to bring a man food if it be his will. “Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.”
docs/study/1-kings/17.md|1 Kings 17:7-16:
“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” That reverence goes into the honor of feeding the man first, just as the widow did.

The widow of Zarephath had only “an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse”, and was gathering two sticks to dress a last meal for herself and her son, “that we may eat it, and die.” Elijah told her, “make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.” The man of God eats first. That is a precept.

She trusted and obeyed, “and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail”. For trusting in the Lord and obeying, she was sustained.

So sisters must trust in the Lord when he tells them to reverence their husbands and be submissive in all things, and not lean to their own understanding.
docs/study/1-kings/18.md|1 Kings 18:17-1:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Those who seek wisdom, she lays hold of and lifts up.

Especially with the new, the Most High deals with each one differently and gives time to get it right. Wisdom is not taken from a man the first time he stumbles. Ahab was not one who sought her; he held on to his sin, followed Baalim, and let Jezebel feed the prophets of Baal and the prophets of the groves at her table without ever checking her.

“For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” Wisdom torments a man in his mind at the first, until he rids his body of sin.

“Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” That is for the one who comes through the trying.

“But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.” That is what happened to Ahab. He went wrong, wisdom forsook him, and he was given over to his own ruin: blaming Elijah for troubling Israel while he and his father’s house had forsaken the commandments, and letting Jezebel feed eight hundred and fifty false prophets at her table.

“For froward thoughts separate from God”. “For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.” Sin comes in and wisdom goes out. “For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.”

That is Ahab. He was full of sin, so his wisdom was hindered and he had thoughts without understanding. When he saw Elijah he said, “Art thou he that troubleth Israel?” That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the ordained prophet of God for the trouble rather than his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul.

Elijah answered him with the truth: “I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.” It was Ahab following the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, worshipping the golden calves, that brought the trouble.
docs/study/1-kings/18.md|1 Kings 18:20-2:
Christ said, “I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.”

On Mount Carmel Elijah asked the people, “How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.” That is the lukewarm: one foot in and one foot out, playing the middle ground.

That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves. Cast away every burden and sin, and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments. The lukewarm who know the truth but keep no commandments will be cast away. Being spewed out of Christ’s mouth is the end of the middle ground, and the next step after that is death.
docs/study/1-kings/18.md|1 Kings 18:25-2:
“I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.” That is why no fire came for Baal.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock and called on Baal “from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered.” Eight hundred and fifty men leaped upon the altar, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon he mocked them: “Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.”

They cried aloud and “cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them”, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. Still “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” The Most High will not give his glory to another.

“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

The idols of the nations are not real. They are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them, the idols cannot answer. Only the Most High made the heavens.

That is why, from morning until past the time of the evening sacrifice, with all their crying and cutting, “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” There was no one there to answer.
docs/study/1-kings/18.md|1 Kings 18:30-4:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Against the pastors that feed his people he says, “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.”

When the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench, the people fell on their faces and said, “The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.” Then Elijah said, “Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape.” They were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there.

In the last days it will be the same. When the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape. They that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee. The same judgment that fell on the prophets of Baal will fall on the false shepherds today; the Lord will visit upon them the evil of their doings.
docs/study/1-kings/2.md|1 Kings 2:1-4|Ps:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

David charged Solomon to keep the charge of the Lord his God, “to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses”. And the throne came with a stipulation: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

The truth David’s seed was to walk in is the law. The righteousness of the Most High is everlasting, and his law is the truth. Reading through the kings, many broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous; the throne stood or fell on whether they walked in that truth.
docs/study/1-kings/21.md|1 Kings 21:1-3|:
“The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.” The land belonged to the Most High and was held as a family inheritance.

Ahab wanted Naboth’s vineyard in Jezreel because it was hard by his palace, and offered a better vineyard or “the worth of it in money.” But Naboth answered, “The Lord forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.” He could not simply hand off an inheritance that was given to him. He was keeping the law.
docs/study/1-kings/21.md|1 Kings 21:15-1:
“In thee have they taken gifts to shed blood; thou hast taken usury and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by extortion, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord God. Behold, therefore I have smitten mine hand at thy dishonest gain which thou hast made, and at thy blood which hath been in the midst of thee.”

When Naboth was dead, Jezebel said, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for money”, and Ahab rose up to go down and take it. That is extortion: seizing what another has by violence and force, and greedily gaining of a neighbour with blood.

Ahab shares the guilt. He sat by and let Jezebel commit the crime because he coveted the field, then turned his face from the evil and went to claim the reward. The Most High smites his hand at that dishonest gain.
docs/study/1-kings/21.md|1 Kings 21:20-2:
The same judgment was spoken over Jeroboam: “Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.”

The words “him that pisseth against the wall” mean the males. The Most High said he would cut them off entirely. Now Elijah speaks the same words over Ahab, because he “sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord”: every male cut off, and his house made “like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat”, for the provocation by which he made Israel to sin.

This is how the judgment on Baasha was carried out: “when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.” When Zimri reigned, not one male was left.

So when the Most High tells Ahab, “And will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah”, it is plain what that means. The house of Baasha was wiped out to the last male, and the same was coming on Ahab’s house for the provocation wherewith he provoked the Most High and made Israel to sin.
docs/study/1-kings/21.md|1 Kings 21:23-2:
“And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.” That is one of the curses of disobedience in the law.

The Most High declared, “The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Him that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat.” The judgment on Ahab’s house matches the curse spoken in the law: their carcases left as meat for the beasts and the birds.
docs/study/1-kings/21.md|1 Kings 21:8-10:
“And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.” A king sealed the den with his own signet so the decree could not be changed. That is the binding authority of a royal seal.

Jezebel “wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal”. The seal was a signet, the official mark of the king’s authority, so when those letters reached the elders and nobles of Naboth’s city, they carried royal weight as if Ahab himself had written them.

“Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.”

That is exactly what the sons of Belial were hired to do. Jezebel wrote, “set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.” A fast proclaimed, Naboth set on high, and false witnesses brought in to kill him. It was evil counsel and a murderous plot, built on breaking the commandment.
docs/study/1-kings/22.md|1 Kings 22:1-6|:
“Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no gods.”

Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and forsook the Levites. He made priests after the manner of the nations, so that any man could consecrate himself to serve gods that are no gods. That is the division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, and it is why the four hundred prophets Ahab gathered could not be trusted, even though Jehoshaphat said, “I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.”

“And Elisha said unto the king of Israel, What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother.”

After the kingdom split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry, so a true prophet of the Most High kept his distance from its corrupted worship. Elisha told a later king of Israel to go to the prophets of his father and his mother; he wanted nothing to do with their manner of worship.

That is the setting in 1 Kings 22. Ahab gathered “about four hundred men” as his prophets, and they said with one mouth, “Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.” These were the prophets of the northern kingdom, not the prophets of the Most High.

“Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.” Amos had said, “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.”

So Amaziah told the prophet, “O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.” The priest of Bethel drove the prophet out of the king’s chapel.

That shows how the northern kingdom rejected the true word. The king’s chapel had its own priests and its own prophets, and the word of the Most High was not welcome there; which is why Ahab could gather four hundred prophets who all said the same thing.
docs/study/1-kings/22.md|1 Kings 22:13-2:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” He leadeth counsellors away spoiled and maketh the judges fools.

Micaiah saw “the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The Lord asked, “Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came forth and said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

“Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil concerning thee.” The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High. He used the lie of the four hundred prophets to bring on Ahab the judgment he had already declared.
docs/study/1-kings/22.md|1 Kings 22:41-5:
David charged the princes of Israel to help Solomon, saying, “Is not the Lord your God with you? and hath he not given you rest on every side? for he hath given the inhabitants of the land into mine hand; and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people.”

The Most High gave the inhabitants of the land into David’s hand, and the land was subdued. That is why, in Jehoshaphat’s day, “There was then no king in Edom: a deputy was king.” Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted, so it had no king of its own.
docs/study/1-kings/3.md|1 Kings 3:5-9|1:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world? and if the world shall be judged by you, are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Know ye not that we shall judge angels? how much more things that pertain to this life?”

The saints shall judge the world and even angels, so those in the church should be able to judge the smallest matters of this life. That is why Solomon’s request is ours too. He asked, “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”.

This is what we still need to pray for: that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another.
docs/study/1-kings/3.md|1 Kings 3:5-9|Ps:
“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.”

The saints are the children of Israel, a people near unto him. So when Paul says the saints shall judge the world, it is Israel that will judge. That is the great people Solomon stood in the midst of, “thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude”, and the people he asked for an understanding heart to judge.
docs/study/1-kings/4.md|1 Kings 4:29-34|:
Solomon speaks of what the Most High gave him: “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: The beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons: The circuits of years, and the positions of stars: The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds, and the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots: And all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

The knowledge the Most High bestowed on Solomon exceeded that of all men who walked the earth. That is why “he spake of trees, from the cedar tree that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the wall: he spake also of beasts, and of fowl, and of creeping things, and of fishes.” He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five, which is why we have Proverbs and the Song of Songs.

“Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.” Since his wisdom already excelled Egypt’s, we have no need to dabble in Egyptology or any doctrine outside the scriptures given to us.
docs/study/1-kings/5.md|1 Kings 5:10-12|:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.” He told out “threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

Then he sent to Huram the king of Tyre: “As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.” This is why a good name and inheritance matter. Solomon could say, deal with me as you dealt with David my father, and slide into the benefit of the friendship his father had built.

The house was for the name of the Lord, “to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.”

So Hiram gave cedar and fir, Solomon gave wheat and pure oil year by year, and “there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.” It is wise to be at peace with the nations where we can, dealing righteously, being wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

“Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the Lord hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them.” He said, “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.”

Hiram sent “a cunning man, endued with understanding”, “The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson”.

Hiram and his craftsman were joined to Israel by lineage: the craftsman’s mother was of the daughters of Dan. That is part of why there was peace between Hiram and Solomon and they two made a league together, and why “the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him” is seen in how he dealt with Hiram.
docs/study/1-kings/5.md|1 Kings 5:13-18|:
“And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom. And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.”

That is the same ordered labor described here: “threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains”, and over them the chief of Solomon’s officers, “which ruled over the people that wrought in the work.” Solomon had order in the work, bearers, hewers and overseers.

The levy was an enlistment for service, thirty thousand men sent to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses, “a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home”, gathered to bring the wood back to Jerusalem, with Adoniram over the levy. The temple was built successfully because our forefathers had a spirit to work together under rank and structure, without murmuring over who did which task.
docs/study/1-kings/5.md|1 Kings 5:2-6|Ec:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” Nathan was the prophet of David’s day, the one through whom the Lord spoke to David.

Solomon reminds Hiram of what the Lord spoke to David his father: “Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build an house unto my name.” That word came in the time of David, and now Solomon purposes to build the house.

“After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever.”

That is exactly what Solomon tells Hiram: “But now the Lord my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.” God made all quiet round about him so that he might build the house. So Solomon purposes to build it, and asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, where the best cedar grew, “for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.” The Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation.

“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.” He slew a giant “when he was yet but young”, and beat down “the boasting of Goliath”, “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.”

David was a man of war from his youth. That is why Solomon tells Hiram that “David my father could not build an house unto the name of the Lord his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet.”
