So David feared after Uzzah. “David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah”, and “David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?” He had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of him and his judgments.

So David would not bring the ark into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. It stayed there three months, “and the Lord blessed Obed–edom, and all his household” because of the ark.
docs/study/2-samuel/7.md|2 Samuel 7:12-1:
The Lord told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.” The word reaches past Solomon. The angel told Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.”

Solomon built the house and sat on the throne, but his kingdom was not established for ever. His son Rehoboam would not hear counsel, and the kingdom split into two nations. The seed whose kingdom is established for ever is Jesus Christ the black Messiah, who came through David's lineage.

“He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David.”

That is the promise to David fulfilled: “I will be his father, and he shall be my son.” Christ is called the Son of the Highest, and the Lord God gives him the throne of his father David. Christ came through David's lineage, and he is the seed the Lord spoke of when he said, “I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

“And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.”

The Lord told David, “thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.” Solomon's kingdom did end; it split into two nations under Rehoboam. The phrase “for ever” points to Christ, whose kingdom has no end. He reigns over the house of Jacob for ever.

The Lord said of David's seed, “If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men.” Solomon was not chastened with the rod of men in his lifetime.

Micah shows who was: “they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.” That was fulfilled in Christ, not Solomon. Jesus the Christ was smitten with the rod upon the cheek, and he did no sin, though it was Solomon who sinned.

The Lord did not make the Bible easy in every place, that he might see who would research and learn precept upon precept.

“But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

Out of Bethlehem, the city of David, comes the ruler in Israel. His goings forth have been from everlasting, and that is the one whose throne the Lord said “shall be established for ever.” The same judge of Israel smitten with a rod upon the cheek is the ruler who came forth out of Bethlehem: Jesus Christ, of David's line.
docs/study/2-samuel/7.md|2 Samuel 7:17-2:
David asked, “what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself”? The Most High did not redeem one man alone but a whole people, and he will bring them out again as a people.

Ezekiel shows how: “I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king.

The teaching applies to us now. Though a brother or sister may have a difference, we must forgive one another and come back together, for the Most High chose us as one people. We lost our heritage in captivity, and coming back to it we must let go of grudges.

“And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd.” The one king is Jesus Christ. He is called David, and called the throne of David, because he comes of David's line and David ruled over all twelve tribes. David will be present, but he is not the king.

That is the house the Lord spoke of to David “for a great while to come”, and why David sat before the Lord and said, “Who am I, O Lord God? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?” Under that one king and one shepherd, Israel “shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them.”

“Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.”

The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life: all of it is Christ. The God of peace brought him again from the dead, and he is the one shepherd over Israel, made one nation again. That is what the Lord meant when he told David he had spoken of his house “for a great while to come.”

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land.”

The children of Judah, the southern kingdom, and the children of Israel, the northern kingdom, are gathered together under one head, and that head is Christ. David said, “thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever.” The same people he redeemed from Egypt he gathers again and brings up out of the land.

“I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.”

The one shepherd that Israel shall have is Christ. He is the good shepherd who lays down his life. He is the one king over the twelve tribes, called by David's name because he comes of David's line, and he is the shepherd who gathers the sheep back into one nation.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.”

Christ is the one who brings Israel up. The Most High redeemed Israel from Egypt, “from the nations and their gods”, and he will do it again: the one king and one shepherd gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.
docs/study/2-samuel/9.md|2 Samuel 9:1|1:
David asked, “Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?” Saul's son Jonathan and David were always very close.

That closeness goes back to the beef between Saul and David in the book of Samuel. Jonathan was always there for David; that was David's homeboy. “Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.”

So even with Saul gone, David remembered the covenant, and sought out whoever was left of Saul's house to show him kindness for Jonathan's sake.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:12-13|Acts 1:
“Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.”

That Simeon is Simon Peter. The same man is Simon, Simeon, Peter and Cephas. That is why the lists of the apostles read differently from book to book: the men are the same, known by different names.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:12-13|Jude 1:
“Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James.”

Judas the brother of James is the same apostle as Lebbeus Thaddeus, and he is also called Jude. He is not Judas Iscariot the traitor. He called himself Jude, or Thaddeus, so as not to be associated with the traitor.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:12-13|Luke 6:
Luke's own list shows the differing names for the same men: “Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelotes, And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.”

Where Matthew has Simon the Canaanite, Luke has “Simon called Zelotes”; where Matthew has Lebbeus Thaddeus, Luke has “Judas the brother of James.” And Luke keeps Judas the brother of James apart from “Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.” They are not the same man.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:12-13|Matthe:
They returned from the mount called Olivet, a sabbath day's journey from Jerusalem, and went up into an upper room where the eleven abode, and their names are listed. The lists differ across the gospels, because the same men go by different names.

Matthew's list: “The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alpheus, and Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus; Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.”

Simon is also called Peter and Cephas. Simon the Canaanite is the same man as Simon Zelotes in Acts. And Lebbeus, whose surname was Thaddeus, is the same man Acts calls Judas the brother of James.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:14|Galatians:
“But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.”

James the Just, the Lord's brother, came to believe after Christ's death. He is one of the brethren in the upper room, and he became an apostle and was later killed. The brother who once did not believe in him became an apostle of him.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:14|John 7:3-:
During his ministry his own brothers did not believe in him. “His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.” They told him, “If thou do these things, shew thyself to the world. For neither did his brethren believe in him.”

But after his death and the miracles they came to believe. That is why the same brethren who doubted him are found in the upper room, continuing with one accord in prayer and supplication.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:14|Matthew 1:
“These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.” His brethren are Christ's own brothers, his family: “Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?”

It was not only the men in that upper room. The women also had to learn, and the men always understood that the women learn alongside them. A camp that keeps the women out of the congregation is wrong. Our people came into slavery together and will come out of captivity together.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:1|2 Timothy:
“Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.”

Luke traveled with Paul. When others had gone, Luke was still with him. And the Mark Paul calls for is the one who wrote the Gospel of Mark. These were the men under the apostles, the ones the teaching was passed down to, and that is how Luke came to write his former treatise and then the Acts.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:1|Colossians:
“Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you.”

Paul knew Luke personally and calls him the beloved physician. That shows Luke was present throughout the ministry. He was not one of the twelve, but he was there, and what he wrote of “all that Jesus began both to do and teach” was delivered to him by eyewitnesses and written by a man who walked with the apostles.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:1|Luke 1:1-4:
Luke wrote both the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts. “The former treatise” is the Gospel of Luke, and it was addressed to the same man: “to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus.” The two books are two letters from the same hand.

“Many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us, Even as they delivered them unto us, which from the beginning were eyewitnesses, and ministers of the word.” The scriptures we have are a collection of the apostles' teaching passed down to the young men under them, the seventy, and the other disciples. Luke was not one of the twelve, though it is speculated he was of the seventy, and he was there from the beginning, “having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first.” Just as the bishops and elders pass down history to us today so that we can speak on it though we were not there, that knowledge was passed down to Luke.

Theophilus' name means love of God. He was an Israelite, not a gentile, and Luke calls him “most excellent”, a title of nobility or government office, the same way Paul addressed most noble Festus. Luke wrote “That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed.”
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:2|Acts 2:5:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

That is what “all nations” looks like. These were not gentiles; they were Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, because every nation that ruled over Israel carried them off into exile. So when Christ commanded that repentance be preached “among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem”, it began with Israelites gathered at Jerusalem from every land they had been scattered into.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:2|Deuteronom:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

This is why the commandment was to preach “among all nations.” The Most High said he would scatter Israel among the nations and leave them few in number among the heathen. That scattering placed our people in every captivity: Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece, Rome, and then out of Africa through the slave trades. The apostles were sent to Israel wherever the Lord had led them.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:2|Luke 24:46:
Luke gave a full historical account of everything Christ did, from his birth “Until the day in which he was taken up”, and the end of Luke segues straight into Acts. The commandments Christ gave through the Holy Ghost are right there: “Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.”

“All nations” does not mean the Chinese or the Japanese. Prophetically it means the Israelites scattered among all nations: into Assyria, which is why Jonah preached to Nineveh, where the northern kingdom was exiled; then Babylon, Persia, Media, Greece and Rome; then into Africa and out through the transatlantic and Indian Ocean slave trades. That prophecy did not happen only once; it happened all through history. Repentance was to be preached to Israel wherever they were scattered.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:3|1 Corinthi:
After his passion Christ “shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days.” He did not appear for only a day or two; he stayed forty days, speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of the Most High, to open their understanding further.

Within that time he was seen by many: “he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles.” Cephas is another name for Peter, and it means stone.

“And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.” Paul was the last to see him. Those are the many infallible proofs: Christ alive, seen by hundreds of witnesses.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|Acts 7:51:
“Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.”

The first form of the Holy Ghost is the law. Israel received it and did not keep it, and that is resisting the Holy Ghost. The order is the same as in Proverbs: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit. The stiffnecked never get past the first step, as their fathers did before them.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|John 14:26:
“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

Christ could teach only so much in three years, because a man can bear only so much. The Comforter would open their understanding in increments after his death, guiding them into all truth and bringing his words back to their remembrance. That is the promise of the Father they were told to wait for in Jerusalem.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|John 16:7:
Christ commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem but to “wait for the promise of the Father”, and the promise of the Father is the Holy Ghost, given only after Christ was glorified.

“Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.” He had to die for the Holy Ghost to be given. That is why they had to wait.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|John 20:22:
After he rose, “he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.”

The Holy Ghost comes in measure and in order. They received it when he breathed on them after he rose, and still he told them to wait in Jerusalem for the promise of the Father. The Comforter would keep opening their understanding in increments.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|Proverbs 1:
The Holy Ghost comes in an order, and it begins with the law. “Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.”

The first stipulation is turning at his reproof. Turn, keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and makes known his words, opening the understanding. The promise of the Father is not given to a man who will not turn.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:4|Wisdom of:
“And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above?”

No man knows the counsel of the Most High unless he gives wisdom and sends his Holy Spirit from above. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth. That is why the apostles had to wait for the promise of the Father before they went out.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:5|John 4:1-2:
“When therefore the Lord knew how the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John, (Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples,)”

Christ himself baptized not with water, but with the Holy Ghost. His disciples baptized with water because they had followed John; two of John's own disciples heard Christ and followed him. That is why in Acts the disciples were still baptizing with water. John decreased and Christ increased, in increments.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:5|John 7:38-:
“He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.”

When you believe on Christ as the scripture says, rivers of living water flow out of your belly. That means wisdom and understanding flow out of the mind, the part that consumes and filters information.

“But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.” That is why they were to be baptized with the Holy Ghost “not many days hence.” It could not come until he was glorified.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:5|Luke 1:5:
“There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.”

John was of the tribe of Levi. His father Zacharias was a priest, and his mother Elisabeth was of the daughters of Aaron. That is why he baptized with water: baptism comes out of the purification laws of the priesthood. His washing was a symbol, preparing the way for the one who would baptize with the Holy Ghost.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:5|Matthew 3::
“For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.” There is a distinction between what John taught and what Christ brought.

John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire.” John's water baptism was always symbolic, a preparation leading up to Christ. Baptism comes from the word baptizo, out of the purification laws.

John said he must decrease and Christ must increase, and that happens in increments.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:5|Proverbs 2:
“The spirit of man is the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts of the belly.”

The belly is the mind. That is where the rivers of living water flow from, the place where wisdom and understanding are searched out. And the spirit is a candle: it can be put out like a candle.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:6|2 Thessalo:
“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.”

The kingdom could not be restored in the disciples' time. The falling away had to come first and the man of sin be revealed. He could not be openly named under Rome, where you were jailed for sedition, so Paul wrote in allegory. He would be revealed in a land like America, where the freedom to speak allows the man of sin to be identified plainly.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:6|Daniel 7:7:
“After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces.”

The fourth beast is Rome. The disciples knew Daniel's beasts up to Rome because their fathers had lived through them, so they thought Rome was the last and the kingdom would be restored in their day. But they did not yet understand what came after: the little horn, Babylon the great and America. That fuller understanding was given later to John, to Peter, and now in these last days.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:6|Matthew 11:
“Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?”

The disciples asked about restoring the kingdom because they thought Rome was the last captivity. John the Baptist thought the same. He sent from prison to ask whether Christ was the one, because he too expected deliverance at that time.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:6|Revelation:
“Restore” means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem, and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations. It is not pie in the sky when you die.

The new Jerusalem “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” The kingdom is for the twelve tribes, not for everyone else. That is why the disciples asked, “wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?”

“Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

The disciples did not yet understand the seven seals, because only the Lion of the tribe of Judah could open them. The book was not yet opened to them when they asked if the kingdom would be restored at that time. That understanding was given later to John, and now in these last days.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:6|Romans 12::
Even after all of this they asked, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” That shows the Holy Ghost was not yet fully given.

It is given in measures: “God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” Every man is dealt a measure of faith that he has to grow in. In Christ there was no measure, but the disciples knew only so much at that time, and their understanding grew in increments.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:8|Acts 2:4:
“And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

That is one instance of the power coming to pass, the promise of Acts 1:8 fulfilled. But tongues is only one of the signs. The power of the Holy Ghost is casting out devils, new tongues, taking up serpents, drinking any deadly thing unharmed, and laying hands on the sick to recover. With that power they were witnesses “both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.”
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:8|Mark 16:16:
“But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.” Christians misunderstand this power as merely speaking in tongues, but the Bible defines the power of the Holy Ghost by the signs that follow.

“He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned. And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.”

That is the power the apostles received. Peter was sought to heal by his shadow, and Paul by his handkerchief.
docs/study/acts/1.md|Acts 1:9|Psalms 104:
“While they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” He was taken up in the middle of his speaking, after forty days. That was the exit.

The Most High “maketh the clouds his chariot.” So this was not merely a cloud but a chariot, an instrument of the angels, the same as the moon is an instrument of the armies above. Christ was received up by a chariot, not carried by little white angels in the clouds as the Christian movies depict.

The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem: a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:11-12|Eccl:
“I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.”

The beasts, creeping things and fowls in the sheet are men. Scripture testifies that men in their estate are as beasts. So the whole allegory is about the state of the northern kingdom, mingled among the nations, and not about food.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:11-12|Hose:
Peter saw “a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth.” Christians use this vision to justify eating unclean food, but it is symbolic, and it points back to the northern kingdom.

The vessel is Israel: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” Israel, swallowed up among the nations, is that vessel let down to Peter.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:11-12|Isai:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek.” The Gentiles who seek him are the remnant of his people: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.”

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” That is the sheet knit at the four corners. It is the Israelite diaspora, the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah gathered from the four corners of the earth, which is why the Most High used a sheet from four corners.

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart”, “Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” The northern kingdom and the southern kingdom are gathered together, and that is what was let down to Peter.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:11-12|Psal:
“They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works. And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them. Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils.”

That is the state of the northern kingdom. Israel did not destroy the nations but mingled among the heathen, learned their works and served their idols. That is why the vessel in Peter's vision is full of every kind of beast: it shows Israel after mingling among the nations, not a lesson about food.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:13-14|Levi:
A voice said, “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” Peter answered, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” Peter refuses because he knows the dietary law: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

There is a beast that may be eaten and a beast that may not. The Most High did not change the duty of a pig, a hawk or a vulture. The unclean animals are the scavengers, the garbage disposal of the earth, made to filter the filth, while the clean animals have a filtration system so their meat is safe. Nothing in the vision changed the nature of any animal.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:15|Ezekiel:
The voice spoke a second time: “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” Praying over pork does not change the toxicity of the animal or its eating habits. What the Most High cleansed is man, not the swine. The vision is about people the Most High cleansed from idolatry.

He promised it: “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” That is the man that is cleansed: Israel, saved out of all the places where they sinned.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:15|Job 14::
“Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.”

That speaks of the animals. The unclean animals were made unclean from the beginning, and no prayer makes them clean. But the northern kingdom was planted a holy and righteous seed, so it can be cleansed again. That is why the Most High can say, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”: he is speaking of Israel, not of swine.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:19-23|Psal:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”

That is why Cornelius is said to fear God. The fear of the Most High belongs to all that do his commandments. Cornelius, “a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews”, was known by the Jews themselves as a keeper of the law.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:19-23|Roma:
The men told Peter, “Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews.” Now Cornelius is called just, adding to devout from verse 2.

“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” To be just is to keep the law that is holy, just and good. A just man is one who keeps the law.

Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him. So they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:1|Acts 18::
“There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band.” When our people read “Italian band” they automatically picture a Caucasian. But Caesarea Maritima sat on a seacoast in the land of Israel, and Cornelius was an Israelite officer in the Roman army, not a man of another nation.

It was common for Israelites to live in Italy and Rome. Paul “found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:)”. A Jew born in Pontus, living in Italy, and there were enough Jews in Rome for Claudius to command them all to depart.

Jews of the diaspora were fully enmeshed in Roman culture. They took Greek and Latin names and built careers in the Roman military, so a black man, an Israelite, serving under the Italian band is nothing strange. It is the same as so-called black people and Latinos serving in the American military today, from the Buffalo Soldiers to a general like Colin Powell.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:1|Acts 22::
“Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.”

Paul is an Israelite, and still he says yes, because Roman is his citizenship, not his race. The Israelites were scattered through every province and took the names of their captivities, so scholars cannot tell a Roman Jewish soldier from a Roman by his name alone. The New Testament was written in Greek because Israel spoke Greek under the Greeks.

So a centurion of the Italian band with a Latin name like Cornelius can be an Israelite. The centurions of scripture were often Israelite servants in the army.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:1|Revelati:
“What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia; unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.”

The seven churches were in Asia Minor because the Israelite diaspora settled there, and that is why the letters were sent to them. Israel was scattered through every province of the empire, in Asia, in Italy, in Rome, and so an Israelite could be found anywhere, even as a centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:1|Romans 1:
The same Paul who told the chief captain he was a Roman answers plainly: “I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

His Roman citizenship never made him a Roman by nation. That is how to read Cornelius: a Roman officer by his post and his name, and an Israelite by his seed.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|1 Ki:
Peter says, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation.” “One of another nation” is not other races. It is the northern kingdom, and this whole verse rests on the split between Judah and Ephraim.

The division began when Rehoboam refused the people: “the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord.” Then Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Adoram, made Jeroboam king over all Israel, “there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.”

“So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.” That is where the enmity begins that you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament.

Rehoboam gathered “all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men” to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back. But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God: “Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me.”

The division was from the Most High. The southern kingdom, Judah and Benjamin, and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and they were still brethren, “your brethren the children of Israel.” The one of “another nation” in Peter's mouth is that brother, the northern kingdom.

Jeroboam sealed the split with idolatry. He “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Bethel and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin.”

He “made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah.” A feast of his own, out of his own heart.

From there the northern kingdom sank deeper and deeper into idol worship. That idolatry is why Judah would not keep company with them.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|1 Pe:
Peter himself wrote it: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.”

That is Hosea's word to Ephraim, word for word in meaning: not a people, now the people of God; had not obtained mercy, now have obtained mercy. The Gentiles being brought in are the northern kingdom, and Peter, who once said he would not keep company with one of another nation, wrote to them as a holy nation.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|2 Ch:
Rehoboam had “Judah and Benjamin on his side. And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts. For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord.”

So the southern kingdom was Judah, Benjamin and Levi. And not only the Levites: “after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem.” A remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah.

Jeroboam “ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” The north went one way and Judah another, and that is the line Peter speaks of when he says a Jew may not keep company with one of another nation.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|2 Ki:
“In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.”

That is the first transporting of Israel out of the land. The Assyrian kings began the exile of the northern kingdom in the days of Pekah.

“Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.” The northern kingdom conspired with Syria against Judah, their own brethren.

Ahaz sent to the king of Assyria, “I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, which rise up against me.” He took the silver and gold of the house of the Lord and sent it as a present, and the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, took it, “and slew Rezin.”

That conspiracy of Israel with Syria against Judah is what began the exile of the north by the Assyrian kings.

“Therefore the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only.”

“For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin.” The children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam and departed not from them, “Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.”

Hosea said Ephraim would be utterly taken away and carried into Assyria, and here it is. The northern kingdom was removed out of the land and scattered among the nations. Judah, too, “kept not the commandments of the Lord their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.”

The hatred carried straight through the history. Elisha told the king of Israel, “As the Lord of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee.”

The prophet would not even look toward the king of Israel. He dealt only with Jehoshaphat of Judah. That is the same wall Peter speaks of: a Jew did not keep company with the northern kingdom.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Acts:
“Men and brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whosoever among you feareth God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.”

The word of this salvation is sent to the children of the stock of Abraham, the lineage passing through Isaac and Jacob to the twelve tribes. The whosoever that feareth God is among them, just as Cornelius was “one that feareth God.”

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”

Peter spoke this to the men of Israel. The whosoever of Joel is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel, and that includes the northern kingdom he would be sent to in Cornelius' house.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Amos:
“They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.”

Dan was where Jeroboam set one of the golden calves, and Dan fell so hard that the tribe was absorbed. Those who swore by the sin of Samaria and the god of Dan fell and never rose up again.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Ephe:
“Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”, “That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.” These are the ones who were once Gentiles in the flesh, aliens from the commonwealth of Israel: the northern kingdom, broken and scattered.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man.”

The twain are Judah and Ephraim, the two sticks. The middle wall of partition is the enmity Peter spoke of when he said it was unlawful for a Jew to keep company with one of another nation. Christ broke it down: “ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God.”
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Ezek:
The restoration is two sticks made one nation. “Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.”

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.”

And Ephraim, joined to idols, is cleansed: “Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols”, “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them.” That is what God showed Peter: not to call any man common or unclean whom he has cleansed.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Gene:
“And it came to pass after these things, that one told Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.”

Joseph's two sons are Manasseh and Ephraim, and Ephraim became the head over Samaria. So the parcel of ground Jacob gave to Joseph is Ephraim's land, and a woman of Samaria is of the northern kingdom.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Hebr:
“For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.”

The law of commandments contained in ordinances, the sacrifices offered year by year, was a shadow. That is the law being taken out of the way when Christ abolished the enmity and made of twain one new man.

The gifts and sacrifices were “a figure for the time then present”, which “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

The time of reformation is Christ. The ordinances that kept Judah apart from the unclean were imposed only until he came, and that is why God showed Peter not to call any man common or unclean.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Hose:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

Ephraim, once Lo-ammi, “not a people”, is called back and named the sons of the living God. The same house of Israel that was broken and taken away is restored in the very place where it was called not my people.

Hosea said the same. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away. But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah.”

Then: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” The house of Israel, the northern kingdom, would get no more mercy and would be utterly taken away, and they were called not my people. That is why they were counted as one of another nation.

“I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.”

The house of Israel was told “I will no more have mercy”, and here the Most High has mercy on her that had not obtained mercy. Ephraim, who was not his people, is called his people again. That is who God showed Peter not to call common or unclean.

“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”

That is why the prophets would not deal with the north. Ephraim was joined to the idols Jeroboam set up, the calves in Bethel and Dan, and the word was to let him alone. Judah kept that word, and it hardened into the wall Peter speaks of.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Isai:
“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.”

Christ ends the enmity of the split. From Rehoboam and Jeroboam, through the golden calves, through Pekah and Rezin and the Assyrian captivity, Judah and Ephraim were enemies, and the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. Now Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. That is why Peter came to Cornelius “without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.”

The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, the outcasts of Israel that Christ came to be a light to. That is why he spoke openly to the woman of Samaria, and why Peter was sent to Cornelius.

“I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.”

That is the northern kingdom, which began to seek him. Ephraim was “not a people”, a nation no longer called by his name, and still he was found of them.

Isaiah prophesied against that conspiracy: “Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have taken evil counsel against thee, saying, Let us go up against Judah, and vex it”, “Thus saith the Lord God, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.”

“For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people. And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son.”

Because Ephraim conspired with Syria, Ephraim would be broken within sixty-five years, “that it be not a people.” Broken and removed from the land, they lost their nationality, culture and heritage and were assimilated into the nations. That is how the northern kingdom became “another nation.”
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Joel:
“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” The whosoever is inside Israel: the Most High in the midst of Israel, deliverance in Zion and Jerusalem, in the remnant he calls.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|John:
The woman asks, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?”

She calls Jacob “our father”, and Jacob fathered only the twelve tribes. She is claiming Israel through Ephraim. She was telling Christ she was of the tribe of Ephraim dwelling in Samaria.

“The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things. Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.”

The Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans, but Christ spoke to her openly. His first duty was to bring light to the northern kingdom, and he revealed himself as the Messiah to a woman of Ephraim. His light went first to the north.

“Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Now Jacob’s well was there.”

Samaria is the parcel of ground Jacob gave to Joseph, Ephraim's land. The woman at the well was dwelling on the inheritance of Joseph's house.

“Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.”

This is the same wall. Samaria was Ephraim's territory, “the head of Ephraim is Samaria.” The Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans for the same reason Peter says it is unlawful for a Jew to keep company with one of another nation: the split between Judah and Ephraim.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Reve:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Twelve thousand are sealed of each tribe: Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin.

Dan is missing. Dan fell into the idolatry of the golden calf and was absorbed, and so Dan is left out of the sealed tribes. That is how deep the northern kingdom's idolatry went.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:28-29|Roma:
“Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles? As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.”

Paul quotes Hosea and Isaiah, not Jeremiah or Ezekiel, because his subject is the northern kingdom broken before the Assyrian captivity. The Most High called a people not of the Jews only but also of the Gentiles, meaning Ephraim: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.”

“Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved.” And “Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.” Paul's whosoever is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:2|2 Esdras:
Ezra asks, “what people have so kept thy commandments? Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.”

Israel by name kept the precepts; the heathen did not. So a commandment-keeper is Israel. Cornelius, devout, fearing God with all his house, giving alms and praying always, is keeping the precepts, and that marks him as an Israelite and not one of the heathen.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:2|Acts 22::
Cornelius was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” To be devout is to be devout according to the law, a man who keeps the commandments.

Scripture measures it that way: “one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there.” Devout is always measured by keeping the law. So when Cornelius is called devout, he is being called a keeper of the commandments.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:2|Hebrews:
“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright. For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected: for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.”

Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance, though he sought it with tears. A Roman, being of Esau, would have no place of repentance. So salvation opening to Cornelius is the proof that he was not of Esau's Rome. He could not be a Roman by nation.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:2|Psalms 1:
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.”

To fear the Most High is to keep his commandments. So when Cornelius is called “one that feared God with all his house”, he is a man that does the commandments, and with his whole house. That is the law, which was given to Israel only.

“He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them.”

The law, the statutes and the judgments were shown to Jacob and to Israel only, never to any other nation. So a man keeping the commandments and called devout is being marked as an Israelite. Israel followed the nations into idolatry; the nations never turned around and started keeping the law of the Most High.

Scholars themselves suppose from this language that Cornelius was a Jew, or a proselyte instructed in the Jewish religion, because the pagan Romans worshipped the sun, the moon, and gods like Mars, Venus, Jupiter and Hermes, not the commandments.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:2|Romans 9:
“As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.”

Scholars also record that Esau is the forefather of the Roman Empire. Esau is the father of Edom and of Rome. So if Cornelius were truly a Roman, he would be an Edomite, and the Most High rejected Esau. A devout man whose prayers the Most High hears cannot be of the one he hated.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:3-4|Psalms:
The angel told Cornelius, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” The Most High only regards the prayer of Zion, of the destitute, of the prisoner, so his hearing Cornelius marks Cornelius as Israel.

“When the Lord shall build up Zion, he shall appear in his glory. He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.” And he looks down from heaven “To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death.”

Israel were the prisoners of Rome, the oppressed. The Most High hears the prayer of the oppressed, not the prayer of the oppressor. Salvation coming up as a memorial belongs to Zion and to Jerusalem, not to the captor.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.”

Scripture says plainly who the saints are: “even of the children of Israel.” The prayers that come up before him are the prayers of his saints, the people near unto him. Cornelius' prayers came up for a memorial before God because he was of that people.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:3-4|Revela:
An angel stood at the altar with a golden censer, “and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne. And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel’s hand.”

The prayers that ascend before the Most High are the prayers of the saints, and the saints are Israel. So when Cornelius' prayers “are come up for a memorial before God”, they are rising the way the prayers of the saints rise.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|2 Ma:
Once scattered, they were mingled among the nations, learned their works and served their idols. And by decree they were forbidden to keep their law: “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.”

They were “brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices”, and a decree went out “that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices: And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.”

This is the same butchering endured in slavery, where it became unlawful to hold any Israelite name, custom or nationality. That is how Israelites became Gentiles in the flesh, in every nation.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Acts:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

So “in every nation” means the diaspora of Israel: devout men out of every nation under heaven, because Israel was scattered everywhere. When Peter says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, he is speaking of those Israelites.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Deut:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

The Gentiles are the dispersed northern tribes, scattered among the heathen and left few in number. That is who Peter means when he says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Exod:
Peter says, “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons.” That does not mean the nations are equal. “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.”

The Most High plainly had respect unto Israel and chose Israel above all people. He does respect Israel by nation. So “no respecter of persons” has to mean something else.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Ezek:
“Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings.” “Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries.”

That is how Israel came to be “in every nation.” Israel defiled their own land, so the Most High scattered them among the heathen and dispersed them through the countries. This is the diaspora, the same scattering some now call the African diaspora.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Gene:
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

The peace Peter preaches is Christ, Shiloh, unto whom the gathering of the people shall be. “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”. He is Lord of all the twelve tribes, gathering Judah first and then the scattered of every nation.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Isai:
“And they shall pass through it, hardly bestead and hungry: and it shall come to pass, that when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God.”

“And they shall look unto the earth; and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and they shall be driven to darkness.” That is the northern kingdom after the Assyrian flood: driven into darkness. These are the people who sat in darkness until Christ came.

“The riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.” Because the people refused “the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son”, the Lord brought up upon them “the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory.”

“He shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks”, and “gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces.” That is Ephraim broken and carried into Assyria, the beginning of the darkness the northern tribes sat in.

“Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern tribes driven into darkness, are the ones who saw the great light. That light is Christ, and Matthew says so plainly.

“Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah.”

Manasseh and Ephraim are named together, and that confirms who the darkened people are: the northern tribes. The people of Galilee of the Gentiles who walked in darkness are Israel's north, set against Judah, and they are the Gentiles Peter speaks of.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Jame:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad among the heathen. That is the “every nation” of Peter's word: not every race, but every nation where Israel was scattered.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|John:
“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”

The dispersed among the Gentiles are the scattered of Israel. When the Jews asked whether Christ would go and teach the Gentiles, they meant Israelites dispersed among the nations. That is who the Gentiles are in Peter's word: the northern tribes in the diaspora.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Matt:
Christ “came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying, The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; The people which sat in darkness saw great light.”

“Galilee of the Gentiles” proves the point. Zebulun and Naphtali are northern tribes, broken and driven into darkness, and they are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching repentance, for the kingdom of heaven was at hand. They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Prov:
“It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment.”

That is the kind of respect being denied. The Most High does not respect persons in judgment concerning his law. Whether a man sins outside the law or inside it, he is judged. He chose Israel by nation, but he does not excuse a man in judgment because of who he is.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Psal:
“Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron.”

Those that sit in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron, are the scattered Israelites. That is the same people of whom Matthew says, “to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.”
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Roma:
“Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile; But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: For there is no respect of persons with God.”

No respect of persons means judgment by the law: evil is repaid and good is rewarded, whoever does it. And it says the Jew first, and also the Gentile, because prophecy set Judah, Benjamin and Levi to rise up first. The Gentiles are the dispersed northern tribes scattered among the heathen.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:34-36|Zech:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.”

That is why it is “the Jew first.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first, so Judah wakes up before the rest. Then come the Gentiles, the northern tribes.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|1 Jo:
“Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Only Israel could receive remission, because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law was given to Israel alone. Only those given the law can break it and need remission of it.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|1 Ki:
Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes “that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.”

Zion is the city of David, which is Israel. So the stone laid in Zion is laid in Israel, and believing in Zion is believing in Israel. The whosoever that receives remission of sins through his name is whosoever of Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|2 Es:
“Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and their’s also that dwell the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel.”

The name of the Most High is found nowhere but in Israel, not among the nations. So remission of sins “through his name” is found in Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Acts:
“And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.”

The promise made of God unto the fathers is the hope of the twelve tribes, not of every nation. That promise, remission of sins through his name, is what Peter preached in Cornelius' house.

“Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.”

Peter told the same people, the men of Israel, to repent and be baptized for the remission of sins, the forgiveness of sins. It is the same message he brought to Cornelius: “through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.”

“Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.”

Peter says it to the men of Israel: ye are the children of the covenant. In Abraham's seed shall all the kindreds be blessed, and that seed is Christ blessing the twelve tribes.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Amos:
“And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.”

The prophets and Nazarites were raised up of the children of Israel. So when Peter calls them “the children of the prophets”, he is calling them Israel. And “To him give all the prophets witness”: the prophets were Israel's, and their witness was to Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Deut:
“Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.”

This is the curse of the law, and it was commanded to the people of Israel. They are the ones who said Amen to it. So the ones Christ redeemed from the curse of the law are Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Exod:
“And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the hill, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.”

He took the book of the covenant and read it to the people, “and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

The blood of the first covenant was sprinkled on the people of Israel, by twelve pillars for the twelve tribes. Only Israel was under the first covenant, and so only Israel is redeemed from its transgressions.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Gala:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.” That is the one “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.”

“That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.” The Gentiles here are the northern tribes. Christ redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on them.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Gene:
“Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?”

All nations blessed in Abraham means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth, for Abraham did not father every nation. The blessing of Abraham that comes on the Gentiles through Christ comes on the tribes of his seed.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Hebr:
The same covenant is written again in Hebrews: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts.”

“For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.” It is the house of Israel whose sins are remembered no more. Remission of sins belongs to that covenant.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.”

Christ died for the transgressions that were under the first testament. The first testament of animal sacrifice was given to Israel alone, so the redemption is for those who were under it.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Isai:
“Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.”

The stone laid in Zion is Christ. Those who believe on him shall not be ashamed. The stone is laid in Zion, and the believer Isaiah speaks of is in Zion. That is the whosoever of Peter's word.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Jere:
Remission of sins is the forgiveness and canceling of the debt, and it is the new covenant made with the house of Israel, not with every nation. “But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.”

“For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.” The Most High promised to forgive Israel's iniquity and remember their sins no more. That is the remission of sins Peter preached in Cornelius' house.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Luke:
“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.”

It is “the mercy promised to our fathers”, his holy covenant, “The oath which he sware to our father Abraham.” And John was sent before the face of the Lord “To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins.”

Remission of sins was given unto his people, Israel, the people the Lord God of Israel visited and redeemed. That is the remission all the prophets gave witness to.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Matt:
“For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.”

Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under the first covenant. The new testament is the covenant with the house of Israel, and the many are the many of Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:37-43|Roma:
Peter ends his rehearsal of Christ's ministry with this: “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” The whosoever is whosoever of Israel, of Zion.

Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel: “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” That defines the whosoever. The salvation he is speaking of is Israel's.

“For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.”

Paul says this in the same chapter where his prayer is for Israel to be saved. The scripture he is quoting is the stone laid in Zion, and the whosoever that believes on that stone is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:44-48|Ezek:
“While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.” They of the circumcision were astonished, “because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.”

But the Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel: “Neither will I hide my face any more from them: for I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel, saith the Lord God.” So the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom. The Most High hid his face from them no more.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:44-48|Jere:
“The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

Israel is the green olive tree. Its branches were broken “for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.” Both houses are branches of the one tree, and both were broken for their evil. That is why the one grafted back in is no stranger to the tree, and why neither may boast against the other.
docs/study/acts/10.md|Acts 10:44-48|Roma:
Ephraim is the wild olive tree grafted back in among the tribes: “thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches.”

The north believed on Christ while much of the south, the Pharisees, stumbled at him. “Because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith.” But that is no ground to boast: “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

That is what the circumcision saw in Cornelius' house: the wild olive grafted back in, receiving the same Holy Ghost, speaking with tongues, which were known languages, not unknown, as in Acts 2. So Peter asked, “Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?” and commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord.
docs/study/acts/11.md|Acts 11:18|Acts 5::
“When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.”

Repentance goes to Israel: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.”

So the Gentiles granted repentance are Israelites who took on Gentile customs. Either the northern kingdom, broken off before Assyria when Pekah the son of Remaliah conspired against Judah, or Judah who became Gentiles under the Greeks. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, and these Gentiles are Israel.
docs/study/acts/11.md|Acts 11:19-20|Zech:
“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.” They went where the Israelites were scattered. Phenice was the coastal region north of Israel, modern Lebanon; Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean; Antioch was a major Roman city in ancient Syria, now Antakya, Turkey.

They preached to the Jews only because of the prophecy: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The Most High saves the tents of Judah first.

Then some of them, “men of Cyprus and Cyrene”, came to Antioch and “spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.” Those Grecians, or Hellenists, were Greek-speaking Jews. The Holman Christian Standard Bible calls them Hellenists, and the Zondervan compact Bible dictionary defines a Hellenist as a Jew who made Greek his tongue and adopted Greek ideas and practices.
docs/study/acts/11.md|Acts 11:1|Acts 10::
“And the apostles and brethren that were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.” Now Peter is rehearsing what happened in Acts 10.

Cornelius said, “Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing, And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God. Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter.”

The Gentiles in Acts 11:1 are a reference to Cornelius. He was not Italian by nation. He was an Israelite who served as a general over a hundred men in the Roman army, just as today there are black generals and black soldiers in the American army, and America is an extension of ancient Rome.

“Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons.”

That does not mean the Most High has no respect for his chosen nation. He is a respecter of persons concerning his chosen race. What Peter means is that God shows no partiality in judgment, whether a man is poor or mighty.

“The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”

The word was sent unto the children of Israel, and Cornelius received it. That marks Cornelius as an Israelite. He was specifically of the northern kingdom of Israel, a just man giving alms and keeping the commandments even while scattered.
docs/study/acts/11.md|Acts 11:1|Acts 22::
